# Point-in-time restore

Deleted the wrong records, ran a bad migration, or let a script loose on production? Pick a moment from before it
happened, and your app's data goes back to how it was then.

This is on for every PocketOne app. You don't need to set anything up.

## How far back you can go

PocketOne records every change to your database as it happens and keeps **the last 72 hours**. You can restore to any
second inside that window.

If history recording is turned off, the app restores from your PocketBase backups instead: the latest backup made at or
before the moment you pick. The steps below are the same either way. The app tells you which point it used.

## Restore from the dashboard

1. Sign in to the dashboard as a superuser and open **Settings → Backups**.
2. Find **Restore to a moment**. It shows how far back you can go.
3. Under **Restore to**, pick the date and time to go back to, then click **Restore**.

The app keeps serving while it rebuilds the old data, then restarts with it. That takes a few seconds for most apps.

## Changed your mind? Undo the restore

The data you replaced is kept, and changes keep being recorded after a restore. So after a restore, the section shows
when you restored and to what time, with an **Undo this restore** button. Click it to put things back as they were
just before you restored.

## What's covered

- **Restored:** your database: records, collections, rules, settings and superusers.
- **Not restored:** uploaded files, `pb_hooks`, `pb_public` and the logs. Keep those in your PocketBase backups, or in
  your own source control.

Only superusers can see or run a restore.

## From your terminal

Sign in to your app once ([Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote)), then:

```bash
pocketone remote restore points        # how far back you can go
pocketone remote restore to --at -2h   # back to two hours ago
```

`--at` takes a duration from now (`-2h`, `-30m`), a local time (`2026-11-10 15:00`) or an RFC 3339 time
(`2026-11-10T15:00:00Z`).

On the machine that runs the app, you can also work from its files directly. Pull a copy of the old database to look
through without touching the live one, or restore in place while the server is stopped (it's swapped in at the next
start):

```bash
pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-10T15:00:00Z --to /tmp/then.db   # a copy, safe any time
pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-10T15:00:00Z                     # in place, server stopped
```

## From an agent

An agent connected to your app over [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) has two tools: `restore_points` to see how far back it
can go, and `restore_restore_to` to restore. It needs a token with the `restore` scope, and only a superuser can grant
one.

## Keep history somewhere safer

By default, history is kept on the same disk as your database. That protects you from mistakes, but not from losing
the disk. To keep it in your own S3-compatible bucket, open **Settings → Backups → Point-in-time restore**, tick **Store
the history in my own S3 bucket**, fill in the bucket details, click **Test connection**, then **Save**.

## Change how far back it goes, or turn it off

In `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
pitr:
  retention: 168h   # keep a week instead of 72 hours
  # enabled: false  # stop recording; restores then use your backups
```

A longer window uses more storage. Every key is in the [pocketone.yaml reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/config-reference).

## How it works

- [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) records the history with Litestream and restores to any second.
- [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups) restores from PocketBase's own backups when PITR is off.
- Both answer the same [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1) contract, which is why the dashboard, the command and
  the MCP tools don't care which one is on.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/isolates

# PocketBase isolates: hundreds of apps in one process

An isolate is a complete PocketOne app: its own folder, `pb_data`, `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, dashboard and
superusers, at its own hostname. What's different is where it runs. Instead of a process or container of its own, it
runs inside one shared `pocketone` process, with its own JavaScript VM, and the host routes each request to it by
hostname.

Most apps sit idle most of the time, so a process or container per app is mostly paying for nothing. Isolates make a
server full of PocketBase apps cheap: SaaS with one app per customer, a site per client, a preview app per branch.

It's built into `pocketone`. You don't need Docker, Kubernetes or a separate host program.

## Try it in a minute

Put this `pocketone.yaml` in an empty folder:

```yaml
server: { http: "127.0.0.1:8090" }
multisite: {}
instances: { dev: true }
pocker: { root: ./pb_root }
```

Start it, then ask for any hostname:

```bash
pocketone serve
curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health
curl -H 'Host: shop.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health
```

In dev mode, each new hostname becomes an app: its folder appears under `pb_root/` and it starts on that first
request. Open `http://blog.localhost:8090/_/` for that app's own dashboard.

On a laptop, each new app answered its first request in about 45 ms, and later requests in under a millisecond. A
hundred running apps took the process from 53 MB to 365 MB: about 3 MB each.

## Run it for real

List your apps and their hostnames in an instances file:

```yaml
# instances.yaml
instances:
  - id: blog                          # also its folder: pb_root/blog
    hosts: [blog.example.com]
  - id: shop
    hosts: [shop.example.com]
    secrets: { STRIPE_KEY: sk_live_... }   # seen only by this app's hooks
    limits: { max_js_execution: 60s }
```

```yaml
# pocketone.yaml
multisite: {}
instances: { file: ./instances.yaml }
pocker: { root: ./pb_root }
```

The host checks the file every 2 seconds, so adding, changing or removing an app needs no restart. In production,
only the hostnames listed there are served. [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) gets certificates for them.

## What each app gets

- **Everything a PocketOne app has.** [Point-in-time restore](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/restore), [API tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens),
  [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/mcp), [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/sites), [bulk mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/bulk-mail) and the rest
  are on in every isolate. Each can be turned off per app.
- **Its own deploys.** [`pocketone deploy`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/deploy) and the [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote) work
  against each app's hostname.
- **Its own restarts.** A change to its `pb_hooks`, a restore or its settings restarts that app alone. Nothing else
  notices.

## Sandboxed from each other

Isolates share a process, so PocketOne puts the walls inside it. Assume every app's owner is hostile:

- **Memory:** each app's JS has a hard cap (64 MiB by default). Going past it is an out-of-memory error for that app
  only.
- **CPU:** every JS call (hook, route, cron, migration) is stopped after `max_js_execution`. At most
  `max_concurrent_js` calls per app run at once.
- **Files, SQL and network:** an app's hooks and SQL reach only its own data. Outbound requests can't reach private
  networks unless you allow them.
- **Failures stay put:** a broken hooks file, a panic or a failed migration takes down that app alone. It answers 502
  until it's fixed.
- **Secrets:** each app's hooks see only its own `secrets`.

Every limit has a default for the whole host and an override per app. [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox) lists every
check.

## When to use containers instead

An isolate runs the PocketOne code in the `pocketone` binary. For an app that needs a specific PocketBase release, use
the [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) runtime, which runs each app in its own container with the official binary of the
version it asks for. One host can run both.

## How it works

- [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) takes over `serve` when `pocketone.yaml` has a `multisite` section. It
  routes each request by hostname, applies the gates, and hands it to a runtime.
- [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) is the runtime that runs apps as isolates in the host's process.
- [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox) confines each isolate's JS, SQL and outbound network.
- [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) is the container runtime, for apps that need it.

# Desktop apps

Your app is a folder: `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations` and `pb_public`. `pocketone serve` runs it as a server, as always.
`pocketone desktop build` turns the same folder into an app your users double-click:

```sh
pocketone serve                  # the app as a server
pocketone desktop build          # a desktop app for this machine, in dist/
pocketone desktop build --all    # macOS, Windows and Linux, arm64 and amd64
```

All you need is `pocketone` and Docker. The build runs in a build image that holds Go and PocketOne's source, so
there's no Go, C compiler or Xcode to install, and every platform builds from any machine.

> **Preview.** Desktop builds work today, but how a desktop app handles trust and settings is still settling (see
> [What's next](#whats-next)). The desktop runtime uses Wails' cgo-free backends, which Wails marks experimental on
> macOS and Linux.

## How it works

The desktop app is your PocketOne app plus a window:

1. Your `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations` and `pb_public` are embedded in the executable. Nothing is read from disk, so
   nobody can change a shipped app's hooks.
2. When it starts, it runs your app's server on a private `127.0.0.1` port, applying your migrations to the user's data.
3. It opens a native window on that server, using the system's own webview: WebKit on macOS, WebView2 on Windows,
   WebKitGTK on Linux.

Your pages call the API with `fetch`, exactly as they do in a browser. The PocketBase JS SDK, realtime and file
uploads work the same, because it's the same server.

## Try it: hello world

PocketOne's source has a hello-world app in `ext/desktop/example/hello`: a hook, a migration and one page that lists
and adds greetings.

```js
// pb_hooks/main.pb.js
routerAdd("GET", "/api/hello", (e) => {
  const rows = $app.findRecordsByFilter("greetings", "", "-created", 50, 0)
  return e.json(200, { message: "Hello from PocketOne hooks", greetings: rows.map((r) => r.get("text")) })
})
```

Its `pocketone.yaml` keeps the server's data in the folder and names the desktop app:

```yaml
app:
  dir: pb_data
server:
  public_dir: pb_public
desktop:
  name: Hello
  id: dev.pocketone.hello
  width: 900
  height: 640
```

Run it both ways:

```sh
cd ext/desktop/example/hello
pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com password
pocketone serve                  # http://127.0.0.1:8090
pocketone desktop build          # dist/darwin-arm64/Hello.app on an Apple Silicon Mac
open dist/darwin-arm64/Hello.app
```

The server and the desktop app keep separate data: the server's in `pb_data/`, the desktop app's in your app-data
folder.

## Next

- [Building](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/build): targets, the build image, building with your own Go, and what lands in `dist/`.
- [How the app runs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/runtime): where each user's data lives, upgrades, the window and what each platform needs.
- [Signing and sharing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/signing): signing and notarizing for macOS, signing for Windows, and checksums for Linux.
- [Extension reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/extension): the `desktop` section of `pocketone.yaml` and building on the runtime from Go.

## What's next

A desktop app has one person at the keyboard and data on their machine, so PocketBase's users and superusers don't
quite fit. Being worked out:

- **Trust:** requests from the app's own window run as its owner, and nothing else on the machine can reach the server.
- **Settings:** a native Preferences window for the settings your app and its extensions declare, since the superuser
  dashboard isn't part of a shipped app.

# Starter kits

A starter kit is a whole PocketOne app to begin from: a `pb_pages` folder (and sometimes migrations), written in
TypeScript with [ETS templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets), run by the stock `pocketone` binary with no build step.
Start an app from one, then run it:

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter <kit>
cd myapp
pocketone superuser upsert you@example.com <password> --dir ./pb_data
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

`pocketone pages create myapp` with no `--starter` uses **minimal**, and `pocketone pages starters` lists the kits. The
folder must not exist yet.

| [daisyui](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/daisyui) | A layout with a responsive navbar and drawer, built with [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) and [DaisyUI](https://daisyui.com/) (cupcake theme). |

# Example apps

Small, complete apps that show what a PocketOne app looks like. Each is a PocketOne app with no Go: a `pb_pages`
folder (and sometimes migrations and hooks) run by the stock `pocketone` binary. Their source is in the PocketOne
repository, ready to copy.

## Starter kits

To start an app of your own instead, begin from a [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters): `pocketone pages create myapp --starter
<kit>`.

# HTMX Integration with Pages

[HTMX](https://htmx.org) lets HTML elements fetch HTML from the server and swap it into the page. Pages renders that HTML.

## Setting up HTMX

Add HTMX to your layout:

```html
<script
  src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/htmx/2.0.11/htmx.min.js"
  integrity="sha512-YdHy6FzjD4qoyI/yWGIbsKnJHe98r96np9XeYp3ovFL+0sNP/NbDrYlSLDr5a6Ndi5sRi9GgJj+suE7yLeUMNQ=="
  crossorigin="anonymous"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
></script>
```

## Route organization

HTMX requests want HTML fragments, not whole pages wrapped in your layout. Put the layout in a group, and the fragment routes outside it:

```
pb_pages/
  (site)/             # Pages with layouts
    +layout.ets       # Main site layout
    index.ets         # /
    products/
      index.ets       # /products
  xapi/               # HTMX endpoints (no layouts)
    products/
      search.ets      # /xapi/products/search
      create/
        index.ets     # /xapi/products/create
        index.ts      # its code
```

1. `(site)` holds full pages. Its `+layout.ets` wraps them, and the group adds nothing to the URL.
2. `xapi/` holds fragments. No layout applies to them, because there is no `+layout.ets` at the root.

Don't name the folder `api/`: `/api/` belongs to PocketBase.

A handler can also send a fragment directly with `ctx.res.html()`, which never applies layouts.

## Sharing partials

Render the same fragment on the first page load and in HTMX responses by keeping it in a `_private/` partial:

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    product-card.ets    # shared partial
  (site)/
    products/
      index.ets         # includes the partial
  xapi/
    products/
      more.ets          # includes the same partial
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/_private/product-card.ets -->
<div class="product-card" id="product-<%= product.id %>">
  <h3><%= product.getString('name') %></h3>
  <p><%= product.getString('description') %></p>
</div>
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/products/index.ets -->
<% const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 20) %>
<div class="products-container">
  <% for (const product of products) { %>
    <%- include('product-card', { product }) %>
  <% } %>
</div>
<button hx-get="/xapi/products/more?page=2" hx-target=".products-container" hx-swap="beforeend">
  Load More
</button>
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/more.ets -->
<%
  const page = Number(ctx.req.query('page') ?? 1)
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 20, (page - 1) * 20)
%>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { product }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Search as you type

```html
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/index.ets -->
<input
  type="search"
  name="q"
  hx-get="/xapi/products/search"
  hx-trigger="input changed delay:500ms"
  hx-target="#search-results"
  placeholder="Search products..."
/>
<div id="search-results"></div>
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/search.ets -->
<%
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter(
    'products', 'name ~ {:q}', 'name', 20, 0, { q: ctx.req.query('q') ?? '' }
  )
%>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { product }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Forms

```html
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/products/new.ets -->
<form hx-post="/xapi/products/create" hx-target="#products-list" hx-swap="beforeend">
  <input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Product Name" required />
  <textarea name="description" placeholder="Description" required></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Create Product</button>
</form>
<div id="products-list"></div>
```

```ts
// pb_pages/xapi/products/create/index.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { name, description } = ctx.req.body()
    const product = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('products'))
    product.set('name', name)
    product.set('description', description)
    ctx.app.save(product)
    return { product }
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/create/index.ets -->
<%- include('product-card', { product: data.product }) %>
```

## Out-of-band updates

Update more than one element with a single response:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/products/create/index.ets -->
<%- include('product-card', { product: data.product }) %>
<div id="product-count" hx-swap-oob="true"><%= ctx.app.countRecords('products') %> Products</div>
```

## Polling

```html
<div hx-get="/xapi/products/latest" hx-trigger="every 30s">
  <!-- refreshed every 30 seconds -->
</div>
```

## Realtime updates

With the [`realtime` plugin](plugins/realtime.md), a page can push rendered HTML to every subscriber. A template has `include()`, so render the partial there and send it:

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] }
```

```ts
// pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ts
module.exports = {
  post() {}, // accept POST; the page below does the work
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ets -->
<% ctx.realtime.send('chat', include('chat-msg', { message: ctx.req.body().message })) %>
```

```html
<!-- pb_pages/(site)/index.ets -->
<form hx-post="/xapi/chat" hx-swap="none" hx-on::after-request="if(event.detail.successful) this.reset()">
  <input type="text" name="message" />
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
<div id="chat"></div>
```

In the browser, subscribe to the topic with the PocketBase JS SDK and append what arrives:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pocketbase/dist/pocketbase.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)
  pb.realtime.subscribe('chat', (html) => {
    document.getElementById('chat').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', html)
  })
</script>
```

## Best practices

1. **Route organization**: keep fragment routes outside the layout group, in a folder like `xapi/`.
2. **Response size**: return only the HTML the swap needs.
3. **Loading states**: use `hx-indicator` to show progress.
4. **Security**: check `ctx.auth` in middleware before changing data, validate input on the server, and debounce triggers like search inputs.

# Speedrun: Connecting Your Fly.io App to a Custom Domain with Cloudflare Proxy

Custom domains on your Fly.io app with Cloudflare in front can be a little complex because you must validate the domain on Fly.io BEFORE turning on Cloudflare proxying. Follow these steps.

## 1. Create the Fly.io App

- Start by deploying your app on [Fly.io](https://fly.io/). Follow the standard process to get your app up and running.

## 2. Register Your Domain

- If you haven't already, register your domain. It's often convenient to register it through [Cloudflare](https://cloudflare.com), which will also handle your DNS and proxying needs.

## 3. Configure DNS in Cloudflare

- In Cloudflare's DNS settings, add **A** and **AAAA** records pointing to your Fly.io app's public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
- **Important:** Turn off proxying (the orange cloud icon) for these records. This ensures that the Fly.io app can be accessed directly.

## 4. Add a Certificate in Fly.io

- In your Fly.io dashboard, add an SSL certificate for your custom domain.
- Since proxying is turned off, Fly.io should be able to validate the certificate immediately. Your app should now respond on your custom domain, but it's not yet proxied through Cloudflare.

## 5. Verify Domain Ownership and Proxying

- From the Fly.io certificate area, add the **CNAME** record required for domain ownership verification.
- **Important:** Turn off proxying for the CNAME record as well. Fly.io needs to verify ownership whenever the SSL certificate is renewed, which requires direct access.
- Go back to Fly.io, check the certificate, and ensure domain ownership verification is successful.

## 6. Turn On Proxying in Cloudflare

- Once everything is verified and working, return to Cloudflare and turn on proxying (enable the orange cloud) for your A and AAAA records.
- In Cloudflare’s **SSL/TLS** settings, set the encryption mode to **Full** (not Full Strict) to ensure proper SSL handshakes between Cloudflare and Fly.io.

## 7. Test Your Setup

- Finally, browse to your new domain to confirm everything is working as expected with Cloudflare proxying enabled.

You now have a fully functioning Fly.io app served through a custom domain with Cloudflare as the proxy!

# Google OAuth2 Setup Guide

This guide walks you through setting up Google OAuth2 sign-in for your PocketOne app.

## 1. Create/Select Google Cloud Project

1. Go to [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com)
2. Either select an existing project or create a new one
3. If creating new, provide a project name when prompted

![Creating a new Google Cloud project](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-54-56.png)
![Naming the new project](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-56-00.png)
![Selecting the project](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-56-28.png)

## 2. Configure OAuth Credentials

1. Navigate to "Credentials" in the left sidebar
2. Click "Create Credentials" and select "OAuth client ID"

![Navigating to credentials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-56-56.png)
![Creating OAuth credentials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-07.png)

### Configure Application Type

1. Select "Web application" as the application type
2. Configure your authorized origins and redirect URIs:
   - **Authorized JavaScript origins**: Your application domain (e.g., `http://localhost:8090`)
   - **Authorized redirect URIs**: Your auth callback URL (e.g., `http://localhost:8090/auth/oauth/confirm`)

![Selecting web application](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-57.png)
![Configuring URIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-07-00-42.png)

### Configure Consent Screen (if needed)

If you haven't set up a consent screen before, you'll need to configure it:

1. Choose External/Internal user type
2. Fill in the required application information

![Consent screen setup](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-19.png)
![Consent screen details](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-57-27.png)

### Download Credentials

1. After creating the OAuth client, download the JSON credentials file
2. Store this file securely - it contains sensitive information

![Downloading credentials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-58-27.png)
![Credentials JSON format](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-58-37.png)

## 3. Configure OAuth2 in the dashboard

OAuth2 providers belong to an auth collection, usually `users`:

1. Open your app's dashboard (`/_/`) and go to **Collections**.
2. Open the `users` collection's settings (the gear icon) and its **Options** tab.
3. Under **OAuth2**, turn it on.
4. Click **Add provider** and pick **Google**.

![OAuth2 settings for the users collection](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-00.png)
![OAuth2 providers section](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-09.png)
![Adding new provider](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-17.png)
![Selecting Google provider](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-24.png)

There's no site URL to set for this. The `auth` plugin builds the redirect URL from the address the request came in
on: the scheme and host the browser used, plus `/auth/oauth/confirm`. So the redirect URI in Google must match that
address exactly. `http://localhost:8090` and `http://127.0.0.1:8090` are different to Google, so add each one you
use, plus your live domain (`https://example.com/auth/oauth/confirm`). Behind a proxy, the host is the one the
browser asked for, and HTTPS is detected from `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

### Provider Configuration

1. Enter your Client ID and Client Secret from the downloaded credentials
2. Configure any additional auth options as needed
3. Save your changes

![Configuring Google provider](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-32.png)
![Saving changes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2/2025-02-08-06-59-59.png)

## Customizing the Return URL

By default, the `auth` plugin uses `/auth/oauth/confirm` as the OAuth2 return path. Change it when you start the flow:

```ts
ctx.session.requestOAuth2('google', { redirectPath: '/custom/oauth/callback' })
```

Remember to add the new redirect URL to your Google OAuth2 configuration too.

## Implementation Guide

### 1. Turn on the auth plugin

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

### 2. Login form

```html
<form method="post" action="/auth/oauth">
  <input type="hidden" name="provider" value="google" />
  <button type="submit">Sign in with Google</button>
</form>
```

### 3. Start the flow

```ts
// pb_pages/auth/oauth.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.requestOAuth2(ctx.req.body().provider)
  },
}
```

`requestOAuth2` stores its state in a cookie and redirects the user to Google's consent screen.

### 4. Callback

```ts
// pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/index.ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(ctx.req.query('state'), ctx.req.query('code'))
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/index.ets -->
<mark><%= data.error %></mark>
```

### 5. Migration

Set up Google OAuth2 in a PocketBase migration:

```js
migrate(
  (app) => {
    const users = app.findCollectionByNameOrId('users')
    users.oauth2.enabled = true
    users.oauth2.providers = [
      {
        name: 'google',
        clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
        clientSecret: 'YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET',
      },
    ]
    app.save(users)
  },
  (app) => {
    const users = app.findCollectionByNameOrId('users')
    users.oauth2.enabled = false
    users.oauth2.providers = []
    app.save(users)
  }
)
```

### 6. Protected routes

```ts
// pb_pages/account/+middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

### 7. Auth state in the UI

```ets
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <div>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></div>
  <form method="post" action="/logout"><button>Log out</button></form>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```

### 8. Logout

```ts
// pb_pages/logout.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

See [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication) and the [auth plugin](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth).

## Troubleshooting

Common issues and solutions:

- **Invalid redirect URI**: Ensure your redirect URI exactly matches what's configured in Google Cloud Console
- **Consent screen not showing**: Make sure you've properly configured the OAuth consent screen
- **Authentication failed**: Verify your client ID and secret are correctly copied to the dashboard

## Security Considerations

- Always use HTTPS in production
- Keep your client secret secure
- Regularly rotate credentials
- Review Google OAuth2 access regularly in your Google Cloud Console

# Speedrun: Setting Up Email with Google Suite and AWS SES

<!-- @import "[TOC]" {cmd="toc" depthFrom=2 depthTo=6 orderedList=false} -->

## Prerequisite: Make sure you can receive emails first

To receive emails, you'll need an email provider. I use Google Suite, but you can choose any provider you prefer.

[Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail).

(Someone should write about how to do it using Proton.me)

## Create an SES Identity

Log in to your Amazon SES account and follow their getting started guide to create a FROM address and sending domain. Make sure you're in the region you prefer. This is important if you have existing domains because AWS frowns upon approving multiple sending regions.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-20-29-10.png)

Start by creating an Identity:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-20-30-52.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-20-33-41.png)

## Add DNS Records

You'll need to add DNS records provided by SES to your DNS provider. Unlike Google Suite, you'll need to enter these values manually. They do not provide integrations with any DNS providers.

![AWS SES DNS Setup](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-03-06-20-55.png)

**Note for Cloudflare users: If you’re using Cloudflare, make sure these records are not proxied.**

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-28-33.png)

## Add a custom FROM domain

Deliverability is better if you add a custom FROM domain:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-38-12.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-38-51.png)

It requires a few additional DNS entries. Note that the MX `priority` goes into a separate field, not the MX server field:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-41-08.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-42-35.png)

## Add DMARC settings

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-45-05.png)

## Verifying the Setup

After adding the DNS records, go back to AWS SES and wait for the domain to show as verified. Then, send a verification email. You should receive it if everything is set up correctly.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-32-26.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-35-46.png)

If verification takes too long, go to **Identities > DKIM**, click **Edit**, then **Save** to trigger an immediate re-verification.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-33-32.png)

## Submit for Approval

Before you can send emails to anyone, you must submit everything for approval in AWS SES. This step is crucial to avoid issues when sending emails outside your verified domain.

If you have previously had a domain approved, you may be able to skip this step. To find out, simply try sending a test message to anything with a different domain.

## Creating SMTP Credentials

Create SMTP credentials in the AWS SES console. These credentials will be used in your app's dashboard for sending emails.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-48-53.png)

## Configure SMTP in the dashboard

Once you have your SMTP credentials, head over to the dashboard (Settings → Mail).

Enter the SMTP credentials in the dashboard, and ensure the **SENDER** address is correctly set. If SES hasn't verified your email yet, you can test it by sending an email to `test@<yourdomain>`, which should go through if the domain is the same.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses/2024-09-08-22-53-02.png)

# Go API

The Go packages under [`ext/contracts`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts): each [contract](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts)'s interface, the types its operations take and return, and the helpers it ships, for a custom build or an extension that calls one. Generated from the source with `go/doc`, examples included. An extension's JavaScript side is in the [JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript).

## Contracts

| Package | |

# REST API

Every PocketOne app serves a JSON API under `/api/`: its collections' records, signing in, files, realtime and, for
superusers, the admin endpoints the dashboard uses. The [JavaScript SDK](https://pocketone.dev/docs/authentication#sign-in-from-a-client)
wraps it, but anything that speaks HTTP can use it.

| Area | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [Records](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records) | list, view, create, update and delete a collection's records |
| [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/authentication) | sign in, refresh, sign up flows, verify, reset, change email, impersonate |
| [Realtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/realtime) | subscribe to record changes over server-sent events |
| [Files](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/files) | download files and thumbnails, protected-file tokens |
| [Batch](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/batch) | several record writes in one transaction |
| [Collections](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/collections) | create and change collections (superusers) |
| [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/settings) | the app's settings, test mail and S3 (superusers) |
| [Logs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/logs) | request and app logs (superusers) |
| [Crons](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/crons) | list and run scheduled jobs (superusers) |
| [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/backups) | make, download, upload and restore backups (superusers) |
| [SQL](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/sql) | run a SQL query (superusers) |
| [Health](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/health) | is the app up |
| [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) | the endpoints PocketOne's extensions add, under `/api/_c/` |

## Requests

The base URL is your app's address: `https://myapp.example.com/api/...`, or `http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/...` locally.
Send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json`, or `multipart/form-data` when you upload files.

## Auth

Sign in through an [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/authentication) endpoint and you get a token. Send it as the
`Authorization` header, with or without `Bearer `:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records \
  -H "Authorization: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..."
```

A request with no token is a guest. What each request may do is decided by the collection's [API
rules](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules); endpoints marked **superusers** need a token from the `_superusers` collection. An [API
token](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens) works the same way for scripts and other apps.

## Lists

Every list endpoint takes the same query parameters:

| Parameter | Does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | the page, from 1 | `page=2` |
| `perPage` | items per page, up to 1000 (default 30) | `perPage=100` |
| `sort` | fields, `-` for descending, `@random` for random order | `sort=-created,title` |
| `filter` | a [filter](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules#the-filter-language) | `filter=(published=true && title~'hello')` |
| `expand` | relations to include, nested with dots, up to 6 levels | `expand=author,comments_via_post.author` |
| `fields` | only these fields in the answer; `*` for all at a level, `:excerpt(200,true)` to shorten | `fields=id,title,expand.author.name` |
| `skipTotal` | skip counting `totalItems` and `totalPages` (faster for big tables) | `skipTotal=1` |

A list answers:

```json
{
  "page": 1,
  "perPage": 30,
  "totalItems": 2,
  "totalPages": 1,
  "items": [{ "id": "...", "collectionName": "posts", "title": "Hello" }]
}
```

URL-encode `filter` and `sort` values in real requests (`curl --get --data-urlencode` does it for you).

## Errors

Errors answer with a status and a JSON body:

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "message": "Failed to create record.",
  "data": {
    "title": { "code": "validation_required", "message": "Cannot be blank." }
  }
}
```

| Status | Means |
|---|---|
| 400 | the request is invalid; `data` names each field's problem |
| 401 | the endpoint needs auth and the request has none (or its token is invalid) |
| 403 | the request's auth may not do this |
| 404 | not found, or a rule hides it (so ids don't leak) |
| 429 | too many requests (rate limits, set in Settings) |

## Next

- [Records](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records): the endpoints most clients use.
- [API rules and filters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules): who may call what.
- [Custom routes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/routes): add endpoints of your own.

# CLI reference

Every command of the `pocketone` binary with its [standard extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard): PocketBase's own, the ones extensions add, and a `pocketone remote …` command for every operation of every contract, generated from it ([how](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote)). `pocketone <command> --help` says the same.

## Global flags

Every command takes these.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--config` | string | – | the config file (default ./pocketone.yaml, else next to the executable) |
| `--env-file` | string | – | secrets for $VAR references in the config file (default .env beside it); never passed to the app |

## pocketone cache

Shows each extension's folder in pb\_cache and its size

```
pocketone cache
```

pb\_cache, next to pb\_data, holds files extensions can rebuild (one folder each). It's never backed up or deployed, and emptying it is always safe.

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

### pocketone cache clear

Empties pb\_cache (every extension's folder, or the ones named)

```
pocketone cache clear [extension...]
```

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

## pocketone clone

Starts a local project from a running app: makes the folder, links and signs in, and pulls its code

```
pocketone clone <url> [dir]
```

Makes dir (default: named after the app's host, e.g. pocketcon for https://pocketcon.dev), adds the app as the project's default remote, signs in (in the browser when the app offers it, else with an API token), and pulls pb\_hooks, pb\_migrations, pb\_pages, pb\_public, pb\_templates, package.json, the lockfile and patches/. pb\_data never comes. Then run `dev` in the folder to keep both sides in step.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--device` | bool | – | sign in on another device with a code (SSH, headless) |
| `--name` | string | `default` | remote name |
| `--no-browser` | bool | – | print the sign-in URL instead of opening a browser |
| `--token` | string | – | use this API token (pbt\_..., a PocketHost token, or a JWT) |
| `--token-stdin` | bool | – | read the token from stdin |

From [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy).

## pocketone config

Lists the pocketone.yaml sections this binary understands, with their defaults

```
pocketone config
```

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | bool | – | print the sections as JSON (name, doc, owning extension, keys with types and defaults) |

From [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config).

### pocketone config check

Checks the config file: every section known and valid, every $VAR set

```
pocketone config check
```

From [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config).

## pocketone deploy

Deploys pb\_hooks, pb\_migrations, pb\_pages, pb\_public and packages to a remote

```
pocketone deploy [remote]
```

Deploys the project's code set (pb\_\* folders except pb\_data and pb\_cache, package.json, bun.lock(b), patches/, and the production node\_modules tree) to a remote. Only changed files are uploaded and the remote swaps them in. Hooks, pages and public files take effect by themselves; migrations and packages apply when the app restarts: pass --restart, or run 'pocketone restart' later. A deploy stops when files changed on the remote since your last deploy, pull or dev (an edit through the file drive, a migration the dashboard wrote) and lists them; --force overwrites them. A project with no record of the remote yet (a fresh checkout, CI) deploys without that check.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | – | list what would be deployed, deploy nothing |
| `-e`, `--exclude` | stringSlice | – | exclude patterns (pb\_data and pb\_cache are always excluded) |
| `--force` | bool | – | deploy even when files changed on the remote since your last deploy, pull or dev, overwriting them |
| `-i`, `--include` | stringSlice | – | add include patterns (default set: pb\_\*,pb\_\*/\*\*/\*,package.json,bun.lockb,bun.lock,patches,patches/\*\*/\*) |
| `--no-node-modules` | bool | – | don't ship node\_modules; leave the remote's alone |
| `--node-modules` | bool | – | ship the production node\_modules tree (default with a package.json) |
| `--out` | string | – | write the deploy set to a local folder instead of deploying |
| `--restart` | bool | – | restart the app after deploying when migrations or packages changed |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | bool | – | list every file |

From [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy).

## pocketone desktop

Commands under desktop

From [Desktop](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/extension).

### pocketone desktop build

Build this folder's app as a native desktop app (this platform; --all for every platform)

```
pocketone desktop build
```

Compiles the PocketOne app in the current folder into a desktop app: pb\_hooks, pb\_migrations and pb\_public are
embedded in the executable, which runs the app's server on a private 127.0.0.1 port and shows it in a native window.
Each user's data lives in their own app-data folder, named by the app id.

Without flags it builds for this machine. --all builds macOS (arm64, amd64), Windows (amd64, arm64) and Linux
(amd64, arm64); --target picks some. The apps land in dist/, macOS's as an .app and a .dmg.

With a sign section in pocketone.yaml it signs what it built afterwards, here on this machine: macOS with your
Developer ID (and notarizes), Windows with your command, Linux with GPG. --no-sign skips it.

It runs in Docker, in the build image matching this pocketone (Go and PocketOne's source, vendored, so it needs
nothing else and works offline once the image is here). --local builds with your own Go and a PocketOne checkout.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | – | build for every platform |
| `--image` | string | – | the build image (default pocketone-build:dev) |
| `--local` | bool | – | build with your own Go instead of the build image |
| `--no-sign` | bool | – | skip pocketone.yaml's desktop.sign section (builds stay signed ad hoc) |
| `--out` | string | `dist` | the folder the apps are written to |
| `-r`, `--remote` | string | – | the remote (a name or URL); default: the project's default remote |
| `--source` | string | – | a PocketOne checkout: `--local` builds against it; a development pocketone builds its image from it (default $P1\_SOURCE, else the checkout this folder is in) |
| `--target` | stringSlice | – | platforms to build, as os/arch (darwin/arm64,windows/amd64,...) |

From [Desktop](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/extension).

### pocketone desktop image

Build the desktop build image from a PocketOne checkout

```
pocketone desktop image
```

Builds the image desktop build runs in (Go plus this checkout's source, vendored) and tags it. A release
publishes it as ghcr.io/pocketonehq/pocketone-build:v&lt;version&gt;; a development pocketone builds pocketone-build:dev on first use.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-r`, `--remote` | string | – | the remote (a name or URL); default: the project's default remote |
| `--source` | string | – | the PocketOne checkout (default $P1\_SOURCE, else the one this folder is in) |
| `--tag` | string | `pocketone-build:dev` | the image's tag |

From [Desktop](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/extension).

### pocketone desktop prepare

Write the build image's vendored module into &lt;dir&gt; (the build image's Dockerfile runs this)

```
pocketone desktop prepare <dir>
```

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-r`, `--remote` | string | – | the remote (a name or URL); default: the project's default remote |
| `--source` | string | – | the PocketOne source tree |

From [Desktop](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/extension).

## pocketone dev

Keeps the project's code and a remote in step both ways (and streams the remote's logs)

```
pocketone dev [remote]
```

Syncs pb\_hooks, pb\_migrations, pb\_pages, pb\_public and the other pb\_\* folders, package.json, bun.lock(b) and patches/ both ways: edits here are uploaded half a second after you save, and changes on the remote (such as migrations the dashboard writes) are downloaded within seconds. node\_modules is only uploaded, when package.json or the lockfile changes. pb\_data is never synced. Hooks, pages and public files take effect by themselves; migrations and packages you upload apply when the app restarts: type r and Enter. State is kept in .pocketone/; files to leave out go in .pocketoneignore.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-e`, `--exclude` | stringSlice | – | exclude patterns (pb\_data and pb\_cache are always excluded) |
| `-i`, `--include` | stringSlice | – | add include patterns (default set: pb\_\*,pb\_\*/\*\*/\*,package.json,bun.lockb,bun.lock,patches,patches/\*\*/\*) |
| `--no-logs` | bool | – | don't stream the remote's logs |
| `--no-node-modules` | bool | – | don't ship node\_modules; leave the remote's alone |
| `--node-modules` | bool | – | ship the production node\_modules tree (default with a package.json) |
| `--poll` | duration | `5s` | how often to check the remote for changes |
| `--prefer` | string | – | on the first sync, files that differ: local (upload yours) or remote (download theirs); default asks |
| `--push-only` | bool | – | only upload changes (the old one-way dev); never download |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | bool | – | list every file |

From [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy).

## pocketone extensions

Manages the extensions' own schema (their migrations)

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

### pocketone extensions migrate

Applies or reverts an extension's migrations

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

### pocketone extensions migrate down

Reverts an extension's last n migrations (default 1; 0: all of them)

```
pocketone extensions migrate down <extension> [n]
```

Reverting drops what the migrations created, data included. The next start applies them again, unless the extension is turned off (`&lt;extension&gt;: {enabled: false}` in pocketone.yaml).

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

### pocketone extensions migrate up

Applies pending extension migrations (startup does this too)

```
pocketone extensions migrate up [extension]
```

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

### pocketone extensions migrations

Lists each extension's migrations and whether they're applied

```
pocketone extensions migrations
```

Extensions apply their migrations at startup, after PocketBase's own and before the app's pb\_migrations, and record them in \_extension\_migrations (apart from the app's \_migrations).

From [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

## pocketone migrate

Executes app DB migration scripts

```
pocketone migrate
```

Supported arguments are:
- up            - runs all available migrations
- down [number] - reverts the last [number] applied migrations
- create name   - creates new blank migration template file
- collections   - creates new migration file with snapshot of the local collections configuration
- history-sync  - ensures that the \_migrations history table doesn't have references to deleted migration files


| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dev` | bool | – | enable dev mode, aka. printing logs and sql statements to the console |
| `--dir` | string | `<the binary's folder>/pb_data` | the PocketBase data directory |
| `--encryptionEnv` | string | – | the env variable whose value of 32 characters will be used as encryption key for the app settings (default none) |
| `--hooksDir` | string | – | the directory with the JS app hooks |
| `--hooksPool` | int | `15` | only with `--jsvm` goja: the JS runtimes kept ready for hooks |
| `--jsvm` | string | `quickjs` | the JS engine: quickjs (PocketOne's) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility) |
| `--migrationsDir` | string | – | the directory with the user defined migrations |
| `--queryTimeout` | int | `30` | the default SELECT queries timeout in seconds |

From PocketBase.

### pocketone pitr restore

Restore the database as it was at --at, into --to, or in place on the next start

```
pocketone pitr restore
```

With --to, writes the database as it was at --at into that file (any time, also on a fresh machine with the same bucket config). Without --to, stages the restore in place; run it while the server is stopped: the swap happens on the next start.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--at` | string | – | time to restore to (RFC 3339) |
| `--to` | string | – | write into this file instead of restoring in place |

From [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr).

### pocketone pitr status

Show the restorable window and history size

```
pocketone pitr status
```

From [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr).

## pocketone serve

Starts the web server (default to 127.0.0.1:8090 if no domain is specified)

```
pocketone serve [domain(s)]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--automigrate` | bool | `true` | enable/disable auto migrations |
| `--autotls` | bool | – | HTTPS certificates through CertMagic instead of the built-in autocert (with serve &lt;domain&gt; or `--https`): other CAs, extra domains, wildcards through DNS-01 |
| `--autotlsCA` | string | – | certificate authority for `--autotls`: letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL |
| `--autotlsDNS` | string | – | DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges with `--autotls` (supported: cloudflare) |
| `--autotlsDNSTokenEnv` | string | `CF_API_TOKEN` | environment variable holding the DNS provider's API token for `--autotlsDNS` |
| `--autotlsDomains` | stringSlice | – | extra domains for `--autotls`, obtained at start (comma separated; wildcards like \*.example.com need `--autotlsDNS`) |
| `--autotlsEmail` | string | – | ACME account email for `--autotls` (expiry notices from the CA) |
| `--dev` | bool | – | enable dev mode, aka. printing logs and sql statements to the console |
| `--dir` | string | `<the binary's folder>/pb_data` | the PocketBase data directory |
| `--encryptionEnv` | string | – | the env variable whose value of 32 characters will be used as encryption key for the app settings (default none) |
| `--hooksDir` | string | – | the directory with the JS app hooks |
| `--hooksPool` | int | `15` | only with `--jsvm` goja: the JS runtimes kept ready for hooks |
| `--hooksWatch` | bool | `true` | auto restart the app on pb\_hooks file change; it has no effect on Windows |
| `--http` | string | – | TCP address to listen for the HTTP server (if domain args are specified - default to 0.0.0.0:80, otherwise - default to 127.0.0.1:8090) |
| `--https` | string | – | TCP address to listen for the HTTPS server (if domain args are specified - default to 0.0.0.0:443, otherwise - default to empty string, aka. no TLS) The incoming HTTP traffic also will be auto redirected to the HTTPS version |
| `--indexFallback` | bool | `true` | fallback the request to index.html on missing static path, e.g. when pretty urls are used with SPA |
| `--jsvm` | string | `quickjs` | the JS engine: quickjs (PocketOne's) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility) |
| `--migrationsDir` | string | – | the directory with the user defined migrations |
| `--origins` | stringSlice | `[*]` | CORS allowed domain origins list |
| `--pagesDir` | string | – | the directory with the app's pages (default pb\_pages next to pb\_data); served when it exists |
| `--pitr` | bool | `true` | point-in-time restore: replicate data.db into pb\_data/litestream/ while serving |
| `--pitrRetention` | duration | `72h0m0s` | how far back a point-in-time restore can go |
| `--publicDir` | string | `<the binary's folder>/pb_public` | the directory to serve static files |
| `--queryTimeout` | int | `30` | the default SELECT queries timeout in seconds |
| `--s3Redirect` | bool | `true` | answer file downloads with a short-lived signed redirect to the bucket when S3 file storage is on |
| `--s3RedirectTTL` | duration | `5m0s` | how long each signed file download URL stays valid |

From PocketBase.

## pocketone upgrade

Upgrades this executable to the latest release, keeping the old one as &lt;name&gt;-&lt;version&gt;

```
pocketone upgrade
```

Upgrades this executable to the latest release, keeping the old one as &lt;name&gt;-&lt;version&gt;.

The newest release is offered, prereleases included. Moving from a stable release to a prerelease asks first
(no means the newest stable release instead, if there's a newer one); from one prerelease to the next it doesn't.

| Flag | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backup` | bool | `true` | Back up pb\_data after upgrading, if this folder has one |
| `-y`, `--yes` | bool | – | Move from a stable release to a prerelease without asking |

From [Upgrade](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/upgrade).

# MCP reference

A PocketOne app serves MCP at `/mcp` ([MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp)): PocketBase's whole API as `pb_*` tools, the tools your `pb_hooks` add, and one tool per operation of every contract the app provides, listed here for the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard). Each contract tool calls the contract, so it passes the same token scope check and hooks as the REST API and the CLI ([how](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote)). Uploads and downloads have no tool.

## api-tokens.verify/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1). Answered by [API Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `api-tokens_verify_verify` | Checks an API token and says who it acts as and what it may do (its scopes, with their values). |  | `api_tokens_verify` | `token` (string), `ip` (string) |

## bulkmail/v1

[Contract page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1). Answered by [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) in the standard set.

| Tool | What it does | Reads only | Token scope | Arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bulkmail_count` | Says how many recipients an audience reaches, how many of them are suppressed, and a few sample addresses. |  | `bulkmail:read` | `audience` (json) |
| `bulkmail_start` | Queues a campaign's recipients and starts sending (Limit &gt; 0: at most that many new recipients). |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string), `limit` (int) |
| `bulkmail_pause` | Stops sending a campaign; Resume carries on. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `bulkmail_resume` | Carries on sending a paused campaign. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `bulkmail_cancel` | Stops a campaign for good; recipients not yet sent to are dropped. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string) |
| `bulkmail_preview` | Renders a campaign's message for one recipient (the first in its audience when Email is empty). |  | `bulkmail:read` | `campaign` (string), `email` (string) |
| `bulkmail_test` | Sends a campaign's message to one address, marked as a test. |  | `bulkmail` | `campaign` (string), `to` (string) |

## cache.clear/v1

| `instance_watch_unwatch` | Stops changes for a hostname on a stream. |  | `fleet` | `conn` (string), `host` (string) |

# pocketone.yaml reference

Every section the `pocketone` binary understands, from `pocketone config --json`. Each extension owns its own section. `pocketone config check` checks a file. How the file works (where it's found, `.env` secrets) is on the [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config) page.

#### `api-tokens:`

Turns the api-tokens extension off on a single app (`enabled: false`). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's `extensions.api-tokens`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. |

Owned by [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

#### `app:`

The single app, for every command that opens it: data dir, dev mode, encryption, JS engine, hooks, migrations, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used on a multisite host.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string |  | The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. |
| `dev` | bool |  | Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. |
| `encryption_env` | string |  | Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. |
| `query_timeout` | duration |  | Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. |
| `hooks_dir` | string |  | The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. |
| `jsvm` | string |  | The JS engine for pb_hooks and pb_migrations: quickjs (PocketOne's, the default) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility: pages, $mcp, $apiTokens and JS contracts are off). The --jsvm flag wins. |
| `hooks_pool` | int |  | Only with jsvm: goja: how many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. |
| `migrations_dir` | string |  | The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. |
| `env_allow` | list of string |  | Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none. |
| `js_limits.memory` | int |  | The app's JS memory: the JS heap plus the Go objects JS holds, such as 128MiB. Default 64MiB. |
| `js_limits.task_time` | duration |  | JS time one stretch of a task (a request, a hook, a cron job, each part between awaits) may use, Go calls and waits not counted, such as 10s. Default 5s. |
| `js_limits.task_wall` | duration |  | Wall time one stretch of JS may take, sync Go calls included, such as 60s; an async handler's awaits end a stretch and don't count. Default 30s. |
| `js_limits.await_time` | duration |  | How long an async handler (a request, a hook, a cron job) may take in all, awaits included, such as 30m; past it, or when the client goes away, the handler stops at its next await. Default 15m. |

#### `autotls:`

Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls* flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | bool |  | Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. |
| `email` | string |  | ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. |
| `ca` | string |  | letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. |
| `storage` | string |  | Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. |
| `domains` | list of string |  | Extra domains to get at start; wildcards (*.example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. |
| `dns.provider` | string |  | DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. |
| `dns.api_token` | string |  | The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. |
| `dns.api_token_env` | string |  | Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv. |

Owned by [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls).

#### `backups:`

Turns the backups extension off on a single app (`enabled: false`). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's `extensions.backups`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. |

Owned by [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

#### `bulkmail:`

Turns the bulkmail extension off on a single app (`enabled: false`). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's `extensions.bulkmail`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. |

Owned by [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

#### `cache:`

The cache (cache/v1): one store for every app in the process (memory, disk tier), and caps per bucket.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | Turns the cache off when false; extensions then run uncached. |
| `eviction` | string |  | Which values leave memory (or disk) first when the store reaches its ceiling: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. |
| `max_memory` | int |  | Memory for every bucket together, such as 512MiB. Default 128MiB. |
| `disk` | bool |  | Turns on a disk tier in pb_cache/cache, next to pb_data (on a multisite host, the host's own pb_cache). |
| `disk_path` | string |  | Puts the disk tier in a cache folder there instead of pb_cache, and turns it on. Relative: to the app's folder (the one holding pb_data) when the app has the process to itself, the working directory when several apps share it (Pocker). |
| `max_disk` | int |  | Size of the disk tier for every bucket together, such as 10GiB. Default 1GiB. |
| `defaults.eviction` | string |  | Which of the bucket's entries go first when it's full: lru, mru, fifo or lifo. |
| `defaults.max_items` | int |  | Most entries the bucket holds. |
| `defaults.max_memory` | int |  | Most bytes of keys and values the bucket holds in memory, such as 32MiB (the default). |
| `defaults.max_disk` | int |  | Most bytes of disk files the bucket's keys point at, each counted in full, such as 256MiB (the default). |
| `defaults.ttl` | int |  | How long an entry lives unless the code says otherwise, such as 10m. |
| `buckets` | map of object |  | Caps per bucket name, over what its code asks for. |

Owned by [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache).

#### `deploy:`

Turns the deploy extension off on a single app (`enabled: false`). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's `extensions.deploy`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. |

Owned by [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

#### `desktop:`

How `pocketone desktop build` names and sizes the desktop app built from this folder.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | The app's name: the window title and the executable's name. Default: the folder's name. |
| `id` | string |  | Reverse-DNS app id (dev.example.notes): names the app's data folder on each user's machine and its single-instance lock. Default: app.pocketone.<name>. |
| `width` | int |  | The window's starting width. Default: 1024. |
| `height` | int |  | The window's starting height. Default: 768. |
| `sign.macos.identity` | string |  | The signing identity in your keychain, as security find-identity -v -p codesigning shows it: Developer ID Application: Your Name (TEAMID). |
| `sign.macos.notary_profile` | string |  | The notarytool keychain profile (xcrun notarytool store-credentials <profile>). Set: each DMG is notarized and stapled. Empty: signed, not notarized. |
| `sign.windows.command` | string |  | The command that signs one executable in place; {file} is its path. signtool on Windows, osslsigncode anywhere, or your signing service's tool. |
| `sign.linux.gpg_key` | string |  | The GPG key to sign with (its email or id). Each build gets <name>.sha256 and a detached <name>.asc signature. |

Owned by [Desktop](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop).

#### `docker:`

Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `socket` | string |  | The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. |
| `image` | string |  | Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. |
| `binaries` | string |  | Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. |
| `versions` | list of string |  | The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). |
| `root` | string |  | Folder with one folder per instance (<root>/<id>). Required. |
| `home` | string |  | The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. |
| `default_version` | string |  | Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0.*. Empty: such instances fail. |
| `min_upstream` | string |  | Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. |
| `idle_ttl` | duration |  | Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. |
| `max_concurrent_starts` | int |  | Containers starting at once. Default 4. |
| `start_timeout` | duration |  | How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. |
| `nano_cpus` | int |  | CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. |
| `pids_limit` | int |  | Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. |
| `nofile` | list of int |  | Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. |
| `cap_drop` | list of string |  | Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. |
| `no_new_privileges` | bool |  | Set no-new-privileges on every container. |
| `network` | string |  | Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. |
| `adopt_image` | string |  | Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager). |

Owned by [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker).

#### `edges:`

The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `self` | string |  | This edge's id, such as lax-1. |
| `list` | list of object |  | The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. |

Owned by [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge).

#### `firewall:`

Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_cidrs` | list of string |  | Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. |
| `client_ip_headers` | list of string |  | Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. |
| `trusted_clients` | list of string |  | Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. |
| `trusted_client_headers` | list of string |  | Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. |
| `rate_limit_header_prefix` | string |  | Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit. |

Owned by [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall).

#### `instances:`

Where a multi-instance host's instances come from (a YAML file), and dev mode (serve unknown hostnames).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | `instances.yaml` | The instances file (id, hosts and settings for each instance), reloaded when it changes. |
| `dev` | bool |  | Also serve unknown hostnames: each becomes an instance named after it, in dev mode, with its folder made on first use. |

Owned by [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite).

#### `kv:`

Turns the kv extension off on a single app (`enabled: false`). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's `extensions.kv`.

# Extensions

PocketOne is PocketBase plus extensions. An extension is a Go module in [`ext/`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext) that adds one feature to an
app: point-in-time restore, deploys, API tokens, MCP, bulk mail, AI models, server-rendered pages. Each is compiled into
the binary, registers itself on every app, and is configured in `pocketone.yaml`. PocketBase's own code ("core")
changes only where an extension needs a place to hook in.

This page is the reference for how extensions work. To build one, see [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension); for the
idea behind contracts, [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/how-pocketone-fits-together).

## Kinds

| Kind | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | ships in every `pocketone` binary and runs on every app unless turned off | the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard) |
| **Community** | in `ext/`, added to a custom Go build | the [catalogue](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/all) |
| **Host** | runs many apps on one server (isolates, docker, edges) | in the standard set, on only in that mode |

Every extension has its own README (its page in the catalogue), a version, a changelog and owners.

## Turning one on and off

- **Standard extensions** are on. Turn one off on a single app with `enabled: false` in its `pocketone.yaml` section:

  ```yaml
  bulkmail:
    enabled: false
  ```

  Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why.
- **Community extensions** are added to a custom build in Go: `set.Add(myextension.New(...))` on the standard set.
- **On a multisite host**, each instance's `extensions.<name>` settings sit over the defaults, and `enabled: false`
  keeps an extension from running for that instance.

## What an extension is made of

| Part | What it does | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `Name()` | its config key, table prefix and log name | `pocketone.yaml` section `<name>:`, collections `_<name>_*` |
| `Register(app, cfg)` | binds it to an app: its hooks, its contracts | every app it runs on |
| `Contracts()` | the contracts it implements, requires, wraps and works with | the startup lines, the contract catalogue |
| Settings | its `pocketone.yaml` section, read on start | `pocketone config`, the [pocketone.yaml reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/config-reference) |
| Migrations | its own tables, tracked apart from the app's `pb_migrations` | `_<name>_*` collections |
| `BindJS`, `TypeScript()` | a global for hooks and page code (`$llm`, `$kv`) and its types | the [JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript) |
| A dashboard screen | the contract's `UI` | the dashboard's sidebar |
| Disposable files | caches it can rebuild | `pb_cache/<name>/` |

An extension has no HTTP routes of its own. Everything a client can call is a contract.

## Contracts

A contract is a named, versioned Go interface in [`ext/contracts`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts): `deploy/v1`,
`kv/v1`, `llm.text/v1`. Extensions meet only through contracts, never by importing each other:

- An extension **provides** a contract (`Contract.Provide`) or a default that steps aside for any other provider
  (`ProvideDefault`).
- An extension, a hook or a custom build **looks one up** by contract (`Contract.Must(app)`), not by extension.
- A **wrapper** decorates whatever provides a contract (`Contract.Wrap`).
- **`providers:`** in `pocketone.yaml` picks one when two extensions provide the same contract:

  ```yaml
  providers:
    restore/v1: backups
  ```

At startup, PocketOne resolves every contract and prints who provides it:

```
standard: restore/v1 ← pitr
standard: bulkmail off: needs mail.fallback/v1, which nothing provides
```

A contract's major version is part of its name. Its promise never changes within a version; a different promise is a
new version beside the old one. Each contract has a README with its owners, how to use it and how to provide it, and
a generated list of the extensions that provide, require and work with it: the [contract catalogue](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts).

## Extension APIs

A contract with operations is a wire API. Every operation is, from one definition:

| Surface | Where |
|---|---|
| An HTTP endpoint | `/api/_c/<contract>/<operation>`: the [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) reference |
| A `pocketone` command | `pocketone remote <contract> <operation>`: the [CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli) |
| An MCP tool | at `/mcp`: the [MCP tools](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) reference |
| A hook in Go and JS | `deployv1.OnUpload`, `onDeployUpload`: change the input or refuse the call |

Every caller passes the same check: a superuser's auth token, or an [API token](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens) with the
operation's scope. Only paths a standard fixes stay outside `/api/_c/`: `/.well-known/*` and `/mcp`.

## From JavaScript

An app's own JS takes part in contracts too:

- Extensions with a JS API add a global (`$llm`, `$kv`, `$bulkmail`) whose types land in the app's `types.d.ts`.
- Each wire operation has a hook, `on<Contract><Operation>`, that sees the call's input and may change or refuse it.
- `onContracts` in `pb_hooks` provides contracts from JS, and declares the ones the app requires:

  ```ts
  // pb_hooks/contracts.pb.ts
  onContracts((e) => {
    e.provide("mail.fallback/v1", { send(m) { /* deliver it some other way */ } })
    e.require("restore/v1")
    e.next()
  })
  ```

The [Contracts JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript/contracts) lists every hook and type.

## Find your way

- [All extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/all): every extension, by group, each with its reference page.
- [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts): every contract, who provides it and who uses it.
- [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis): every endpoint under `/api/_c/`.
- [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension): build one, step by step.
- [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/how-pocketone-fits-together): why everything is a contract.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts

# Contracts

New to the idea? Read [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/how-pocketone-fits-together) first. This page is the list of every
contract and how to write one.

Every API a PocketOne extension offers is a contract: a versioned Go interface, and the HTTP API, hooks and MCP tools
that come with it, at `/api/_c/<id>/`. Extensions have no routes of their own. An extension says what it
**implements**, **requires** and **works with** in terms of these contracts, never another extension's name, so any
extension that implements a contract can stand in for another. PocketOne answers "who provides this contract on this
app?" at startup and prints the answer.

Every contract lives here, standard or community; extensions live in `ext/<name>`. Each contract is a package named
for its id and major version: `deploy/v1` is `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/deploy/v1`,
`mail.fallback/v1` is `.../mail/fallback/v1`. A change to what a contract promises is a new major version (`v2`) next
to the old one.

The table is generated from each contract's README and every extension's `Contracts()`: run
`go run ./.github/extensions contracts` (CI fails when it's stale).

| [`mail.feedback/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1) | Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on. | bulkmail (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.suppression/v1`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1) | Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries. | bulkmail (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
