# instance.tokens/v1

A multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued. `pocketone login` and `pocketone clone` sign in
to the instance (its oauth/v1) and get the instance's own token. Where the host, not the instance, answers deploy/v1
and remote/v1, the host checks that token with this contract, so signing in works the same way on every host.

A service contract ([tokens.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/tokens/v1/tokens.go)), one provider, on the host's scope. It holds no auth of its own: the host
decides what an instance token may do there (for example, only the instance's superusers may deploy).

## Use

```go
tk, ok := tokensv1.Contract.In(host.Scope)       // after the host's seal
res, err := tk.Verify(ctx, tokensv1.Input{Instance: id, Token: token})
switch {
case errors.Is(err, tokensv1.ErrNoInstance):     // not one of this runtime's instances, or it has no API tokens
case err != nil:                                 // the instance failed to start: not a refusal
case !res.Valid:                                 // res.Reason: "invalid" or "expired"
default:                                         // res.Grant: the owner (collection, id) and scopes, as api-tokens/v1 says
}
```

The answer is [api-tokens.verify/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1)'s `Result`. A token the instance didn't
issue is `Valid: false`, never an error, so a host can tell a refused token from an instance that won't start.
Verifying may start an instance that isn't running.

## Provide

A runtime that can reach inside its instances provides it on the host scope (`ProvideIn`): look up the instance's
app and ask its api-tokens/v1 (`Verify`), mapping `apitokensv1.ErrInvalid` and `ErrExpired` to `Valid: false`.
A runtime that can't (stock PocketBase images) doesn't provide it.

# instance.watch/v1

An edge follows a mothership without holding every instance. It opens one stream; the first time a request names a
hostname, it asks for it; from then on it hears every change to what that hostname serves, until it stops caring.
Nothing is sent that no edge asked for, except the list of edges and the edge's standing set (instances it must hold
whatever its traffic, such as a copy waiting to be made).

A wire contract ([watch.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/watch/v1/watch.go)) at `/api/_c/instance.watch/v1/`. Superusers only (scope `fleet`).

## Use

| Operation | | |
|---|---|---|
| `stream` | `GET /stream?edge=<edge id>` | Server-sent events, each `{kind, seq, ...}`: `hello` first (`conn`, `self`, `edges`, `standing`), then `host` (`host`, `answer`), `edges`, `standing`, and `ping` when idle |
| `watch` | `POST /watch {conn, edge, host}` | Registers `host` on the stream `conn` and sends its answer there. With no live `conn`, the answer comes in the reply and nothing is watched |
| `unwatch` | `POST /unwatch {conn, host}` | Stops changes for `host` on `conn` |

The promise is in the order:

- The hostname is registered before it is read, so no write between the two is missed.
- The answer goes on the stream, never in the reply, so the answer and every later change arrive in the order they
  happened. A `host` event with no `answer` means the hostname couldn't be resolved (an error, not "not found").
- "No such host" is an answer (`found: false`), watched like any other: the instance that later takes the name
  arrives.
- A change is sent only when the answer differs from the one sent last on that stream.
- `seq` numbers a stream's events from 1; a gap means something was lost and the edge reconnects.
- A dropped stream forgets every watch. An edge starts over on its next stream; what it cached before is unwatched.

In Go, [ext/mothership/client](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mothership/client/client.go) is the edge side: it is a multisite host's
instance.source/v1 and [instance.lookup/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.lookup/v1).

## Provide

Implement `watchv1.Watcher` and provide it on the mothership app. [ext/mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership)'s
`Server` is the provider: it keeps each stream's watches in memory, indexes them by the deps
[instance.resolve/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.resolve/v1) returns, and resolves again after every committed write that
touches them.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### stream

Opens this edge's stream: a hello first, then answers and changes for the hostnames it watches, the edges list when it changes, and its standing set when that changes.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/stream` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote instance watch stream --edge <value>` |
| MCP | `instance_watch_stream` |
| Token scope | `fleet` |
| Answer | a stream of JSON entries (server-sent events); the command prints one line each |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `edge` | `--edge` | string |

### watch

Registers a hostname on a stream and sends its answer there (or, with no live stream, in the reply).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/instance.watch/v1/watch` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote instance watch --conn <value> --edge <value> --host <value>` |
| MCP | `instance_watch_watch` |
| Token scope | `fleet` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `conn` | `--conn` | string |
| `edge` | `--edge` | string |
| `host` | `--host` | string |

### unwatch

Stops changes for a hostname on a stream.

| | |
|---|---|

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `conn` | `--conn` | string |
| `host` | `--host` | string |

# kv/v1

An app's key-value store: a name and a JSON value, kept without a collection or a migration. Use it for an app's
settings, a feature's state, anything that is one blob rather than many records. Each value is a row in PocketBase's
own `_params` table, so it rides along in backups.

A wire contract ([kv.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/kv/v1/kv.go)) plus Go helpers ([helpers.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/kv/v1/helpers.go)).

## Use

**From Go** (an extension, a hook), call the helpers. They need no provider and work inside a transaction when given
one:

```go
var s Settings
found, err := kvv1.Get(app, "storytime/settings", &s) // found is false and s untouched when there's no value
err = kvv1.Set(app, "storytime/settings", s)          // any value json.Marshal takes
err = kvv1.Delete(app, "storytime/settings")          // no error when there was no value
entries, err := kvv1.List(app, "storytime/")          // by name prefix, sorted by name; "" lists all (private too)
e, found, err := kvv1.Lookup(app, "storytime/settings") // the raw entry, with created and updated
```

Declare `WorksWith: extkit.IDs("kv/v1")` when you do.

**From page code and pb_hooks**, the provider gives `$kv` (sync, local):

```js
const settings = $kv.get("storytime/settings") ?? defaults // the parsed value, or null
$kv.set("storytime/settings", { title: "Story Time", minutes: 10 })
$kv.delete("storytime/settings")
$kv.list("storytime/") // [{ name, value, created, updated }]
```

**Over HTTP** (superusers, or an API token with the scope):

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| List | `GET /api/_c/kv/v1?prefix=storytime/` | `kv:read` |
| Get | `GET /api/_c/kv/v1/get?name=storytime/settings` | `kv:read` |
| Set | `POST /api/_c/kv/v1/set` with `{"name": "storytime/settings", "value": {...}}` | `kv` |
| Delete | `POST /api/_c/kv/v1/delete` with `{"name": "storytime/settings"}` | `kv` |

Get answers `404 not_found` for a name with no value. The same operations are `pocketone remote kv ...` commands and
MCP tools (`kv_list`, `kv_get`, `kv_set`, `kv_delete`).

**Names** are 1 to 128 characters: letters, digits and `_ - . : /`, starting with a letter or digit. Start yours with a
prefix of your own (`storytime/`, `myext:`) so they stay apart from other apps' and extensions'. A value is any JSON up
to 1 MiB.

**Private names** start with `_` (`_myext/settings`): the Go helpers read and write them, but the wire API (HTTP, the
CLI, MCP) and `$kv` refuse them (`403 private`) and leave them out of lists. Keep secrets there, such as API keys and
signing keys, which a `kv:read` token must never see.

**Moving an extension's own row:** an extension that kept a `_params` row of its own before kv/v1 moves it once with
`kvv1.MoveParamOnce(app, "oldrow", "_myext/settings")` before reading (`MoveParam` for a one-off): the value and its
times move to the name and the old row goes away.

**Storage:** name `storytime/settings` is the `_params` row with id `kv:storytime/settings`, its value the row's
`value`. The `kv:` prefix keeps every name apart from PocketBase's own params (`settings`) and from rows extensions
keep there themselves. Write through the helpers, never the table, so the rules above hold.

## Provide

**The wire API and `$kv`:** ext/kv provides `kvv1.Store` by default, over the helpers. Another provider implements
`kvv1.Store` and provides it in `Register` (`kvv1.Contract.Provide(app, s)`); it must keep the storage above, since the
helpers read and write it directly.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### list

Returns the values whose names start with prefix (all of them when it's empty), sorted by name. Private names (starting with \_) are left out.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/kv/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote kv list --prefix <value>` |
| MCP | `kv_list` |
| Token scope | `kv:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix` | `--prefix` | string |

### get

Returns one value. A name with no value is a not\_found error; a private name is a private error.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/kv/v1/get` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote kv get --name <value>` |
| MCP | `kv_get` |
| Token scope | `kv:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `--name` | string |

### set

Stores a JSON value under a name, replacing any value it had.

| | |
|---|---|

# llm.align/v1

A model says when each line and each word of a known text is said in its audio. Nothing is transcribed or guessed:
every word that comes back is one you sent, in order. For captions timed to a narration, karaoke-style highlighting,
or finding a phrase in a recording. Every call names its model as `provider/model`: a provider the app's admins added
in Settings → LLM, a slash, and that provider's own id for the model. Shared types (`File`, `Usage`, `ModelInfo`, the
errors) are in [`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.align/v1` ([align.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/align/v1/align.go)), one provider. The
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension provides it, over Vultr (`aligner-1`).

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.align` (bound by the llm extension):

```js
const r = await $llm.align.alignAsync({
  model: "vultr/aligner-1",
  audio: speech.file,                 // { name: "story.mp3", data }
  text: "Once upon a time...\nEvery night...",
  mode: "speech",
})
r.lines // [{ index, text, start, end, score, certain }], seconds from the start
r.words // [{ line, text, start, end, score }]
```

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Align | `POST /api/_c/llm.align/v1/align` | `{"model": "...", "audio": {"name": "story.mp3", "data": "<base64>"}, "text": "...", "mode": "speech"}` | `llm` |
| Models | `GET /api/_c/llm.align/v1/models` | `?provider=` (optional) | `llm:read` |

It answers `{"duration", "lines", "words", "unaligned", "model", "usage"}`. `text` has one line per line of the audio;
a line in square brackets (`[Chorus]`) labels the lines under it and isn't timed. `mode` is `speech` for a voice
recording, or `lyrics` (the provider's default) to separate a sung vocal from the music first. Lines the model couldn't
place are listed in `unaligned`, not dropped. Vultr takes up to 25 MiB, 15 minutes and 12,000 characters per call.

Errors: `bad_request` (no audio or text, an unknown mode), `not_configured` (no providers), `unknown_model`,
`not_supported`, `provider` (the cloud's own error), `timeout`.

From Go: `alignv1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/align/v1`).

## Provide

Implement `alignv1.Align` and provide it in `Register` (`alignv1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`). Route on the
`provider/` prefix, answer `not_supported` for a provider that can't align, `unknown_model` for a missing model or
provider, and `provider` with the cloud's own message (never its key) when the cloud refuses. Return only words of the
text sent, in order. Fill `model` with the full `provider/model` that answered, and `usage` with what the provider
reports.

# llm.chat/v1

A chat is a conversation with a language model that the provider stores: the app keeps only its id. Each question goes
to [llm.text/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.text/v1) with the chat's recent messages and a summary of the older ones, and both
turns are saved. The cloud providers keep no conversations themselves (every call sends the whole conversation), which
is what this contract is for. Chats aren't tied to users: an app that has them puts the user's id in the chat's `meta`,
lists by it, and decides who may read what.

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1` ([chat.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/chat/v1/chat.go)), one provider. It requires llm.text/v1. The
[llm-chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-chat) extension provides it.

## Use

In page code (the [llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension binds these on `$llm.chat` when a provider runs):

```js
const id = $llm.chat.new({ title: "Support", meta: { user: ctx.auth.id } })
const chat = $llm.chat.open(id, { model: "vultr/glm-5.2", system: preamble, context: (q) => findExcerpts(q) })
const answer = await chat.sendAsync(question)  // or sendAsync(question, { onText }) to stream it
chat.history({ limit: 20 })                   // [{ id, role, content, created }], oldest first
$llm.chat.list({ meta: { user: ctx.auth.id } })
$llm.chat.forget({ meta: { user: deletedUserId } })
```

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the `chat` scope):

| Operation | HTTP (`POST`) | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| New | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/new` | `{"title": "", "meta": {}}` | `chat` |
| Send | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/send` | `{"id": "...", "text": "...", "model": "vultr/glm-5.2", "system": "", "window": 12, "summarizeEvery": 6, "context": ""}` | `chat` |
| Send, streamed | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/send-stream` | as Send; server-sent events of llm.text/v1 chunks | `chat` |
| Get | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/get` | `{"id": "..."}` | `chat:read` |
| History | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/history` | `{"id": "...", "limit": 0, "before": ""}` | `chat:read` |
| Update | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/update` | `{"id": "...", "title": "...", "meta": {}}` | `chat` |
| List | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/list` | `{"meta": {"user": "..."}, "limit": 50, "offset": 0}` | `chat:read` |
| Forget | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/forget` | `{"id": "..."}` | `chat` |
| Forget by meta | `/api/_c/llm.chat/v1/forget-where` | `{"meta": {"user": "..."}}` | `chat` |

`send` needs `model` and answers `{"answer": <llm.text/v1's result>, "summarized": bool}`; it also takes `reasoning`,
`schema`, `maxTokens` and `temperature`. A chat is `{id, title, summary, meta, messages, created, updated}`. `meta`
filters match each top-level key exactly (strings, numbers, true/false, null). `context` is sent after the question;
`history` shows the question alone, and later turns send it with its context again, so each prompt starts exactly like
the last one did (which the providers' prompt caches reward). Errors: `not_found` (404) for an unknown chat, and
llm.text/v1's.

## Provide

Implement `chatv1.Chats` and provide it in `Register`. Keep chats in the app's own database (each instance of a host
has its own) and call llm.text/v1 for answers and summaries.

# llm.image/v1

A model makes pictures from a prompt, and from reference pictures it's given. They come back as files. Every call names its model as `provider/model`: a provider the app's admins added in Settings → LLM, a slash, and
that provider's own id for the model. Shared types (`File`, `Usage`, `ModelInfo`, `Job`, the errors) are in
[`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.image/v1` ([image.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/image/v1/image.go)), one provider. The
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension provides it, over Vultr, Cloudflare Workers AI, OpenRouter and any
OpenAI-compatible API.

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.image` (bound by the llm extension):

```js
const r = await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model: "vultr/z-image-turbo", prompt: "a lighthouse at dusk, watercolor", aspectRatio: "16:9" })
record.set("cover", $llm.file(r.files[0]))
```

`references` are pictures the model draws from: one to change as the prompt says, or one whose style and characters
a new scene keeps. Paint an anchor picture first, then every other picture with it as the reference, and a story's
pictures share one look:

```js
const anchor = (await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model, prompt: "a red fox in a blue scarf and a small owl in round glasses, watercolor" })).files[0]
const next = await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model, prompt: "Same style and characters as the reference. Show them rowing across a misty pond.", references: [anchor] })
```

Only a model whose listing has the feature `"reference images"` takes references (`ModelInfo.Features`, from
`models`); offer them only then. Any other model answers `not_supported`, or the provider's own error.

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generate | `POST /api/_c/llm.image/v1/generate` | `{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "n": 1, "size": "1024x1024", "references": [File]}` | `llm` |
| Models | `GET /api/_c/llm.image/v1/models` | `?provider=` (optional) | `llm:read` |

Generate answers `{"files": [File], "model", "usage"}`. A `File` is `{"name", "type", "data", "url"}`: `data` is the bytes
(base64), `url` the provider's own copy when it keeps one.

Errors: `not_configured` (no providers), `unknown_model`, `not_supported`, `provider` (the cloud's own error), `timeout`.

From Go: `imagev1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/image/v1`).

## Provide

Implement `imagev1.Image` and provide it in `Register` (`imagev1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`). Route on the
`provider/` prefix, answer `not_supported` for a provider that can't do this kind, `unknown_model` for a missing model
or provider, and `provider` with the cloud's own message (never its key) when the cloud refuses. Fill `model` with the
full `provider/model` that answered, and `usage` with what the provider reports.

List `"reference images"` (`llm.FeatureReferenceImages`) in a model's `Features` only when both the model and your
provider take `references`; answer `not_supported` for references you can't send.

## Decisions

- **References are a field of Generate, not an Edit operation** (Ben, 2026-11-24). Drawing a new scene from a
  reference isn't editing it, and providers treat both the same way: Vultr answers a generation with images as an edit.
  The earlier `Edit` operation and `EditInput` are gone.
- **A feature says which models take them**, not `inputs` containing `"image"`: `inputs` is what the provider says the
  model reads, but whether `references` work also depends on the provider here (Cloudflare lists models that read
  images, and its driver sends none).

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### generate

Makes pictures from a prompt, and from the reference pictures it's given.

| CLI | `pocketone remote llm image generate --model <value> --prompt <value> --n <n> --size <value> --aspectratio <value> --references <json> --options <json>` |
| MCP | `llm_image_generate` |
| Token scope | `llm` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `--model` | string |
| `prompt` | `--prompt` | string |
| `n` | `--n` | int |
| `size` | `--size` | string |
| `aspectRatio` | `--aspectratio` | string |
| `references` | `--references` | json |
| `options` | `--options` | json |

### models

Lists the image models of every provider in Settings → LLM.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/llm.image/v1/models` |

| MCP | `llm_image_models` |
| Token scope | `llm:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.ledger/v1

# llm.ledger/v1

Every `llm.*` call that reaches a provider, and every call a limit refuses, is recorded in the app's ledger: its kind
and model, whom it was for, the tokens and seconds it used and what it cost. This contract reads it: how much of each
limit a user or guest has left, what someone has spent, totals by model, kind, subject or day, and the rows
themselves. A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.ledger/v1` ([ledger.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/ledger/v1/ledger.go)), one provider: the
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension, over its `_llm_calls` collection.

A subject is whom calls were for: `user:<collection>/<id>`, `guest:<id>`, `guest:ip:<address>`, or a name an app's
`$llm.onCall` handler gave it (`team:acme`). See `llm.WithSubject` in
[`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.ledger` (bound by the llm extension). These are local reads, not provider calls, so they're
plain. Through `$llm.for(ctx)`, `remaining` and `spent` answer about that request's user or guest:

```js
const llm = $llm.for(ctx)
llm.ledger.remaining()      // [{ limit: "each guest, $0.10 a day", metric: "cost", used, amount, left, resets }], tightest first
llm.ledger.spent("day")     // { calls, refused, input, cached, output, seconds, costMicroUSD }

$llm.ledger.summary({ by: "model", window: "month" })            // [{ key: "vultr/glm-5.3", calls, costMicroUSD, ... }]
$llm.ledger.calls({ subject: "user:users/abc", limit: 20 })        // { calls: [...], more }
```

Over HTTP:

| Operation | HTTP | Query | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remaining | `GET /api/_c/llm.ledger/v1/remaining` | `subject` (optional) | anyone signed in: a user (or their API token) gets their own; a superuser (or a superuser's token) any subject |
| Spent | `GET /api/_c/llm.ledger/v1/spent` | `subject`, `window` (`day`, `month`) or `since`/`until`, `kind`, `model` | as for Remaining |
| Summary | `GET /api/_c/llm.ledger/v1/summary` | `by` (`model`, `kind`, `subject`, `day`), the window, `subject`, `kind`, `model`, `limit` | a superuser, or a superuser's token with `llm:read` |
| Calls | `GET /api/_c/llm.ledger/v1/calls` | the window, `subject`, `kind`, `model`, `status` (`ok`, `refused`), `limit`, `offset` | a superuser, or a superuser's token with `llm:read` |

Windows are UTC: `day` and `month` are the calendar day and month holding now, the same windows limits count in;
`since` and `until` take RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD` (`until` is exclusive). Money is `costMicroUSD`, millionths of a US
dollar, as in every result's `usage`. A guest can't ask over HTTP (an operation sees credentials, not the guest
cookie); page code answers guests through `$llm.for(ctx)`.

Errors: `bad_request` (an unknown window, `by` or `status`, a time it can't read), `unauthorized` (Remaining or Spent
with no credentials), `forbidden` (a user asking about someone else).

From Go: `ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/ledger/v1`). Name the subject in the
input, or carry it in the context with `llm.WithSubject`.

## Provide

Implement `ledgerv1.Ledger` and provide it in `Register` (`ledgerv1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`), over the same record
of calls the provider's limits count from, so `remaining` agrees with what the next refusal will say. Answer a
non-superuser caller about their own subject only. Sort `remaining` tightest first (the smallest share left) and
`summary` costliest first (by day, latest first).

# llm.music/v1

A model makes music from a prompt (and lyrics). It takes a while, so it's a job. Every call names its model as `provider/model`: a provider the app's admins added in Settings → LLM, a slash, and
that provider's own id for the model. Shared types (`File`, `Usage`, `ModelInfo`, `Job`, the errors) are in
[`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.music/v1` ([music.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/music/v1/music.go)), one provider. The
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension provides it, over Vultr, Cloudflare Workers AI, OpenRouter and any
OpenAI-compatible API.

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.music` (bound by the llm extension):

```js
const job = await $llm.music.createAsync({ model: "vultr/ace-step-1.5", prompt: "gentle lullaby", seconds: 60, wait: "5m" })
if (job.status === "done") record.set("music", $llm.file(job.files[0]))
```

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create | `POST /api/_c/llm.music/v1/create` | `{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "lyrics": "", "seconds": 60, "wait": ""}` | `llm` |
| Get | `POST /api/_c/llm.music/v1/get` | `{"id": "vultr:music_..."}` | `llm:read` |
| Content | `POST /api/_c/llm.music/v1/content` | `{"id": "...", "index": 0}` | `llm:read` |
| Models | `GET /api/_c/llm.music/v1/models` | `?provider=` (optional) | `llm:read` |

`create` and `get` answer a job: `{"id", "status" (queued, running, done, failed), "progress", "files", "outputs",
"error", "model", "usage"}`. With `wait` (`"5m"`) `create` returns once the job stops, its files included; without it,
at once. The id carries the provider (`vultr:music_02a2…`), and the provider keeps the job. `content` returns one of a
done job's files.

Errors: `not_configured` (no providers), `unknown_model`, `not_supported`, `provider` (the cloud's own error), `timeout`.

From Go: `musicv1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/music/v1`).

## Provide

Implement `musicv1.Music` and provide it in `Register` (`musicv1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`). Route on the
`provider/` prefix, answer `not_supported` for a provider that can't do this kind, `unknown_model` for a missing model
or provider, and `provider` with the cloud's own message (never its key) when the cloud refuses. Fill `model` with the
full `provider/model` that answered, and `usage` with what the provider reports.

# llm.search/v1

Knowledge bases (buckets) an app searches with hybrid search, for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). An app makes the bucket it needs (`ensure`); its admins fill it
with sources, each one tracked unit however many documents it brings: a file, pasted text, a folder, a zip, a web
page, a Git repository or one of the app's collections. Adding a source of the same name again replaces it (unchanged
documents cost nothing, missing ones go); pages and repositories are read again on an interval, collections kept in
sync. The provider splits each document into chunks that keep their source (document, section, lines, record), embeds
them with the app's one embedding model (llm.embed/v1, picked automatically; identical chunks anywhere in the app are
embedded once), and returns the best chunks for a query across the buckets asked for. It never answers the question
itself; llm.text/v1 and llm.chat/v1 calls take `enrich` to add a search's passages to their prompt, through the
[`Enrich`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1/enrich.go) helper every provider of those contracts uses.

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.search/v1` ([search.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1/search.go)), one provider. The [llm-search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-search)
extension provides it. It brings the dashboard's **Search** screen ([ui/main.js](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1/ui/main.js)), which calls only this
contract (and llm.embed/v1's model list), so it works whoever provides it.

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.search` (bound by the llm extension), and `enrich` on `$llm` calls:

```js
$llm.search.ensure({ name: "help", title: "Help center", description: "Our help articles." })
$llm.search.addURL({ bucket: "help", url: "https://github.com/acme/docs", every: "day" })
const r = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: ["help"], query: "export to PDF", limit: 5, viewer: ctx.auth })
const answer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question, enrich: ["help"] })
```

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status | `GET /api/_c/llm.search/v1/status` | | `search:read` |
| Set model | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/set-model` | `{"model"}` (`""` picks one again) | `search` |
| Buckets | `GET /api/_c/llm.search/v1/buckets` | | `search:read` |
| Bucket | `GET /api/_c/llm.search/v1/bucket` | `?name=` | `search:read` |
| Ensure | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/ensure` | `{"name", "title", "description", "owner"}` | `search` |
| Update | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/update` | `{"name", "title"?, "description"?, "maxDocuments"?, "maxBytes"?}` | `search` |
| Delete | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/delete` | `{"name"}` | `search` |
| Sources | `GET /api/_c/llm.search/v1/sources` | `?bucket=` | `search:read` |
| Add | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/add` | `{"bucket", "name", "text", "kind"?, "replace"?}` (a file or text) | `search` |
| Upload | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/upload` | `?bucket=&name=&replace=`, the file (or `.zip`) as the body | `search` |
| Put | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/put` | `{"bucket", "source", "path", "text", "replace"?}` (a folder's file) | `search` |
| Prune | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/prune` | `{"bucket", "source", "keep": [...]}` (ends a folder) | `search` |
| Add URL | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/add-url` | `{"bucket", "url", "kind"?, "every"?, "commits"?, "exclude"?}` | `search` |
| Detect URL | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/detect-url` | `{"url"}` → `{"kind"}`: `git` when the server answers the Git protocol, else `page` | `search:read` |
| Follow | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/follow` | `{"bucket", "collection", "fields": [...], "filter"?}` | `search` |
| Add folder | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/add-folder` | `{"bucket", "path", "include"?, "exclude"?, "url"?}` (a folder of the app's files on the server) | `search` |
| Refresh | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/refresh` | `{"bucket", "source"}` | `search` |
| Remove | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/remove` | `{"bucket", "sources": [...]}` | `search` |
| Documents | `GET /api/_c/llm.search/v1/documents` | `?bucket=&source=&prefix=` | `search:read` |
| Search | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/search` | `{"buckets": [...], "query", "limit", "prefix", "viewer"}` | `search:read` |
| Sample | `POST /api/_c/llm.search/v1/sample` | `{"buckets": [...], "count", "prefix"}`: chunks picked at random (no query, no embedding) | `search:read` |

A source answers `{"bucket", "name", "kind", "url", "every", "commits", "exclude", "collection", "fields", "filter",
"path", "include", "pageURL", "hash", "status", "error", "documents", "chunks", "embedded", "bytes", "pending", "costMicroUSD", "refreshed", "next"}` (`embedded` below `chunks`: embedding under way; documents carry the same); `kind` is
`file`, `text`, `folder`, `dir` (a server folder), `zip`, `page`, `git` or `collection`, `status` is `reading`, `ready` or `error`, and `hash` is
a file's or zip's sha256, to spot an exact duplicate under another name. `replace` names an existing source the new one
replaces under its new name. Search answers `{"results": [{"bucket", "source", "document", "text", "heading",
"startLine", "endLine", "record", "url", "score"}], "model", "usage"}`; no buckets searches every bucket. `viewer`
(`{"collection", "id"}`, or `{}` for a guest) leaves out records it can't view by the collection's view rule. Status
answers `{"model", "chunks", "embedded", "note"}`: `embedded` below `chunks` means embedding is under way.

Errors: `not_found` (no such bucket or source), `bad_request` (a bad name, URL, collection or field, an empty query,
binary content), `too_large` (over the bucket's limits, a document over 10 MB, a zip over 100 MB), `not_configured` (no
embedding model), and llm.embed/v1's errors from embedding the query.

From Go: `searchv1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1`), and
`searchv1.Enrich(ctx, app, enrich, query)` for the passages a model call adds.

## Provide

Implement `searchv1.Search` and provide it in `Register` (`searchv1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`). Keep these promises:

- `Ensure` is idempotent: an existing bucket keeps its settings; only an empty title, description or owner is filled in.
- A source is identified by its name within its bucket; adding one of the same name (or naming it in `replace`)
  replaces it, leaving sources in other buckets alone. Unchanged documents cost nothing; documents the new version
  doesn't have go.
- One embedding model for the app, so any buckets can be searched together; vectors from two models are never
  compared, a new model embeds every chunk again, and a chunk's content is embedded once however many sources hold it.
- A collection source's documents follow its records: saved, filtered out, deleted. Pages and repositories with an
  interval are read again when it comes round; a server folder is read again every few minutes.
- A server folder's path stays inside the app's own folder (the one holding `pb_data`) and never reaches `pb_data`, by
  the path or by a link.
- A result's `url`, when set, is where the passage is published: a page's URL, or a server folder's `url` pattern with
  `{path}` filled in and the section's heading id as the anchor.
- With a `viewer`, no result comes from a record the viewer can't view.
- Results are chunks with their source, best first, at most `limit` (default 5, at most 50); `score` orders them.
- Searching is the only operation that waits on a model; adding and reading sources return before embedding is done.

### add

# llm.speech/v1

A model reads text aloud and returns the audio as a file. Every call names its model as `provider/model`: a provider the app's admins added in Settings → LLM, a slash, and
that provider's own id for the model. Shared types (`File`, `Usage`, `ModelInfo`, `Job`, the errors) are in
[`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.speech/v1` ([speech.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/speech/v1/speech.go)), one provider. The
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension provides it, over Vultr, Cloudflare Workers AI, OpenRouter and any
OpenAI-compatible API.

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.speech` (bound by the llm extension):

```js
const r = await $llm.speech.speakAsync({ model: "vultr/qwen3-tts-12hz-1.7b", text: page, voice: "vivian", instructions: "slow and calm" })
record.set("narration", $llm.file(r.file))
await $llm.speech.voicesAsync("vultr/qwen3-tts-12hz-1.7b")
// a voice cloned from a stored clip: leave voice and instructions out
await $llm.speech.speakAsync({ model: "vultr/qwen3-tts-12hz-1.7b", text: page, reference: { audio: $llm.fromRecord(clip, "audio"), text: clip.getString("passage") } })
```

**Voice cloning.** `reference` (`{audio: File, text}`) asks the model to read in the voice of that clip; `text` is what
the clip says, optional but closer with it. A model clones when one of its voices has `mode: "clone"` (`voices`), and a
provider that doesn't clone answers `not_supported`. Nothing is saved at the provider: the clip goes with every call.
`instructions` can't go with a `reference`.

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speak | `POST /api/_c/llm.speech/v1/speak` | `{"model": "...", "text": "...", "voice": "", "format": "mp3"}` | `llm` |
| Voices | `POST /api/_c/llm.speech/v1/voices` | `{"model": "..."}` | `llm:read` |
| Models | `GET /api/_c/llm.speech/v1/models` | `?provider=` (optional) | `llm:read` |

`speak` answers `{"file": File, "model", "usage"}`; `voices` answers `{"voices": [{"id", "name", "language", "mode",
"description"}]}` (empty when the provider doesn't list them; `mode` is `builtin`, `design` or `clone` when it says).

Errors: `not_configured` (no providers), `unknown_model`, `not_supported`, `provider` (the cloud's own error), `timeout`.

From Go: `speechv1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/speech/v1`).

## Provide

Implement `speechv1.Speech` and provide it in `Register` (`speechv1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`). Route on the
`provider/` prefix, answer `not_supported` for a provider that can't do this kind, `unknown_model` for a missing model
or provider (and for a `reference` on a provider that can't clone), and `provider` with the cloud's own message (never its key) when the cloud refuses. Fill `model` with the
full `provider/model` that answered, and `usage` with what the provider reports.

| Token scope | `llm` |

# llm.text/v1

A language model answers a prompt or a conversation, whole or as it's written. With a JSON schema the answer's parsed value comes back as `data`. Every call names its model as `provider/model`: a provider the app's admins added in Settings → LLM, a slash, and
that provider's own id for the model. Shared types (`File`, `Usage`, `ModelInfo`, `Job`, the errors) are in
[`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.text/v1` ([text.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/text/v1/text.go)), one provider. The
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension provides it, over Vultr, Cloudflare Workers AI, OpenRouter and any
OpenAI-compatible API.

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.text` (bound by the llm extension):

```js
const r = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.2", system: "Label the ticket.", prompt: body, reasoning: "off",
  schema: { type: "object", properties: { label: { enum: ["bug", "billing", "question"] } }, required: ["label"] } })
r.data.label
await $llm.text.streamAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.2", prompt: question }, (piece) => { /* show it */ })
```

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Complete | `POST /api/_c/llm.text/v1/complete` | `{"model": "vultr/glm-5.2", "prompt": "...", "maxTokens": 200}` | `llm` |
| Stream | `POST /api/_c/llm.text/v1/stream` | as Complete; server-sent events | `llm` |
| Count | `POST /api/_c/llm.text/v1/count` | `{"text": "..."}` or `{"system": "...", "messages": [...]}` | `llm:read` |
| Models | `GET /api/_c/llm.text/v1/models` | `?provider=vultr` (optional) | `llm:read` |

`complete` takes `prompt` or `messages` (`[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]`), and optionally `system`, `schema`,
`maxTokens`, `temperature`, `stop`, `reasoning` (`"off"`, `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`; thinking counts toward
`maxTokens`) and `options` (the provider's own fields). It answers `text`, `data`, `reasoning` (the model's thinking,
when the provider returns it), `stopReason`, `model` and `usage`. `stream` sends one `event: stream` per piece,
`{"text": "..."}` (or `{"reasoning": "..."}`), then `{"done": true, "result": {...}}`. `count` estimates at about four
characters a token.

Errors: `not_configured` (no providers), `unknown_model`, `not_supported`, `provider` (the cloud's own error), `timeout`.

From Go: `textv1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/text/v1`).

## Provide

or provider, and `provider` with the cloud's own message (never its key) when the cloud refuses. Fill `model` with the
full `provider/model` that answered, and `usage` with what the provider reports.

# llm.video/v1

A model makes a video from a prompt (and a first frame). Like music, it's a job. Every call names its model as `provider/model`: a provider the app's admins added in Settings → LLM, a slash, and
that provider's own id for the model. Shared types (`File`, `Usage`, `ModelInfo`, `Job`, the errors) are in
[`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/llm.go).

A wire contract at `/api/_c/llm.video/v1` ([video.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/llm/video/v1/video.go)), one provider. The
[llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension provides it, over Vultr, Cloudflare Workers AI, OpenRouter and any
OpenAI-compatible API.

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.video` (bound by the llm extension):

```js
const job = await $llm.video.createAsync({ model: "vultr/<video model>", prompt: "waves at a lighthouse", seconds: 5 })
// later
const now = await $llm.video.getAsync(job.id)
if (now.status === "done") record.set("clip", $llm.file(await $llm.video.contentAsync(now.id, 0)))
```

Over HTTP (a superuser, or a token with the scope shown):

| Operation | HTTP | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create | `POST /api/_c/llm.video/v1/create` | `{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "image": File, "seconds": 5, "aspectRatio": "16:9", "wait": ""}` | `llm` |
| Get | `POST /api/_c/llm.video/v1/get` | `{"id": "..."}` | `llm:read` |
| Content | `POST /api/_c/llm.video/v1/content` | `{"id": "...", "index": 0}` | `llm:read` |
| Models | `GET /api/_c/llm.video/v1/models` | `?provider=` (optional) | `llm:read` |

The job is the same as [llm.music/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.music/v1)'s.

Errors: `not_configured` (no providers), `unknown_model`, `not_supported`, `provider` (the cloud's own error), `timeout`.

From Go: `videov1.Contract.Must(app)` (from `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/video/v1`).

## Provide

Implement `videov1.Video` and provide it in `Register` (`videov1.Contract.Provide(app, impl)`). Route on the
`provider/` prefix, answer `not_supported` for a provider that can't do this kind, `unknown_model` for a missing model
or provider, and `provider` with the cloud's own message (never its key) when the cloud refuses. Fill `model` with the
full `provider/model` that answered, and `usage` with what the provider reports.

# mail.fallback/v1

Where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off. Providers form an ordered chain: each sends a message or passes it on;
when all pass, PocketBase sends it its own way (`sendmail`). An app with SMTP on never reaches the chain.

A service ([fallback.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1/fallback.go)), many providers, open to `pb_hooks`.

## Use

Nothing to call: mail an app sends with SMTP off goes through the chain. Order the providers in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay]
```

## Provide

Implement `fallbackv1.Sender` (`Send(ctx, *mailer.Message)`, returning `fallbackv1.ErrPass` to pass), provide it,
and bind the chain once:

```go
fallbackv1.Contract.Provide(app, mySender{})
fallbackv1.Bind(app)
```

From `pb_hooks`:

```js
onContracts((e) => {
  e.provide("mail.fallback/v1", {
    send(m) {
      if (!m.to.some((a) => a.address.endsWith("@example.com"))) throw new ContractError("pass")
      // send it your way
    },
  })
  e.next()
})
```

# mail.feedback/v1

What mail providers report back about mail an app sent: bounces, spam complaints, unsubscribes. The provider of this
contract receives the reports and raises one event per address; any number of extensions act on them through one
hook. A suppression list adds the address, a CRM marks the contact, `pb_hooks` logs it.

A wire contract ([feedback.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/feedback/v1/feedback.go)). Its operations are public: SES messages are checked by their SNS
signature, webhook calls by a shared secret.

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | What sends it |
|---|---|---|
| SES | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses` | an Amazon SNS HTTPS subscription for SES bounce and complaint notifications |
| Webhook | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook` with `X-Feedback-Secret` | any provider: `{"type": "bounce\|complaint\|unsubscribe", "email": "...", "campaign": "..."}` |

Act on the events in Go:

```go
feedbackv1.OnEvent(app).BindFunc(func(e *feedbackv1.Event) error {
	// e.Kind: bounce, complaint or unsubscribe; e.Email, e.Campaign, e.Source
	return e.Next()
})
```

## Provide

Implement `feedbackv1.Receiver`: check each report, then call `feedbackv1.Raise(app, &feedbackv1.Event{...})` for
each address. Where the webhook secret comes from is the provider's (Bulk Mail keeps it in its settings).

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### s_e_s

Takes an Amazon SNS delivery carrying SES bounce and complaint notifications (and confirms the topic subscription). Point an SNS HTTPS subscription here.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses` |
| Token scope | public |
| Body | the raw upload, not JSON |

### webhook

Takes {"type": "bounce|complaint|unsubscribe", "email": ..., "campaign": ...} from any provider, with the shared secret in the X-Feedback-Secret header.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook` |
| Token scope | public |
| Body | the raw upload, not JSON |

# mail.suppression/v1

The addresses an app must not send bulk mail to (unsubscribed, bounced, complained, added by hand), and the
unsubscribe link in every bulk message. Anything that mails many people checks it.

A wire contract ([suppression.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/suppression/v1/suppression.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Check | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/check?email=` | superusers (`suppression:read`) |
| Suppress | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/suppress` `{"email", "reason", "source", "campaign"}` | superusers (`suppression`) |
| Unsuppress | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsuppress` `{"email"}` | superusers (`suppression`) |
| UnsubscribePage | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=<signed token>` | public: the link in a message |
| Unsubscribe | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` | public: the page's form, or a mail provider's one-click POST |

Reasons: `unsubscribed`, `bounced`, `complained`, `manual`. The page never unsubscribes on a `GET` (link scanners
open every URL in a message); one-click unsubscribes follow RFC 8058 (`List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`). The token is
signed by the provider, so only links it issued work.

## Provide

Implement `suppressionv1.List`; sign the tokens in the links your messages carry, and point `List-Unsubscribe`
at `/api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=...`.

## Commands and APIs

# mcp/v1

The app's [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude
Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it. It stays at `/mcp`: people paste that URL, MCP versions itself
in the protocol, and OAuth tokens are bound to the resource URL.

What every provider serves the same way, the contract owns:

- **The routes:** `/mcp`, and its protected resource metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.
- **The tools:** every wire contract the app provides, one tool per operation (`restore_points`, `bulkmail_start`,
  ...), with an input schema from the operation's types and called through the contract, so the same superuser
  check, scopes and hooks apply as over HTTP; and tools extensions add with `AddTool`.

A provider brings the protocol, sign-in and any tools of its own ([MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) adds `pb_*` tools over
the REST API). Replace it and the contract tools stay.

A service ([mcp.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mcp/v1/mcp.go)).

## Use

Add `https://<host>/mcp` to an MCP client and sign in. In Go, an extension adds a tool that isn't a contract
operation, and tells agents what its tools are for:

```go
mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{
	Name:        "notes_summarize_week",
	Description: "Summarizes this week's notes.",
	ReadOnly:    true,
	Call: func(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, args json.RawMessage) (any, error) { ... },
})
mcpv1.AddInstructions(app, "Use notes_summarize_week for weekly reviews.")
```

`mcpv1.Tools(app)` lists what every provider serves.

## Provide

Implement `mcpv1.Endpoint` (`ServeMCP` for requests to `/mcp`, `Metadata` for the protected resource metadata),
provide it, and bind the routes once:

```go
mcpv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myServer{})
mcpv1.Bind(app)
```

Serve `mcpv1.Tools(app)` in `tools/list` and `tools/call`, calling each tool as the signed-in caller.

`/mcp` skips PocketBase's `pbRejectUnknownToken`, so the provider rejects a bad token itself: a request with an
`Authorization` header and no signed-in caller (`e.Auth` is nil) gets 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
error="invalid_token"` challenge, never a guest's answer.

## Extensions

|---|---|
| [mcp](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | provides (default) |

# oauth/v1

An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app: authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, and
client registration (dynamic, or by a client metadata document). The CLI's browser login and MCP clients such as
Claude sign in through it, and get API tokens ([api-tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens/v1)).

A routed contract ([oauth.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/oauth/v1/oauth.go)): the OAuth specs fix its API's shape, so its provider serves it as it is.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | the server's metadata (RFC 8414 puts it at the root) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize` | sign in and consent (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token` | codes and refresh tokens for access tokens |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device` | start a device-code sign-in |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify` | enter the device code (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke` | revoke a token |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register` | dynamic client registration (when on) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback` | sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...) |

`authorize` and `device` take an optional `account`: the auth collection the client needs the token from (the CLI
sends `_superusers`). The sign-in shows only that form, and no other collection is issued a token.

In Go, another extension (MCP) turns on dynamic registration and sets token lifetimes:
`oauthv1.Contract.Of(app)` → `EnableDynamicRegistration()`, `SetAccessTTL(path, ttl)`, `Issuer(e)`.

## Provide

Implement `oauthv1.Server` and serve the routes above (`extkit.EventServer` or `extkit.RouteBinder`); issue access
tokens through api-tokens/v1.

## Commands and APIs

Its own HTTP API under `/api/_c/oauth/v1/`, described above. It has no generated commands or MCP tools. [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote) explains how PocketOne apps are managed from afar.

|---|---|

# remote/v1

Remote control of an app from afar: who your credential is and what the app offers, its status, a restart, and its
log. Every client starts here: `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` is the one fixed path, and its answer lists every other
contract the app offers. Contracts that add an area (deploy/v1) require this one.

A wire contract ([remote.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remote.go)); a multisite host can provide it for its instances, so it works for
instances running stock PocketBase images.

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| Whoami | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | public (the answer says more when you're signed in) |
| Status | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote:read` |
| Restart | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote` |
| Logs | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100` (server-sent events) | `remote:read` |

- **CLI:** `pocketone remote whoami | status | restart | logs`.
- **Go:** `remotev1.Contract.Must(app)` in the app, or `remotev1.NewClient(url, token, http)` from outside. The
  command-line client (linked remotes, saved logins, sign-in) is [remoteclient](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient).
- **Hooks:** `remotev1.OnRestart(app)` in Go, `onRemoteRestart` in `pb_hooks`, for every operation.
- **MCP:** a tool per operation (`remote_status`, ...).

## Provide

Implement `remotev1.Remote` and provide it in your extension's `Register`:

```go
remotev1.Contract.Provide(app, myRemote{})
```

A multisite host provides it for every instance with `remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory)` and
serves it with `remotev1.W.HostHandler` in its instance routes (`multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`, after the gates;
see [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) and
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker)).

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

# restore/v1

Put an app's data back as it was at a moment. You ask for a moment ("Tuesday 15:00"); the app restores the closest
point it has at or before it and tells you which one it used. Providers differ only in how close they get:

- [pitr](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) keeps continuous history: any second inside its window.
- [backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups), the default, uses PocketBase's own backups (local or S3): the latest backup
  made at or before the moment. It steps aside when pitr is on for the app.

The app restarts to apply a restore; its data from before the restore is kept until the next one.

A wire contract ([restore.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1/restore.go)); a multisite host may provide it for its instances (from host-level
snapshots).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| Points: what can be restored | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` | `restore:read` |
| RestoreTo a moment | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` with `{"at": "<RFC 3339 time>"}` | `restore` |

`Points` answers with the provider's name and either a `window` (`kind: "continuous"`) or a list of `snapshots`
(`kind: "snapshots"`, newest first), whether a restore is running, and the last restore. `RestoreTo` answers with
the `point` it restores from; `422 no_point` when there's nothing at or before the moment, `409 busy` while another
restore runs. Only superusers may call either.

- **Dashboard:** Settings → Backups gets a "Restore to a moment" section from this contract ([ui/main.js](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1/ui/main.js)),
  whichever extension provides it: a time picker over pitr's window, or one that says which backup a moment uses.
- **Go:** `restorev1.Contract.Must(app).RestoreTo(ctx, auth, restorev1.RestoreInput{At: t})`, or
  `restorev1.NewClient(url, token, http)` from outside.
- **Hooks:** `restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, fn)` in Go, `onRestoreRestoreTo` in `pb_hooks`: refuse or log a restore.
- **MCP:** `restore_points` and `restore_restore_to`.

## Provide

Implement `restorev1.Restorer` and provide it in your extension's `Register` (`ProvideDefault` if a better
provider should replace yours). Report the point you'll actually restore from, and restart the app to apply it.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### points

Says what the app's data can be restored to: a window of time (continuous history) or a list of moments (backups), and whether a restore is running.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote restore points` |
| MCP | `restore_points` |
| Token scope | `restore:read` |

### restore_to

Puts the app's data back as it was at the given moment, from the latest point at or before it. The app restarts to apply it; its current data is kept aside until the next restore.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote restore to --at <time>` |
| MCP | `restore_restore_to` |
| Token scope | `restore` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `at` | `--at` | time |

# runtime/v1

What runs a multisite host's instances: [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) as isolates,
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) in containers. A host runs exactly one, and every instance runs on it; an instance
it can't serve (by PocketBase version, for example) is refused. Having a `multisite` section makes the binary a host;
its runtime is this contract's provider.

A host-scope service contract, one provider ([runtime.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/runtime/v1/runtime.go)).

## Use

The stock `pocketone` binary runs docker when `pocketone.yaml` has a `docker` section, else pocker. A build that
registers more than one runtime picks with `providers:`:

```yaml
multisite: {}
providers:
  runtime/v1: docker
```

## Provide

Implement `runtimev1.Runtime` (`Name`, `Serves`, `ServeInstance`, `Ready`) and any optional hooks the host
calls (`Prechecker`, `Syncer`, `Starter`, `Shutdowner`, `Statser`). Provide it in a host extension's
`RegisterHost`, only when it's configured (a second provider on the same host is a conflict at startup unless
`providers:` picks):

```go
runtimev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myRuntime)
```

# settings/v1

The settings an app's own superusers change for its extensions (PITR's S3 bucket, Bulk Mail's sending limits), behind
one API: list them, read one, save one, test one without saving. Each extension keeps its settings its own way and
registers a section; the provider serves them all. Settings an operator sets for a whole host stay in
`pocketone.yaml`.

A wire contract ([settings.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/settings/v1/settings.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| List | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1` | `settings:read` |
| Get | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=pitr` | `settings:read` |
| Save | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save` with `{"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}}` | `settings` |
| Test | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test` with `{"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}}` | `settings` |

Each extension's `values` are its own shape (see its README). Secrets come back empty with a flag that they're set;
saving an empty secret keeps the saved one. `Test` answers `{"ok": false, "message": ...}` when the settings don't
work. Only superusers may call any of them.

## Provide

**An extension with settings** registers a section in its `Register`:

```go
settingsv1.Add(app, mySection{}) // Info, Get, Save; Test too if the settings can be checked
```

and declares `WorksWith: extkit.IDs("settings/v1")`.

**A provider of the API** (ext/settings by default) implements `settingsv1.Settings` over
`settingsv1.Sections(app)`.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### list

Names the extensions whose settings this app's admins can change.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings list` |
| MCP | `settings_list` |
| Token scope | `settings:read` |

### get

Returns one extension's settings. Secrets come back empty, with a flag saying they're set.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings get --extension <value>` |
| MCP | `settings_get` |
| Token scope | `settings:read` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `--extension` | string |

### save

Replaces one extension's settings and applies them. A secret left empty keeps its saved value. Settings a host sets are read-only here.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings save --extension <value> --values <json>` |
| MCP | `settings_save` |
| Token scope | `settings` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `--extension` | string |
| `values` | `--values` | json |

### test

Checks one extension's settings without saving them (a test write to a bucket, a test message).

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote settings test --extension <value> --values <json>` |
| MCP | `settings_test` |
| Token scope | `settings` |

| Input field | Flag | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `extension` | `--extension` | string |
| `values` | `--values` | json |

# templates/v1

An extension that serves pages of its own (tokens' OAuth sign-in, consent and MFA screens) keeps them as a set of Go
`html/template` files, usually embedded in the binary. A project themes them by ejecting the set and editing its copy:
any file it has replaces the built-in one, and anything it leaves out falls back. The format is always Go templates,
so the built-in pages and the ejected ones are the same files.

A set is every `*.tpl` file in an `fs.FS`, at any depth. Each file is one template named by its path without `.tpl`
(`signin`, `parts/head`), so pages include shared pieces with `{{template "parts/head" .}}`.

An app service contract, one provider ([templates.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/templates/v1/templates.go)).

## Use

Add your set in `Register`, then render a page through the provider at request time, falling back to your own set
when nothing provides the contract:

```go
//go:embed templates/oauth
var oauthFiles embed.FS

files, _ := fs.Sub(oauthFiles, "templates/oauth")
templatesv1.Add(app, "oauth", files)

// in a handler
if t, ok := templatesv1.Contract.Of(app); ok {
	return t.Render(e, "oauth", "signin", http.StatusOK, data)
}
set, err := templatesv1.Parse(files, nil)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
return templatesv1.Write(e, set, "signin", http.StatusOK, data)
```

Declare the contract in `WorksWith`. Pass anything that must not be escaped (ready-made HTML) as `template.HTML`.

## Provide

Implement `templatesv1.Templates` (`Render`, `Eject`) and provide it in `Register`. Read the sets with
`templatesv1.Set` and `templatesv1.Names`, and build each page with `templatesv1.Parse(set, projectCopy)` and
`templatesv1.Write`, so every provider renders the same way:

```go
templatesv1.Contract.Provide(app, myTemplates)
```

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates) | provides |
| [api-tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) | works with |

# tls/v1

The TLS of a multisite host's main listener. Its provider hands the host a `tls.Config` (certificates on demand,
for hostnames an instance serves) and, for HTTP challenges, a wrapper for the plain-HTTP listener. With no provider
the host uses the certificate files in its `server` section, or plain HTTP.

A host-scope service contract, one provider ([tls.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tls/v1/tls.go)).

## Use

Nothing to call: the host's listener uses it. Turn the provider on in its own section (`autotls: { auto: true }`).

## Provide

Implement `tlsv1.Provider` and provide it in a host extension's `RegisterHost`; only issue certificates for
hostnames `served` reports true for.

```go
tlsv1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myTLS)
```

# vacuum/v1

SQLite keeps a database file as big as it ever was; compacting it (`VACUUM`) gives the space freed by deleted records
back to the disk. This contract says who does that for an app, how often, and how the last run went.

A wire contract at `/api/_c/vacuum/v1` ([vacuum.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/vacuum/v1/vacuum.go)), one provider. On a single app the
[vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum) extension provides it, on the schedule the app's admins set. A multisite host may
provide it for its instances instead: then the host compacts them on its own schedule, the app's vacuum extension steps
aside (no settings, no schedule of its own), and the app's admins see the host's status.

## Use

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: <token with vacuum:read>" https://your.app/api/_c/vacuum/v1
```

`provider` is who compacts (`vacuum` for the app itself, or the host), `enabled` and `every` the schedule, `last` the
last run (bytes saved, databases skipped as not worth it, any error) and `next` the next one.

## Provide

Implement `vacuumv1.Vacuum` and provide it in `Register` (`vacuumv1.Contract.Provide(app, v)`), or on a host for every
instance (`vacuumv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(hostScope, func(id string) vacuumv1.Vacuum {...})`). An app half that
also has settings or a schedule checks `extkit.HostProvides(app, "vacuum/v1")` in `Register` and leaves them out when
the host owns it.

## Commands and APIs

Every operation is a REST endpoint, a `pocketone` command and an MCP tool, all generated from the contract and behind the same token scope check and hooks. See [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote), or the full [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli), [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis) and [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp) references.

### status

Says who compacts the app's databases, whether and how often, and how the last run went.

| | |
|---|---|
| REST | `GET /api/_c/vacuum/v1` |
| CLI | `pocketone remote vacuum status` |
| MCP | `vacuum_status` |
| Token scope | `vacuum:read` |

## Extensions
