# Key-Value Store

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A place for an app's settings and small pieces of state: a name and a JSON value, kept without a collection or a
migration. Values live in PocketBase's own `_params` table, so they ride along in backups. Page code reads and writes
them with `$kv`, Go code with the [kv/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1) helpers, and superusers through the API, the
CLI or an agent.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The Key-Value Store is built into `pocketone` and **on by default**; there's nothing to install. In your own Go build:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{kv.New()}, nil, nil)
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/kv`.

## Configure

There's nothing to configure. To turn it off on a single app (`$kv` and the API go away; the helpers keep working):

```yaml
kv:
  enabled: false
```

## Use

In page code and `pb_hooks`, `$kv` is sync and local:

```js
const defaults = { title: "Story Time", minutes: 10 }
const settings = $kv.get("storytime/settings") ?? defaults // the stored value, or null when there is none
$kv.set("storytime/settings", { ...settings, minutes: 15 })  // any value JSON.stringify takes, up to 1 MiB
$kv.delete("storytime/settings")                             // no error when there was no value
$kv.list("storytime/")                                       // [{ name, value, created, updated }], sorted by name
```

Names are 1 to 128 characters: letters, digits and `_ - . : /`, starting with a letter or digit. Start yours with a
prefix of your own (`storytime/`) so they stay apart from other code's. Names starting with `_` are private to the
app's Go code: extensions keep their secrets there (`_llm/settings`, `_bulkmail/settings`), and neither `$kv` nor the
API below reaches them.

Superusers (or an API token with the `kv` / `kv:read` scope) reach the same values over HTTP:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" "https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1?prefix=storytime/"             # list
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" "https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1/get?name=storytime/settings"   # one value
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -d '{"name":"storytime/settings","value":{"minutes":15}}' \
  https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1/set
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -d '{"name":"storytime/settings"}' https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1/delete
```

The same operations are `pocketone remote kv ...` commands and MCP tools (`kv_list`, `kv_get`, `kv_set`, `kv_delete`).

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### [kv/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1)

| Operation | CLI | REST | MCP |
|---|---|---|---|
| [list](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1#list) | `pocketone remote kv list --prefix <value>` | `GET /api/_c/kv/v1` | `kv_list` |
| [get](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1#get) | `pocketone remote kv get --name <value>` | `GET /api/_c/kv/v1/get` | `kv_get` |
| [set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1#set) | `pocketone remote kv set --name <value> --value <json>` | `POST /api/_c/kv/v1/set` | `kv_set` |
| [delete](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1#delete) | `pocketone remote kv delete --name <value>` | `POST /api/_c/kv/v1/delete` | `kv_delete` |

### JavaScript API

What it adds to `pb_hooks` and page code: [Key-Value Store JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript/kv).

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [LLM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension), [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail), [API Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) | Keep their settings and keys here, under private names. |
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | kv/v1 is the contract. Other extensions keep their own values with its Go helpers (`kvv1.Get(app, name, &v)`, `kvv1.Set`, `kvv1.Delete`, `kvv1.List`), which need no provider, and declare `WorksWith: kv/v1`. |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension) | Page code gets `$kv`. |
| [API Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) | Tokens with the `kv:read` or `kv` scope reach the API. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | Agents get the operations as tools. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Every instance that runs PocketOne has its own store, in its own `_params`. |

## Example

The example serves a PocketBase app with the store, and keeps a greeting in it from Go:

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with the key-value store (kv/v1): page code and pb_hooks get $kv, and
// superusers read and change values at /api/_c/kv/v1, e.g.
// `curl -H "Authorization: <superuser token>" "http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/_c/kv/v1/get?name=example/greeting"`.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	kvv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/kv/v1"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/extkit"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/kv"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{kv.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	// a value from Go, kept until someone changes it
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(e *core.ServeEvent) error {
		var greeting string
		if found, err := kvv1.Get(e.App, "example/greeting", &greeting); err != nil {
			return err
		} else if !found {
			if err := kvv1.Set(e.App, "example/greeting", "Hello from the key-value store"); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		return e.Next()
	})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

MIT

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension

# LLM

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

LLM gives your app cloud models to call, one kind at a time: text, pictures, speech, transcription, music, video and
embeddings. You add providers in Settings → LLM, each with your own key, and every call names its model as
`provider/model`:

```ts
const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: "Summarize: " + body, reasoning: "off" })
const pic = await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model: "or/black-forest-labs/flux.2-klein-4b", prompt: "a lighthouse at dusk, watercolor" })
record.set("cover", $llm.file(pic.files[0]))
```

```go
r, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{
	Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: "Summarize: " + body, Reasoning: "off"})
```

`vultr` is the name you gave a provider; what follows the first slash is that provider's own id for the model. Any
call can name any model of any provider, so one app can use two picture providers, or a cheap text model for labels and
a large one for writing.

Providers come in four types:

| Type | What it reaches |
|---|---|
| `vultr` | [Vultr Serverless Inference](https://docs.vultr.com/products/compute/serverless-inference): every kind, music, video and alignment included. |
| `cloudflare` | [Workers AI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/) on your Cloudflare account: text, pictures, speech, transcription and embeddings. |
| `openrouter` | [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai): hundreds of models behind one key; text, pictures, speech, transcription, video and embeddings. |
| `openai` | Any API shaped like OpenAI's: OpenAI itself, Groq, Together, or Ollama and llama-server on localhost. Add as many as you like. |

The answers come from your provider accounts, on your keys; PocketOne adds no limits or charges.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

LLM is built into `pocketone` and on in every app and every instance of a host (a standard member). It does nothing
until you add a provider. In your own Go build:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{llm.New()}, nil, nil)
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/llm`.

## Configure

**Settings → LLM** (superusers) lists your providers. Press **New provider**, pick its type, give it a name (the part
before the slash in a model) and enter its key: an endpoint for `openai` providers (with its version path, like
`https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`), the account ID for Cloudflare (with a token that has Workers AI permission). Vultr,
Cloudflare and OpenRouter providers can't be saved without a key; an `openai` one can (a local Ollama has none). Each
provider's **Test** checks its key, typed or saved, without spending anything, and its check mark turns green when it
passes. Saving applies at once.

Keys stay on the server: the screen never shows a saved key again, and a key is never sent to an endpoint other than the
one it was entered for (change a provider's endpoint and you enter its key again). The settings are in the app's
[key-value store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/kv/extension), under the private name `_llm/settings` (only Go code reaches it; the kv/v1 API
and `$kv` don't).

Under the providers, **Limits** cap what the app spends: the whole app, each signed-in user, each guest or all guests
together, at most so many US dollars, output tokens, input tokens or calls a UTC day or month, optionally for one kind
or model. Every call passes them before it reaches a provider, and a used-up limit refuses it with code `limit` (429).
Page code says whom a call is for with `$llm.for(ctx)` (a page's `ctx` or a route's `e`): its signed-in user, or else a
guest told apart by a signed cookie. Guest calls are refused until there's a limit for all guests together. Every call
is recorded in the `_llm_calls` collection, and the screen shows today's and this month's spend from it
([Limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits), [Users and guests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests)). `$llm.ledger` reads it: what's left of
each limit, what someone spent, totals by model or person ([Spend and the ledger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend)). The screen's
limits are the built-in handler on `$llm.onCall`; your own handlers there add plan tiers, credits or anything else
([Custom limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits)).

There's no pocketone.yaml configuration besides the switch: `llm: {enabled: false}` turns it off on a single app (on a
host, an instance's `extensions.llm`), and with it `$llm` and the `llm.*` contracts.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `llm:`

Cloud models for $llm (the llm.* contracts); providers and keys are set in Settings → LLM.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | false turns the extension off on this app ($llm and the llm.* contracts are gone). |

## Use

In page code it's `$llm.<kind>`. Every call that reaches a provider is async, and its name says so: await it in an async
handler (`await $llm.text.completeAsync({...})`). It runs off the app's JS VM, so the app keeps serving other requests
while a model works; there are no blocking versions to reach for. Each call names its `model`:

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `$llm.search.searchAsync({ query, buckets?, limit?, viewer? })` and the rest of `$llm.search` | Hybrid search over knowledge bases (buckets) of your content, through the [LLM Search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-search) extension ([Search and RAG](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/search)). |
| `$llm.text.completeAsync({ model, system?, prompt \| messages, schema?, maxTokens?, temperature?, stop?, reasoning?, enrich?, options? })` | Answers: `{ text, data, reasoning, stopReason, model, usage, passages }`. With `schema`, `data` is the parsed JSON. With `enrich` (RAG: buckets to search, `["help"]`), the best passages from them are sent after the prompt and listed in `passages` ([LLM Search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-search)). |
| `$llm.text.streamAsync(opts, onText, onReasoning?)` | The same, calling `onText` with each piece as it's written (`false` stops it). |
| `$llm.text.count(text \| messages)` | About how many tokens (four characters each). Local, so not async. |
| `$llm.image.generateAsync({ model, prompt, references?, n?, size?, aspectRatio? })` | Pictures: `{ files, model, usage }`. `references` are pictures to draw from, on models with the feature `reference images`. |
| `$llm.speech.speakAsync({ model, text, voice?, format?, speed?, instructions?, reference? })`, `voicesAsync(model)` | Audio: `{ file, model, usage }`. `reference: { audio, text? }` reads in the voice of that clip (voice cloning). |
| `$llm.transcribe.transcribeAsync({ model, audio, language?, prompt? })` | Text from audio: `{ text, language, model, usage }`. |
| `$llm.align.alignAsync({ model, audio, text, mode?, language? })` | When each line and word of `text` is said in `audio`: `{ duration, lines, words, unaligned, model, usage }`, in seconds. For captions timed to a voice. |
| `$llm.music.createAsync({ model, prompt, lyrics?, seconds?, wait? })`, `getAsync(id)`, `contentAsync(id, index)` | Music, as a job (below). |
| `$llm.video.createAsync({ model, prompt, image?, seconds?, size?, aspectRatio?, wait? })`, `getAsync(id)`, `contentAsync(id, index)` | Video, as a job. |
| `$llm.embed.embedAsync({ model, input, dimensions? })` | One vector per text: `{ vectors, model, usage }`. |
| `$llm.<kind>.modelsAsync({ provider? })` | The models your providers offer of that kind, with their prices, size, features and languages where known (below). |
| `$llm.file(file)`, `$llm.fileAsync(file)` | A generated file as a PocketBase file, for `record.set("field", ...)`; `fileAsync` also downloads one the provider gave only a URL for. |
| `$llm.fromRecord(record, field)` | The other way: a record's stored file as a file with its bytes, to send to a model (a voice clip, audio to transcribe). |
| `$llm.chat.*` | Stored conversations, from the [LLM Chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-chat) extension. |

**`reasoning`** is how much a reasoning model thinks before answering: `"off"`, `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, or left
out for the model's own default. Many models think by default, and the thinking counts toward `maxTokens`: for short
jobs (labels, titles, JSON) say `"off"`, or the answer can come back empty with `stopReason: "length"`.

**`options`** passes a provider's own fields through unchanged (`seed`, `steps`, OpenRouter's `provider` routing...), for
what the common fields don't cover.

**Files** come back as `{ name, type, data, url }`: `data` is the bytes (base64 in JSON), `url` the provider's own copy
when it keeps one (it may expire). Audio to transcribe is sent the same way.

**Jobs:** music and video take a while. `createAsync` starts one and returns `{ id, status }`; follow it with `getAsync(id)` until
`status` is `done`, then fetch each of its `outputs` with `contentAsync(id, index)`. Or pass `wait: "5m"`: `createAsync` then
resolves once the job is done, its `files` included. The id names the provider
(`vultr:music_02a2…`), so `get` finds it again after a restart; the provider keeps the job, not your app.

**Cost:** every result's `usage.costMicroUSD` is what the call cost, in millionths of a US dollar (`1000000` is $1), a
whole number on every answer of every kind: what the provider charged when it says (OpenRouter on every call, Vultr for
media), else worked out from the model's listed prices and what the call used (tokens, cached tokens, pictures,
seconds, characters), with `usage.costEstimated` true, else `0` (free, or no prices it can count).

**Models and prices:** each model in a `models` answer carries what its provider says about it: `contextTokens`,
`size` ("27B", "30B (3B active)"), `features` (`tools`, `structured output`, `vision`, `audio input`, `voice cloning`,
`voice design`, `built-in voices`, `lyrics`), `languages`, and `prices`. A price is a rate on one meter, in US dollars
per `unit`, and every provider's are given in the same units: `1M input tokens`, `1M output tokens`,
`1M cached input tokens`, `second` (of audio or video made, or read), `megapixel`, `image`, `1K characters` (read
aloud), `request`. Its `source` is `listed` (the provider's own list) or `measured`: what this app's calls to the model
were actually billed, from the ledger, over `calls` calls (text in `1M tokens`, in and out together, since a bill
doesn't split them; pictures per `request`). Costs worked out from listed prices never count toward a measured one.
No prices means the price isn't known. Extras a call may not use (web search, cache writes, images sent in) aren't
listed, and a model with a price in a unit that can't be put in these (per inference step) lists none rather than
look cheaper than it is.

Settings → LLM lists every model of each kind across your providers under **Models**, searchable and cheapest first.
Other dashboard screens use the same pieces through `window.pocketone.llm`: `select({ kind, value, onchange })` is a
searchable dropdown of a kind's models with their prices. Give it the work the model is
for, `job: () => ({ "1M input tokens": 0.006, "1M output tokens": 0.002 })` (how much of each price unit the work uses)
and `per: "a story"`, and each model also shows what that work costs on it ("≈ $0.0012 a story", "≥" when it lists only
one side of the tokens), cheapest first. `browser({ kinds?, kind? })` is the whole list, and `models(kind)`,
`prices(model)`, `priceText(model)`, `rank(model)` and `costFor(model, job)` the data underneath.

**Errors** have a code: `not_configured` (no providers yet), `unknown_model` (no model named, or no provider by that
name), `not_supported` (that provider type doesn't do this kind), `provider` (the provider's own error, its message
kept, with the provider's name in front), `timeout` (the provider didn't answer in time; the request was cancelled).
Text calls always stream from the provider, so a stalled answer fails after a few seconds of silence (10 s on Vultr and
OpenRouter), and every call has an overall limit by kind. To give up sooner, pass `signal` (an `AbortSignal`) in any
call's options, `{ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000) }`: the promise rejects with its reason and the provider's request
is cancelled ([Time limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm#time-limits)).

**Over HTTP** each kind is a contract at `/api/_c/llm.<kind>/v1/` (`llm.text/v1/complete`, `llm.image/v1/generate`...),
for superusers and for API tokens with the `llm` scope (`llm:read` for `models`, `voices`, `get` and `content`); see
[llm.text/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.text/v1) and the others in the [catalogue](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts).

What each provider type covers:

| | Text | Pictures | Speech | Transcription | Music | Video | Embeddings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vultr` | yes | yes (and references) | yes, with voices and cloning | yes | yes (job) | yes (job) | yes |
| `cloudflare` | yes | yes | yes | yes | | | yes |
| `openrouter` | yes | yes (and references) | yes, with voices and cloning | yes | | yes (job) | yes |
| `openai` | yes | yes | yes | yes | | | yes |

An `openai` provider's model list names only ids, so each model's kind is guessed from its name (`whisper` is
transcription, `tts` is speech, `embed` is embeddings, and so on; anything else is text).

## Integrations

| With | What happens |
|---|---|
| [LLM Chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-chat) | Stored conversations on top of `llm.text/v1`: `$llm.chat.new()`, `$llm.chat.open(id).sendAsync(text)`. |
| [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings) | Settings → LLM is its `settings/v1` section. |
| [API Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) | A token with the `llm` scope can call the contracts over HTTP, and MCP clients get them as tools. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Each instance has its own Settings → LLM, providers and keys. |

## Example

The example is a PocketBase app with LLM that, once you've added a provider named `vultr` in Settings → LLM, answers
one question at start-up and logs it.

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with the llm extension. Add a provider named "vultr" in Settings → LLM (or
// change the model below), run `go run . serve`, and watch the log for "llm: answer".
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"

	textv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/text/v1"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/extkit"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/llm"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{llm.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(e *core.ServeEvent) error {
		go func() {
			res, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(context.Background(), extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{
				Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: "In one sentence: what is PocketBase?", MaxTokens: 200, Reasoning: "off"})
			app.Logger().Info("llm: answer", "text", res.Text, "model", res.Model, "error", err)
		}()
		return e.Next()
	})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

The [ask starter kit](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/ask/README.md) (`pocketone pages create mydocs --starter ask`) is a whole PocketOne app
(no Go) on `$llm`: it answers questions from a folder of Markdown docs kept in an LLM Search bucket, citing its pages.

# LLM Chat

Version 0.1.0 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

LLM Chat keeps conversations with a language model. Cloud models remember nothing between calls, so every turn has to
send the conversation again; LLM Chat stores it for you. Start a chat, keep its id, and send it questions: it stores
every turn, sends the model the recent ones with each new question, and folds older ones into a summary so long chats
stay quick and cheap.

```ts
const id: string = $llm.chat.new({ meta: { user: ctx.auth.id } })
const answer: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.chat.open(id, { model: "vultr/glm-5.2", system: preamble }).sendAsync("How do I export my notes?")
```

In Go:

```go
chats := chatv1.Contract.Must(app) // llm.chat/v1, from pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/chat/v1
c, err := chats.New(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.NewInput{Meta: json.RawMessage(`{"user":"` + e.Auth.Id + `"}`)})
res, err := chats.Send(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.SendInput{ID: c.ID, Model: "vultr/glm-5.2", System: preamble, Text: "How do I export my notes?"})
```

It needs the [LLM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) extension (llm.text/v1), which answers. Chats aren't tied to users: your app
keeps the id (on its own records, or in its frontend) and may put anything in a chat's `meta` to find it again.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

LLM Chat is built into `pocketone` and on by default, in every app and every instance of a host (a standard member).
In your own Go build, next to LLM:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{llm.New(), llmchat.New()}, nil, nil)
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/llm-chat`. Its two collections come from its own migration, `0001_chats` in
[schema.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/llm-chat/schema.go), which runs on the first start (`pocketone extensions migrations` lists it). They stay empty
until your app starts a chat.

## Configure

There's nothing to configure. Each send names its model and can say how much of the chat to send (below). Turn it off
on a single app with `llm-chat: {enabled: false}` in pocketone.yaml (on a host, an instance's `extensions.llm-chat`);
its collections and their data stay. `pocketone extensions migrate down llm-chat` removes them, data included.

## Use

`$llm.chat.new({ title?, meta? })` returns a new chat's id. `$llm.chat.open(id, options)` returns the chat:

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sendAsync(text, { onText?, onReasoning?, schema?, ...options })` | Asks, saves both turns, resolves to llm.text/v1's answer (`text`, `usage`, ...). With `onText`, streams the answer to it as it's written. The only call that reaches a provider, so the only async one. |
| `history({ limit?, before? })` | The chat's messages, oldest first: `{ id, role, content, created }`. |
| `summary()` | What the older messages were folded into. |
| `title(text?)`, `meta(object?)` | Read, or set and return. |
| `forget()` | Deletes the chat and its messages. |

Options for `$llm.chat.open(id, ...)`, used by every send (a send can override them):

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | | Required (here or on the send): the `provider/model` that answers, and writes the summaries. |
| `reasoning` | the model's | As in `$llm.text.completeAsync`. Summaries always use `"off"`. |
| `system` | | The preamble, first on every turn. |
| `context` | | Text, or a function of the question returning text, sent after the question: the passages that answer it. `history()` shows the question alone; later turns send it with its context again, so each prompt starts the same way. |
| `enrich` | | Search buckets whose best passages go after the question (`["help"]`, or `{ buckets, limit, query, viewer }`; `viewer: ctx.auth` applies collections' view rules), saved with it like `context`; the answer's `passages` lists them. Needs the [LLM Search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-search) extension. |
| `window` | 12 | Messages sent before the summary takes over. |
| `summarizeEvery` | 6 | Once that many messages have piled up past the window, the oldest are folded into the summary (a second, short call). If that call fails, the answer is still returned and saved, and the next send tries again. |
| `maxTokens`, `temperature` | the provider's | As in `$llm.text.completeAsync`. |

`$llm.chat.list({ meta?, limit?, offset? })` lists chats, most recently updated first; `meta` keeps those whose meta has
each of its top-level keys with that value. `$llm.chat.forget({ meta })` deletes every match and returns how many.

The chats are in `_llm_chat_chats` and `_llm_chat_messages`, superuser-only: your routes decide what users see. A
typical route checks that the chat's `meta.user` is the caller before sending:

```ts
// pb_pages/ask/[chat].ts: POST /ask/<chat id> {"question": "..."}
export async function post(ctx: any) {
  const chat = $llm.chat.open(ctx.params.chat, { model: "vultr/glm-5.2", system: preamble(ctx) })
  if (!ctx.auth || chat.meta().user !== ctx.auth.id) throw ctx.httpError(404, "no such chat")
  return ctx.res.json(await chat.sendAsync(ctx.req.body().question))
}
```

**How a send is built:** the system text, then the summary (when there is one), then every message since the last
fold, then the question with its context. That start stays the same from one turn to the next until the next fold,
which the providers' prompt caches bill cheaper.

## Example

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with stored chats: the llm extension answers, llm-chat keeps the
// conversations. Add a provider and a text default in Settings → LLM, run `go run . serve`, and ask over HTTP as a
// superuser:
//
//	POST /api/_c/llm.chat/v1/new  {"title": "Support"}            -> {"id": "..."}
//	POST /api/_c/llm.chat/v1/send {"id": "...", "text": "Hello"}  -> {"answer": {"text": "..."}}
//
// In page code the same is $llm.chat.new() and $llm.chat.open(id).sendAsync(text).
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"

	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/extkit"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/llm"
	llmchat "pocketone.dev/ext/llm-chat"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{llm.New(), llmchat.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

# LLM Search

Version 0.1.0 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

LLM Search is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for PocketOne apps, part of [AI in your app](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension). It
keeps **buckets**, knowledge bases of your content, and runs the pipeline: **ingestion** (sources become documents,
documents become chunks that remember their section, lines and record), **embeddings** with the app's one embedding
model (picked for you from Settings → LLM), and **hybrid search** (semantic search by vector similarity and keyword
search by BM25, merged). Your app makes the bucket it needs; you fill it on the dashboard's **Search** screen with
**sources**: files, folders and zips you drop, pasted text, web pages and Git repositories it keeps current, or
collections it keeps in sync. **Chat** on that screen lets you try it out.

The usual use is grounding a model's answer in your content. Name the buckets on a model call (`enrich`) and the best
passages go into the prompt:

```ts
const answer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question, enrich: ["help"] })
// answer.passages: what was added, to show where the answer came from
```

Or search yourself:

```ts
$llm.search.ensure({ name: "storytime", title: "Story Time library", description: "Stories, characters and places to draw on." })
const found = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: ["storytime"], query: "a fox who lives by the sea", limit: 5 })
for (const r of found.results) console.log(r.bucket, r.document, r.heading, r.text)
```

In Go:

```go
s := searchv1.Contract.Must(app) // llm.search/v1, from pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1
s.Ensure(ctx, extkit.Internal, searchv1.EnsureInput{Name: "storytime", Title: "Story Time library"})
res, err := s.Search(ctx, extkit.Internal, searchv1.SearchInput{Buckets: []string{"storytime"}, Query: "a fox who lives by the sea"})
```

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

LLM Search is built into `pocketone` and on by default, in every app and every instance of a host (a standard member). In
your own Go build, next to LLM:

```go
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{llm.New(), llmsearch.New()}, nil, nil)
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/llm-search`; page code reaches it as `$llm.search`, bound by the LLM extension. Its collections (`_llm_search_buckets`, `_llm_search_documents`, `_llm_search_chunks`)
and its keyword index (the SQLite FTS5 table `_llm_search_fts`) come from its own migration, `0001_buckets` in
[schema.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/llm-search/schema.go), which runs on the first start. They stay empty until something makes a bucket.

## Configure

Searching needs an AI provider with embedding models in Settings → LLM (Vultr's `qwen3-embedding-4b`, say). There's
nothing else to set:

- **The embedding model** is one for the whole app, so every bucket can be searched together. The first time anything
  needs it, Search picks the cheapest embedding model your providers list and keeps it (in kv, `_llm_search/model`).
  Change it on the Search screen: every bucket is embedded again in the background, with its progress shown there, and
  search keeps working meanwhile (chunks not yet done are still found by their words). Content added before there's a
  provider waits, and is embedded once there is one.
- **Each bucket** has a title, a description of what belongs in it, and limits: at most 2,000 documents and 50 MB of
  text. A document is at most 10 MB, a zip 100 MB.

Turn the extension off on a single app with `llm-search: {enabled: false}` in pocketone.yaml (on a host, an instance's
`extensions.llm-search`); its collections and data stay.

## Use

**Buckets.** `$llm.search.ensure({ name, title?, description?, owner? })` makes a bucket if it's missing and
returns it; call it at startup for the bucket your app needs. An existing bucket keeps its settings (only an empty
title, description or owner is filled in), so your admins' changes stick. The description is what the Search
screen shows them: say what to load. A name is letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64.

**Sources.** A bucket holds sources, each one tracked unit however many documents it brings:

| Source | Add it | Documents | Adding it again |
|---|---|---|---|
| File | drop it, or `$llm.search.add({ bucket, name, text })`, or `POST upload?bucket=&name=` with the file as the body | one | replaces it |
| Text | **paste text**, or `add` with `kind: "text"` | one | replaces it |
| Folder | drop it (sent file by file, then pruned) | one per text file, by its path in the folder | updates changed files, adds new ones, **removes missing ones** |
| Zip | drop it, or `upload` a `.zip` | one per text file inside (a shared top folder is dropped) | the same, from the new zip |
| Web page | **add a URL**, or `$llm.search.addURL({ bucket, url, every })` | one | read again on its interval |
| Git repository | add its URL, with or without `.git`: the server is asked whether it's a repository (the Git protocol's `info/refs`), on any host | one per text file on the default branch, plus one per recent commit (300; `commits`) | read again on its interval: one small request when nothing changed |
| Collection | **follow a collection**, or `$llm.search.follow({ bucket, collection, fields, filter })` | one per record the filter keeps | kept in sync as records are saved and deleted |
| Server folder | `$llm.search.addFolder({ bucket, path, include?, exclude?, url? })`: a folder of the app's own files | one per text file, by its path in the folder | read again every five minutes: changed files are embedded again, removed ones leave |

A source's name identifies it in its bucket: the file, folder or zip name, the URL, the collection, or the server
folder's path. Adding one of
the same name replaces it, and the screen asks first. A new version under another name (`notes-v2.zip` for
`notes-v1.zip`) replaces the old one when you say so: **Upload a new version** on its row, or `replace: "<old name>"`.
Dropping content that's already in the bucket under another name (same sha256) asks before adding it again. Each
bucket's sources are its own: replacing `foo.zip` in one bucket leaves a `foo.zip` in another as it was.

Nothing is embedded twice. A document whose text didn't change is left alone, a changed one embeds only its chunks
whose text changed, and a chunk whose content was embedded anywhere in the app (another source, another bucket) reuses
that vector. So two buckets following the same collection, or the same zip in two buckets, cost one embedding.

Folders, zips and repositories leave out binaries, files over 1 MB, dot folders and dotfiles (`.git`, `.github`),
`node_modules`, `vendor` and lockfiles; a repository also takes `exclude` patterns (`"docs/old"`, `"*.min.js"`). Markdown is
split at headings (each chunk carries its heading path, led by the front matter's `title`), code and text at blank
lines, into chunks of about 500 tokens; a page's HTML becomes Markdown (scripts, navigation and footers left out) and
a commit is its subject, body, author, date and the files it changed (no diffs). A collection's record is its first
field as the title and the others below it (editor fields' HTML as text); results from it name their `record`.

Everything is embedded in the background: 64 chunks to a request, under 120 requests a minute, picking up where it
left off after a restart. **Refresh** on a row (or `$llm.search.refresh(bucket, source)`) reads a source again now;
`$llm.search.remove(bucket, sources)` takes sources out; `$llm.search.deleteBucket(name)` removes a bucket. URL and repository
intervals (`every`: `hour`, `day`, `week`) are checked every five minutes. Fetches use Go's default HTTP client, so on
a multitenant host (Pocker) the host's outbound guard applies; only `http` and `https` URLs are taken, public
repositories only, with a 30-second limit per page and five minutes per repository.

**Server folders.** `addFolder` reads files that are already on the server: your docs in `pb_pages`, notes in
`pb_public`, or any folder you put beside them. `path` is relative to the app's own folder (the one holding `pb_data`,
`pb_pages` and `pb_public`) and must stay inside it: no absolute paths, no `..`, no links out of it, and never
`pb_data`. `include` keeps matching files (`["*.md"]`, against the name or the path in the folder), `exclude` leaves out
matches (`["_private", "drafts"]`), beside the usual skips. The folder is read in the background when added and every
five minutes after; an unchanged folder (same files, sizes and times) costs a walk of it. A deploy that changes files
shows up within five minutes, with no restart. `url` says where each file is published, with `{path}` for its path
without the extension (an index file is its folder): with `url: "/docs/{path}"`, `guides/install.md` links to
`/docs/guides/install`, and a result from its "macOS" section to `/docs/guides/install#macos`. Anchors are the ids
PocketOne's Pages (and most Markdown sites) give headings.

```ts
$llm.search.ensure({ name: "docs", title: "Our docs" })
$llm.search.addFolder({ bucket: "docs", path: "pb_pages/docs", include: ["*.md"], exclude: ["_private"], url: "/docs/{path}" })
const found = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: "docs", query: "install on a Mac" })
// found.results[0].url → "/docs/install#macos"
```

**Drawing at random.** `$llm.search.sample({ buckets?, count?, prefix? })` returns chunks picked at random from the buckets named, in the same shape as search results (no score): material to draw from, for a "surprise me" or a topic nobody has asked about. Nothing is embedded, so it's local and free.

**Searching.** `await $llm.search.searchAsync({ query, buckets?, limit?, prefix?, viewer? })` returns the best chunks across
the buckets named (every bucket when none are): `{ results: [{ bucket, document, text, heading, startLine, endLine,
record, url, score }], model, usage }`; `url` links to where the passage is published, for a web page or a server folder
with a `url` pattern. `limit` is 5 by default, at most 50; `prefix` keeps documents whose name starts with
it. Each search embeds the query once (a few tokens; a repeated query is cached), the only part that calls a provider,
so it's the only async call. Ranking merges similarity of meaning (a loop in Go over vectors cached in memory) with
keyword matching (BM25), so exact names like `onRecordCreate` or a character's name rank where they should.

**Who sees what.** A bucket holds a copy of its records' text, so pass `viewer` to apply the collection's view rules:
`viewer: ctx.auth` (or `e.auth`) leaves out matches from records that user can't view, and `null` is a signed-out
guest. Without `viewer` a search sees everything, as your own server code. Over HTTP and MCP only superusers and API
tokens with the `search` scope (or `search:read` to list and search) get in.

**Enriching a model call.** `enrich` on `$llm.text.completeAsync`, `streamAsync` and LLM Chat's `sendAsync` (or a
chat's options) searches the buckets with the prompt and sends the best passages after it, numbered so the model can
cite them; `answer.passages` lists them. Give the buckets (`enrich: ["help"]`) or `{ buckets, limit?, query?, viewer? }`
(default 5 passages, at most 20); `viewer: ctx.auth` applies collections' view rules, as for a search. LLM Chat saves the passages with the question, so later turns send the same thing.

**Cost.** Embedding goes through llm.embed/v1, billed to your provider account like any other `$llm` call. Each
document shows what embedding it cost. `qwen3-embedding-4b` on Vultr is $0.05 per million tokens, about 4 MB of text.

## Integrations

| With | What happens |
|---|---|
| [LLM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension) | Embeds chunks and queries (llm.embed/v1), and adds passages to text calls with `enrich`. Search's own HTTP and MCP API is the [llm.search/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.search/v1) contract. |
| [LLM Chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-chat) | `enrich` on a chat or a send. |
| [Key-Value Store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/kv/extension) | Keeps the app's embedding model. |
| [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox) | On a Pocker host, its egress guard covers page and repository fetches. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Each instance keeps its own buckets and model in its own database. |

## Example

```go
// Command example is a PocketBase app with search buckets: the llm extension embeds, search keeps the buckets. Add a
// provider with embedding models in Settings → LLM, run `go run . serve`, open the dashboard's Search screen, make a
// bucket and drop Markdown files on it. Or over HTTP as a superuser:
//
//	POST /api/_c/search/v1/ensure   {"name": "docs"}
//	POST /api/_c/search/v1/add      {"bucket": "docs", "name": "install.md", "text": "# Install\n..."}
//	POST /api/_c/search/v1/search   {"buckets": ["docs"], "query": "how do I install it"}
//
// In page code the same is $search.ensure(...), $search.add(...) and await $search.searchAsync(...).
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"

	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/extkit"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/llm"
	llmsearch "pocketone.dev/ext/llm-search"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{llm.New(), llmsearch.New()}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

# MCP

Version 0.0.2 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

> Walkthrough for app owners: [MCP for AI agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/mcp). This page is the technical reference.

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint at `/mcp`, so an agent (Claude Code, a Claude
connector, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with your app. No sidecar process.

- **Every tool is one REST call, run as the caller.** A tool call becomes a request to your app's own API, made
  in-process as whoever signed in. API rules, request hooks, middleware and rate limits apply because it *is* the REST
  request. MCP makes no permission decisions of its own.
- **The whole stock API is built in** as `pb_*` tools (records, files, auth, collections, settings, logs, crons, SQL,
  backups). An app that only uses the stock API needs nothing else.
- **Your own endpoints get tools the same way:** write the REST endpoint, then the tool wrapper (`$mcp.addEndpoint`
  in `pb_hooks`, or `AddEndpoint` from Go).
- **Every contract the app provides is there too.** Its operations are tools (`restore_points`,
  `bulkmail_start`, `remote_status`, ...), with input schemas from the contract's types, called through the contract
  so its superuser check, scopes and hooks apply. MCP provides the [mcp/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mcp/v1) contract:
  another MCP server can replace this one, and serves the same contract tools.
- **Sign-in with OAuth** through [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth): add `https://<host>/mcp` to Claude and sign
  in in a browser, as a superuser or an app user. The connection stays signed in until you revoke it.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

MCP is built into `pocketone` and always on, with [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) and
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth) for sign-in and `$mcp` in `pb_hooks`. There's nothing to install or turn on.

MCP is a member of the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard), so every PocketOne app has it: a standalone app or an
instance on a [multisite host](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite), from the stock binary or your own Go build made with
`standard.New()`. The set also registers Tokens (with its OAuth server) for sign-in and binds `$mcp` in `pb_hooks`:

```go
set := standard.New()
app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
app.Start()
```

Tools that `pb_hooks` declare before MCP registers wait for it. The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/mcp`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag, environment variable or settings screen for MCP. In `pocketone` it serves
`/mcp` with every built-in tool, and:
- anyone who can sign in through [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth) can connect: superusers and app users of
  any auth collection, each with their own rights;
- an agent's connection doesn't expire; it lasts until you revoke it;
- the server's name for clients comes from **Settings → Application → Application name**.

A Go build can change the path, the tools, the caps and the sign-in (see [Go config](#go-config)).

### Scopes

MCP registers no scopes of its own. When an agent connects, the consent page offers **Full access** (the account's
rights, like a PocketBase auth token) or **Only these**, with a box for each of your
[token scopes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens#your-own-scopes) (scopes that only reach contract APIs under `/api/_c/`, like `deploy`, aren't
offered unless the client asks for them). The protected resource metadata lists the same scopes in
`scopes_supported`, so a client can ask for some up front; the user can still change the ticks.

A connection limited to scopes is held to them exactly like an API token with those scopes on the REST API:

- Each tool call is checked against the scopes' paths and methods (or `Match` guards). A request they don't cover is
  refused with `403`, and the tool returns that as an error.
- Collection rules see only those scopes in `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>`.
- `tools/list` hides tools none of the scopes reaches, and the instructions name the scopes.

The token itself still works only on `/mcp`. To limit an agent further, sign it in as an account with fewer rights.

### Behind a proxy

The OAuth resource URL must match the URL clients use. MCP builds it from the request's host, taking the scheme from
**Settings → Application URL** when its host is the same, else from TLS or `X-Forwarded-Proto`. If your proxy rewrites
the host, set `Config.PublicURL` in a Go build.

### Browsers

Requests with an `Origin` header from another site get `403`. Clients that send no `Origin`, such as Claude's servers
and Claude Code, pass. A Go build can allow more origins with `Config.AllowedOrigins`.

## Use

### Connect Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http my-app https://<host>/mcp
claude mcp login my-app        # or /mcp in a session
```

A browser opens on your app's sign-in page. Sign in (as an app user, or with **Sign in as a superuser**), check what
the consent page says and click **Allow**. Claude and Claude Code can connect without registering, through their
published client metadata documents.

For a Claude connector, add `https://<host>/mcp` as a custom connector and sign in the same way. Other MCP clients
register themselves with your app first.

### Paste a token instead

A PocketBase auth token, or an API token not bound to any resource, works on `/mcp` as it does on the REST API, and
tool calls forward it unchanged. A scoped API token works only if one of its scopes covers `/mcp`; to limit an agent
to scopes, connect it through the consent page instead (see [Scopes](#scopes)).

### Who a tool call runs as

Whoever signed in. A superuser gets what the API gives superusers; an app user gets what your collection rules give
them. Superuser-only tools are left out of other callers' tool list (that's presentation; the endpoint still
decides).

### See and revoke connected agents

Each sign-in creates an API token bound to `/mcp`, named "<client> (OAuth)". They're listed under
**Settings → API tokens** with an `oauth: <client id>` label; click **Revoke** to disconnect an agent.

### Built-in tools

One per stock endpoint:

| Group | Tools | Who |
|---|---|---|
| `health` | `pb_check_health` | everyone |
| `records` | `pb_list_records` (`perPage` 20 by default), `pb_get_record`, `pb_create_record`, `pb_update_record`, `pb_delete_record`, `pb_run_batch` | per collection rules |
| `auth` | `pb_list_auth_methods`, `pb_request_otp`, `pb_request_verification`, `pb_confirm_verification`, `pb_request_password_reset`, `pb_confirm_password_reset`, `pb_request_email_change`, `pb_confirm_email_change` | per collection |
| `files` | `pb_download_file` (protected files through a file token made as the caller; images as images, text as text, others as embedded data; up to 10 MB) | per view rules |
| `collections` | `pb_list_collections`, `pb_get_collection`, `pb_create_collection`, `pb_update_collection`, `pb_delete_collection`, `pb_truncate_collection`, `pb_import_collections`, `pb_get_collection_scaffolds`, `pb_list_oauth2_providers`, `pb_dry_run_view` | superusers |
| `settings` | `pb_get_settings`, `pb_update_settings`, `pb_test_s3`, `pb_test_email`, `pb_generate_apple_client_secret` | superusers |
| `logs` | `pb_list_logs`, `pb_get_log`, `pb_get_log_stats`, `pb_truncate_logs` | superusers |
| `crons` | `pb_list_crons`, `pb_run_cron` | superusers |
| `sql` | `pb_run_sql` | superusers |
| `backups` | `pb_list_backups`, `pb_create_backup`, `pb_upload_backup`, `pb_download_backup`, `pb_delete_backup`, `pb_restore_backup` | superusers |

- Record create and update take field values in `data`, with files as `{"name", "base64", "type"}` objects
  (`"field+"` appends, `"field-"` removes).
- `pb_delete_collection`, `pb_truncate_collection`, `pb_delete_backup` and `pb_restore_backup` need `confirm` set to
  the name.
- Endpoints that hand out a new token (auth-with-*, auth-refresh, impersonate) and realtime (a stream) aren't tools.
- Each tool call counts against the API's rate limits, like any request. Batch sub-requests skip route middleware
  (PocketBase behaviour).

### Add your own tools from pb_hooks

Write the endpoint as you would anyway, then declare its tool at the top level of a hooks file:

```js
// pb_hooks/blog.pb.js
routerAdd('POST', '/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish', (e) => { /* … */ }, $apis.requireSuperuserAuth())

$mcp.addEndpoint({
  name: 'blog_publish_post',
  description: 'Publish a draft post and email subscribers.',
  method: 'POST',
  path: '/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish', // {id} comes from args.id
  inputSchema: { type: 'object', required: ['id'], properties: { id: { type: 'string' } } },
  // optional; request is the default mapping, return a changed copy
  request: ({ args, auth, request }) => ({ ...request, body: { at: args.when } }),
  // optional; throw for an error the model can read
  response: ({ status, json }) => (status === 200 ? { published: json.id } : json),
})
$mcp.instructions('blog_publish_post also emails subscribers.')
```

- The tool runs the request as the caller, so the route's own auth check is what protects it. One tool serves every
  caller.
- `title`, `outputSchema` and `annotations` are optional. Without annotations, `GET` tools are marked read-only and
  `DELETE` tools destructive.
- `request` gets `{args, auth, request}` and returns `{method, path, query, body, headers, files}` (missing keys keep
  the default; `$mcp.pathValue(v)` escapes a path segment).
- `response` gets `{args, auth, status, headers, body, json, truncated}`.
- Both run one at a time on the VM that loaded the hooks and may use the file's top-level variables; the REST call
  itself runs outside it. Keep them small: the work belongs in the endpoint.
- `$mcp.tools()` lists the registered tool names.

Agents are told to prefer the app's own tools: when an app has any, the instructions sent on connect say to use them
when one fits and fall back to `pb_*`, and the tool list shows them first. Put work that spans collections in a
custom endpoint (one transaction, the app's checks), not in a chain of `pb_*` calls. A wrapper can sit over a stock
endpoint too, to give it the app's meaning (for example `notes_add_note` over `POST /api/collections/notes/records`).

### In the logs

Without the OAuth server on the app, MCP logs a warning on serve:
`mcp: the OAuth server (ext/api-tokens) is off; /mcp accepts pasted PocketBase auth tokens only, and clients can't sign in by themselves`.
In `pocketone` it always is.

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### JavaScript API

What it adds to `pb_hooks` and page code: [MCP JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript/mcp).

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Signs MCP clients in. MCP points clients at it from the protected resource metadata, turns on its client self-registration, and makes tokens bound to `/mcp` never expire. Who may sign in comes from its `Collections` (default: superusers and every auth collection). |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) | The access tokens are API tokens bound to `https://<host>/mcp` (RFC 8707): they work nowhere else, and are listed and revoked under Settings → API tokens. |
| Your token scopes | On a full-access connection a tool call holds every scope you registered (except ones its collection can't hold): `$apiTokens.requireScope` guards pass, and `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>` is `"1"` in collection rules. On a connection limited to scopes it holds only those, and requests they don't cover are refused (see [Scopes](#scopes)). |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension) | A `pb_pages` endpoint (a `.ts` file with no template) is a REST endpoint like any other; declare its tool with `$mcp.addEndpoint`. |
| [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) | `pb_download_file` follows its one redirect to storage. |
| JS hooks | `$mcp` in `pb_hooks` (above). |

On a [multisite host](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite), every instance that runs PocketOne has MCP from the standard set, with
its own tokens, OAuth sign-in and `/mcp`; with Pocker, an instance turns it off with `extensions.mcp.enabled: false`.

### Tools from Go

An extension registered on the same app reaches the server with `mcp.For(app)`:

```go
server := mcp.For(app) // or the *mcp.Server that mcp.MustRegister returned

// the endpoint, as you'd write it anyway
app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
    se.Router.POST("/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish", publish).Bind(apis.RequireSuperuserAuth())
    return se.Next()
})

// the tool wrapper
server.MustAddEndpoint(mcp.Endpoint{
    Name:        "blog_publish_post",            // lowercase <extension>_<verb>_<noun>; pb_ is the built-ins'
    Title:       "Publish post",
    Description: "Publish a draft post and email subscribers.",
    Method:      http.MethodPost,
    Path:        "/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish", // {id} is filled from args.id
    InputSchema: map[string]any{"type": "object", "required": []any{"id"},
        "properties": map[string]any{"id": map[string]any{"type": "string"}}},
    Annotations: mcp.Write,                      // default from the method: GET read-only, DELETE destructive
    Request:     nil,                            // optional: func(c *mcp.Call) (*mcp.Request, error)
    Response:    nil,                            // optional: func(c *mcp.Call, res *mcp.Response) (any, error)
})
server.AddInstructions("blog_publish_post also emails subscribers.")
```

The default mapping:

- `{name}` path segments come from the argument of the same name, escaped. Empty, `.` and `..` are refused (the
  router would clean them into another route).
- Other arguments go to the query string for `GET`, `HEAD` and `DELETE`, and to the JSON body for other methods.
- An argument holding a file, `{"name": "a.png", "base64": "…", "type": "image/png"}` or a list of them, makes the
  body multipart (other arguments ride along as `@jsonPayload`), the way PocketBase takes uploads. Up to 10 MB per
  file.
- Arguments are checked against the schema's `required`, top-level `type`s, `enum`s and `additionalProperties: false`
  before the request is made; the endpoint validates the rest.
- The result: 2xx JSON comes back as the result (also as `structuredContent` when it's an object); other 2xx bodies
  as text; 4xx/5xx as a tool error with PocketBase's `{status, message, data}`, so the model can fix its call. JSON
  results are capped at 1 MB and say when they were cut.

`Request` sees the caller (`c.Auth()`) but can't change who the request runs as: an `Authorization` header it sets is
dropped. Build paths with `c.Path(template)` or `mcp.PathValue`, never by joining raw strings. `c.Do` makes another
request as the same caller (e.g. a file token before a download). `Response` may return any JSON-able value, a
string, or an `mcp.Content` list (images, text, embedded files). `SuperuserOnly: true` hides a tool from other
callers' tool list.

### Tools from an extension

An extension's API is contracts, and a contract's operations are already tools: nothing to add. For a tool that
isn't a contract operation, an extension calls `mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{...})` (and `mcpv1.AddInstructions`)
in its `Register`, which works with whichever extension provides mcp/v1.

A PocketOne extension that adds tools names them `<extension>_<verb>_<noun>`: its name (with `-` as `_`), then at least two
lowercase words, such as `notes_list_notes` or `oauth_server_revoke_client`. Each has a description, and an input
schema, when it has one, is a JSON Schema object. The [conformance test](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension) checks all of this
when the extension's test puts an MCP server on the test apps:

```go
conformance.Run(t, newExtension, conformance.Options{Setup: func(app core.App) error {
    _, err := mcp.Register(app, mcp.Config{})
    return err
}})
```

### How sign-in works

With Tokens (with its OAuth server) on the app, `/mcp` uses OAuth the way Claude connectors and Claude Code expect:

1. A request without a token gets `401` with
   `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`.
2. The protected resource metadata names the app as its authorization server (the OAuth server's issuer). The OAuth server
   publishes the authorization server metadata, with PKCE S256, client metadata documents and dynamic registration.
3. The client registers itself (Claude's published identity through a client metadata document, or dynamic
   registration), and the user signs in in a browser.
4. The access token is an API token bound to `https://<host>/mcp`. It carries the account's rights but works only on
   `/mcp`. Each MCP request makes a PocketBase auth token for the same account, and tool calls reach the REST API
   with it (as Pages' `ctx.pb()` does). For a token limited to scopes, those requests carry the scopes
   (`tokensv1.WithScopes`, through the api-tokens/v1 contract), and Tokens checks them as it would a scoped token's request.

Without the OAuth server, `/mcp` falls back to `PocketBaseTokenAuth`: pasted PocketBase auth tokens (`Collections` limits
which auth collections, default any), and the warning above. `Config.Auth` overrides the choice; `mcp.OAuth{Issuer}`
overrides the authorization server listed in the metadata.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mcp/example/main.go) runs one app with an MCP endpoint at `/mcp`: the built-in `pb_*` tools, a tool over a Go route and one over a JS route.

```bash
cd example
go run . serve
```

The example registers [devusers](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go), so the logins are `admin@example.com` / `password`
(superuser) and `user@example.com` / `password` (user). It also registers Tokens (with its OAuth server) for OAuth sign-in,
and adds a tool over a Go route (`example_get_whoami`) and one over a JS route (`example_list_recent_users`, in
[`pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mcp/example/pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js)). Then:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http pb-example http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp
claude mcp login pb-example
```

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with an MCP endpoint at /mcp: the built-in pb_* tools (the whole stock REST
// API), a tool over a Go route, and a tool over a JS route from pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js.
//
//	cd ext/mcp/example && go run . serve
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
//
// Sign-in is OAuth (the OAuth server in ext/api-tokens): add the endpoint to Claude Code and sign in in the browser when it
// asks. Tool calls run as whoever signed in.
//
//	claude mcp add --transport http pb-example http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp
//	claude mcp login pb-example   (or /mcp in a session)
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/api-tokens"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/extkit/js"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/mcp"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	// OAuth sign-in: API tokens + the authorization server. ext/mcp picks it up on serve and turns on dynamic client
	// registration.
	apitokens.MustRegister(app, apitokens.Config{}) // its OAuth server comes with it

	server := mcp.MustRegister(app, mcp.Config{
		Name:        "pb-example",
		Description: "Example PocketOne app with ext/mcp.",
	})

	// A tool from Go: write the REST endpoint, then the tool wrapper. The tool runs the request as the caller, so
	// the route's own auth check is what protects it.
	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		se.Router.GET("/api/example/whoami", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"collection": e.Auth.Collection().Name, "email": e.Auth.Email()})
		}).Bind(apis.RequireAuth())
		return se.Next()
	})
	server.MustAddEndpoint(mcp.Endpoint{
		Name:        "example_get_whoami",
		Title:       "Who am I",
		Description: "The signed-in record's collection and email.",
		Method:      http.MethodGet,
		Path:        "/api/example/whoami",
	})

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
		OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { mcp.BindJS(app, rt) },
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Go config

| Field | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `Name`, `Version`, `Description`, `Icons` | app name slug, `dev` | `serverInfo` |
| `Instructions` | generated | first paragraph of the instructions sent on connect |
| `PublicURL` | the request's host | origin used for the OAuth resource URL; set it when a proxy rewrites the host |
| `Auth` | `OAuth{}` with Tokens' OAuth server on, else `PocketBaseTokenAuth{}` | the `Authenticator` |
| `BuiltinGroups` | all | which `pb_*` groups (`mcp.BuiltinGroups`) |
| `ReadOnlyBuiltins` | `false` | keep only the read-only `pb_*` tools |
| `NoBuiltins` | `false` | drop every `pb_*` tool |
| `MaxResponse` | 1 MB | cap on a JSON result |
| `MaxFile` | 10 MB | cap on one file uploaded or downloaded through a tool |
| `AllowedOrigins` | none | extra browser origins allowed besides the app's own |

The endpoint speaks MCP Streamable HTTP, stateless: each POST carries one JSON-RPC message and gets JSON back.
Protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-03-26`. Tools only for now.

# Pages

Version 0.2.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

> Walkthrough for app owners: [PocketOne apps](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/sites). This page is the technical reference.

Server-rendered pages from a `pb_pages` folder, next to your `pb_data`. Each file becomes a route: `.ets` templates
(EJS tags holding TypeScript) or [TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx) components, Markdown pages, layouts, `.ts` middleware and API
routes, plus static files. Every file type is listed in [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types). Page code runs in your app's JS VM, so it
can use your data directly. Coming from the npm PocketPages package? See [Moving from PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x).

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Pages is built into `pocketone` and **on whenever a `pb_pages` folder exists** next to `pb_data`. There's no switch:
no folder, no pages. If the folder appears while the app runs, it starts serving it.

In your own Go build, register it after the JS VM ([ext/jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm)), since page code runs there:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{})   // page code runs in the app's JS VM
pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{}) // serves pb_pages next to pb_data
pages.RegisterCommand(app.RootCmd)      // the `pages create` and `pages starters` commands
app.Start()
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/pages`. See [example/main.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/example/main.go) and
[Create your own extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension).

## Configure

### Where the folder is

By default the folder is `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`. To use another one:

```bash
pocketone serve --pagesDir /path/to/pb_pages
```

A relative path resolves against the working directory, like `--hooksDir`. Its `pocketone.yaml` key is `server.pages_dir`.

### +config.ts

Settings for your pages live in the folder itself, in `pb_pages/+config.ts`:

```ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
  debug: false,
}
```

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `[]` | Module names (a `_private/` file, a `node_modules` package or a path, loaded with `require`), built-in plugins by name (`auth`, `realtime`, used when no module by that name is found), or custom plugins such as the [add-ons](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/README.md). ETS and Markdown are always on. |
| `debug` | `false` | Detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output even outside dev mode. |

`+config.ts` runs on each page request. Unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page
answer with an error, and the reason goes to the log.

### Dev mode

When the app runs in dev mode (`--dev`, or `app.dev` in `pocketone.yaml`), or `+config.ts` sets `debug: true`, you
get detailed error pages with the file and line, and `ctx.log.debug` output. Otherwise visitors see a plain
"Something went wrong" page and the full error goes to the log.

## Use

### Start from a starter kit

```bash
pocketone pages starters                         # list the kits
pocketone pages create myapp --starter daisyui-docs
cd myapp
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. `pages create` makes a new folder (it must not exist yet) with `pb_pages` and
anything the kit needs beside it, such as `pb_migrations`. Without `--starter` you get `minimal`.

| Kit | What it is |
|---|---|
| [minimal](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/minimal/README.md) | One page, no layout, no build step (the default). |
| [mvp](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/mvp/README.md) | One page styled with MVP.css. |
| [htmx](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/htmx/README.md) | A realtime chat and counter with htmx and the `realtime` plugin. |
| [daisyui](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/daisyui/README.md) | A navbar and drawer layout with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. |
| [daisyui-docs](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/daisyui-docs/README.md) | A docs site from Markdown pages. |
| [datastar](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/datastar/README.md) | A realtime chat with rooms, with Datastar. |
| [auth](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/starters/auth/README.md) | Sign-up, sign-in (password, OTP, OAuth2, anonymous), email flows and a protected account page. |

### Write pages

Add or edit files in `pb_pages` and reload the browser; no restart is needed. A few examples of what the folder holds:

```
pb_pages/
  +config.ts         settings (above)
  +layout.ets        wraps every page
  +error.ets         your error page
  index.ets          /
  about.md           /about
  blog/[slug].ets    /blog/anything
  feeds/rss.ts       /feeds/rss, an endpoint (code, no template)
  _private/          partials, never served
  assets/app.css     a static file
```

The full contract is in [SPEC.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec): routes and precedence, middleware, page code and endpoints (`.ts`), ETS,
partials, slots and layouts, Markdown, JSX and TSX, the `ctx` object, errors, the built-in `auth` and `realtime`
plugins, custom plugins, add-ons and the changes from 0.x.

Highlights:

- Static files get ETags and fingerprinted URLs through `asset()`.
- `ctx.pb()` is the bundled PocketBase JS SDK, called in-process as the visitor.
- `ctx.res.sse()` streams server-sent events.
- The `auth` plugin gives cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: password, OTP, anonymous, register, OAuth2 and the email
  flows (verification, password reset, email change). Accounts that need MFA (the collection's MFA is on and its rule matches) are refused by every pages sign-in method; pages has no second sign-in step yet.

### What you'll see in the log

Problems in the folder (a bad file name, two files claiming the same route) are logged as `pages: ...` errors. If the
site served cleanly before, pages keeps the previous routes until the folder builds cleanly again. Errors thrown by
page code are logged in full.

### Try the demo

[`example/`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/example) is a demo app with ETS, Markdown, TSX, auth, `ctx.pb()`, SSE and a JSON route. It has a live
speed check at `/speed`.

```bash
cd example && go run . serve --dir=./pb_data
```

|---|---|
| [`pocketone pages create <name>`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pages-create) | Create a folder with a starter kit (pb\_pages and anything it needs) |
| [`pocketone pages starters`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-pages-starters) | List the starter kits |

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Pages is in the standard set, so every instance that runs PocketOne serves its own `pb_pages` (below). |
| [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache) | Compiled templates and modules go in the `pages.compiled` bucket (cache/v1, at most 32 MiB per app), keyed by content, so old versions are evicted instead of piling up. On a multisite host, instances serving the same files share one compiled copy. On a multisite host they also outlive an instance's restarts, since the cache belongs to the host. With the cache off, each JS VM compiles a file the first time it meets it. |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | `pb_pages` deploys with your other `pb_*` folders. `pull` doesn't fetch it by default; name it: `pocketone pull prod pb_pages`. |

### On a multisite host

Pages is a member of the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard), so every instance serves its own
`<instance dir>/pb_pages`, in the stock `pocketone` binary and in any host built on `standard.New()`. With an
isolate runtime ([Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)), where instances are isolates in one process:

- Each start of an instance's app gets its own route table, compiled templates (in its own `pages.compiled` bucket; identical files share one copy in the host's cache) and caches. An instance that sleeps
  drops them; nothing is shared between instances.
- Page code runs in the instance's own sandboxed JS VM ([jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm)), under its limits (execution time,
  memory, stack). `include`, `require`, `ctx.resolve`, `ctx.res.file` and `asset` never reach outside the instance's
  `pb_pages`; `$os` file access stays inside the instance folder. Tests:
  [multiinstance_test.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/multiinstance/multiinstance_test.go).
- An instance turns pages off in its settings with `extensions: { pages: { enabled: false } }`.

To try it: copy sites into `multiinstance/example/pb_root/<name>.localhost/pb_pages`, run
`go run ./multiinstance/example`, and open `http://<name>.localhost:8791`.

### Building on pages

- **Read the routes.** `pages.For(app)` returns the service: `Dir()` is the folder, `Table()` the current route
  table, `Errors()` the problems from the last build.
- **Custom plugins.** A factory in `+config.ts` can add to `ctx`, run on each request and transform rendered HTML
  ([SPEC.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec), section 9.2). [Add-ons](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/README.md) are built this way.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/example/main.go) serves the demo in [`example/pb_pages`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/example/pb_pages): ETS, Markdown, TSX, auth, SSE and a JSON route. Run `go run . serve --dir=./pb_data` in `example/` and open http://127.0.0.1:8090.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app that serves the demo in ./pb_pages (ETS templates and TypeScript, Markdown,
// a TSX page, auth, ctx.pb(), SSE, a JSON route, +404). ./pb_migrations creates a "notes" collection with three seed
// notes. From this folder:
//
//	go run . serve --dir=./pb_data
//
// Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090. Edit anything in pb_pages and reload; no restart needed.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com /
// password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/pages"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // page code runs in the app's JS VM
	pages.MustRegister(app, pages.Config{})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Speed

`ext/pages` against npm PocketPages 0.22.5 (the last 0.x release), serving the same starter kit pages: the 0.x kits
in `pb_hooks/pages` on stock PocketBase 0.41.1, the v1 ports in `pb_pages` on the PocketOne binary.

| Page | Version | Requests/s (50 concurrent) | p50 | p99 | One at a time (median) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `minimal` `/` (EJS) | npm 0.22.5 | 620 | 30 ms | 670 ms | 5.7 ms |
| | **ext/pages** | **10,850** | **1.8 ms** | **37 ms** | **0.2 ms** |
| `daisyui-docs` `/docs/overview` (layouts, Markdown, partial) | npm 0.22.5 | 580 | 28 ms | 1.1 s | 6.5 ms |
| | **ext/pages** | **6,510** | **4.1 ms** | **49 ms** | **0.4 ms** |
| PocketBase's own `/api/health` (the ceiling) | PocketOne | 55,000 | 0.9 ms | 2.4 ms | 0.1 ms |

About **17.5× more requests per second** on the simple page and **11×** on the docs page, with p99 latency 20× lower.
Single requests take 0.2 to 0.4 ms instead of 6 ms. Memory after each run was similar (170 to 350 MB for both).

Why: 0.x parsed routes, ran EJS through a JS implementation and loaded its plugins inside the JS VM on every request.
v1 builds the route table once, compiles each template once (EJS to JS in Go, Markdown with goldmark) and enters the
JS VM once per request.

How it was measured (2026-11-11): Apple M1 Max, 10 cores, macOS 27, Go 1.27.4, `hey` against `127.0.0.1`. Each server
was warmed with 500 requests, then `hey -z 10s -c 50` and `hey -n 2000 -c 1`; two rounds, which agreed within 5%.
Every response was a 200 with the full page. The 0.x docs kit inlines about 6 KB of CSS into each page where v1
links `app.css`. Rerun it with [`bench/run.sh`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/bench/run.sh):

```bash
cp -R starters/daisyui-docs /tmp/v1-docs
pocketone superuser upsert admin@example.com password --dir=/tmp/v1-docs/pb_data
bench/run.sh v1-docs 8804 /docs/overview "$(which pocketone)" /tmp/v1-docs
```
