Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox

# Sandbox

Version 0.0.4 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Confines one PocketOne app's JS hooks and migrations, so apps from people you don't know can share one process.
File access stays inside the app's folder, host primitives are gone, every JS call has a time limit, raw SQL can't
leave the app's own database files, and outbound connections reach public addresses only.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Sandbox isn't a switch in `pocketone`: [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) applies it to every instance it runs. With
a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml` (pocker as the runtime), every instance is sandboxed and there's nothing to install. A standalone app
served by `pocketone` without a `multisite` section is not sandboxed.

In your own Go build, give it to the [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) engine as an extension:

```go
sb := &sandbox.Sandbox{Dir: dir, Env: map[string]string{"GREETING": "hi"}}
execution, sleep := sb.Limits()
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
	HooksDir:   filepath.Join(dir, "pb_hooks"),
	Extensions: []any{sb},
	VM:         jsvm.VMConfig{TaskWall: execution, MaxSleep: sleep},
})
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/sandbox`. The SQL guard and the outbound network rules are
separate calls (see Integrations).

## Configure

Sandbox has no `pocketone.yaml` section of its own. Under Pocker its limits are set in the `pocker` section, as
defaults for every instance, and each instance can override them in its own `limits`:

```yaml
pocker:
  max_js_execution: 30s       # each JS call (hook, route, cron, migration) is interrupted after this
  max_js_allocation: 64MiB    # biggest single file read or reader JS can ask for
  max_call_stack_size: 2000   # unused: the JS engine caps its stack by size
  max_sleep: 10s              # cap on sleep()
  max_query_duration: 30s     # deadline for SQL statements that have none
  http_send_max_timeout: 60s  # cap on $http.send timeouts
  http_send_max_body: 10MiB   # cap on $http.send response size
  max_concurrent_js: 16       # JS calls one instance runs at once
  egress_allow: []            # private networks apps may still reach, such as an internal SMTP relay
```

The values shown are Pocker's defaults. An instance gets only its own `secrets` as environment.

In a Go build, the same settings are `Sandbox` fields: `Dir` (required), `Env`, `MaxExecution` (default 30 s,
negative turns it off), `MaxSleep`, `MaxAllocation`, `HTTPSendMaxTimeout`, `HTTPSendMaxBody`, and `Console` to send
`console.*` output somewhere other than the process's stdout and stderr. `Limits()` gives the execution and sleep
limits for `jsvm.Config.VM`; the memory cap and `MaxConcurrent` are set there too.

## Use

There's nothing to operate day to day. Hooks that stick to normal app code (`routerAdd`, `onRecord*`, `cronAdd`,
`$app.findRecordById` and the rest) run unchanged. What changes for a hook author:

- `$os.cmd`, `$os.exec`, `$os.exit` and `$filesystem.local` fail with "not available on this host (sandboxed)";
  `$os.args` is empty; process-wide Go methods such as `$app.restart` read as `undefined`. The app's `types.d.ts`
  declares each of them `never`, so `tsc` and your editor refuse a call to one before you deploy it.
- Files outside the app's folder can't be read or written, by any API, including through `..` or symlinks.
- `$os.getenv` and `process.env` see only the app's own environment.
- A JS call that runs past its time limit is interrupted with an error; so is one that asks for a huge allocation.
- `$http.send` to a private or loopback address is refused.

Under Pocker, `console.*` output and hook errors go to the instance's own `logs/exec.log`.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Runs every instance through the sandbox, the SQL guard and the outbound network rules, with limits from the `pocker` section and each instance's `limits`. Its attack tests are in [`sandbox_test.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pocker/sandbox_test.go). |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Carries the per-instance `limits` from `instances.yaml` or a mothership. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | Rate and concurrency limits in front of every request. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | The alternative for untrusted apps: a container per instance instead of checks inside one process. Docker doesn't use the sandbox. |

### Building on Sandbox

- **`Sandbox`** is a jsvm extension (`OnInit`, `Modules`, `HTTPClient`, `HideField`/`HideMethod` to hide
  process-reaching Go members, and `FilterTypes` to declare those members `never` in the app's `types.d.ts`); add it
  to `jsvm.Config.Extensions`.
- **`GuardedDBConnect(maxQuery)`** is a `core.DBConnectFunc`: set it as the app's `DBConnect` to open the databases
  through SQLite's authorizer, with a deadline for statements that have none.
- **`InstallEgressPolicy(sandbox.EgressPolicy{Allow: ...})`** routes Go's default HTTP transport through the
  public-only dialer, for the whole process. `EgressPolicy.Dialer()` gives the same check for your own connections.
- **`BindMail(app)`** sends the app's own SMTP through that dialer.
- **`ErrSandboxed`** is the error disabled bindings return.

## Example

One app whose JS hooks are sandboxed: file access confined to the app folder, host primitives disabled, and a 5 s
limit per JS call. Run it from this folder with `go run ./example serve`.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app whose JS hooks are sandboxed: file access is confined to the app folder,
// host primitives ($os.exec, $os.exit, ...) are disabled, and every JS call has a time limit.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/sandbox"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	dir, _ := os.Getwd()
	sb := &sandbox.Sandbox{
		Dir:          dir,                                 // JS may only touch this folder
		Env:          map[string]string{"GREETING": "hi"}, // the only environment JS sees
		MaxExecution: 5 * time.Second,
	}

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
		HooksDir:   filepath.Join(dir, "pb_hooks"),
		Extensions: []any{sb}, // OnInit, Modules, HTTPClient and the member filter
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How is this safe?

With [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), PocketOne can serve hundreds of instances from one Go process, each with its own owner, hooks and data.
This section explains why that's safe enough to run code from people you don't know, and where it isn't.

Configuration and the engine API are in [POCKER.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker). The attack tests are in [`sandbox_test.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pocker/sandbox_test.go).

### Why one process

Most hosted PocketBase instances are idle most of the time. A container per instance means paying idle memory and a
cold start of a second or more for each one. In one process an instance's app starts on its first request in tens of
milliseconds, costs a few MB while it runs, and shares the Go runtime with everyone else.

What you give up is the kernel boundary between tenants. Everything below replaces it with checks inside the process.

### The threat

Assume every instance's owner is hostile. They control:
- their `pb_hooks` (JavaScript, run by the instance's own QuickJS VM, [ext/jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm));
- their `pb_migrations`;
- their collections, rules and settings;
- any SQL their hooks run;
- requests to their own instance.

They must not be able to:
- read or change another instance's files, database, environment or settings;
- read the host's files, environment, credentials or private network;
- take the process down, or starve everyone else of CPU and memory.

### The layers

#### 1. Each instance is its own app

- Every instance has its own `core.App`, database, settings, JS VMs, migrations list, settings encryption key and
  log.
- Requests are routed by hostname to exactly one app. Nothing in one app holds a reference to another.
- In production only hostnames the instance source maps are served; unknown hosts get 404 and never create a folder.

#### 2. Files: confined by the kernel, not by string checks

Every file API reachable from JS goes through an `os.Root` opened on the instance's folder. That covers:
- `$os.*`
- `$filepath.glob`/`walk`
- `$filesystem.fileFromPath`
- `$template.loadFiles`
- `$apis.static`
- `require()`

The kernel resolves each path beneath that root and refuses `..` and symlinks that lead out. There is no path
string for an attacker to get clever with.

#### 3. Host primitives: removed

The following are gone from JS:
- process control: `$os.cmd`, `$os.exec`, `$os.exit`, `$os.args`;
- `$filesystem.local`;
- PocketBase internals that reach the whole process: `$app.restart`, `bootstrap`, `$app.onTerminate` (use
  `onTerminate(...)`), binding or firing hooks from a running handler, `*sql.DB` handles;
- Go's `os/exec`, `net`, `syscall` and `database/sql/driver`.

A field-name mapper hides them, so they read as `undefined`. Everything a normal app uses still works: `routerAdd`,
`onRecord*`, `cronAdd`, `$app.findRecordById` and the rest. The app's own serve hook stays open:
`$app.onServe().bindFunc(...)` fires once when the app starts serving, which is how a hook file registers a superuser
UI extension (`e.uiExtensions.push({ name, fs: $os.dirFS(...) })`); the event's server and listener stay hidden.

#### 4. Environment: only the instance's own

`$os.getenv` and `process.env` return the instance's own secrets and nothing else. Platform values never go through
the environment:
- the settings encryption key;
- superusers the host keeps in sync;
- private tokens for the host's Go code.

#### 5. SQL: SQLite's own authorizer

Raw SQL is allowed (`$app.db().newQuery(...)`), because PocketBase apps depend on it. Instead of parsing statements,
PocketOne installs SQLite's authorizer callback on every connection, so SQLite itself refuses:
- `ATTACH` and `VACUUM INTO` outside the instance's `pb_data`;
- `load_extension`;
- the pragmas that move SQLite's files elsewhere.

Statements without a deadline get one (`max_query_duration`).

#### 6. Outbound network: public addresses only

PocketOne installs one dialer process-wide, on Go's default HTTP transport and PocketBase's SMTP client. It covers:
- `$http.send`
- `$filesystem.fileFromURL`
- S3 storage and backups
- OAuth2/JWKS fetches
- SMTP

The dialer refuses:
- loopback, private ranges, link-local and cloud metadata;
- CGNAT, multicast, reserved and documentation ranges;
- the IPv6 forms of all of these, including IPv4-in-IPv6.

It checks the address actually connected to, after DNS, so DNS rebinding doesn't help. `$http.send` timeouts and
response sizes are capped.

#### 7. CPU, memory and concurrency

| Resource | What's enforced |
|---|---|
| CPU | Every JS call (hook, route, cron, migration) is interrupted after `max_js_execution`, Go calls included. `sleep()` is capped. |
| Concurrency | At most `max_concurrent_js` JS calls per instance in flight at once; more wait, then fail. Per-IP and per-instance rate and concurrency limits sit in front of every request. |
| Memory | Each instance's VM has a hard cap (default 64 MiB): the JS heap plus the Go objects JS holds. A script that grows past it, slowly or at once, gets an out-of-memory error; other instances are unaffected. The JS stack is capped by size, so deep recursion is an error, never a crash. File reads are capped at `max_js_allocation`. |

Every limit has a process default and a per-instance override.

#### 8. Failures stay with their instance

- A broken hooks file, a panic during start or a failed migration fails that instance alone: it answers 502 and logs
  to its own `logs/exec.log`. Every other instance keeps serving.
- `console.*` output goes to the instance's own log, never to the host's.

### What it doesn't cover

Be clear about these before you host strangers:

- **Go memory is estimated.** Go objects JS holds are charged to the instance by estimate, and Go's garbage collector
  can let the process use up to about twice that; set `GOMEMLIMIT` for the process.
- **It's one address space.** A bug in Go, QuickJS, SQLite or PocketOne's own checks would cross tenants in a way a
  container boundary wouldn't. The sandbox tests cover the known paths, but they don't prove nothing else exists.
- **No OS-level layer yet.** Seccomp, Landlock and a second, OS-level egress filter aren't built in.

### How to run it

For untrusted tenants, add the OS layers yourself:
- run PocketOne as a non-root user that owns only the instances folder;
- run it under a cgroup memory limit (with swap), so the worst case is a restart, not a host OOM;
- add an OS firewall rule that lets that user reach public addresses only, an egress layer independent of the
  process;
- keep secrets for host code out of the process environment; use `private:` values instead;
- put a proxy or the built-in firewall in front, with rate limits on.

If you only run your own apps, the defaults are already more than stock PocketBase gives you.

# Stats

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Looks after the data of the instances a host serves. Today it measures facts about each instance (disk used, last
request served) and reports them. Later it will also carry out decisions about that data, such as archiving.

> **Status.** Working, first step: facts and the `measure` decision. Archiving, restoring, offloading backups and
> purging come next, as further decisions. The [rules engine](#rules-criteria-an-app-can-replace) is ready as a Go
> library but isn't read from `pocketone.yaml` yet.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Lifecycle runs on a host that serves many instances ([ext/multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite), with [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)
or [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker)), not on a standalone app.

The stock `pocketone` binary turns it on by itself in host mode: when `pocketone.yaml` has a `multisite` section,
every instance under the first runtime's root folder is measured. There's no switch to flip.

```yaml
multisite: {}
instances: { file: ./instances.yaml }
```

In your own host build, add it as a gate (to see requests) and a background job:

```go
lc := &stats.Lifecycle{Directory: h.Directory, Folder: func(i multisite.Instance) string { return filepath.Join(root, i.ID) }}
h.Gates = append(h.Gates, lc)                // records each local instance's last request
h.Background = append(h.Background, lc.Run) // measures and reports on the policy's schedule
```

`Folder` says where an instance's data lives. The stock binary uses the instance's own `dir` when it has one, else
`<root>/<id>`.

## Configure

The `lifecycle` section in `pocketone.yaml` sets the schedule. Everything is optional.

```yaml
lifecycle:
  measure_every: 24h   # how old a disk measurement may get
  report_every: 1h     # how often changed last-request times are reported
  concurrency: 2       # instances measured at once
```

### The policy

What to do comes from a policy. The built-in one (`YAMLPolicy`) reads this section and decides one thing: measure an
instance when it was never measured, or when its measurement is older than `measure_every`. Zero or missing values
fall back to the defaults.

Rules with criteria, `all`/`any`/`not`, vetoes and budgets exist in the [rules engine](#rules-criteria-an-app-can-replace),
but the `lifecycle` section doesn't take them yet.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `lifecycle:`

Instance data on this host: how often disk use is measured and last-request times are reported.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `measure_every` | duration | `24h0m0s` | How old an instance's disk measurement may get before it is measured again. Default 24h. |
| `report_every` | duration | `1h0m0s` | How often changed last-request times are reported to the sink. Default 1h. |
| `concurrency` | int | `2` | How many instances are measured at once. Default 2. |

## Use

### What it measures

For each instance this host serves itself (not the ones it forwards to another edge):

- `disk_bytes`: the size of the regular files in the instance's folder (symlinks aren't followed; 0 when there's no
  folder), and `measured_at`, when that was measured.
- `last_active`: the last request this host served for it, recorded at most once a minute per instance.

### When

- As soon as the instance list loads, every instance is measured, because none has been measured yet.
- After that it checks once a minute and measures the instances whose measurement is older than `measure_every`.
- Changed last-request times are reported every `report_every`.

Facts are kept in memory. With the default log sink, a restart measures everything again.

### What you'll see

Log lines from the default sink and the measuring pass:

```
INFO lifecycle: facts instances=12 disk_bytes=48213504
INFO lifecycle: measured instances=12 disk_bytes=48213504 ms=37
```

`lifecycle: facts` is each report the sink receives (after a measuring pass, and for last-request times).
`lifecycle: measured` follows a measuring pass, with how long it took. Problems show as warnings: `lifecycle:
measuring` (a folder couldn't be read), `lifecycle: report` (the sink failed; last-request times are retried next
time) and `lifecycle: policy`.

### Try it

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/stats/example/main.go) measures the instance folders under a root once and prints each instance's size:

```bash
go run ./example --root ./pb_root --instances instances.yaml
```

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Lifecycle is a `multisite.Gate` (it sees each request to record `last_active`) and a host background job (`Run`). It lists instances from `multisite.Directory`. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Instances under `pocker.root` (default `./pb_root`), one folder per instance. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Instances under `docker.root`, the same `<root>/<id>` layout. |

It knows nothing about plans, payments or tenants: that belongs to whichever policy provider is configured.

### Your own policy

Set `Lifecycle.Policy` to anything that implements `PolicyProvider`:

```go
type PolicyProvider interface {
	Decide(ctx context.Context, facts []Facts) ([]Decision, error) // what to do now, and why
	ReportEvery() time.Duration                                    // how often last-request times are reported
	Concurrency() int                                              // instances worked on at once
}
```

A control plane can provide its own, for example one that delegates the decisions to a mothership, and providers can
wrap each other. Only the `measure` action is carried out today; any other action is logged as `lifecycle: action not
supported yet`.

### Your own sink

Set `Lifecycle.Sink` to anything that implements `Sink` (`Report(ctx, facts []Facts) error`) to send facts somewhere
other than the log. A sink that also implements `Loader` (`Load(ctx) ([]Facts, error)`) gives the facts back at start,
so a restart doesn't measure everything again or forget last-request times.

### Rules: criteria an app can replace

`rules` (package `pocketone.dev/ext/stats/rules`, standard library only) is the engine policies
are built from, on an edge or a mothership. A subject is whatever the caller evaluates: an instance's facts on an
edge, an account with its instances on a mothership.

- **Criteria** answer one question about a subject (stale? orphaned? over its plan?) and say why. They live in a
  `Registry` by name: an app registers its own or replaces a built-in one (`Register("stale", ...)`), and every rule
  that refers to the name (`Ref("stale")`) follows, so what "stale" means is the app's to decide.
- **Where they come from** is pluggable too: code, or definitions from config (`Load`) built from kinds the app
  registered (`RegisterKind("idle", ...)`) and combined with `all`, `any` and `not`. A YAML section and a mothership
  are both just sources of definitions. `Load` registers nothing when a definition is wrong.
- **Rules** lead from a criterion to an action, with named vetoes that always win and a budget per run.
- **Reports** list each decision with its reasons, what was vetoed and by what, what the budget held back and what
  failed. `Summary` gives one line per rule (`archive-stale: 3 decided, 1 vetoed`). Evaluating does nothing by itself:
  acting on the decisions, or only logging them in a dry run, is the caller's.

A definition, as config would supply it:

```yaml
stale:      { kind: idle, params: { after: 8760h } }
archivable: { kind: all, of: [stale, free_plan] }
keep:       { kind: not, of: [archivable] }
```

And in Go:

```go
r := rules.NewRegistry[Facts]()
r.RegisterKind("idle", idleFor)                       // params: { after: 8760h }
_ = r.Load(map[string]rules.Def{
	"stale":      {Kind: "idle", Params: map[string]any{"after": "8760h"}},
	"archivable": {Kind: "all", Of: []string{"stale", "free_plan"}},
})
e := rules.Engine[Facts]{Key: id, Rules: []rules.Rule[Facts]{{
	Name: "archive-stale", Action: "archive", When: r.Ref("archivable"),
	Unless: []rules.Veto[Facts]{{Name: "pinned", If: r.Ref("pinned")}}, Budget: 200,
}}}
report := e.Evaluate(ctx, facts)
```

Every rule sees every subject, so one subject can get several decisions. Make rules exclusive by building them from
exclusive criteria.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/stats/example/main.go) measures the instance folders under a root once and prints their facts, which is what a host's lifecycle does daily.

```go
// Measure the instance folders under a root once and print their facts (what a host's lifecycle does daily).
//
//	go run ./example --root ./pb_root --instances instances.yaml
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"log/slog"
	"path/filepath"

	"pocketone.dev/ext/multisite"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/stats"
)

func main() {
	root := flag.String("root", "./pb_root", "one folder per instance: <root>/<id>")
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file")
	flag.Parse()

	src := &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances, Required: true}
	list, err := src.Snapshot(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	dir := multisite.NewDirectory(slog.Default())
	dir.Load(list)

	lc := &stats.Lifecycle{
		Directory: dir,
		Folder: func(i multisite.Instance) string {
			if i.Dir != "" {
				return i.Dir
			}
			return filepath.Join(*root, i.ID)
		},
		Sink: stats.LogSink{},
	}
	lc.Step(context.Background()) // never measured: every instance is measured now
	for _, f := range lc.Local() {
		fmt.Printf("%-24s %12d bytes\n", f.Instance, f.DiskBytes)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Go module `pocketone.dev/ext/stats`. The stock binary wires it in
  [`examples/pocketone/binary/multi.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/binary/multi.go).
- `Run` loads recorded facts from a `Loader` sink, then waits for the host's instance list to load (checking every
  second). From then on, once a minute, it asks the policy for decisions on the current facts, measures the instances
  it was asked to (`concurrency` at a time) and reports what it measured to the sink.
- Measuring walks the folder and adds up regular file sizes. An instance's pending last-request time goes out with its
  measurement, so it isn't reported twice.
- `Admit` records `last_active` only for instances this host serves itself (`Remote` empty), and never refuses a
  request.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay

# Mail Relay

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Outgoing mail for instances on a [multisite host](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) that haven't set up SMTP, when they share one
process: isolates (an isolate runtime such as [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)).

Stock PocketBase falls back to the host's `sendmail` when SMTP is off. With apps sharing a process, that would run
`sendmail` on the shared host for every tenant. With this extension:

- **SMTP on** in an instance's Settings → Mail: the app sends the mail itself. Bring your own SMTP always wins.
- **SMTP off:** the mail goes through your relay as `<instance>@<Domain>`, within per-instance limits. `sendmail`
  never runs.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Mail Relay is not in the `pocketone` binary. In your own host build, add it to the standard set your runtime gets
(`Standard` on a Pocker server), with your sending domain and relay:

```go
set.Add(mailrelay.New(mailrelay.Config{
    Domain:   "mail.example.com",
    Upstream: mailrelay.SMTPUpstream{Addr: "smtp.provider.com:587", Username: "…", Password: "…"},
}))
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/mailrelay`. It also registers on a standalone app, but a standalone
app can set up its own SMTP and doesn't need a relay.

## Configure

### The relay (Go)

`Domain` and `Upstream` are required; the host doesn't start without them.

- **`Domain`**: every relayed message is From `<local part>@Domain`.
- **`Upstream`**: what delivers the mail. `SMTPUpstream` ships here: `Addr` (host:port), optional `Username` and
  `Password` (PLAIN auth, only over TLS or to localhost), `ImplicitTLS` for port 465 (otherwise STARTTLS when the
  server offers it), and `Timeout` (default 30 s). It dials with its own dialer, so Pocker's egress rules for tenants
  (public addresses only) don't block a relay on a private address. Anything with
  `Send(ctx, from, to, raw)` works, for example an Amazon SES `SendRawEmail` sender.
- **`LocalPart`**: picks an instance's address from its id. The default is the first label of the id, lowercased:
  `blog.localhost` → `blog`.
- **Limits:** `PerMinute` (default 20) and `Daily` (default 200) per instance, `MaxRecipients` (To + Cc + Bcc,
  default 5) and `MaxSize` (encoded message, default 1 MiB) per message.

### Defaults for every instance (`pocketone.yaml`)

```yaml
mailrelay: { per_minute: 20, daily: 200 }
```

Limits set in Go win over this section. Each instance can override it (see [Per-instance settings](#per-instance-settings-pocker)).

## Use

Once it's in, there's nothing to run. Each instance's mail is relayed whenever its SMTP is off.

- **Settings → Mail** in an instance's dashboard shows its superusers the relay: the address it sends as, its limits
  and how many messages it sent today. When sending is off for the instance, it says so and points to the SMTP
  settings.
- **The app's log** (Admin > Logs, which Pocker copies to the instance's own log) gets one line per message, with
  masked addresses: `mailrelay: sent from=blog@… to=a***@x.org`. Refusals and upstream failures are warnings.
- **A refused message** returns an error to whoever triggered the mail, such as a password-reset request: sending
  off, too many recipients, too large, or the limit reached.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | Provides `mail.fallback/v1`: with SMTP off, an app's mail goes to the contract's providers in order (`providers: { mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay] }`); Mail Relay sends it within the instance's limits. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | What it's built for: isolates, instances that share the host's process (an isolate runtime such as [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)). Every instance gets the relay, its own address and its own limits. |
| [Mail Trap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | In development, point `SMTPUpstream` at the trap's SMTP port and every relayed message lands in one inbox, tagged with the instance. The example below does this. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | Campaigns go through PocketBase's mailer by default, so with SMTP off they are relayed and count against the instance's limits. |

### Per-instance settings (pocker)

Each instance can override the defaults in its `extensions.mailrelay` settings, from `instances.yaml` or your instance
source (for example, per plan):

```yaml
instances:
  - id: free-plan-app
    extensions: { mailrelay: { send: false } }               # refuse its mail unless it uses its own SMTP
  - id: big-app
    extensions: { mailrelay: { per_minute: 60, daily: 2000 } }
```

A change to these settings restarts the instance's app on its next request.

Use `send: false`, not `enabled: false`, to stop an instance sending. `enabled: false` turns the extension off for that
instance, and with SMTP off PocketBase then falls back to the host's `sendmail`. Don't set it when apps share a process.

### Building on Mail Relay

- **Your own upstream.** Implement `mailrelay.Upstream` (`Send(ctx, from, to, raw)`) to deliver through an API.
- **Your own hooks first.** The relay runs after the app's own `onMailerSend` hooks, so they can still change or
  drop a message.
- **Go API.** `(*mailrelay.Extension).Address(id)` returns the From address an instance sends as.
- **settings/v1** (superusers): `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=mailrelay` returns the instance's relay status, a read-only section: `active`, `send`, `address`,
  `perMinute`, `daily`, `sentToday`.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mailrelay/example/main.go) runs a Pocker host whose relay sends to the dev mail trap, so every instance's
mail lands in one inbox at http://127.0.0.1:8025. Run `go run ./example --dev` from this folder, then trigger a
password reset on any instance:

```bash
curl -X POST http://alpha.localhost:8090/api/collections/users/request-password-reset -d email=user@example.com
```

Log in to an instance's dashboard as `admin@example.com` / `password` to see the relay on Settings → Mail. `--listen`
changes the instances' port; `P1_MAILTRAP_HTTP` and `P1_MAILTRAP_SMTP` change the trap's.

```go
// Command example is a Pocker build with mailrelay, relaying into PocketOne's dev mail trap: every instance
// without its own SMTP sends as <instance>@mail.localhost, and all of it lands in one inbox.
//
//	go run ./example --dev
//
// Then trigger mail on any instance, for example a password reset (each instance has the test user below):
//
//	curl -X POST http://alpha.localhost:8090/api/collections/users/request-password-reset -d email=user@example.com
//	curl -X POST http://beta.localhost:8090/api/collections/users/request-password-reset -d email=user@example.com
//
// and read it in PocketOne's dev mail trap at http://127.0.0.1:8025 (filter by instance; P1_MAILTRAP_HTTP and
// P1_MAILTRAP_SMTP change its ports). Settings → Mail in each dashboard shows the relay.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/signal"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/mailrelay"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/mailtrap"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/pocker"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/standard"
)

func main() {
	dev := flag.Bool("dev", false, "serve any hostname (alpha.localhost, beta.localhost, ...); otherwise instances.yaml is required")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "", "HTTP address for the instances (default :8090)")
	flag.Parse()

	cfg := pocker.DefaultConfig()
	cfg.Dev = cfg.Dev || *dev
	if *listen != "" {
		cfg.Listen = *listen
	}

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
	defer stop()

	// The dev mail trap (ext/mailtrap) stands in for the operator's real relay (SES, a provider's SMTP, ...)
	inbox, err := mailtrap.Default("mailrelay example: the relay sends to the trap")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	srv := &pocker.Server{
		Config:   cfg,
		Standard: standard.New(), // every instance gets the standard extensions
		Extensions: []pocker.Extension{
			mailrelay.New(mailrelay.Config{
				Domain:   "mail.localhost",
				Upstream: mailrelay.SMTPUpstream{Addr: inbox.SMTPAddr},
			}),
		},
		// local testing: every instance gets superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
		SetupApp: func(_ pocker.Instance, app core.App) error { return devusers.Ensure(app) },
	}
	if err := srv.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- The extension binds PocketBase's `OnMailerSend` on every instance, last, after the app's own hooks. No core change.
- When SMTP is off it doesn't call `e.Next()`, so PocketBase's `sendmail` fallback never runs. It relays the message
  in-process instead.
- Nothing is written to the instance's settings. A backup restored somewhere else has no relay credentials in it, and
  falls back to stock PocketBase behavior.

For each message:

1. **Check it's allowed.** May this instance send (`send`)? Are there no more than 5 recipients (To + Cc + Bcc)? Is
   the encoded size no more than 1 MiB?
2. **Count it.** Each message counts once against the instance's limits, however many recipients it has. The day
   resets at midnight UTC. Counts are kept in memory.
3. **Set the sender.** The From address becomes `<local part>@<Domain>`. The display name is kept, minus anything
   that looks like an address or a link. The app's own sender address becomes `Reply-To`, unless it's PocketBase's
   `@example.com` placeholder.
4. **Build and send.** Bcc stays out of the headers. An `X-Pocker-Instance` header is added, then the message goes to
   the `Upstream`.
5. **Log it** to the app's log.

# Server Timing

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A `Server-Timing` response header on every request to an instance of a [multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) host: how
long the instance's own handler took, and how long it took to wake the instance for the request (under
[Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)). Your browser's dev tools show
it in the request's Timing tab.

```
Server-Timing: origin;dur=12.4, wake;dur=0.0
```

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Server Timing is built into `pocketone` and on whenever it serves many instances, whatever the provider. There's
nothing to install. It isn't used for a single app.

In your own host build, list it first among the host extensions, so its header covers every other hop:

```go
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Extensions: []multisite.Extension{servertiming.New() /*, other host extensions */}})
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/servertiming`.

## Configure

There's nothing to configure: no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or settings screen.

## Use

Open your browser's dev tools, pick a request to an instance and look at its timing, or read the header with curl:

```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://alpha.localhost:8090/api/health | grep -i server-timing
```

| Entry | What it measures |
|---|---|
| `origin` | The instance's own handler: from handing it the request until it sent its response headers. |
| `wake` | Starting the instance for this request. `0` when it was already running. |

Each value is in milliseconds, one decimal, up to the response headers (time to first byte). The innermost hop comes
first; values a server in front already sent are kept, and this host's entries are added after them.

## Integrations

- **[Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)** registers `origin` and `wake` for every request it hands to an instance.
- **Add your own entries.** Host code and other extensions call `multisite.Timing(ctx, fn)` during a request; `fn` returns
  `[]multisite.TimingEntry{{Name, Dur, Desc}}` and runs when the headers go out. Only extensions listed after Server Timing
  are covered. Put names in `Desc`, never addresses.
- **Go API.** `FormatTiming`, `AppendServerTiming` and `WithServerTiming` render entries, append them to a header and
  wrap a response writer, for a server that isn't a multisite host.

## Example

There's no `example/main.go`. See it used in [`examples/pocketone/binary/multi.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/binary/multi.go), which
lists it first in the `pocketone` binary's host extensions.

## How it works

It's a host wrapper (`multisite.Wrapper`). For each request it starts collecting timing entries in the request's
context, then stamps them into the `Server-Timing` header just before the response headers go out (not on interim
1xx responses). Flush, Hijack and `http.ResponseController` keep working through its writer.

# Bundle

Version 0.1.0 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Ship an app's files inside the binary instead of folders on disk: its JS hooks (`pb_hooks`), migrations
(`pb_migrations`) and public files (`pb_public`). Nothing is written to disk and nothing on disk can override them.
PocketHost's mothership uses it for its own hooks.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Bundle is not in the `pocketone` binary. Add it to your own Go build: embed the folders, pass the hooks and migrations
to [jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) as extensions, and serve the public files.

```go
//go:embed hooks migrations public
var files embed.FS

hooks, _ := fs.Sub(files, "hooks")
migrations, _ := fs.Sub(files, "migrations")
public, _ := fs.Sub(files, "public")
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
	Extensions: []any{bundle.Hooks(hooks), bundle.Migrations(migrations)},
})
bundle.Public(app, public, true)
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/bundle`.

## Configure

Nothing to configure. List only what you bundle: without `bundle.Hooks`, hooks still come from `HooksDir` on disk,
and the same for migrations.

## Use

- **Hooks:** `.pb.js` files come from the FS's root only. `HooksDir` is ignored, nothing is written to it, and hooks
  aren't watched.
- **Migrations:** files come from the FS's root only; `MigrationsDir` is ignored.
- **`require()`:** `__hooks` is the virtual root `/pb_embedded/pb_hooks`. Paths under it, and relative paths, load
  from the hooks FS. Everything else is "module not found": absolute disk paths, `..` escapes, `node_modules`. JS that
  reads files itself (`$os.readFile(__hooks + ...)`) gets "no such file", since the root doesn't exist on disk.
- **Public files:** `bundle.Public(app, fsys, indexFallback)` serves the FS at `GET /{path...}` like `pb_public`,
  unless the app has its own route there. With `indexFallback`, unknown paths serve `index.html` (single-page apps).

## Integrations

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) | `Hooks` and `Migrations` are jsvm extensions (`HookFiles`, `Modules`, `MigrationFiles`). |

## Example

```go
// Command example serves its JS hooks and public files from files embedded in the binary: no pb_hooks or pb_public
// folder on disk.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hello
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"io/fs"
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/bundle"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm"
)

//go:embed hooks public
var files embed.FS

func main() {
	hooks, err := fs.Sub(files, "hooks")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	public, err := fs.Sub(files, "public")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{Extensions: []any{bundle.Hooks(hooks)}})
	bundle.Public(app, public, true)
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

`Hooks` implements jsvm's `HookFiles` and `Modules`: the engine asks it for the hook files and for every module
`require()` resolves, and it serves only paths under the virtual root, from the FS. `Migrations` implements
`MigrationFiles`. `Public` binds the static route with `apis.Static` at the lowest priority, as PocketBase does for
`pb_public`.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap

# Mail Trap

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A development mail catcher (like MailDev or Mailpit) for testing an extension or app that sends mail. In dev mode, an
app whose SMTP is off sends its mail here instead of the host's `sendmail`, and you read it at http://127.0.0.1:8025.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Mail Trap is built into `pocketone`, for every app it runs: a standalone app, or an instance on a multisite host.
There's nothing to install: run `pocketone serve --dev` with SMTP off and it's active.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
mailtrap.MustRegister(app)
app.Start()
```

With ext/standard's set, add it as an extra, as the stock binary does: `set.Add(mailtrap.New())`. The module is
`pocketone.dev/ext/mailtrap`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section or settings screen. It turns itself on only when both are true:

- the app is in dev mode (`serve --dev`, or a dev instance on a multisite host), and
- the app's SMTP is off (Settings → Mail).

Turn SMTP on, or run without `--dev`, and it does nothing. Two environment variables move its ports:

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `P1_MAILTRAP_HTTP` | `127.0.0.1:8025` (the web inbox) |
| `P1_MAILTRAP_SMTP` | `127.0.0.1:1025` (SMTP) |

Never expose these ports: anyone who can reach them can read the mail.

## Use

1. Start the app with `--dev`. It prints the inbox address once it's active.
2. Make your extension or app send mail: a verification, a password reset, `$app.newMailClient()`, a bulk mail campaign.
   Each caught message is also printed as one line in the terminal.
3. Open http://127.0.0.1:8025. The list refreshes every 2 seconds. Click a message to see it as **HTML**, **Text** or
   **Raw** source. **Clear** empties the inbox.

It keeps the last 500 messages, in memory only; they're gone when the process exits. If its ports are taken, it still
catches mail and prints each message in the terminal.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | Provides `mail.fallback/v1`: with SMTP off, an app's mail goes to the contract's providers in order (`providers: { mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay] }`); in dev mode Mail Trap takes it, otherwise it passes it on. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | With an isolate runtime ([Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)), one inbox for every dev instance. Each message is labeled with the instance that sent it (its `X-Pocker-Instance` header), and the inbox filters by instance. |
| [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) | Mail Relay's example uses the trap's SMTP port as its relay, so relayed mail goes through the real SMTP path and lands here. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | In dev mode with SMTP off, campaign mail lands in the inbox instead of being sent. |

### Building on Mail Trap

- **Its hook runs last.** It binds `OnMailerSend` after the app's own hooks, so your `onMailerSend` hooks still run
  and can change the message first. When it takes a message it never calls the next handler, so `sendmail` never runs.
- **SMTP for other tools.** The SMTP listener accepts any message (and any AUTH), so anything that speaks SMTP can
  send to it.
- **Go API.** `mailtrap.Default(reason)` returns the process-wide trap, starting it on first use. A `Trap` has
  `Messages()`, `Clear()`, `Add(from, to, raw, label)` and `AddMessage(msg, label)`, and `Handler()` serves the inbox.
  `Trap{SMTPAddr, HTTPAddr}.Start(ctx)` runs a separate trap, for example in a test.
- **Inbox API.** `GET /api/messages` (newest first, without bodies), `GET /api/messages/{id}`,
  `GET /api/messages/{id}/raw` (.eml) and `DELETE /api/messages`, on the inbox address.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/mailtrap/example/main.go) runs one app in dev mode with the trap. Run `go run ./example serve --dev` from
this folder, request a password reset for `user@example.com` (password `password`) from the dashboard (log in as
`admin@example.com` / `password`), and read the mail at http://127.0.0.1:8025.

```go
// Command example runs one app in dev mode with the dev mail trap: request a password reset for user@example.com
// in the dashboard and read the mail at http://127.0.0.1:8025.
//
//	go run ./example serve --dev
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/devusers"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/mailtrap"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app)
	mailtrap.MustRegister(app)
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

It's built on PocketBase's own `OnMailerSend` hook (the same way [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) takes over an
instance's mail), so PocketBase is unchanged.

MIT

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard

# Standard Set

Version 0.1.3 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

The extensions every PocketOne app has: settings, page templates, a cache, API tokens (with the OAuth server), remotes (remote/v1), MCP,
Pages, an S3 fallback bucket and S3 redirects, point-in-time restore, backups, bulk mail, deploy, WASM modules called from pb_hooks, dashboard cache headers (UI Cache), and a key-value store ($kv). Every
app uses it, standalone or an instance on a multisite host, so an app never misses one because its host forgot to
list it. Members can be reconfigured or turned off per app, never removed.

The set also gives every app's superuser dashboard PocketOne's logo and favicon, the running PocketOne version in the
footer (linked to its releases) and a Docs link to pocketone.dev/docs.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The standard set is built into `pocketone`. In your own Go build, make the app with it instead of
`pocketbase.New()`:

```go
set := standard.New()
app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
app.Start()
```

`NewApp` registers the members, loads `pb_hooks` with their JS APIs (`$mcp`, `$apiTokens`, `$bulkmail`, `$wasm`, `$llm`) and resolves
their contracts. On an app you built yourself, call `set.Register(app, jsvmConfig)` instead.

To build the app from `pocketone.yaml`'s `app` section (data folder, dev mode, hooks and migrations folders, JS engine
and its limits), load the file and pass what `AppFromConfig` returns:

```go
cfg, err := config.Load(config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
a, err := standard.AppFromConfig(cfg)
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
app := standard.New().NewApp(a.PocketBase, a.JS)
```

Every `app` key reaches your build this way, including ones added in later releases. Your own flags override the
fields they cover.

## Configure

- **Reconfigure a member:** replace it, e.g. `set.PITR = pitr.New(pitr.Config{Retention: 7 * 24 * time.Hour})`. A
  member set to nil is an error.
- **Turn one off:** on a single app, `enabled: false` in its `pocketone.yaml` section (`api-tokens: {enabled: false}`);
  for every instance under Pocker, in its `pocker: isolate_config:` section, and for one instance, in its
  `extensions.<name>`. Extensions that require it turn off too, and
  say why. cache, storage (s3-fallback), s3redirect and pitr read `enabled` in their own sections: off, they stay registered and do nothing.
- **Keep one off in code:** a binary whose own code does what a member does sets `set.Switches`, which `Register`
  reads each member's `enabled` from (nil: `standard.ConfiguredSwitches`, the `pocketone.yaml` sections). Wrap it:
  `if name == "bulkmail" { return extkit.Config{{"enabled": false}} }; return standard.ConfiguredSwitches(name)`.
- **Add your own:** `set.Add(myextension.New())`. Extras register after the members, under the same rules.
- **Pick providers:** `set.Providers` is `pocketone.yaml`'s `providers:` section, for a contract more than one
  extension provides.

## Use

Each app logs what it got when it starts:

```
standard: on: settings, templates, cache, api-tokens, remotes, mcp, pages, storage, s3redirect, pitr, backups, bulkmail, deploy, wasm, uicache, kv, llm, llm-chat
standard: api-tokens/v1 ← api-tokens
```

With remotes off (deploy requires its remote/v1):

```
standard: remotes off: enabled: false
standard: deploy off: needs remote/v1, which nothing provides
```

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone cache`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-cache) | Shows each extension's folder in pb\_cache and its size |
| [`pocketone cache clear [extension...]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-cache-clear) | Empties pb\_cache (every extension's folder, or the ones named) |
| [`pocketone extensions migrate down <extension> [n]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-extensions-migrate-down) | Reverts an extension's last n migrations (default 1; 0: all of them) |
| [`pocketone extensions migrate up [extension]`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-extensions-migrate-up) | Applies pending extension migrations (startup does this too) |
| [`pocketone extensions migrations`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-extensions-migrations) | Lists each extension's migrations and whether they're applied |

## Integrations

| With | What happens |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Every instance that runs PocketOne gets the set. Pocker gives it to each instance (`Server.Standard`) with the instance's own `extensions.<name>` settings and the host's extras. A Docker instance on a PocketOne image runs the stock `pocketone` binary: the set with its defaults, no extras. One on a PocketBase image has none. |
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) | Members find each other through contracts (`api-tokens/v1`), resolved per app; the startup lines show who provides what. |

## Example

```go
// A PocketOne app with the standard set and one extra extension: run it with `go run . serve`.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/mailtrap"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/pitr"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/standard"
)

func main() {
	set := standard.New()
	set.PITR = pitr.New(pitr.Config{Retention: 7 * 24 * time.Hour}) // reconfigure a member
	set.Add(mailtrap.New())                                         // add your own

	app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

# apitokensv1

```go
import apitokensv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/api-tokens/v1"
```

Package apitokensv1 is the api-tokens/v1 contract: an app's API tokens. ext/api-tokens provides it. In Go, [Issuer](#issuer) checks a token; over HTTP, its API at /api/\_c/api-tokens/v1 lists, creates and revokes them (a routed contract):

	GET    /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/scopes      the scopes a token may hold, and who may own tokens
	GET    /api/_c/api-tokens/v1             your tokens (superusers: ?owner=, ?ownerCollection=)
	POST   /api/_c/api-tokens/v1             create one ({name, scopes, expires|ttl}); the secret is shown once
	DELETE /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/{id}        revoke one (`pocketone logout` revokes its own)
	POST   /api/_c/api-tokens/v1/revoke-all  revoke all of yours

Extensions that accept API tokens (deploy, mcp, remotes) work with it through this package alone: they register their scopes with the [Issuer](#issuer), read the token a request came with ([FromRequest](#fromrequest)) and limit in-process requests ([WithScopes](#withscopes)). The OAuth server requires it.

Source: [`ext/contracts/api-tokens/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/api-tokens/v1).

## Constants

<a id="offlineaccess"></a>

```go
const OfflineAccess = "offline_access"
```

OfflineAccess is the OAuth scope asking for a refresh token; it limits nothing.

<a id="requestkey"></a>

```go
const RequestKey = "api-tokens.grant"
```

RequestKey is the request store key holding the \*Grant of a request authenticated by an API token.

<a id="scopevaluesep"></a>

```go
const ScopeValueSep = "="
```

ScopeValueSep joins a scope name and a value in a token's scope list: "instances=abc123".

## Variables

<a id="errinvalid"></a><a id="errexpired"></a>

```go
var (
	ErrInvalid = errors.New("invalid API token") // unknown, malformed or revoked
	ErrExpired = errors.New("expired API token")
)
```

Errors [Issuer.Verify](#issuer) returns for a token that isn't valid; any other error is the provider failing.

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Issuer]("api-tokens/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is api-tokens/v1.

<a id="prefix"></a>

```go
var Prefix = extkit.Routed(Contract)
```

Prefix is where the token API is served: /api/\_c/api-tokens/v1.

## Functions

### CoversScope

```go
func CoversScope(scopes []string, scope string) bool
```

CoversScope reports whether a token with these scopes may hand out scope to a token it creates: "instances" covers "instances" and "instances=abc"; "instances=abc" covers only "instances=abc". No scopes: everything.

### HoldsScope

```go
func HoldsScope(scopes []string, scope string) bool
```

HoldsScope reports whether a token with these scopes may act with scope (see [Grant.HasScope](#granthasscope)). No scopes: every scope.

### IntersectScopes

```go
func IntersectScopes(a, b []string) []string
```

IntersectScopes is what both lists allow (both non-empty: an empty list here means nothing, not full rights): "instances" ∩ "instances=abc" is "instances=abc". The result is sorted.

### JoinScope

```go
func JoinScope(name, value string) string
```

JoinScope is "name=value", or name when value is "".

### ScopesFromContext

```go
func ScopesFromContext(ctx context.Context) ([]string, bool)
```

ScopesFromContext returns the scopes set with WithScopes, and whether there are any limits.

### SplitScope

```go
func SplitScope(scope string) (name, value string)
```

SplitScope splits a token scope into its name and value ("" when it has none).

### ValuesOf

```go
func ValuesOf(scopes []string, scope string) (values []string, all bool)
```

ValuesOf is [Grant.ScopeValues](#grantscopevalues) for a scope list. No scopes: every value.

### WithScopes

```go
func WithScopes(ctx context.Context, scopes []string) context.Context
```

WithScopes limits in-process requests made with ctx to these scopes, the way a token limited to them would be (ext/mcp's tool calls on a scoped connection). A nested WithScopes can only narrow it. An empty (or nil) list allows nothing but the token-wide paths, so call it only for a scoped connection.

## Types

### Grant

```go
type Grant struct {
	TokenID         string   `json:"tokenId"`
	Name            string   `json:"name,omitempty"` // the token's label
	OwnerCollection string   `json:"ownerCollection"`
	OwnerID         string   `json:"ownerId"`
	Scopes          []string `json:"scopes"`             // empty: the owner's full rights
	Audience        string   `json:"audience,omitempty"` // the resource it's bound to (RFC 8707), or ""
	ClientID        string   `json:"clientId,omitempty"` // the OAuth client it was issued to, or ""

	Owner *core.Record `json:"-"` // the owner's record (inside the app)
}
```

Grant is what a verified token allows.

### FromRequest

```go
func FromRequest(e *core.RequestEvent) *Grant
```

FromRequest returns the API token a request was authenticated with, or nil (no auth, or a JWT).

### Grant.HasScope

```go
func (g *Grant) HasScope(scope string) bool
```

HasScope reports whether the token may act with scope: unscoped tokens have every scope. A bare name ("instances") is held by "instances" and by any "instances=\<value>"; "instances=abc" is held by "instances" or "instances=abc".

### Grant.HasScopeFor

```go
func (g *Grant) HasScopeFor(scope, value string) bool
```

HasScopeFor reports whether the token may act with scope on value: it holds the scope with no value (every value), or holds "scope=value". Unscoped tokens may.

### Grant.ScopeValues

```go
func (g *Grant) ScopeValues(scope string) (values []string, all bool)
```

ScopeValues lists the values the token holds scope for. all is true when it holds the scope for every value (an unscoped token, or the bare name); otherwise values may be empty (it doesn't hold the scope).

### Issuer

```go
type Issuer interface {
	// Verify resolves a token secret to who it acts as and what it may do.
	Verify(ctx context.Context, secret string) (Grant, error)
	// RegisterScope adds a scope a token can be limited to (an extension's own, e.g. deploy's).
	RegisterScope(s Scope) error
	// Scopes lists the registered scopes.
	Scopes() []Scope
	// Reaches reports whether a token limited to scopes may call method on path.
	Reaches(scopes []string, method, path string) bool
}
```

Issuer is an app's API tokens. Its provider also serves the token API (extkit.RouteBinder) and authenticates requests that carry a token (setting [RequestKey](#requestkey)).

### Scope

```go
type Scope struct {
	// Name, e.g. "deploy" or "notes:write": lower-case letters, digits, ":" and "_", starting with a letter or digit.
	Name string `json:"name"`
	// Description is shown on the consent page and in the token screens.
	Description string `json:"description"`
	// Paths are URL path prefixes where a token with this scope authenticates as its owner.
	Paths []string `json:"paths,omitempty"`
	// Methods, when not empty, limits Paths to these HTTP methods (GET also covers HEAD). Empty: every method.
	Methods []string `json:"methods,omitempty"`
	// Match is an optional guard: a token with this scope also authenticates on any request it returns true for.
	// It runs before the owner is loaded, so it may look only at the request, not at e.Auth.
	Match func(e *core.RequestEvent) bool `json:"-"`
	// Collections, when not empty, limits which auth collections may hold a token with this scope.
	Collections []string `json:"collections,omitempty"`
	// Values, when set, lets a token hold the scope for some values only ("instances=abc123"), e.g. record ids. The
	// bare name still means every value. Paths and Match don't see values: whoever serves the scope's requests
	// checks them ([Grant.HasScopeFor], [Grant.ScopeValues]).
	Values *ScopeValues `json:"values,omitempty"`
}
```

Scope is a named slice of an owner's rights that a token can be limited to. A token whose scopes are set authenticates only on requests its scopes match (Paths + Methods, or Match).

### Scope.Infrastructure

```go
func (s Scope) Infrastructure() bool
```

Infrastructure reports whether the scope only reaches PocketOne's own routes (contract APIs under /api/\_c/): a client that needs one asks for it; consent pages and MCP don't offer it otherwise.

### ScopeValues

```go
type ScopeValues struct {
	// Description says what a value is (e.g. "an instance id"); token screens show it.
	Description string `json:"description"`
	// Check, if set, vets a value when a token is created for owner (e.g. that owner owns that record); an error
	// refuses the token.
	Check func(owner *core.Record, value string) error `json:"-"`
}
```

ScopeValues describes what a scope's values are.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/api-tokens/verify/v1

# verifyv1

```go
import verifyv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/api-tokens/verify/v1"
```

Package verifyv1 is the api-tokens.verify/v1 contract: another server checks an app's API token. A host in front of its apps (a PocketHost edge in front of the mothership's accounts) is handed a token by a client and asks the app that issued it who the token acts as and what it may do. Whatever provides api-tokens/v1 provides it too.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/api-tokens.verify/v1, for superusers only: it answers for any token.

Source: [`ext/contracts/api-tokens/verify/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/api-tokens/verify/v1).

## Constants

<a id="invalid"></a><a id="expired"></a>

```go
const (
	Invalid = "invalid"
	Expired = "expired"
)
```

Reasons a token isn't valid.

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Verifier]("api-tokens.verify/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is api-tokens.verify/v1.

<a id="w"></a>

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "api_tokens_verify", func(inner Verifier, g *extkit.Guard[Verifier]) Verifier {
	return &guardVerifier{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[Verifier]{
		Name:   "verify",
		Desc:   "Checks an API token and says who it acts as and what it may do (its scopes, with their values). A token that isn't valid is an answer (Valid false), not an error, so callers can tell a refused token from an outage.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(Input{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Verifier, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in Input
			if err := extkit.DecodeInput(req.JSON, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Verify(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
)
```

W is api-tokens.verify/v1's wire side: routes at /api/\_c/api-tokens.verify/v1/\<op>, action hooks, MCP tools and the client.

## Functions

### OnVerify

```go
func OnVerify(owner any, fn func(e *extkit.CallEvent, in *Input) error)
```

OnVerify binds fn to verify calls on owner (an app, or a host's scope for calls the host answers). Call e.Next() to continue; return an error to refuse. in is the call's input; changes reach the provider.

## Types

### Client

```go
type Client struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Client is api-tokens.verify/v1 over HTTP, for the CLI and other apps. It implements Verifier; the token it was made with is the credential, so the extkit.Auth argument is ignored.

### NewClient

```go
func NewClient(baseURL, token string, hc *http.Client) *Client
```

NewClient calls api-tokens.verify/v1 on the app at baseURL with token (a PocketBase auth token or an API token).

### Client.Verify

```go
func (c *Client) Verify(ctx context.Context, _ extkit.Auth, in Input) (Result, error)
```

### Input

```go
type Input struct {
	Token string `json:"token"` // the secret the client sent ("pbt_...")
	// IP is the client's address, recorded as the token's last use; "" leaves the last use alone.
	IP string `json:"ip,omitempty"`
}
```

Input is the token to check.

### Result

```go
type Result struct {
	Valid bool `json:"valid"`
	// Reason says why a token isn't valid: "invalid" (unknown, malformed or revoked) or "expired".
	Reason string             `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	Grant  *apitokensv1.Grant `json:"grant,omitempty"`
}
```

Result is whether the token is valid and, when it is, what it grants.

### Verifier

```go
type Verifier interface {
	// Verify checks an API token and says who it acts as and what it may do (its scopes, with their values). A token
	// that isn't valid is an answer (Valid false), not an error, so callers can tell a refused token from an outage.
	//
	//op: POST /
	Verify(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Input) (Result, error)
}
```

Verifier checks an app's API tokens for another server.

# bulkmailv1

```go
import bulkmailv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/bulkmail/v1"
```

Package bulkmailv1 is the bulkmail/v1 contract: campaigns to many recipients, sent at a safe pace. Campaigns are records in the provider's collection (created and edited with PocketBase's records API); this contract runs them: count an audience, start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign. Unsubscribes and bounces are mail.suppression/v1 and mail.feedback/v1.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/bulkmail/v1.

Source: [`ext/contracts/bulkmail/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/bulkmail/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Campaigns]("bulkmail/v1", extkit.One).JS(extkit.JSHooks, nil).JSTypes(jsTypes)
```

Contract is bulkmail/v1.

<a id="w"></a>

var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "bulkmail", func(inner Campaigns, g *extkit.Guard[Campaigns]) Campaigns {

				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Count(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Campaigns]{
		Name:   "start",
		Desc:   "Queues a campaign's recipients and starts sending (Limit > 0: at most that many new recipients).",

		In:     reflect.TypeOf(StartInput{}),

			var in StartInput

				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Start(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Campaigns]{
		Name:   "pause",
		Desc:   "Stops sending a campaign; Resume carries on.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "pause",

		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Campaigns, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in Ref

				return nil, err

		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Campaigns]{
		Name:   "resume",
		Desc:   "Carries on sending a paused campaign.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "resume",

# clearv1

# cachev1

```go
import cachev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/cache/v1"
```

Package cachev1 is the cache/v1 contract: named buckets of bytes an app keeps for a while, so extensions and apps can remember what was expensive to compute. Who keeps them (memory and disk in this process, Redis, Memcached) is the provider's business; code that caches talks only to this contract.

A caller opens a bucket by name with the limits it wants (how many items, how much memory, how long, where to spill to disk) and then gets and sets keys in it:

	b, err := cachev1.Open(app, "pages.render", cachev1.Options{MaxItems: 1000, TTL: 10 * time.Minute})
	if v, ok, _ := b.Get(ctx, key); ok {
		return v
	}
	v := render()
	_ = b.Set(ctx, key, v, 0)

The promise is a cache's, not a store's: a provider may drop any entry at any time, even right after Set, and a Get may miss for any reason. It never returns a value that was deleted, cleared or replaced since, nor one past its TTL.

Source: [`ext/contracts/cache/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/cache/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Cache]("cache/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is cache/v1: one provider per app.

## Functions

### Clear

```go
func Clear(ctx context.Context, app core.App) error
```

Clear empties every bucket app has, through whoever provides cache/v1; with no provider there's nothing to empty.

### Load

```go
func Load(ctx context.Context, b Bucket, key string, fn func(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)) ([]byte, error)
```

Load returns key's value from b, or on a miss computes it with fn and stores it. Callers asking for the same key of the same bucket while fn runs share that one call (a cold key under load computes once, not once per request):

  - every caller is released only after the value is stored, so none of them misses again right after;
  - fn's error goes to the callers waiting then and is never stored: the next caller tries again;
  - each caller waits on its own ctx: one that gives up returns ctx's error and leaves fn running for the others.

fn runs with ctx's values but not its cancellation (the first caller leaving mustn't fail the rest), so it bounds its own time. A failed store still returns the value. A bucket whose type can't be a map key isn't coalesced.

### ValidName

```go
func ValidName(name string) error
```

ValidName checks a bucket name: 1 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9, '.', '\_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. Prefix it with your extension's name ("pages.render") so two extensions don't share a bucket by accident.

## Types

### Bucket

```go
type Bucket interface {
	// Get returns key's value and true, or false on a miss. The returned slice is the caller's to keep or change.
	Get(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]byte, bool, error)
	// Set stores value under key, replacing what was there. ttl 0 uses the bucket's TTL; a negative ttl deletes key.
	// The bucket keeps its own copy of value.
	Set(ctx context.Context, key string, value []byte, ttl time.Duration) error
	// Delete removes key. Deleting a missing key is not an error.
	Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
	// Clear removes every key of the bucket.
	Clear(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

Bucket is one named cache: keys to byte values.

### Open

```go
func Open(app core.App, name string, opts Options) (Bucket, error)
```

Open returns app's bucket name from whoever provides cache/v1, or a bucket that keeps nothing when nothing does, so code that only works better with a cache declares cache/v1 in WorksWith and needs no other branch. Call it after registration (in hooks, at serve time), and keep the bucket.

### Cache

```go
type Cache interface {
	// Bucket returns the bucket name, creating it with opts on first use. Later calls with the same name return the
	// same bucket and ignore their opts. name must pass [ValidName]. A provider may override opts with an
	// operator's settings for that bucket, and treats each field as a hint it keeps as well as its storage allows.
	Bucket(name string, opts Options) (Bucket, error)
	// Clear empties every bucket the app has, opened since it started or not.
	Clear(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

Cache gives an app its buckets. Each app has its own: a bucket named "x" on one app never sees another app's "x", on a multisite host too, even when the provider keeps every app's entries in one shared store.

### Decoder

```go
type Decoder struct {
	Version string
	Decode  func([]byte) (Item, error)
}
```

Decoder turns bytes back into an item: a [Marshaler](#marshaler)'s bytes of the same Version, or bytes Set as a value (whose version is "").

### Eviction

```go
type Eviction string
```

Eviction is which entry a full bucket drops to make room.

<a id="lru"></a><a id="mru"></a><a id="fifo"></a><a id="lifo"></a>

```go
const (
	// LRU drops the least recently used entry (read or written). The default.
	LRU Eviction = "lru"
	// MRU drops the most recently used entry: for scans that won't come back to what they just read.
	MRU Eviction = "mru"
	// FIFO drops the oldest written entry; reads don't count.
	FIFO Eviction = "fifo"
	// LIFO drops the newest written entry; reads don't count. (Also called FILO.)
	LIFO Eviction = "lifo"
)
```

### Eviction.Valid

```go
func (e Eviction) Valid() bool
```

Valid reports whether e is one of the strategies above, or "" for the provider's default.

### Item

```go
type Item interface {
	// CacheSize is roughly how many bytes the item holds in memory, counted against the bucket's memory limits in
	// place of a byte value's length.
	CacheSize() int64
}
```

Item is a Go value a bucket keeps as it is: a parsed template, a compiled program, a decoded struct. Each key holds its own: a bucket never hands one key's item to another key, another bucket or another app, so the code that owns the bucket owns its items, and every Get of a key returns that key's item (not a copy).

An item that is only an Item lives in memory alone: it never goes to disk or to another server, and when memory is full it is simply dropped. To let it leave memory, make it a [Marshaler](#marshaler).

### ItemBucket

```go
type ItemBucket interface {
	Bucket
	// GetItem returns key's item and true, or false on a miss. decode turns bytes into an item when the key doesn't
	// hold one in memory (it was Set as bytes, or its item was moved to disk or kept across a restart).
	GetItem(ctx context.Context, key string, decode Decoder) (Item, bool, error)
	// SetItem stores item under key, replacing what was there; the bucket keeps item itself, not a copy. ttl is as in
	// [Bucket.Set].
	SetItem(ctx context.Context, key string, item Item, ttl time.Duration) error
}
```

ItemBucket is the optional interface of a [Bucket](#bucket) that keeps [Item](#item) values without marshaling them. Byte values and items share the bucket's keys: Get on a key holding a Marshaler returns its bytes (and misses on an item that can't marshal), and GetItem on a key holding bytes of the decoder's version returns them decoded, as that key's item from then on. Bytes of another version are a miss. An item held in memory is returned as it is, whatever the decoder's version.

### Items

```go
type Items[T Item] struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Items is a bucket of T values: typed Get and Set over any [Bucket](#bucket). On an [ItemBucket](#itembucket) the values stay Go values; on a bucket of bytes each Set marshals (keeping nothing for a T that isn't a [Marshaler](#marshaler)) and each Get decodes, with the version written in front of the bytes.

### NewItems

```go
func NewItems[T Item](b Bucket, version string, decode func([]byte) (T, error)) *Items[T]
```

NewItems returns typed access to b's values.

### OpenItems

```go
func OpenItems[T Item](app core.App, name string, opts Options, version string, decode func([]byte) (T, error)) (*Items[T], error)
```

OpenItems opens bucket name as [Open](#open) does, for T values that decode turns back from bytes of version (T's CacheVersion; "" for a T that isn't a [Marshaler](#marshaler)).

### Items.Bucket

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Bucket() Bucket
```

Bucket returns the bucket underneath.

### Items.Clear

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Clear(ctx context.Context) error
```

Clear removes every key of the bucket, items and byte values alike.

### Items.Decoder

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Decoder() Decoder
```

Decoder is the items' [Decoder](#decoder).

### Items.Delete

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Delete removes key.

### Items.Get

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (T, bool, error)
```

Get returns key's value and true, or false on a miss. A key holding an item of another type is a miss.

### Items.Load

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Load(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func(ctx context.Context) (T, error)) (T, error)
```

Load is [Load](#load) for a bucket of T values: a miss computes the value with fn once for every caller waiting on the same key, stores it, then releases them all.

### Items.Set

```go
func (it *Items[T]) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, v T, ttl time.Duration) error
```

Set stores v under key; ttl is as in [Bucket.Set](#bucket).

### Marshaler

```go
type Marshaler interface {
	Item
	MarshalCache() ([]byte, error)
	// CacheVersion names MarshalCache's format. Change it whenever the format changes: a provider keeps it beside the
	// bytes (bucket, key, version -> content), and a Decoder of another version never sees them.
	CacheVersion() string
}
```

Marshaler is an [Item](#item) that can leave memory. MarshalCache promises that its bytes, given to a [Decoder](#decoder) of the same CacheVersion, come back as an item equivalent in every way. Only then may a provider move it to disk, keep it across restarts or send it to another server; a provider may also keep identical bytes from many keys once, there.

A provider marshals when it moves the item, which may be later than Set and on another goroutine. Changing an item after Set changes what its key holds in memory, and may or may not reach a copy already marshaled: Set it again to be sure.

### None

```go
type None struct{}
```

None is a bucket that keeps nothing: every Get misses.

### None.Clear

```go
func (None) Clear(context.Context) error
```

Clear implements [Bucket](#bucket).

### None.Delete

```go
func (None) Delete(context.Context, string) error
```

Delete implements [Bucket](#bucket).

### None.Get

```go
func (None) Get(context.Context, string) ([]byte, bool, error)
```

Get implements [Bucket](#bucket): always a miss.

### None.Set

```go
func (None) Set(context.Context, string, []byte, time.Duration) error
```

Set implements [Bucket](#bucket): keeps nothing.

### Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// Eviction is which of the bucket's entries goes first when the bucket is full; "" is LRU.
	Eviction Eviction
	// MaxItems caps the bucket's entries; 0 is no cap of its own.
	MaxItems int
	// MaxMemory caps the bytes of the bucket's keys and of the values it holds in memory; 0 is no cap of its own.
	MaxMemory int64
	// TTL is how long an entry lives when Set gives no ttl; 0 is until it's evicted.
	TTL time.Duration
}
```

Options are a bucket's limits: caps on what this app's bucket may hold, inside whatever room the provider has in all. A zero field leaves the choice to the provider (and to the operator's settings). Where entries live (memory, disk, another server) and how much room there is in all are the provider's business, not the bucket's.
