Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/cli/commands/v1

# clicmdv1

```go
import clicmdv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/cli/commands/v1"
```

Package clicmdv1 is the cli.commands/v1 contract: the \`pocketone\` command tree. Each command path ("remote restore to") has at most one provider. Every operation of every wire contract linked into the binary is a command by default, under \`remote\` ([Generated](#generated)); an extension replaces one by providing the same path, or adds its own:

	clicmdv1.Contract.Provide(app, clicmdv1.Command{Path: "remote rehash", Short: "...", Run: ...})

[Mount](#mount) builds the tree once the app's contracts are sealed. Two extensions providing one path are a startup error until pocketone.yaml picks one (\`providers: {cli.commands/v1: {"remote rehash": rehasher}}\`).

Source: [`ext/contracts/cli/commands/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/cli/commands/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewKeyedContract[Command]("cli.commands/v1", func(c Command) string { return c.Path })
```

Contract is cli.commands/v1, keyed by command path.

## Functions

### Mount

```go
func Mount(app core.App, root *cobra.Command)
```

Mount adds app's commands to root: every provided cli.commands/v1 command (replacing a command already at its path), then the generated ones nothing provides and root doesn't already have. Call it once app's contracts are sealed (after the standard set's Register, or extkit.Setup).

### PathOf

```go
func PathOf(id extkit.ContractID, op string) string
```

PathOf is the command path of a contract operation: \`remote\`, the contract id's words (without a leading "remote"), then the operation, with the last id word dropped from its front: restore/v1's restore\_to is "remote restore to", remote/v1's status is "remote status", mail.suppression/v1's check is "remote mail suppression check".

## Types

### Command

```go
type Command struct {
	Path  string // the words after the binary's name: "remote restore to"
	Use   string // its arguments as help shows them ("<name> <url>"); "" for none
	Short string
	Long  string
	Args  cobra.PositionalArgs // nil: any
	Flags func(fs *pflag.FlagSet)
	Run   func(c *Ctx, args []string) error
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Command is one \`pocketone\` command.

### Generated

```go
func Generated() []Command
```

Generated is a command for every operation people call of every wire contract linked into the binary: flags from its input's fields (and --json for the whole input), the answer printed as JSON. Public operations that take or return a raw body (an unsubscribe page, a mail provider's webhook) are for browsers and services, not people, and get none.

### CommandRef

```go
type CommandRef struct {
	Path     string    `json:"path"` // the words after the binary's name: "remote restore to"
	Use      string    `json:"use"`  // the arguments as help shows them
	Short    string    `json:"short,omitempty"`
	Long     string    `json:"long,omitempty"`
	Aliases  []string  `json:"aliases,omitempty"`
	Flags    []FlagRef `json:"flags,omitempty"`
	Runnable bool      `json:"runnable"` // false: a group of subcommands
	// Source says who answers it: "pocketbase" (PocketBase's own commands), "ext/<name>" (an extension),
	// "contract:<id>" (generated from a contract's operation), "contracts/<id>" (a contract package's shared client),
	// "main" (the binary itself); "" when it can't be told (a group).
	Source string `json:"source,omitempty"`
}
```

CommandRef is one command, every subcommand listed by its full path.

### ContractRef

```go
type ContractRef struct {
	ID       string  `json:"id"`
	Prefix   string  `json:"prefix"` // /api/_c/<id>
	Routed   bool    `json:"routed"` // its own API shape: no generated operations
	Provider string  `json:"provider,omitempty"`
	Provided bool    `json:"provided"`
	Ops      []OpRef `json:"ops,omitempty"`
}
```

ContractRef is a contract with an HTTP API.

### Ctx

```go
type Ctx struct {
	context.Context
	Cmd *cobra.Command
	Out io.Writer
}
```

Ctx is a running command.

### Ctx.Caller

```go
func (c *Ctx) Caller(id extkit.ContractID) (*extkit.Caller, error)
```

Caller calls contract id on the command's remote.

### Ctx.Flags

```go
func (c *Ctx) Flags() *pflag.FlagSet
```

Flags are the command's flags.

### Ctx.Remote

```go
func (c *Ctx) Remote() (*remoteclient.Client, error)
```

Remote opens the remote the command talks to: --remote (a name or URL), else the project's default remote, with its saved login (or the CI token). With no login it still returns the client, unauthenticated, so public operations work and the rest fail with the remote's own "sign in first".

### FieldRef

```go
type FieldRef struct {
	Name string `json:"name"` // in the JSON body / MCP arguments
	Flag string `json:"flag"` // the command's flag, without "--"
	Type string `json:"type"` // string, bool, int, float, time, strings, json
}
```

FieldRef is one field of an operation's input.

### FlagRef

```go
type FlagRef struct {
	Name      string `json:"name"`
	Shorthand string `json:"shorthand,omitempty"`
	Type      string `json:"type"`
	Default   string `json:"default,omitempty"`
	Usage     string `json:"usage,omitempty"`
}
```

FlagRef is one flag.

### JSRef

```go
type JSRef struct {
	Extension string `json:"extension"`
	Types     string `json:"types"`
}
```

JSRef is what one extension adds to an app's JS API (pb\_hooks and page code): its TypeScript declarations, as they go into the app's types.d.ts. Extension "contracts" is extkit's: the contracts' action hooks and types open to JS.

### OpRef

```go
type OpRef struct {
	Name     string     `json:"name"`
	Desc     string     `json:"desc,omitempty"`
	Method   string     `json:"method"`
	REST     string     `json:"rest"` // METHOD's path: /api/_c/<id>/<path>
	Scope    string     `json:"scope"`
	Out      string     `json:"out"` // json, stream or raw
	RawIn    bool       `json:"rawIn,omitempty"`
	Command  string     `json:"command,omitempty"` // the pocketone command; "" for raw public operations
	Tool     string     `json:"tool,omitempty"`    // the MCP tool; "" for uploads and downloads
	ReadOnly bool       `json:"readOnly"`
	Input    []FieldRef `json:"input,omitempty"`
}
```

OpRef is one operation and the ways to call it.

### Reference

```go
type Reference struct {
	Global    []FlagRef     `json:"global"` // the root's persistent flags, which every command takes
	Commands  []CommandRef  `json:"commands"`
	Contracts []ContractRef `json:"contracts"`
	JS        []JSRef       `json:"js,omitempty"`
}
```

Reference is the binary's command tree and the HTTP APIs and MCP tools of every contract linked into it, as \`pocketone reference --json\` prints it. pocketone.dev's CLI, REST and MCP references and each contract's and extension's "Commands and APIs" section are generated from it (site/sync).

### BuildReference

```go

```

BuildReference describes root's command tree and the contract APIs linked into the binary, with their providers on app.

# deployv1

```go
import deployv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/deploy/v1"
```

Package deployv1 is the deploy/v1 contract: a project's code files on an app (check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree). Restart and logs are remote/v1's, which it requires.

A routed contract: its provider is an http.Handler serving the file API under /api/\_c/deploy/v1/ (ext/deploy on a standalone app; a multisite host provides it for its instances, because Docker runs stock PocketBase images with nothing of ours inside). The API's operations:

	POST   /api/_c/deploy/v1/check       which files the remote lacks (JSON)
	POST   /api/_c/deploy/v1/blobs       upload them (gzip bytes)
	POST   /api/_c/deploy/v1/commit      swap the new code set in (JSON)
	GET    /api/_c/deploy/v1/files       list deployed files
	DELETE /api/_c/deploy/v1/files       delete files
	GET    /api/_c/deploy/v1/files/raw   read one file (raw bytes)
	PUT    /api/_c/deploy/v1/files/raw   write one file (raw bytes)
	GET    /api/_c/deploy/v1/tree        the remote's code tree, for two-way sync

Token scopes: deploy (everything) and deploy:read (list, read, tree).

Source: [`ext/contracts/deploy/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/deploy/v1).


Contract is deploy/v1.


Prefix is where deploy/v1 is served: /api/\_c/deploy/v1.

# gatev1

```go
import gatev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/gate/v1"
```

Package gatev1 is the gate/v1 contract: what admits requests on a multisite host, before an instance is served or forwarded (a firewall: peer allow lists, client IPs, rate limits). Gates run in order, every one must admit.

A host-scope service contract: providers register on the host's scope (ProvideIn), not on an app.

Source: [`ext/contracts/gate/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/gate/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Gate]("gate/v1", extkit.Many)
```

Contract is gate/v1, on a host's scope.

## Types

### ClientIPResolver

```go
type ClientIPResolver interface {
	ClientIP(r *http.Request) netip.Addr
}
```

ClientIPResolver is an optional [Gate](#gate) extension: the request's real client (e.g. from CF-Connecting-IP when the peer is a trusted proxy). When a gate implements it, a request served here reaches the app with RemoteAddr set to that client, so PocketBase's logs, e.RealIP() and its own rate limits see the visitor instead of the proxy.

### Gate

```go
type Gate interface {
	AllowPeer(r *http.Request) bool
	Admit(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, inst sourcev1.Instance) (release func(), ok bool)
}
```

Gate admits requests. AllowPeer runs before routing and refuses with 403; Admit runs before an instance's request is served here or forwarded to another server, may answer it itself (ok=false), and otherwise returns a release function called when the response ends (long-lived responses hold it until they end).

# fsv1

```go
import fsv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/instance/fs/v1"
```

Package fsv1 is the instance.fs/v1 contract: one instance's code files on local disk, for extensions that read and write them (ext/deploy today). It answers which folder, where an extension may keep files it can rebuild about the instance (its cache), one writers' lock, and whether the instance runs (and how to restart it around a change).

There is no request lookup and no auth in it: callers say which instance by id. On a single app the app provides it and is its only instance ([Self](#self)); a multisite host provides it on its own scope (ProvideIn) for each of its instances, and its handlers pass the id the request routed to. Who may call is the caller's business (PocketBase's auth on a single app, the host's auth function on a host).

The package also holds the code-path rules: what belongs to an instance's code ([IsCodePath](#iscodepath)), what a file API may reach ([IsReachable](#isreachable)) and how a client path maps to a file without escaping the folder ([Resolve](#resolve)). pb\_data and pb\_cache are never reachable through this contract.

Source: [`ext/contracts/instance/fs/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/instance/fs/v1).

## Constants

<a id="datadir"></a><a id="cachefolder"></a><a id="nodemodulesdir"></a><a id="patchesdir"></a><a id="maxpathlength"></a>

```go
const (
	DataDir        = "pb_data"
	CacheFolder    = "pb_cache" // extensions' disposable files ([FS.CacheDir]; extkit's pb_cache convention)
	NodeModulesDir = "node_modules"
	PatchesDir     = "patches"
	MaxPathLength  = 1024
)
```

<a id="self"></a>

```go
const Self = ""
```

Self is the instance id of a single app: the app itself.

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go

```

Contract is instance.fs/v1.


ErrUnreachable is the reason for a path outside what [IsReachable](#isreachable) allows.

## Functions

### IsCodePath

```go
func IsCodePath(p string) bool
```

IsCodePath reports whether p (relative to the instance folder) belongs to the code: what a deploy may write or delete. node\_modules counts only at the top.

### IsCodeRoot

```go
func IsCodeRoot(name string) bool
```

IsCodeRoot: a top-level name the code lives under (or is).

### IsGitSegment

```go
func IsGitSegment(seg string) bool
```

IsGitSegment: .git, .gitignore, ... never belong to the code.

### IsReachable

```go
func IsReachable(p string) bool
```

IsReachable reports whether a file API may read or write p: the code, node\_modules at the top or inside a code folder, and patches/. Never pb\_data, pb\_cache or .git\*.

### IsSafeRelativePath

```go
func IsSafeRelativePath(p string) bool
```

IsSafeRelativePath: a relative POSIX path with no empty, "." or ".." segments, no backslash or NUL.

### Resolve

```go
func Resolve(dir, raw string) (rel, fsPath string, err error)
```

Resolve maps a client path (slash-separated, relative to dir; "" is dir itself) to a file path inside dir. It refuses paths [IsReachable](#isreachable) doesn't allow, paths that cross a symbolic link, and anything that would land outside dir. rel is the cleaned path.

## Types

### FS

```go
type FS interface {
	// Dir is the instance folder on local disk (it holds pb_hooks, pb_public, ... and pb_data, which this contract
	// never reaches). An error when there's no folder yet (a single app before it bootstraps).
	Dir(ctx context.Context) (string, error)

	// CacheDir is a folder for files an extension can rebuild about the instance (name: the extension's, e.g.
	// "deploy"), made if missing, following PocketOne's pb_cache convention: pb_cache/<name> in Dir on a single app; a
	// host keeps it outside Dir (Pocker and Docker: the host's pb_cache/instances/<id>/<name>). Anything in it may be
	// deleted at any time (a cache clear, an admin, a cleanup) and the extension carries on. It is never code and never
	// reachable ([IsCodePath], [IsReachable]), and it is on the same filesystem as Dir, so renames between them are
	// atomic.
	CacheDir(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error)

	// Lock takes the instance's writers' lock: every write to the code files (a deploy's commit, a file API write)
	// holds it, so they never interleave. Call unlock when done.
	Lock(ctx context.Context) (func(), error)

	// Running reports whether the instance is running now.
	Running(ctx context.Context) (bool, error)

	// Restart applies a change that mustn't happen under a running app: it stops the instance if it runs, calls apply
	// (if not nil) while it's stopped, and has it run again, whether apply failed or not. An instance that isn't running
	// gets apply only and stays as it was. An instance that can't stop itself (a single app) calls apply as it is and
	// then restarts. err is apply's; startErr says the instance didn't come back.
	Restart(ctx context.Context, apply func(context.Context) error) (startErr, err error)
}
```

FS is one instance's code files.

### Files

```go
type Files interface {
	// Instance returns the instance's files ([Self] on a single app). ErrNoInstance when the provider has no such
	// instance.
	Instance(ctx context.Context, id string) (FS, error)
}
```

Files gives each instance's code files.

### Instances

```go
	New func(id string) *Local
```

Instances is a [Files](#files) for a host's instances, for runtimes to provide: it builds each instance's [Local](#local) once and keeps it, so every caller shares its lock.

### Local

```go
type Local struct {
	// Folder returns the instance folder ("" while there is none yet). Required.
	Folder func() string
	// Cache returns an extension's cache folder. Default: <instance folder>/pb_cache/<name>.
	Cache func(name string) string
	// IsRunning reports whether the instance runs. Default: always.
	IsRunning func() bool
	// Stopped calls fn with the instance stopped; the instance runs again after (now or on its next request).
	// Default: fn as it is (an app can't stop itself).
	Stopped func(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context) error) error
	// Start has the instance run again after Stopped, when that doesn't (a single app: its restart). Optional.
	Start func(ctx context.Context) error
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Local is an [FS](#fs) over a folder on local disk, for providers to build on. Zero values are fine except where noted.

# resolvev1

```go
import resolvev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/instance/resolve/v1"
```

Package resolvev1 is the instance.resolve/v1 contract: on a control plane (a mothership), what a hostname serves for a given edge, built from the control plane's own records, and which records each answer was built from. The mothership's watch server (instance.watch/v1) asks it on every watch and asks again after a write to any record an answer depends on, so it only needs to be right, never to track changes itself.

The default provider is ext/mothership's own schema (\`edges\`, \`instances\`). A control plane with its own collections provides its own; one that only adds to the default's answers wraps it (Contract.Wrap).

Source: [`ext/contracts/instance/resolve/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/instance/resolve/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>


Contract is instance.resolve/v1.

## Functions

### Collection

```go
func Collection(collection string) string
```

Collection is the dep on a whole collection: a write to any of its records re-resolves (for lists and queries).

### Host

Host is the dep on a hostname's claims: a write to a record that claims or claimed it re-resolves.


Key is a dep of the resolver's own naming (such as "edge:lax-1" for "which record is edge lax-1"), touched when its Touches says so.

Record is the dep on one record: a write to it re-resolves.

```go

```

RecordDeps are the deps a write to rec touches: its own record, its collection, and touched (from Touches).

## Types

### EdgeList

```go

	Edges []watchv1.Edge `json:"edges"`

}
```

EdgeList is every edge and what the list was built from.

### Query

```go
type Query struct {
	Edge string `json:"edge"`

}
```

### Resolution

```go
type Resolution struct {
	Instance *sourcev1.Instance `json:"instance,omitempty"` // nil: no such host
	Deps     []string           `json:"deps"`
}
```

Resolution is an answer and what it was built from.

### Resolver

```go
type Resolver interface {
	// Resolve answers what Host serves for Edge (an edge id). Not found is an answer (Instance nil), with deps too
	// (at least Host(host)), so the record that later claims the name re-resolves it.
	Resolve(ctx context.Context, in Query) (Resolution, error)

	// Standing lists the instances an edge must hold whatever its traffic (work addressed to it: a copy to make,
	// scheduled calls to send), with their deps. Nil is fine: most edges hold only what they serve.
	Standing(ctx context.Context, edge string) (Standing, error)

	// Edges lists every edge, with their deps.
	Edges(ctx context.Context) (EdgeList, error)

	// Touches lists the deps a write of rec touches besides its own record and collection: Host(name) for each
	// hostname it claims or claimed (compare rec.Original(): a new record's is blank, a deleted one's is rec), so
	// the watches on a name it adds, changes or drops resolve again; and Key(...) deps of the resolver's own. Report
	// only what the write changed: a record written often (an edge's heartbeat) mustn't re-resolve every answer
	// that merely looked it up.
	Touches(ctx context.Context, rec *core.Record) ([]string, error)
}
```

Resolver builds answers from a control plane's records. Every answer lists its Deps: the records it read (see [Record](#record), [Collection](#collection)), the hostnames whose claims decided it ([Host](#host)) and any keys of its own ([Key](#key)). After a write, the server re-asks every answer whose deps the written record touches: its own record and collection, and whatever [Resolver.Touches](#resolver) reports.

### Standing

```go
type Standing struct {
	Instances []sourcev1.Instance `json:"instances,omitempty"`
	Deps      []string            `json:"deps"`
}
```

Standing is an edge's standing set and what it was built from.

### Instance

```go
type Instance struct {
	// ID is a stable, unique identifier. It is also the default folder name under the data root.
	ID string `yaml:"id"`

	// Version is the PocketBase version the instance runs (e.g. "0.41.1" or "0.36.*"), for runtimes that run
	// releases (docker); the host's runtime refuses one it can't serve (runtime/v1's Serves). Empty = the runtime's
	// default.
	Version string `yaml:"version,omitempty"`

	// Hosts are the hostnames (no port) that route to this instance, e.g. "blog.example.com".
	Hosts []string `yaml:"hosts"`

	// Dir overrides the instance folder (default: <data root>/<ID>). The folder holds pb_data, pb_hooks,
	// pb_migrations and pb_public, like a stand-alone PocketBase.
	Dir string `yaml:"dir,omitempty"`

	// Dev runs the app in dev mode (verbose logs, SQL logging).
	Dev bool `yaml:"dev,omitempty"`

	// Secrets are the instance's environment: visible to its JS hooks through $os.getenv and process.env, and to
	// nothing else. No names are reserved; platform settings are explicit fields below.
	Secrets map[string]string `yaml:"secrets,omitempty"`

	// EncryptionKey encrypts the app's stored settings (like `pocketbase serve --encryptionEnv`). Not visible to JS.
	EncryptionKey string `yaml:"encryption_key,omitempty"`

	// Access is the instance owner's network settings (see [Access]).
	Access Access `yaml:"access,omitempty"`

	// Superusers are upserted into the app's _superusers when it starts (in Go, never through env), e.g. so a
	// hosting platform's login works in the dashboard. PasswordHash is the bcrypt hash PocketBase stores.
	Superusers []Superuser `yaml:"superusers,omitempty"`

	// Private holds values for the host application's Go code (see pocker.Server.SetupApp), e.g. a backup token.
	// It is never visible to the instance's JS.
	Private map[string]string `yaml:"private,omitempty"`

	// Limits override the process defaults for this instance (zero fields keep the default).
	Limits Limits `yaml:"limits,omitempty"`

	// Extensions holds per-instance settings for extensions, by extension name (e.g. `extensions: {firewall: {rate_limits:
	// ...}}`). A host application's instance source may set typed values; see multisite.DecodeExtensionConfig. Extensions read
	// them once, when registered, so pocker restarts the instance's app on its next request when they change.
	Extensions map[string]any `yaml:"extensions,omitempty"`

	// Blocked, when set, answers every request for this instance with the given status and message instead of
	// serving it (e.g. suspended, unpaid). A running app is left running.
	Blocked *Blocked `yaml:"blocked,omitempty"`

	// Remote, when set, means another server runs this instance (e.g. "http://10.0.0.2:8080"). The multisite host
	// applies its gates (firewall: peer check, rate limits) and then forwards the request there instead of starting the
	// app here (see ext/multisite's Host.Forward). An app already running here is stopped.
	Remote string `yaml:"remote,omitempty"`
}
```

Instance describes one PocketBase app an edge serves.

### Instance.ExtensionConfig

```go
func (i Instance) ExtensionConfig(name string) any
```

ExtensionConfig returns an instance's settings for the named extension (its \`extensions.\<name>\` value), or nil.

### Limits

```go
type Limits struct {
	MaxJSExecution     time.Duration `yaml:"max_js_execution,omitempty" doc:"Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run."`
	MaxJSAllocation    ByteSize      `yaml:"max_js_allocation,omitempty" doc:"Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB."`
	MaxCallStackSize   int           `yaml:"max_call_stack_size,omitempty" doc:"Deepest JS recursion allowed."`
	MaxSleep           time.Duration `yaml:"max_sleep,omitempty" doc:"Longest a JS sleep() call may wait."`
	MaxQueryDuration   time.Duration `yaml:"max_query_duration,omitempty" doc:"Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run."`
	HTTPSendMaxTimeout time.Duration `yaml:"http_send_max_timeout,omitempty" doc:"Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use."`
	HTTPSendMaxBody    ByteSize      `yaml:"http_send_max_body,omitempty" doc:"Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB."`

	// MaxConcurrentJS caps how many JS calls (hooks, routes, cron jobs) the instance runs at once; further calls
	// wait up to max_js_execution for a slot, then fail.
	MaxConcurrentJS int `yaml:"max_concurrent_js,omitempty" doc:"JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail."`
}
```

Limits are per-instance resource limits. Zero fields fall back to the process defaults (\[Config]); an instance source sets them per instance (e.g. by plan).

	limits:
	  max_js_execution: 60s
	  max_js_allocation: 128MiB
	  max_query_duration: 60s
	  http_send_max_timeout: 30s
	  http_send_max_body: 20MiB


over returns l with zero fields taken from def.

# statusv1

```go
import statusv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/instance/status/v1"
```

Package statusv1 is the instance.status/v1 contract: what a multisite host knows about each instance it runs (starting, running, idle, failed), as it changes. The host's supervisor decides it: an instance is running once its health endpoint answers, and idle or failed when its runtime reports that it ended (runtime/v1's ExitNotifier).

A host-scope service contract; ext/multisite provides it by default.

Source: [`ext/contracts/instance/status/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/instance/status/v1).

## Types

```go

```

State is where an instance is in its run.

<a id="starting"></a><a id="running"></a><a id="idle"></a><a id="failed"></a>

```go
const (
	Starting State = "starting" // launched; its health endpoint hasn't answered yet
	Running  State = "running"  // its health endpoint answered
	Idle     State = "idle"     // not running (stopped by the runtime, or never started)
	Failed   State = "failed"   // it didn't come up, or it ended on its own (Reason has why)
)
```

```go
	InstanceID string
	State      State
	Reason     string // why it failed; empty otherwise
	At         time.Time

```

### Statuses

```go
type Statuses interface {
	// Subscribe calls fn for every change from now on, in order per instance, from the host's own goroutine (fn must
	// not block for long). The returned func stops the calls.
	Subscribe(fn func(Status)) (cancel func())
	// Current lists every instance that isn't idle (starting, running, failed), e.g. to resend the full picture after
	// a control plane reconnects.
	Current() []Status
}
```

Statuses reports instance states as they change.

# tokensv1

```go
import tokensv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/instance/tokens/v1"
```

Package tokensv1 is the instance.tokens/v1 contract: a multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued, so it can accept the instance's own tokens on the routes it answers for that instance (deploy/v1, remote/v1). \`pocketone login\` and \`clone\` sign in to the instance (its oauth/v1), so this is how a host lets them in the same way on every host.

A service contract a runtime provides on the host scope (ProvideIn), for the instances it runs: Pocker checks the token with the instance's own api-tokens/v1. A runtime whose instances it can't reach inside (Docker's stock images) doesn't provide it, and the host accepts only its own credentials there.

Source: [`ext/contracts/instance/tokens/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/instance/tokens/v1).

# watchv1

```go
import watchv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/instance/watch/v1"
```

Package watchv1 is the instance.watch/v1 contract: an edge follows a control plane (a mothership) lazily. It opens one stream, asks for a hostname the first time a request names it, and from then on hears about every change to what that hostname serves, until it says it no longer cares. Nothing is sent that no edge asked for, except the list of edges and the instances an edge must hold whatever its traffic (its standing set).

A wire contract at /api/\_c/instance.watch/v1. The mothership provides it (ext/mothership); edges call it (ext/mothership/client).

The order of things is the promise:

  - The stream's first event is a hello: the connection id, this edge's record, every edge and the standing set.
  - Watch registers the hostname on the connection before it reads anything, then sends the answer as an event on the stream (never in the reply), so the answer and every later change arrive in the order they happened.
  - A Watch naming no live connection (the edge's stream is down) gets the answer in its reply, with nothing registered: the caller may use it once, but nobody will tell it when it changes.
  - A change is sent only when the answer differs from the one sent last for that hostname on that connection.
  - A dropped stream forgets every watch. On reconnect the edge starts over: what it cached is no longer watched.

Source: [`ext/contracts/instance/watch/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/instance/watch/v1).

## Constants

<a id="kindhello"></a><a id="kindhost"></a><a id="kindedges"></a><a id="kindstanding"></a><a id="kindping"></a>

```go
const (
	KindHello    = "hello"    // the first event: Conn, Self, Edges, Standing
	KindHost     = "host"     // Host's answer (the first after a Watch, or a change)
	KindEdges    = "edges"    // the edges list changed: Edges
	KindStanding = "standing" // this edge's standing set changed: Standing (all of it)
	KindPing     = "ping"     // nothing happened: sent when the stream was idle for PingEvery, so a dead one shows
)
```

Event kinds, in Event.Kind.

<a id="pingevery"></a>

```go
const PingEvery = 25 * time.Second
```

PingEvery is how often an idle stream gets a ping; an edge that hears nothing for a few of them reconnects.

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "fleet", func(inner Watcher, g *extkit.Guard[Watcher]) Watcher {

		Method: "GET",

				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Stream(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Watcher]{

		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,

		},
	},
)
```

# kvv1

```go
import kvv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/kv/v1"
```

Package kvv1 is the kv/v1 contract: an app's key-value store. Named JSON values (an app's settings, an extension's state) kept without a collection or a migration, in PocketBase's own \_params table, so they ride along in backups.

Two halves:

  - The helpers in this package ([Get](#get), [Set](#set), [Delete](#delete), [List](#list)) are how Go code (an extension, a hook) reads and writes the store. They work on the app's database directly, inside a transaction when given one, and need no provider.
  - The wire API at /api/\_c/kv/v1 (superusers only) is how the CLI, MCP and a dashboard read and change values. Its provider (ext/kv) serves it over the same helpers, and gives page code $kv.

Each value is one \_params row whose id is [Prefix](#prefix) + its name ("kv:storytime/settings"), so a name can never meet PocketBase's own params ("settings") or another extension's rows. Names are 1 to [MaxNameLength](#maxnamelength) characters: letters, digits and \_ - . : / , starting with a letter or digit. Use a prefix of your own ("myext/...") to keep your names apart from others'. A name starting with \_ ("\_myext/secret") is private: only Go code reaches it, through the helpers; the wire API and $kv never do.

Source: [`ext/contracts/kv/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/kv/v1).

## Constants

<a id="maxnamelength"></a>

```go
const MaxNameLength = 128
```

MaxNameLength is the longest name.

<a id="maxvaluebytes"></a>

```go
const MaxValueBytes = 1 << 20
```

MaxValueBytes is the largest value, as JSON.

<a id="prefix"></a>

```go
const Prefix = "kv:"
```

Prefix starts the \_params id of every value in the store: name "storytime/settings" is row "kv:storytime/settings".

<a id="privateprefix"></a>

```go
const PrivatePrefix = "_"
```

PrivatePrefix starts a private name ("\_llm/settings"): Go code reads and writes it through these helpers, but the wire API (HTTP, the CLI, MCP) and page code's $kv never reach or list it. Keep secrets (API keys, signing keys) there.


ErrInvalidName: the name is empty, too long or has a character names can't have.

ErrInvalidValue: the value isn't JSON, or is bigger than [MaxValueBytes](#maxvaluebytes).


<a id="w"></a>

```go

	return &guardStore{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[Store]{
		Name:   "list",
		Desc:   "Returns the values whose names start with prefix (all of them when it's empty), sorted by name. Private names (starting with _) are left out.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "",
		Scope:  "kv:read",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(ListInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,

			var in ListInput

				return nil, err
			}

		},

	extkit.Op[Store]{
		Name:   "get",

		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "get",
		Scope:  "kv:read",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(Key{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Store, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in Key
			if err := extkit.DecodeQuery(req.Query, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Get(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Store]{
		Name:   "set",
		Desc:   "Stores a JSON value under a name, replacing any value it had.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "set",
		Scope:  "kv",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(SetInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Store, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in SetInput
			if err := extkit.DecodeInput(req.JSON, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Set(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Store]{
		Name:   "delete",
		Desc:   "Removes a value. Deleting a name with no value is not an error.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "delete",
		Scope:  "kv",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(Key{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Store, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in Key
			if err := extkit.DecodeInput(req.JSON, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return nil, impl.Delete(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
)
```

W is kv/v1's wire side: routes at /api/\_c/kv/v1/\<op>, action hooks, MCP tools and the client.

## Functions

### Delete

```go
func Delete(app core.App, name string) error
```

Delete removes name's value. Deleting a name with no value is not an error.

Example:

```go
_ = kvv1.Delete(app, "myapp/settings")
```

### Get

```go
func Get(app core.App, name string, dst any) (found bool, err error)
```

Get decodes name's value into dst (as json.Unmarshal). found is false, and dst untouched, when it has none.

	var s Settings
	if _, err := kvv1.Get(app, "storytime/settings", &s); err != nil { ... }

Example:

```go
var settings struct{ Theme string }
found, err := kvv1.Get(app, "myapp/settings", &settings)
if err != nil {
	return
}
if !found {
	settings.Theme = "light"
}
fmt.Println(settings.Theme)
```

### IsPrivate

```go
func IsPrivate(name string) bool
```

IsPrivate says whether name is private (starts with [PrivatePrefix](#privateprefix)).

### MoveParam

```go
func MoveParam(app core.App, fromID, name string) (moved bool, err error)
```

MoveParam moves the \_params row fromID (an extension's own row from before kv/v1) to name, once: when name has no value yet, it gets the row's value and times, and the row is deleted. When name already has one, a leftover row is just deleted. moved says whether a value was moved. PocketBase's own rows and the store's rows can't be moved.

### MoveParamOnce

```go
func MoveParamOnce(app core.App, fromID, name string) error
```

MoveParamOnce is [MoveParam](#moveparam) at most once per app and row, for a load path that runs often: after the first call that succeeds, later ones return at once.

### OnDelete

OnDelete binds fn to delete calls on owner (an app, or a host's scope for calls the host answers). Call e.Next() to continue; return an error to refuse. in is the call's input; changes reach the provider.

```go
func OnGet(owner any, fn func(e *extkit.CallEvent, in *Key) error)
```

ValidName returns [ErrInvalidName](#errinvalidname) unless name can name a value: after an optional [PrivatePrefix](#privateprefix), a letter or digit, then letters, digits and \_ - . : / , at most [MaxNameLength](#maxnamelength) in all.

### Store

```go
type Store interface {
	// List returns the values whose names start with prefix (all of them when it's empty), sorted by name. Private names
	// (starting with _) are left out.
	//
	//op: GET / scope=kv:read
	List(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in ListInput) (Listing, error)

	// Get returns one value. A name with no value is a not_found error; a private name is a private error.
	//
	//op: GET get scope=kv:read
	Get(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Key) (Entry, error)

	// Set stores a JSON value under a name, replacing any value it had.
	//
	//op: POST set scope=kv
	Set(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SetInput) (Entry, error)

	// Delete removes a value. Deleting a name with no value is not an error.
	//
	//op: POST delete scope=kv
	Delete(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Key) error
}
```

Store reads and changes the app's key-value store.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm

# llm

```go
import llm "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm"
```

Package llm holds what the llm.\* contracts share: a model reference, generated files, usage, model info, jobs and errors. It isn't a contract itself; llm.text/v1, llm.image/v1 and the others import it.

A model is named "provider/model": the name an app's admins gave a provider in Settings → LLM, a slash, and that provider's own id for the model ("vultr/glm-5.2", "or/z-ai/glm-5.2", "cf/@cf/black-forest-labs/flux-1-schnell"). It's split on the first slash. Every call names one: there are no defaults.

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm).

## Constants

<a id="kindtext"></a><a id="kindimage"></a><a id="kindspeech"></a><a id="kindtranscribe"></a><a id="kindmusic"></a><a id="kindvideo"></a><a id="kindembed"></a><a id="kindalign"></a>

```go
const (
```

<a id="unitinputtokens"></a><a id="unitcachedtokens"></a><a id="unitoutputtokens"></a><a id="unittokens"></a><a id="unitsecond"></a><a id="unitmegapixel"></a><a id="unitimage"></a><a id="unitcharacters"></a><a id="unitrequest"></a>

```go
const (
	UnitInputTokens  = "1M input tokens"
	UnitCachedTokens = "1M cached input tokens" // input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache
	UnitOutputTokens = "1M output tokens"       // reasoning tokens count as output
	// UnitTokens is input and output tokens together: the unit of a text model's measured price, since a call's bill
	// doesn't say how much was for input and how much for output.
	UnitTokens     = "1M tokens"
	UnitSecond     = "second" // of audio or video made (speech, music, video) or read (transcribe, align)
	UnitMegapixel  = "megapixel"
	UnitImage      = "image"
	UnitCharacters = "1K characters" // of text read aloud
	UnitRequest    = "request"       // one call, whatever it used
)
```

The units a Price is in. Every provider's prices are given in these, so prices compare across providers.

## Variables

<a id="errnotconfigured"></a><a id="errunknownmodel"></a><a id="errnotsupported"></a><a id="errprovider"></a><a id="errlimit"></a><a id="errtimeout"></a>

```go
var (
	ErrNotConfigured = &extkit.Error{Code: "not_configured", Status: 503,
		Message: "no providers yet: add one in Settings → LLM, then name a model as provider/model"}
	ErrUnknownModel = &extkit.Error{Code: "unknown_model", Status: 400,
		Message: "no such model: name one as provider/model from this kind's models list"}
	ErrNotSupported = &extkit.Error{Code: "not_supported", Status: 400, Message: "that provider doesn't do this"}
	ErrProvider     = &extkit.Error{Code: "provider", Status: 502, Message: "the provider answered with an error"}
	// ErrLimit: a limit in Settings → LLM refused the call before it reached the provider. Each refusal says which
	// limit and when its window resets ("try again after 00:00 UTC").
	ErrLimit = &extkit.Error{Code: "limit", Status: 429, Message: "a limit in Settings → LLM refused this call"}
	// ErrTimeout: the provider didn't answer in time and the request was cancelled. Its message names the model and
	// what ran out: a streamed answer that went quiet ("the provider sent nothing for 10s"), or the call's time limit
	// ("no answer in 3m0s"). Worth a retry, unlike a bad answer. A caller's own deadline or cancellation (a Go
	// context, an AbortSignal in page code) ends the call as that caller's error instead.
	ErrTimeout = &extkit.Error{Code: "timeout", Status: 504, Message: "the provider didn't answer in time"}
)
```

Errors every llm.\* contract may answer. A provider's own error comes back as ErrProvider's code with the cloud's status and message (never the key).

<a id="allkinds"></a>

```go
var AllKinds = []string{KindText, KindImage, KindSpeech, KindTranscribe, KindAlign, KindMusic, KindVideo, KindEmbed}
```

AllKinds lists every kind, in Settings → LLM's order.

## Types

### CallDoneEvent

```go
type CallDoneEvent struct {
	hook.Event
	App     core.App
	Context context.Context

	Kind    string
	Op      string
	Model   string
	Subject string
	Usage   Usage
	Job     string // a job's id, for music and video
}
```

CallDoneEvent is a call that reached a provider, with what it used. A music or video job's comes once its cost is known (when it's done), or never for a job nobody checks again.

### CallEvent

```go
type CallEvent struct {
	hook.Event
	App     core.App
	Context context.Context

	Kind string // "text", "image", "speech", "transcribe", "align", "music", "video" or "embed"
	Op   string // the contract operation: "complete", "stream", "generate", "speak", ...
	// Model is the call's "provider/model"; a handler may change it.
	Model string
	// Subject is whom the call is for (see WithSubject): "user:<collection>/<id>", "guest:<id>",
	// "guest:ip:<address>", "" for nobody in particular, or any name a handler gives it ("team:acme").
	Subject string
	// Input is a pointer to the operation's input (*textv1.CompleteInput, *imagev1.GenerateInput, ...); a handler may
	// change its fields. Its model field is ignored: change Model.
	Input any
	// Auth is who made the call.
	Auth extkit.Auth
	// GuestsCapped says a handler takes care of what guests may spend, so the built-in limits don't refuse guest
	// calls for want of a limit on all guests together.
	GuestsCapped bool
}
```

CallEvent is one billable call on its way to a provider.

### CallEvent.Refuse

```go
func (e *CallEvent) Refuse(message string) error
```

Refuse returns the error that refuses the call with message, the way a used-up limit does (code "limit", 429). Return it from a handler instead of calling e.Next().

### Enrich

```go
type Enrich struct {
	Buckets []string `json:"buckets"`
	Limit   int      `json:"limit,omitempty"` // passages to add (default 5, at most 20)
	Query   string   `json:"query,omitempty"`
	// Viewer is who the answer is for: passages from records they can't view (the collection's view rule) are left
	// out. Nil sees everything, as the app's own server code.
	Viewer *Viewer `json:"viewer,omitempty"`
}
```

Enrich adds passages from the app's search buckets (search/v1) to a call's prompt: the call searches Buckets with Query (default: the prompt, or the last user message) and sends the best Limit passages after it. In JSON it's an object, or just the list of buckets (\["storytime"]).

File is generated media, or media sent in (audio to transcribe, an image to edit). Data is the bytes (base64 over HTTP); URL is the provider's hosted copy when it gave one, which may expire. Name is a suggested file name.

### Job

```go
type Job struct {
	ID       string  `json:"id"`
	Status   string  `json:"status"` // queued, running, done or failed
	Progress float64 `json:"progress,omitempty"`
	Files    []File  `json:"files,omitempty"`

	Outputs int    `json:"outputs,omitempty"`
	Error   string `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Model   string `json:"model"`
	Usage   Usage  `json:"usage"`
}
```

Job is a long generation (music, video): started by create, followed by get, its files fetched by content. The id carries the provider ("vultr:music\_02a2..."), so get and content find it again. Files are filled in once it's done when the provider returns them inline or create was given wait.

### ModelInfo

```go
type ModelInfo struct {
	ID       string   `json:"id"`       // "provider/model", what a call names
	Provider string   `json:"provider"` // the provider's name in Settings → LLM
	Type     string   `json:"type"`     // the provider's type: vultr, cloudflare, openrouter, openai
	Name     string   `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Kinds    []string `json:"kinds"`
	Inputs   []string `json:"inputs,omitempty"` // what it reads: text, image, audio...
	// Reasoning is true for a model that thinks before answering (its thinking counts toward maxTokens).
	Reasoning     bool `json:"reasoning,omitempty"`
	ContextTokens int  `json:"contextTokens,omitempty"`
	// Prices are its listed prices, then the prices measured from this app's own calls, each marked by Source. None
	// means its price isn't known.
	Prices      []Price `json:"prices,omitempty"`
	Description string  `json:"description,omitempty"`
	// Size is how many parameters it has, as its maker names it: "1.7B", "27B", "30B (3B active)" for a
	// mixture of experts.
	Size string `json:"size,omitempty"`
	// Features are what it can do beyond its kind, from the Feature constants.
	Features []string `json:"features,omitempty"`
	// Languages are the languages it speaks, writes or hears (ISO 639-1 codes), when the provider lists them.
	Languages []string `json:"languages,omitempty"`
}
```

ModelInfo is one model, as each contract's models operation lists it. Every field past Kinds is optional: a provider fills what it says about the model, and nothing is guessed.

### Passage

```go
type Passage struct {
	Bucket   string  `json:"bucket"`
	Source   string  `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Document string  `json:"document"`
	Heading  string  `json:"heading,omitempty"`
	Text     string  `json:"text"`
```

Passage is a piece of a search bucket that was added to a prompt, and where it came from.

### Price

```go
type Price struct {
	Unit string  `json:"unit"`
	USD  float64 `json:"usd"`
	// Source is where the price comes from: "listed" (the provider's own model list; also when empty) or "measured"
	// (what this app's calls to the model were billed, from the ledger: cost divided by what they used).
	Source string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	// Calls is, for a measured price, how many billed calls it was measured over.
	Calls int `json:"calls,omitempty"`
}
```

Price is one of a model's prices: USD per Unit, one of the Unit constants. A price is a rate on one meter of a call; a model may list several (input and output tokens), and a call's cost is each meter's use times its rate, added up.

### SubjectParts

```go
type SubjectParts struct {
	Kind       string `json:"kind"`                 // "user", "guest", "" (nobody), or a custom subject's prefix
	Collection string `json:"collection,omitempty"` // a user's auth collection
	ID         string `json:"id,omitempty"`         // a user's record id, a guest's cookie id, or what follows a custom prefix
	IP         string `json:"ip,omitempty"`         // a guest counted by IP
}
```

SubjectParts is a subject taken apart.

### ParseSubject

```go
func ParseSubject(s string) SubjectParts
```

ParseSubject takes a subject apart: "user:users/abc" is {user, users, abc}, "guest:ip:10.0.0.1" is {guest, ip 10.0.0.1}, "team:acme" is {team, acme}.

### Usage

```go
type Usage struct {
	InputTokens     int     `json:"inputTokens,omitempty"`
	OutputTokens    int     `json:"outputTokens,omitempty"`
	CachedTokens    int     `json:"cachedTokens,omitempty"`    // input tokens that came from the provider's prompt cache
	ReasoningTokens int     `json:"reasoningTokens,omitempty"` // output tokens the model spent thinking
	Seconds         float64 `json:"seconds,omitempty"`         // audio or video length billed
	// CostMicroUSD is what the call cost, in millionths of a US dollar (1,000,000 is $1; 1,000 is a tenth of a cent),
	// as a whole number so costs add up exactly. It's what the provider charged when it says (OpenRouter on every call,
	// Vultr for media), else an estimate from the model's listed prices and what the call used (CostEstimated), else 0:
	// 0 means free or not known.
	CostMicroUSD int64 `json:"costMicroUSD"`
	// CostEstimated is true when CostMicroUSD was worked out from listed prices rather than reported by the provider.
	CostEstimated bool `json:"costEstimated,omitempty"`
}
```

Usage is what a call used. The token and seconds fields appear only when known; CostMicroUSD is always there. Every llm.\* contract's reply carries one (chat's in its answer, music's and video's on the job).

```go
type Viewer struct {
	Collection string `json:"collection,omitempty"`
	ID         string `json:"id,omitempty"`
}
```

Viewer is a signed-in auth record (Collection and ID), or a guest (both empty).

# alignv1

```go
import alignv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/align/v1"
```

Package alignv1 is the llm.align/v1 contract: forced alignment. Given a recording and the exact words spoken in it, a model says when each line and each word is said. Nothing is transcribed or guessed: every word that comes back is one that was sent, in the order sent. For captions timed to a narration, karaoke-style highlighting, or finding a phrase in a recording.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/llm.align/v1. In pb\_hooks it's $llm.align.

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm/align/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm/align/v1).

### AlignInput

```go
type AlignInput struct {
	Model string   `json:"model"` // "provider/model", required
	Audio llm.File `json:"audio"` // its Name's extension (story.mp3) or Type tells the provider the format
	// Text is the words in the audio, one line per line. A line in square brackets ([Chorus]) labels the lines under it
	// and isn't timed.
	Text string `json:"text"`
	// Mode is "speech" for a voice recording, or "lyrics" (the provider's default) to separate a sung vocal from the
	// music first.
	Mode string `json:"mode,omitempty"`
	// Language is the text's language as an ISO 639-1 code ("en"); empty lets the model tell.
	Language string      `json:"language,omitempty"`
	Options  llm.Options `json:"options,omitempty"`
}
```

AlignInput is the recording and its words.

### Line

```go
type Line struct {
	Index int     `json:"index"` // which line of Text, counting from 0, skipping labels and blank lines
	Text  string  `json:"text"`
	Start float64 `json:"start"` // seconds from the start of the audio to its first word
	End   float64 `json:"end"`   // seconds to the end of its last word
	// Score is the model's confidence (higher is better); Certain is its judgement that the line is placed right.
	Score   float64 `json:"score"`
	Certain bool    `json:"certain"`
	// Tag is the label of the line's section ("Chorus" for [Chorus]), when there is one.
	Tag string `json:"tag,omitempty"`
}
```

Line is one line's place in the audio.

### Result

```go
type Result struct {
	// Duration is the audio's length in seconds.
	Duration float64 `json:"duration"`
	// Lines are the lines placed in the audio, in order (labels and blank lines aren't lines).
	Lines []Line `json:"lines"`
	// Words are every word of those lines, in order.
	Words []Word `json:"words"`
	// Unaligned are lines the model couldn't place, listed instead of left out.
	Unaligned []Unaligned `json:"unaligned,omitempty"`
	Model     string      `json:"model"`
	Usage     llm.Usage   `json:"usage"`
}
```

Result is when each line and word is said.

```go
type Unaligned struct {
	Line   int    `json:"line"`

	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}
```

Unaligned is a line the model couldn't place.

# chatv1

```go
import chatv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/chat/v1"
```

Package chatv1 is the llm.chat/v1 contract: stored conversations with the app's language model. A chat is an id the app keeps (on its own records, or handed to its frontend), with an optional title and the app's own meta; the provider stores its messages, sends the recent ones with each question (and a summary of the older ones), and saves both turns. It calls llm.text/v1 for the answers. Chats aren't tied to users: an app that has them puts the user in meta and decides who sees what.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/llm.chat/v1. In pb\_hooks it's $llm.chat.new, $llm.chat.open(id) and $llm.chat.list.

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm/chat/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm/chat/v1).

```go
type Chat struct {
```

### Chats

```go
type Chats interface {
	// New starts a chat and returns it; its id is how the app finds it again.
	//
	//op: POST new
	New(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in NewInput) (Chat, error)
	// Send asks the chat a question: the provider sends the system text, the chat's summary, its recent messages and
	// the question (with Context after it) to llm.text/v1, saves both turns, and folds older messages into the summary
	// when it's due.
	//
	//op: POST send
	Send(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SendInput) (SendResult, error)
	// SendStream is Send with the answer as it's written: llm.text/v1 chunks, the last one with done and the result.
	//
	//op: POST send-stream
	SendStream(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SendInput) (extkit.Stream, error)
	// Get returns a chat.
	//
	//op: POST get scope=chat:read
	Get(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Ref) (Chat, error)
	// History returns a chat's messages, oldest first: the last Limit before the message Before (all when 0 and "").
	//
	//op: POST history scope=chat:read
	History(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in HistoryInput) (History, error)
	// Update sets a chat's title or meta (fields left out stay).
	//
	//op: POST update
	Update(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in UpdateInput) (Chat, error)
	// List returns chats, most recently updated first; Meta keeps those whose meta has each of its top-level keys
	// with that value.
	//
	//op: POST list scope=chat:read
	List(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in ListInput) (ChatList, error)
	// Forget deletes a chat, its messages and the model's state for it.
	//
	//op: POST forget
	Forget(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Ref) (Forgotten, error)
	// ForgetWhere deletes every chat whose meta matches (as in List), e.g. all of a user the app deleted.
	//
	//op: POST forget-where
	ForgetWhere(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in ListInput) (Forgotten, error)
}
```

Chats stores an app's conversations with its language model.

### SendInput

```go
type SendInput struct {
	ID   string `json:"id"`
	Text string `json:"text"`
	// System is the preamble, sent first on every turn (keep it the same for the prompt cache).
	System string `json:"system,omitempty"`
	// Window is how many recent messages to send (default 12); older ones reach the model through the summary.
	Window int `json:"window,omitempty"`
	// SummarizeEvery folds the messages that left the window into the summary once that many have (default 6).
	SummarizeEvery int `json:"summarizeEvery,omitempty"`
	// Context is text sent after the question (the passages that answer it, say). The chat keeps the question as sent, to send it the same way next turn; history shows the question alone.
	Context     string          `json:"context,omitempty"`
	Schema      json.RawMessage `json:"schema,omitempty"`
	MaxTokens   int             `json:"maxTokens,omitempty"`
	Temperature *float64        `json:"temperature,omitempty"`
	// Model is the text model to answer with ("provider/model", required).
	Model string `json:"model"`
	// Reasoning is how much a reasoning model thinks first: "", "off", "low", "medium" or "high".
	Reasoning string `json:"reasoning,omitempty"` // Enrich adds the best passages from the app's search buckets after the question, beside Context (search/v1);
	// the answer's Passages lists them.
	Enrich *llm.Enrich `json:"enrich,omitempty"`
}
```

SendInput is a question for a chat and how to ask it.

### SendResult

```go
type SendResult struct {
	Answer     textv1.CompleteResult `json:"answer"`
	Summarized bool                  `json:"summarized,omitempty"`
}
```

SendResult is the answer, and whether this turn folded older messages into the summary.

```go
type UpdateInput struct {
	ID    string          `json:"id"`
	Title *string         `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Meta  json.RawMessage `json:"meta,omitempty"`
}
```

UpdateInput changes a chat's title or meta.

# embedv1

```go
import embedv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/embed/v1"
```

# ledgerv1

### CallsInput

```go
type CallsInput struct {
	// Window is "day" or "month": the UTC calendar day or month holding now. Or give Since and Until (RFC 3339 or
	// YYYY-MM-DD, UTC; Until is exclusive). With none of them, all of the ledger (it keeps 13 months).
	Window  string `json:"window,omitempty"`
	Since   string `json:"since,omitempty"`
	Until   string `json:"until,omitempty"`
	Subject string `json:"subject,omitempty"`
	Kind    string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Model   string `json:"model,omitempty"`
	// Status is "ok" for calls that reached a provider, "refused" for calls a limit refused, empty for both.
	Status string `json:"status,omitempty"`
	Limit  int    `json:"limit,omitempty"` // default 50, at most 500
	Offset int    `json:"offset,omitempty"`
}
```

CallsInput filters and pages the rows.

### Ledger

```go
type Ledger interface {
	// Remaining is, for each limit in Settings → LLM that counts the subject's calls, how much is used and left in
	// its current window, the tightest first.
	//
	//op: GET remaining scope=public
	Remaining(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in RemainingInput) (Remaining, error)
	// Spent is what the subject's calls used in a window.
	//
	//op: GET spent scope=public
	Spent(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SpentInput) (Totals, error)
	// Summary is what calls used, grouped by model, kind, subject or day.
	//
	//op: GET summary
	Summary(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SummaryInput) (Summary, error)
	// Calls lists the ledger's rows, newest first.
	//
	//op: GET calls
	Calls(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in CallsInput) (CallList, error)
}
```

Ledger reads the ledger.

Remaining and Spent answer about one subject (whom calls were for: see llm.WithSubject). A superuser, an API token with the llm:read scope, and page code may name any subject; a signed-in user is answered about themselves only. Page code calling through $llm.for(e) gets the request's own subject when it names none.

### LimitLeft

```go
type LimitLeft struct {
	// Limit is the limit in words: "each guest, $0.10 a day".
	Limit  string `json:"limit"`
	Scope  string `json:"scope"`  // app, user, guest or guests
	Window string `json:"window"` // day or month
	Metric string `json:"metric"` // cost, input, output or calls
	Kind   string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Model  string `json:"model,omitempty"`
	// Amount, Used and Left are in the metric's unit: US dollars for cost, else tokens or calls.
	Amount float64 `json:"amount"`
	Used   float64 `json:"used"`
	Left   float64 `json:"left"`
	// Resets is when the window ends (RFC 3339, UTC).
	Resets string `json:"resets"`
}
```

LimitLeft is one limit and how much of it is left.

### Remaining

```go
type Remaining struct {
	Limits []LimitLeft `json:"limits"`
}
```

Remaining is the limits that count a subject's calls.

### RemainingInput

```go
type RemainingInput struct {
	// Subject is whom to answer about ("user:users/abc", "guest:<id>", "team:acme"); empty means the caller's own
	// subject, or none, which only limits on the whole app count.
	Subject string `json:"subject,omitempty"`
}
```

RemainingInput names the subject.

### SpentInput

```go
type SpentInput struct {
	// Subject: as for Remaining, except that empty with no caller's subject means every call (the whole app).
	Subject string `json:"subject,omitempty"`
	// Window is "day" or "month": the UTC calendar day or month holding now. Or give Since and Until (RFC 3339 or
	// YYYY-MM-DD, UTC; Until is exclusive). With none of them, all of the ledger (it keeps 13 months).
	Window string `json:"window,omitempty"`
	Since  string `json:"since,omitempty"`
	Until  string `json:"until,omitempty"`
	Kind   string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Model  string `json:"model,omitempty"`
}
```

SpentInput is a subject and a window, optionally narrowed to a kind or a model.

### Summary

```go
type Summary struct {
	Rows []SummaryRow `json:"rows"`
}
```

Summary is the groups.

### SummaryInput

```go
type SummaryInput struct {
	// By is what to group by: "model" (the default), "kind", "subject" or "day".
	By string `json:"by,omitempty"`
	// Window is "day" or "month": the UTC calendar day or month holding now. Or give Since and Until (RFC 3339 or
	// YYYY-MM-DD, UTC; Until is exclusive). With none of them, all of the ledger (it keeps 13 months).
	Window  string `json:"window,omitempty"`
	Since   string `json:"since,omitempty"`
	Until   string `json:"until,omitempty"`
	Subject string `json:"subject,omitempty"`
	Kind    string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Model   string `json:"model,omitempty"`
	// Limit is how many groups, the costliest first (by day: the latest first); default 100, at most 1000.
	Limit int `json:"limit,omitempty"`
}
```

SummaryInput groups calls in a window.

### SummaryRow

```go
type SummaryRow struct {
	Key string `json:"key"` // the model, kind, subject or day (YYYY-MM-DD)
	Totals
}
```

SummaryRow is one group's totals.

```go
type Totals struct {

	Cached       int64   `json:"cached"`
	Output       int64   `json:"output"`
	Seconds      float64 `json:"seconds"`
	CostMicroUSD int64   `json:"costMicroUSD"` // millionths of a US dollar
}
```

Totals is what calls used.

# musicv1

```go
import musicv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/music/v1"
```

### CreateInput

```go
type CreateInput struct {
	Model  string `json:"model"`  // "provider/model", required
	Prompt string `json:"prompt"` // the style: "gentle lullaby, music box and soft strings"
	Lyrics string `json:"lyrics,omitempty"`
	// Seconds is how long (the provider's default when 0).
	Seconds float64 `json:"seconds,omitempty"`
	// Wait is how long to wait for the job, as a duration ("5m"); "" returns at once.
	Wait    string      `json:"wait,omitempty"`
	Options llm.Options `json:"options,omitempty"`
}
```

CreateInput is the music to make.

### Music

```go
type Music interface {
	// Create starts making music. With Wait it returns once the job is done (or failed), its files included;
	// otherwise at once, to follow with Get.
	//
	//op: POST create
	Create(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in CreateInput) (llm.Job, error)
	// Get says how a job is going.
	//
	//op: POST get scope=llm:read
	Get(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.JobRef) (llm.Job, error)
	// Content fetches one of a done job's files.
	//
	//op: POST content scope=llm:read
	Content(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.ContentInput) (llm.File, error)
	// Models lists the music models of every provider in Settings → LLM.
	//
	//op: GET models scope=llm:read
	Models(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.ModelsInput) (llm.Models, error)
}
```

Music makes music.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/search/v1

# searchv1

```go
import searchv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1"
```

Package searchv1 is the llm.search/v1 contract: named buckets of content an app searches. An app makes the bucket it needs (Ensure); its admins fill it from the dashboard's Search screen. A bucket holds sources, each one tracked unit however many documents it brings: a file, pasted text, a folder, a zip, a web page, a Git repository or one of the app's collections, or a folder on the server. Adding a source of the same name again replaces it: unchanged documents cost nothing, missing ones go. URL, repository and collection sources keep themselves current. The provider splits each document into chunks with their source (document, section, lines, record), embeds them with the app's one embedding model (llm.embed/v1, picked automatically; identical chunks anywhere in the app are embedded once), and returns the chunks that best match a query across the buckets asked for.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/llm.search/v1. In page code it's $llm.search (bound by the llm extension); llm.text/v1 and llm.chat/v1 calls take \`enrich\` to add a search's best passages to their prompt ([Enrich](#enrich)).

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm/search/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm/search/v1).

## Constants

<a id="enrichdefault"></a><a id="enrichmax"></a>

```go
const (
	EnrichDefault = 5
	EnrichMax     = 20
)
```

EnrichDefault and EnrichMax are how many passages an Enrich adds by default, and at most.

<a id="kindfile"></a><a id="kindtext"></a><a id="kindfolder"></a><a id="kinddir"></a><a id="kindzip"></a><a id="kindpage"></a><a id="kindgit"></a><a id="kindcollection"></a>

```go
const (
	KindFile       = "file"       // one dropped or uploaded file
	KindText       = "text"       // pasted text
	KindFolder     = "folder"     // a dropped folder, file by file
	KindDir        = "dir"        // a folder of the app's files on the server, read again every few minutes
	KindZip        = "zip"        // a zip, a document per text file inside
	KindPage       = "page"       // a web page, fetched
	KindGit        = "git"        // a Git repository: the default branch's files and recent commits
	KindCollection = "collection" // one of the app's collections, a document per record
)
```

Source kinds.

## Functions

### Enrich

```go
func Enrich(ctx context.Context, app core.App, e *llm.Enrich, query string) (string, []llm.Passage, error)
```

Enrich runs e's search on app (with query when e.Query is empty) and returns the text a model call sends after its prompt, and the passages in it. It's how llm.text/v1 and llm.chat/v1 providers fulfil \`enrich\`, so every provider adds passages the same way. With no buckets named it returns nothing; with no matches, no text.

## Types

### AddInput

```go
type AddInput struct {
	Bucket string `json:"bucket"`
	// Name is the source's (and its document's) name, usually a file name ("install.md"). Its extension picks the
	// splitter: Markdown by headings, code and the rest by blank lines.
	Name string `json:"name"`
	Text string `json:"text"`
	// Kind is file (the default) or text, for the dashboard.
	Kind string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	// Replace names an existing source this one replaces under the new name (a renamed new version: notes-v2.zip
	// for notes-v1.zip). Without it, only a source of the same name is replaced.
	Replace string `json:"replace,omitempty"`
}
```

AddInput is a file or pasted text.

### Bucket

```go
type Bucket struct {
	// Name is the bucket's id: letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or digit (at most 64).
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Title string `json:"title"`
	// Description says what belongs in the bucket: the app that made it tells its admins what to load.
	Description  string    `json:"description"`
	Owner        string    `json:"owner"` // who made it (the app's name, say), for the dashboard
	MaxDocuments int       `json:"maxDocuments"`
	MaxBytes     int64     `json:"maxBytes"`
	Sources      int       `json:"sources"`
	Documents    int       `json:"documents"`
	Chunks       int       `json:"chunks"`
	Bytes        int64     `json:"bytes"`
	Pending      int       `json:"pending"` // documents waiting to be embedded
	Errors       int       `json:"errors"`  // documents or sources that failed
	Created      time.Time `json:"created"`
	Updated      time.Time `json:"updated"`
}
```

Bucket is a named set of sources searched together.

### Document

```go
type Document struct {
	Bucket string `json:"bucket"`
	Source string `json:"source"`
	Name   string `json:"name"` // its path in the source, the URL, "commit <sha>" or "<collection>/<id>"
	Kind   string `json:"kind"` // markdown, code or text: how it was split
	Size   int64  `json:"size"`
	Hash   string `json:"hash"` // sha256 of the text
	// Status is queued (waiting to be embedded), embedding, ready or error.
	Status string `json:"status"`
	Error  string `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Chunks int    `json:"chunks"`
	// Embedded is how many of its chunks have the app's model's vectors (Chunks when it's ready).
	Embedded     int        `json:"embedded"`
	Record       *RecordRef `json:"record,omitempty"` // the record it was made from, in a collection source
	Tokens       int        `json:"tokens"`           // the text's estimated size in tokens
	CostMicroUSD int64      `json:"costMicroUSD"`     // what embedding it has cost so far
	Created      time.Time  `json:"created"`
	Updated      time.Time  `json:"updated"`
}
```

Document is one piece of a source: a file, a page, a commit or a record.

### FolderInput

```go
type FolderInput struct {
	Bucket string `json:"bucket"`
	// Path is the folder, relative to the app's own folder (the one holding pb_data, pb_pages and pb_public); it can't
	// leave that folder or be pb_data. "pb_pages/docs", say.
	Path string `json:"path"`
	// Include keeps only files matching one of these patterns (against the file name or its path in the folder:
	// "*.md"); none keeps every text file. Exclude leaves out matches, beside what's always skipped (dot folders and
	// dotfiles, node_modules, vendor, lockfiles, binaries).
	Include []string `json:"include,omitempty"`
	Exclude []string `json:"exclude,omitempty"`
	// URL is where each file is published, with {path} for the file's path in the folder without its extension (an
	// index file is its folder): "/docs/{path}" makes guides/install.md /docs/guides/install and guides/index.md
	// /docs/guides. Results from Markdown files add their section's anchor (#heading-id). "" gives no links.
	URL string `json:"url,omitempty"`
}
```

FolderInput is a folder of the app's files on the server.

```go
type FollowInput struct {
```

### Result

```go
type Result struct {
	Bucket   string `json:"bucket"`
	Source   string `json:"source"`
	Document string `json:"document"`
	Text     string `json:"text"`
	// Heading is the section the chunk is in ("Install › macOS"), for Markdown, records and commits.
	Heading   string     `json:"heading,omitempty"`
	StartLine int        `json:"startLine"`
	EndLine   int        `json:"endLine"`
	Record    *RecordRef `json:"record,omitempty"`
	// URL links to where the passage is published, when its source knows: a web page's URL, or a server folder's URL
	// pattern with the section's anchor ("/docs/guides/install#macos").
	URL   string  `json:"url,omitempty"`
	Score float64 `json:"score"` // orders the results; higher is better
}
```

Result is one matching chunk and where it came from.

### Results

```go
type Results struct {
	Results []Result  `json:"results"`
	Model   string    `json:"model,omitempty"` // the model that embedded the query
	Usage   llm.Usage `json:"usage"`           // what embedding the query cost
}
```

Results are the best matches, best first (a Sample's are in no order, with no score).

```go
type SampleInput struct {

	// Prefix keeps chunks from documents whose name starts with it.
	Prefix string `json:"prefix,omitempty"`
}
```

SampleInput is where to draw random chunks from.

### Search

```go
type Search interface {
	// Status is the app's embedding model and how far embedding has got across every bucket.
	//
	//op: GET status scope=search:read
	Status(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth) (Status, error)
	// SetModel changes the app's embedding model ("provider/model" from llm.embed/v1's models; "" picks one again).
	// Every bucket is embedded again in the background; until a chunk is, keywords still find it.
	//
	//op: POST set-model
	SetModel(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in ModelInput) (Status, error)
	// Buckets lists the app's buckets with their counts.
	//
	//op: GET buckets scope=search:read
	Buckets(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth) (BucketList, error)
	// Bucket returns one bucket with its counts.
	//
	//op: GET bucket scope=search:read
	Bucket(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Ref) (Bucket, error)
	// Ensure makes a bucket if it's missing and returns it. An existing bucket keeps its settings, except that an
	// empty title, description or owner is filled in. Apps call it at startup for the bucket they need.
	//
	//op: POST ensure
	Ensure(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in EnsureInput) (Bucket, error)
	// Update changes a bucket's title, description or limits (fields left out stay).
	//
	//op: POST update
	Update(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in UpdateInput) (Bucket, error)
	// Delete removes a bucket and everything in it.
	//
	//op: POST delete
	Delete(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in Ref) (Removed, error)
	// Sources lists a bucket's sources, by name.
	//
	//op: GET sources scope=search:read
	Sources(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in BucketRef) (SourceList, error)
	// Add puts a file or pasted text in a bucket as its own source (one document), replacing the source of that name.
	// The same text again costs nothing; changed text embeds only its new chunks. It returns at once; the document is
	// embedded in the background (its status says how far it got).
	//
	//op: POST add
	Add(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in AddInput) (Source, error)
	// Upload adds a file sent as the request body: ?bucket=<name>&name=<file name>[&replace=<source>]. A .zip is one
	// source with a document per text file inside it; anything else is a file source.
	//
	//op: POST upload
	Upload(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in extkit.RawIn) (Source, error)
	// Put adds one file to a folder source (made on the first one), the way the dashboard sends a dropped folder;
	// Prune ends it.
	//
	//op: POST put
	Put(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in PutInput) (Document, error)
	// Prune removes the documents of a folder source that aren't in Keep: the files the folder no longer has.
	//
	//op: POST prune
	Prune(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in PruneInput) (Source, error)
	// AddURL adds a web page or a Git repository as a source (named by its URL, replacing one of that name) and reads
	// it in the background; Every keeps it current.
	//
	//op: POST add-url
	AddURL(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in URLInput) (Source, error)
	// AddFolder adds a folder of the app's own files on the server (named by its path, replacing one of that name):
	// every text file in it, read in the background and read again every few minutes, so changed files are embedded
	// again and removed ones leave. With URL, each result from it links to the page that file is published at.
	//
	//op: POST add-folder
	AddFolder(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in FolderInput) (Source, error)
	// DetectURL says how AddURL would read a URL: as a Git repository when its server answers the Git protocol (any
	// host, with or without .git), otherwise as a web page.
	//
	//op: POST detect-url scope=search:read
	DetectURL(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in URLRef) (URLKind, error)
	// Follow adds one of the app's collections as a source (named by the collection): each record the filter keeps is
	// a document, kept in sync as records are saved and deleted.
	//
	//op: POST follow
	Follow(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in FollowInput) (Source, error)
	// Refresh reads a source again now: fetches a URL or repository, rereads a collection, resplits a file or zip.
	//
	//op: POST refresh
	Refresh(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SourceRef) (Source, error)
	// Remove takes sources out of a bucket, with their documents.
	//
	//op: POST remove
	Remove(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in RemoveInput) (Removed, error)
	// Documents lists a bucket's documents (or one source's), by source and name.
	//
	//op: GET documents scope=search:read
	Documents(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in DocumentsInput) (DocumentList, error)
	// Search returns the chunks that best match a query across the buckets named, best first.
	//
	//op: POST search scope=search:read
	Search(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SearchInput) (Results, error)
	// Sample returns chunks picked at random from the buckets named: material to draw from ("surprise me", a topic
	// nobody asked about), not matches. No query, no embedding, so it costs nothing. Like Search without a viewer, it
	// may return any chunk, a followed record's included.
	//
	//op: POST sample scope=search:read
	Sample(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SampleInput) (Results, error)
}
```

Search keeps an app's search buckets and searches them.

### SearchInput

```go
type SearchInput struct {
	// Buckets are searched together; none searches every bucket. Bucket is one more, for a single-bucket search.
	Buckets []string `json:"buckets,omitempty"`
	Bucket  string   `json:"bucket,omitempty"`
	Query   string   `json:"query"`
	Limit   int      `json:"limit,omitempty"` // default 5, at most 50
	// Prefix keeps matches from documents whose name starts with it.
	Prefix string  `json:"prefix,omitempty"`
	Viewer *Viewer `json:"viewer,omitempty"`
}
```

SearchInput is a query.

### Source

```go
type Source struct {
	Bucket string `json:"bucket"`
	// Name identifies it in the bucket: the file, folder or zip name, the URL, or the collection.
	Name string `json:"name"`
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// URL, Every, Commits, Exclude: a page or repository source's settings.
	URL     string   `json:"url,omitempty"`
	Every   string   `json:"every,omitempty"`
	Commits int      `json:"commits,omitempty"`
	Exclude []string `json:"exclude,omitempty"`
	// Path, Include, PageURL: a server folder's settings (Exclude too).
	Path    string   `json:"path,omitempty"`
	Include []string `json:"include,omitempty"`
	PageURL string   `json:"pageURL,omitempty"`
	// Collection, Fields, Filter: a collection source's settings.
	Collection string   `json:"collection,omitempty"`
	Fields     []string `json:"fields,omitempty"`
	Filter     string   `json:"filter,omitempty"`
	// Hash is the sha256 of a file's or zip's content as uploaded, so the dashboard can tell an exact duplicate
	// under another name.
	Hash string `json:"hash,omitempty"`
	// Status is reading (fetching or splitting), ready or error; Error says why.
	Status       string     `json:"status"`
	Error        string     `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Documents    int        `json:"documents"`
	Chunks       int        `json:"chunks"`
	Embedded     int        `json:"embedded"` // chunks with the app's model's vectors
	Bytes        int64      `json:"bytes"`
	Pending      int        `json:"pending"` // documents waiting to be embedded
	CostMicroUSD int64      `json:"costMicroUSD"`
	Refreshed    *time.Time `json:"refreshed,omitempty"` // when it was last read
	Next         *time.Time `json:"next,omitempty"`      // when Every reads it next
	Created      time.Time  `json:"created"`
}
```

Source is one tracked unit in a bucket.

### Status

```go
type Status struct {

	Model string `json:"model"`
	// Chunks is how many chunks the app's buckets hold; Embedded how many have the model's vectors.
	Chunks   int `json:"chunks"`
```
