### URLInput

```go
type URLInput struct {
	Bucket string `json:"bucket"`
	URL    string `json:"url"` // http or https
	// Kind is page or git; "" asks the server (DetectURL).
	Kind  string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
	Every string `json:"every,omitempty"` // hour, day, week; "" reads it only when added or refreshed
	// Commits is how many recent commits of a repository become documents (subject, body, author, date, files; no
	// diffs): 0 is the default (300), -1 none.
	Commits int `json:"commits,omitempty"`
	// Exclude skips a repository's files whose path, or any folder in it, matches one of these patterns ("docs/old",
	// "*.min.js"), beside what's always skipped (binaries, .git, node_modules, vendor, lockfiles).
	Exclude []string `json:"exclude,omitempty"`
}
```

URLInput is a web page or a Git repository.

### URLKind

```go
type URLKind struct {

```

URLKind is how a URL would be read: git or page.

```go
type URLRef struct {
```

```go
type UpdateInput struct {
```

### Viewer

```go
type Viewer struct {
	// Collection and ID are the signed-in auth record; both empty is a guest (signed out).
	Collection string `json:"collection,omitempty"`
	ID         string `json:"id,omitempty"`
}
```

Viewer is who a search is for. Matches from records they can't view (the collection's view rule, as PocketBase checks it) are left out; documents that aren't records are for everyone. A search without one sees everything.

# speechv1

```go
import speechv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/speech/v1"
```

Package speechv1 is the llm.speech/v1 contract: a model reads text aloud.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/llm.speech/v1. In pb\_hooks it's $llm.speech.

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm/speech/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm/speech/v1).

## Constants

<a id="modebuiltin"></a><a id="modedesign"></a><a id="modeclone"></a>

```go
const (
	ModeBuiltin = "builtin"
	ModeDesign  = "design"
	ModeClone   = "clone"
)
```

Voice modes, in Voice.Mode.

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Speech]("llm.speech/v1", extkit.One).JS(extkit.JSHooks, nil).JSTypes(jsTypes)
```

Contract is llm.speech/v1.

<a id="w"></a>

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "llm", func(inner Speech, g *extkit.Guard[Speech]) Speech {
	return &guardSpeech{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[Speech]{
		Name:   "speak",
		Desc:   "Reads the text aloud and returns the audio.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "speak",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(SpeakInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Speech, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in SpeakInput
			if err := extkit.DecodeInput(req.JSON, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Speak(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Speech]{
		Name:   "voices",
		Desc:   "Lists a model's voices, when the provider says.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "voices",
		Scope:  "llm:read",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(VoicesInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Speech, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in VoicesInput
			if err := extkit.DecodeInput(req.JSON, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Voices(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Speech]{
		Name:   "models",
		Desc:   "Lists the speech models of every provider in Settings → LLM.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "models",
		Scope:  "llm:read",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(llm.ModelsInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Speech, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in llm.ModelsInput
			if err := extkit.DecodeQuery(req.Query, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Models(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
)
```

### SpeakInput

```go
type SpeakInput struct {
	Model string `json:"model"` // "provider/model", required
	Text  string `json:"text"`
	Voice string `json:"voice,omitempty"`
	// Format is the audio format: mp3 (default), wav, opus, flac, pcm, as the provider allows.
	Format string  `json:"format,omitempty"`
	Speed  float64 `json:"speed,omitempty"`
	// Instructions describe the delivery ("slow and calm, a bedtime voice"), for models that take them. Not with a
	// Reference: a cloned voice takes its delivery from the clip.
	Instructions string `json:"instructions,omitempty"`
	// Reference clones a voice: the model reads Text in the voice of this clip. Leave Voice empty (or the model's
	// clone voice, Voices' Mode "clone"). Models that clone list a voice with that mode; a provider that doesn't clone
	// refuses the call with llm.ErrNotSupported. Nothing is saved at the provider: send the clip with every call.
	Reference *VoiceReference `json:"reference,omitempty"`
	Options   llm.Options     `json:"options,omitempty"`
}
```

SpeakInput is what to say and how.

### Speech

```go
type Speech interface {
	// Speak reads the text aloud and returns the audio.
	//
	//op: POST speak
	Speak(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in SpeakInput) (Result, error)
	// Voices lists a model's voices, when the provider says.
	//
	//op: POST voices scope=llm:read
	Voices(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in VoicesInput) (VoiceList, error)
	// Models lists the speech models of every provider in Settings → LLM.
	//
	//op: GET models scope=llm:read
	Models(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.ModelsInput) (llm.Models, error)
}
```

Speech turns text into audio.

### Voice

```go
type Voice struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Name     string `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Language string `json:"language,omitempty"`
	Gender   string `json:"gender,omitempty"`
	// Mode is how the voice is made, when the provider says: "builtin" (a speaker the model has), "design" (a new
	// voice described in Instructions) or "clone" (the voice of a Reference clip). A model with a "clone" voice
	// clones.
	Mode        string `json:"mode,omitempty"`
	Description string `json:"description,omitempty"`
}
```

Voice is one voice.

### VoiceList

```go
type VoiceList struct {
	Voices []Voice `json:"voices"`
}
```

VoiceList is a model's voices.

### VoiceList.Clones

```go
func (l VoiceList) Clones() bool
```

Clones reports whether a model's voices include a clone voice, so a Reference works with it.

### VoiceReference

```go
type VoiceReference struct {
	// Audio is the clip, with its data: a short, clean recording (10 to 30 seconds) read the way the model should
	// speak. Its Name's extension (me.wav) or Type tells the provider the format.
	Audio llm.File `json:"audio"`
	// Text is what the clip says, word for word. Optional, but most models match the voice more closely with it.
	Text string `json:"text,omitempty"`
}
```

VoiceReference is a clip of the voice to imitate.

### VoicesInput

```go
type VoicesInput struct {
	Model string `json:"model"` // "provider/model", required
}
```

VoicesInput names the model whose voices to list.

# textv1

```go
import textv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/text/v1"
```

Package textv1 is the llm.text/v1 contract: a language model answers a prompt or a conversation. Each call names its model as provider/model ("vultr/glm-5.2"), a provider being one the app's admins added in Settings → LLM.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/llm.text/v1. In pb\_hooks it's $llm.text.

Source: [`ext/contracts/llm/text/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/llm/text/v1).

### CompleteInput

```go
type CompleteInput struct {
	// Model is "provider/model" (required).
	Model    string    `json:"model"`
	System   string    `json:"system,omitempty"`
	Prompt   string    `json:"prompt,omitempty"`
	Messages []Message `json:"messages,omitempty"`
	// Schema, when set, is a JSON schema the answer must match; the result's Data is then the parsed answer.
	Schema json.RawMessage `json:"schema,omitempty"`
	// MaxTokens caps the answer's length, thinking included (0: the provider's default).
	MaxTokens   int      `json:"maxTokens,omitempty"`
	Temperature *float64 `json:"temperature,omitempty"` // nil: the provider's default
	Stop        []string `json:"stop,omitempty"`
	// Reasoning is how much a reasoning model thinks first: "" (its default), "off", "low" or "high". A model that
	// doesn't reason ignores it.
	Reasoning string      `json:"reasoning,omitempty"`
	Options   llm.Options `json:"options,omitempty"`
	// Enrich adds the best passages from the app's search buckets after the prompt (search/v1).
	Enrich *llm.Enrich `json:"enrich,omitempty"`
}
```

CompleteInput is a prompt: Prompt, or Messages for a conversation (Prompt is then added as the last user message).

### CompleteResult

```go
type CompleteResult struct {
	Text string          `json:"text"`
	Data json.RawMessage `json:"data,omitempty"` // the parsed answer, when a Schema was given
	// Reasoning is the model's thinking, when the provider returns it separately.
	Reasoning  string    `json:"reasoning,omitempty"`
	StopReason string    `json:"stopReason,omitempty"` // "stop", "length" or "cancelled"
	Model      string    `json:"model"`                // the provider/model that answered
	Usage      llm.Usage `json:"usage"`
	// Passages are what Enrich added to the prompt, best first (cite them, or show where the answer came from).
	Passages []llm.Passage `json:"passages,omitempty"`
}
```

CompleteResult is the model's answer.

### CountInput

```go
type CountInput struct {
	Model    string    `json:"model,omitempty"` // optional: the count is an estimate either way
	Text     string    `json:"text,omitempty"`
	System   string    `json:"system,omitempty"`
	Messages []Message `json:"messages,omitempty"`
}
```

CountInput is a text, or a conversation as a call would send it.

### CountResult

```go
type CountResult struct {
	Tokens int  `json:"tokens"`
	Exact  bool `json:"exact"`
}
```

CountResult is a token count. Exact is false when it's an estimate (about four characters a token).

### Message

```go
type Message struct {
	Role    string `json:"role"` // system, user or assistant
	Content string `json:"content"`
}
```

Message is one turn of a conversation.

### Text

```go
type Text interface {
	// Complete answers a prompt or a conversation.
	//
	//op: POST complete
	Complete(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in CompleteInput) (CompleteResult, error)
	// Stream answers like Complete, sending the answer as it's written: a chunk with text (or reasoning) for each
	// piece, then one with done and the whole result.
	//
	//op: POST stream
	Stream(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in CompleteInput) (extkit.Stream, error)
	// Count says about how many tokens a text or a conversation is, for budgeting what to send.
	//
	//op: POST count scope=llm:read
	Count(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in CountInput) (CountResult, error)
	// Models lists the text models of every provider in Settings → LLM.
	//
	//op: GET models scope=llm:read
	Models(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.ModelsInput) (llm.Models, error)
}
```

Text answers prompts with a language model.

### Video

```go
type Video interface {
	// Create starts making a video. With Wait it returns once the job is done (or failed); otherwise at once, to
	// follow with Get. A done job lists how many files it made (Outputs); Content fetches each.
	//
	//op: POST create
	Create(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in CreateInput) (llm.Job, error)
	// Get says how a job is going.
	//
	//op: POST get scope=llm:read
	Get(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.JobRef) (llm.Job, error)
	// Content fetches one of a done job's files.
	//
	//op: POST content scope=llm:read
	Content(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.ContentInput) (llm.File, error)
	// Models lists the video models of every provider in Settings → LLM.
	//
	//op: GET models scope=llm:read
	Models(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in llm.ModelsInput) (llm.Models, error)
}
```

Video makes videos.

# fallbackv1

```go
import fallbackv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1"
```

Package fallbackv1 is the mail.fallback/v1 contract: where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off. Providers form an ordered chain (\`providers: { mail.fallback/v1: \[mailtrap, mailrelay] }\` sets the order): each sends a message or passes it on with [ErrPass](#errpass); when every provider passes, PocketBase sends it its own way (sendmail).

Providers: mailtrap (dev mode: a local inbox), mailrelay (a multisite host's relay), or an app's own pb\_hooks. Each provider calls [Bind](#bind) when it registers; Bind owns the app's mail hook, once.

Source: [`ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Sender]("mail.fallback/v1", extkit.Many).JS(extkit.JSOpen, func(o *extkit.JSObject) Sender { return jsSender{o} }).JSTypes(jsTypes)
```

Contract is mail.fallback/v1.

<a id="errpass"></a>

```go
var ErrPass = errors.New("mail.fallback: passed")
```

ErrPass is a provider's "not mine": the next provider (or PocketBase) sends the message.

## Functions

### Bind

```go
func Bind(app core.App)
```

Bind makes app's mail go through mail.fallback/v1's providers whenever its SMTP is off. Providers call it in Register; it binds the hook once per app, last (the app's own onMailerSend hooks run, and may change the message, first).

## Types

```go
}
```

Sender delivers an app's mail when its SMTP is off.

# feedbackv1

```go
import feedbackv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/mail/feedback/v1"
```

Package feedbackv1 is the mail.feedback/v1 contract: what mail providers report back about mail an app sent (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes), received at one place and turned into \[Event]s that any extension can act on. The provider receives the reports (Amazon SES through SNS, or a generic webhook); handlers bind [OnEvent](#onevent): a suppression list adds the address, a CRM marks the contact.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/mail.feedback/v1. Its operations are public: SES messages are checked by their SNS signature, webhook calls by a shared secret.

Source: [`ext/contracts/mail/feedback/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/mail/feedback/v1).

```go
	Complaint   = "complaint"   // the recipient marked it as spam
	Unsubscribe = "unsubscribe" // the recipient asked to stop
)
```

Kinds of feedback.

# suppressionv1

```go
import suppressionv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/mail/suppression/v1"
```

Package suppressionv1 is the mail.suppression/v1 contract: addresses an app must not send bulk mail to (unsubscribed, bounced, complained), and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries. Anything that sends to many people checks it; whatever provides it keeps the list.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/mail.suppression/v1. The unsubscribe operations are public: the link in a message is signed by the provider, and mail providers POST to it for one-click unsubscribes (RFC 8058).

Source: [`ext/contracts/mail/suppression/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/mail/suppression/v1).

```go
	Complained   = "complained"
	Manual       = "manual"
)
```

Reasons an address is suppressed.

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "suppression", func(inner List, g *extkit.Guard[List]) List {
	return &guardList{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[List]{
		Name:   "check",
		Desc:   "Says whether an address is suppressed, and why.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "check",
		Scope:  "suppression:read",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(Address{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl List, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in Address
			if err := extkit.DecodeQuery(req.Query, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Check(ctx, a, in)
		},
```

# mcpv1

```go
import mcpv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/mcp/v1"
```

Package mcpv1 is the mcp/v1 contract: the app's Model Context Protocol endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it. The endpoint stays at /mcp, the one path people paste: MCP versions itself in the protocol, and OAuth tokens are bound to the resource URL.

The contract owns what every provider serves the same way: the routes (/mcp and its protected resource metadata under /.well-known/), and the tools. Tools come from three places: every wire contract the app provides (its operations, called through the contract, so the same scope check and hooks apply), tools extensions add with [AddTool](#addtool), and the provider's own (ext/mcp's pb\_\* tools over the REST API). Swap the provider and the contract tools stay.

Source: [`ext/contracts/mcp/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/mcp/v1).

## Constants

<a id="metadatapath"></a>

```go
const MetadataPath = "/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" + Path
```

MetadataPath is its protected resource metadata (RFC 9728); the bare well-known path answers too.

<a id="path"></a>

```go
const Path = "/mcp"
```

Path is where the endpoint is served.

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Endpoint]("mcp/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is mcp/v1.

## Functions

### AddInstructions

```go
func AddInstructions(app core.App, text string)
```

AddInstructions adds a paragraph to what the server tells clients when they connect (what your tools are for).

### AddTool

```go
func AddTool(app core.App, t Tool)
```

AddTool adds a tool to app's MCP server (call it in Register). A second tool with the same name replaces the first.

### Bind

```go
func Bind(app core.App)
```

Bind serves the provider's endpoint at /mcp and its metadata on app. Providers call it in Register; it binds once.

### Instructions

```go
func Instructions(app core.App) []string
```

Instructions are the paragraphs extensions added.

## Types

### Endpoint

```go
type Endpoint interface {
	// ServeMCP answers one request to /mcp (Streamable HTTP: POST; GET and DELETE answer 405 without sessions).
	ServeMCP(e *core.RequestEvent) error
	// Metadata is the protected resource metadata for /mcp: where clients sign in.
	Metadata(e *core.RequestEvent) map[string]any
}
```

Endpoint is an app's MCP server.

### Tool

```go
type Tool struct {
	// Name: lowercase `<extension>_<verb>_<noun>`, unique per app.
	Name        string
	Title       string
	Description string
	// InputSchema is a JSON Schema object for the arguments (nil: none).
	InputSchema map[string]any
	ReadOnly    bool
	Destructive bool
	// Scope is the token scope a connection limited to scopes needs to see and call it ("" for any).
	Scope string
	// SuperuserOnly hides it from other callers in tools/list (presentation: Call still decides).
	SuperuserOnly bool
	// Call runs it as a (the signed-in caller, as extkit.Auth); the result is any JSON-able value.
	Call func(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, args json.RawMessage) (any, error)
}
```

Tool is a tool an extension adds to the app's MCP server, whoever provides it.

### Tools

```go
func Tools(app core.App) []Tool
```

Tools are the tools every provider serves on app, by name: every provided wire contract's operations, then the ones extensions added (which win on a name clash).

# oauthv1

```go
import oauthv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/oauth/v1"
```

Package oauthv1 is the oauth/v1 contract: an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app (authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, dynamic and metadata-document client registration), so the CLI and MCP clients like Claude can sign in. ext/api-tokens provides it.

A routed contract: the OAuth specs fix its shape, so its provider serves its own routes under /api/\_c/oauth/v1/:

	GET|POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize         sign in and consent (browser)
	POST     /api/_c/oauth/v1/token             codes and refresh tokens for access tokens
	POST     /api/_c/oauth/v1/device            start a device-code sign-in
	GET|POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify     enter the device code (browser)
	POST     /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke            revoke a token
	POST     /api/_c/oauth/v1/register          dynamic client registration (when on)
	GET|POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...)

Its metadata stays where RFC 8414 puts it: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

Source: [`ext/contracts/oauth/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/oauth/v1).

## Constants

<a id="metadatapath"></a>

```go

```

MetadataPath is where the server's metadata lives (RFC 8414 fixes it at the root): a client that finds oauth/v1 in whoami's contracts reads it here.

# remotev1

```go
import remotev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/remote/v1"
```

Package remotev1 is the remote/v1 contract: remote control of an app. It's the base every client can rely on (who you are, the app's status, restart, logs); contracts that add an area, like deploy/v1, require it.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/remote/v1; whoami at its root is the one fixed path a client starts from. A standalone app gets it from ext/remotes; a multisite host provides it for its instances (so it works for stock images too).

Source: [`ext/contracts/remote/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Remote]("remote/v1", extkit.One).HostProvidable().JS(extkit.JSHooks, nil).JSTypes(jsTypes)
```

Contract is remote/v1.

<a id="w"></a>

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "remote", func(inner Remote, g *extkit.Guard[Remote]) Remote {
	return &guardRemote{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[Remote]{
		Name:   "whoami",
		Desc:   "Says who the credential is, the app's name and URL, and the contracts it offers.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "",
		Scope:  "public",
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Remote, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			return impl.Whoami(ctx, a)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Remote]{
		Name:   "status",
		Desc:   "Reports whether the app is running, its versions, uptime and mode.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "status",
		Scope:  "remote:read",
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Remote, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			return impl.Status(ctx, a)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Remote]{
		Name:   "restart",
		Desc:   "Restarts the app; requests in flight finish first.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "restart",
		Scope:  "remote",
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Remote, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			return impl.Restart(ctx, a)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Remote]{
		Name:   "logs",
		Desc:   "Streams the app's log: the last entries, then new ones as they're written.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "logs",
		Scope:  "remote:read",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(LogsInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutStream,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Remote, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in LogsInput
			if err := extkit.DecodeQuery(req.Query, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.Logs(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
)
```

W is remote/v1's wire side: routes at /api/\_c/remote/v1/\<op>, action hooks, MCP tools and the client.

### Remote

```go
type Remote interface {
	// Whoami says who the credential is, the app's name and URL, and the contracts it offers.
	//
	//op: GET / scope=public
	Whoami(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth) (Whoami, error)

	// Status reports whether the app is running, its versions, uptime and mode.
	//
	//op: GET status scope=remote:read
	Status(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth) (Status, error)

	// Restart restarts the app; requests in flight finish first.
	//
	//op: POST restart scope=remote
	Restart(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth) (RestartResult, error)

	// Logs streams the app's log: the last entries, then new ones as they're written.
	//
	//op: GET logs scope=remote:read
	Logs(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in LogsInput) (extkit.Stream, error)
}
```

Remote controls an app from afar.

### Whoami

```go
type Whoami struct {
	Auth *Identity `json:"auth"` // nil for an anonymous caller
	// Via: "token" (API token), "jwt", or "" (anonymous).
	Via     string   `json:"via"`
	Scopes  []string `json:"scopes"` // a token's scopes; empty: the owner's full rights
	TokenID string   `json:"tokenId,omitempty"`
	App     App      `json:"app"`
	// Contracts are the wire contracts the app offers ("deploy/v1"): each at /api/_c/<id>/.
	Contracts []string `json:"contracts"`
	// Extensions are the extensions running on the app; only for a signed-in caller.
	Extensions []string `json:"extensions,omitempty"`
}
```

Whoami is who a credential is and what the app offers.

# remoteclient

```go
import remoteclient "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient"
```

Package remoteclient is remote/v1's CLI client: the remotes a project links (.pocketone/remotes.yaml), saved logins, sign-in (an API token, a password, or OAuth in the browser or with a device code), and an authenticated HTTP client for a remote. ext/remotes' commands and other extensions' commands (deploy) build on it.

Package remotes gives the command named remotes: other PocketBase instances (or PocketHost instances) a project deploys to, signed in once with \`pocketone login\`.

	pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com
	pocketone login prod
	pocketone deploy prod

Remote names and URLs live in the project's .pocketbase/remotes.json (commit it); secrets live in the user's ~/.config/pocketone/credentials.json (0600), keyed by URL. P1\_TOKEN overrides the saved login (CI sets it). The folder is named after [extkit.Command](/pocketone.dev/ext/extkit#Command) (~/.config/pockethost in that build); the variables are PocketOne's (P1\_) in every build.

The server half is remote/v1's whoami (GET /api/\_c/remote/v1): who the request's token is, its scopes, and which contracts the app offers (deploy/v1, oauth/v1, api-tokens/v1, ...), so clients discover what a remote supports.

Source: [`ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient).

<a id="passwordtokenttl"></a>

```go
const PasswordTokenTTL = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
```

PasswordTokenTTL is how long a password login lasts: the session is swapped for a token of this length (PocketBase's impersonate, which a superuser may do for itself), so it lasts like a browser login. Changing the superuser's password ends it.

<a id="openbrowser"></a>

```go
var OpenBrowser = func(u string) error {
	switch runtime.GOOS {
	case "darwin":
		return exec.Command("open", u).Start()
	case "windows":
		return exec.Command("rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", u).Start()
	default:
		return exec.Command("xdg-open", u).Start()
	}
}
```

OpenBrowser opens url in the user's browser (overridable for tests).

<a id="retrysleep"></a>

```go
var RetrySleep = func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error {
	t := time.NewTimer(d)
	defer t.Stop()
	select {
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	case <-t.C:
		return nil
	}
}
```

RetrySleep waits d before a rate-limited request is sent again, or until ctx ends (overridable for tests).


### Credential

```go
type Credential struct {
	Token string `json:"token"`
	// Via: "token" (a pasted pbt_ or PocketHost token), "jwt" (a pasted PocketBase auth token), "oauth".
	Via          string    `json:"via"`
	Email        string    `json:"email,omitempty"`
	Collection   string    `json:"collection,omitempty"`
```

### LoginOptions

```go
type LoginOptions struct {
	// Token, if set, is used as is (pbt_..., a PocketHost token, or a JWT).
	Token string
	// TokenFrom, if set, gives the token on its first line (--token-stdin).
	TokenFrom io.Reader
	// Browser is the OAuth sign-in tried first on a remote that offers oauth/v1 (normally [OAuthLogin]); nil skips it.
	// It may return (nil, nil) to fall back to the token prompt.
	Browser   func(ctx context.Context, c *Client, w *Whoami, opts BrowserLoginOptions) (*LoginResult, error)
	Device    bool // device code instead of a browser redirect
	NoBrowser bool // print the sign-in URL instead of opening a browser
	// Prompt is where the sign-in is asked for when nothing else signed in (a superuser's email, or a pasted token);
	// nil means there's no terminal to ask in.
	Prompt io.Reader
	// Password reads a password without echoing it (nil: read a line from Prompt).
	Password func(prompt string) (string, error)
	// Out gets the prompts and the result line.
	Out io.Writer
}
```

LoginOptions configure [Login](#login).

### LoginResult

```go
type LoginResult struct {
	Credential *Credential
	// Warning, if set, is shown to the user.
	Warning string
	// TokenId is the API token's id, when the remote reports one.
	TokenId string
}
```

LoginResult is a finished sign-in, ready to save.

### Login

```go
func Login(ctx context.Context, c *Client, opts LoginOptions) (*LoginResult, error)
```

Login signs in to the client's remote, saves the login and says who it signed in as: with opts.Token or opts.TokenFrom when given, else in the browser when the remote offers OAuth, else at opts.Prompt with a superuser's email and password ([PasswordLogin](#passwordlogin)) or a pasted token. It's the sign-in behind \`login\`, \`link\` and \`clone\`.

### LoginWithToken

```go
func LoginWithToken(ctx context.Context, c *Client, token string) (*LoginResult, error)
```

LoginWithToken checks a pasted token (pbt\_..., a PocketHost token, or a JWT) with the remote's whoami when it has one; a remote without whoami (a PocketHost edge today) takes it as is.

### OAuthLogin

```go
func OAuthLogin(ctx context.Context, c *Client, w *Whoami, opts BrowserLoginOptions) (*LoginResult, error)
```

OAuthLogin signs in through the remote's OAuth server: the browser with a loopback redirect and PKCE, or a device code (opts.Device, or when no browser can be opened here).

### PasswordLogin

```go
func PasswordLogin(ctx context.Context, c *Client, email, password string) (*LoginResult, error)
```

PasswordLogin signs in as one of the remote's superusers with email and password, through PocketBase's own auth API. It's for a remote with no browser sign-in (stock PocketBase, such as an instance a multisite host runs in Docker): the host checks the superuser's token with the instance. The session token is swapped for one of [PasswordTokenTTL](#passwordtokenttl) when the remote allows it.

### Whoami

```go
type Whoami struct {
	Auth *struct {
		Collection string `json:"collection"`
		Id         string `json:"id"`
		Email      string `json:"email"`
	} `json:"auth"`
	// Via: "token" (API token), "jwt", or "" (anonymous).
	Via     string   `json:"via"`
	Scopes  []string `json:"scopes"`
	TokenId string   `json:"tokenId"`
	// Contracts are the wire contracts the remote offers ("remote/v1", "deploy/v1"), each at /api/_c/<id>/.
	Contracts []string `json:"contracts"`
	App       struct {
		Name string `json:"name"`
		URL  string `json:"url"`
	} `json:"app"`
}
```

Whoami is remote/v1's whoami (GET /api/\_c/remote/v1).

### Whoami.Offers

```go
func (w *Whoami) Offers(id string) bool
```

Offers reports whether the remote offers a contract ("deploy/v1"): its API is at /api/\_c/\<id>/.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/restore/v1

# restorev1

```go
import restorev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/restore/v1"
```

Package restorev1 is the restore/v1 contract: put an app's data back as it was at a moment. Its providers differ in how close they get: pitr restores any second in its window (continuous history); the default restores the latest backup at or before the moment. Both answer the same calls, so a client (the dashboard, the CLI, an agent) asks for "Tuesday 15:00" and gets the closest the app can do, and is told which point it got.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/restore/v1; a multisite host may provide it for its instances (from host-level snapshots).

Source: [`ext/contracts/restore/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1).

## Constants

<a id="continuous"></a><a id="snapshots"></a>

```go
const (
	Continuous = "continuous" // any moment inside Window
	Snapshots  = "snapshots"  // only the moments in Snapshots
)
```

Kinds of points.

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Restorer]("restore/v1", extkit.One).HostProvidable().JS(extkit.JSHooks, nil).JSTypes(jsTypes)
```

Contract is restore/v1.

<a id="errbusy"></a>

```go
var ErrBusy = &extkit.Error{Code: "busy", Message: "a restore is already running", Status: 409}
```

ErrBusy: a restore is already running.

<a id="errnopoint"></a>

```go
var ErrNoPoint = &extkit.Error{Code: "no_point", Message: "nothing to restore from at or before that moment", Status: 422}
```

ErrNoPoint: nothing to restore from at or before the moment asked for.

<a id="w"></a>

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "restore", func(inner Restorer, g *extkit.Guard[Restorer]) Restorer {
	return &guardRestorer{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[Restorer]{
		Name:   "points",
		Desc:   "Says what the app's data can be restored to: a window of time (continuous history) or a list of moments (backups), and whether a restore is running.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "",
		Scope:  "restore:read",
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Restorer, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			return impl.Points(ctx, a)
		},
	},
	extkit.Op[Restorer]{
		Name:   "restore_to",
		Desc:   "Puts the app's data back as it was at the given moment, from the latest point at or before it. The app restarts to apply it; its current data is kept aside until the next restore.",
		Method: "POST",
		Path:   "restore",
		Scope:  "restore",
		In:     reflect.TypeOf(RestoreInput{}),
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Restorer, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			var in RestoreInput
			if err := extkit.DecodeInput(req.JSON, &in); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return impl.RestoreTo(ctx, a, in)
		},
	},
)
```

W is restore/v1's wire side: routes at /api/\_c/restore/v1/\<op>, action hooks, MCP tools and the client.

# runtimev1

```go
import runtimev1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/runtime/v1"
```

Package runtimev1 is the runtime/v1 contract: what runs a multisite host's instances (ext/pocker as isolates, ext/docker in containers). A host runs exactly one: every instance runs on it. When more than one is registered, \`providers: { runtime/v1: docker }\` picks.

A host-scope service contract: providers register on the host's scope (ProvideIn), not on an app.

Source: [`ext/contracts/runtime/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/runtime/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Runtime]("runtime/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is runtime/v1, on a host's scope.

## Types

### Exit

```go
type Exit struct {
	InstanceID string
	Err        error
	// Restarting: the runtime starts the instance again right away (its pb_hooks or settings changed), so the host
	// reports it as starting and asks its health endpoint again instead of reporting it idle.
	Restarting bool
}
```

Exit is an instance's process ending. Err is nil for a stop the runtime chose (idle, powered off, removed, restarting with new settings or files) and set when it ended on its own (crashed, exited during startup).

### ExitNotifier

```go
type ExitNotifier interface {
	OnExit(fn func(Exit))
}
```

ExitNotifier tells the host each time an instance stops running (or fails to start), so the host's supervisor knows without polling. The host calls OnExit once, before Start. The runtime calls fn synchronously, in order, possibly while it holds its own locks, so fn must return quickly and never call back into the runtime from that goroutine.

### HealthChecker

```go
type HealthChecker interface {
	HealthCheck(instanceID string) (path string, anyStatus bool)
}
```

HealthChecker tells the host's supervisor how to ask a started instance whether it's up: the path (default /api/health) and whether any answer from the instance counts, not only 200 (releases without a health endpoint). Without it the host asks /api/health and wants 200.

### Prechecker

```go
type Prechecker interface {
	Precheck(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, inst sourcev1.Instance) bool
}
```

Prechecker runs before the gates admit a request for a local instance, e.g. to answer 503 for an instance under maintenance, without counting it against rate limits. false = answered.

### RunningLister

```go
type RunningLister interface {
	RunningIDs() []string
}
```

RunningLister lists the instances running now, including ones adopted at Start (containers that kept running across a host restart), so the host's supervisor can confirm them.

### Runtime

```go
type Runtime interface {
	// Name identifies the runtime ("pocker", "docker"), for logs and the host's startup lines.
	Name() string
	// Serves reports whether this runtime can run inst (e.g. its PocketBase version); the host refuses one it can't.
	Serves(inst sourcev1.Instance) bool
	// ServeInstance serves a request for inst, starting it on demand. The host has already resolved the instance,
	// admitted the request (gates) and decided it runs here.
	ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, inst sourcev1.Instance)
	// Ready reports whether the runtime can take requests.
	Ready() bool
}
```

Runtime runs instances on this host.

### Shutdowner

```go
type Shutdowner interface {
	Shutdown()
}
```

Shutdowner is called when the host stops.

### Starter

```go
type Starter interface {
	Start(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

Starter runs once before the host listens, e.g. to adopt containers that kept running across a restart. An error stops the host from starting.

### Statser

```go
type Statser interface {
	RunningCount() int
}
```

Statser reports how many instances it has running, for the health route.

### Syncer

```go
type Syncer interface {
	Sync(c sourcev1.Change, prev *sourcev1.Instance)
}
```

Syncer hears directory changes (stop removed instances, restart changed ones).

# settingsv1

```go
import settingsv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/settings/v1"
```

Package settingsv1 is the settings/v1 contract: the settings an app's admins change for its extensions (pitr's S3 bucket, bulkmail's sending limits), one API for all of them. Each extension registers its section with [Add](#add); the contract's provider (ext/settings) lists them, reads, saves and tests them.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/settings/v1. Settings an operator sets for a whole host stay in pocketone.yaml; these are the ones the app's own superusers change.

Source: [`ext/contracts/settings/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/settings/v1).

# templatesv1

```go
import templatesv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/templates/v1"
```

Package templatesv1 is the templates/v1 contract: an extension's own pages as a set of Go html/template files that a project can override. An extension adds its set (usually go:embed) under a name; the provider renders a page from the set, taking the project's copy of any file it has, and ejects the set for the project to edit.

A set is every \*.tpl file in an fs.FS, at any depth. Each file is one template named by its path without ".tpl" ("signin", "parts/head"), so pages include pieces with {{template "parts/head" .}}.

Source: [`ext/contracts/templates/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/templates/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Templates]("templates/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is templates/v1.

## Functions

### Add

```go
func Add(app core.App, name string, files fs.FS)
```

Add registers an extension's template set on app under name (call it in Register). name is a plain folder name ("oauth"): the project's copy lives in a folder of that name.

### Names

```go
func Names(app core.App) []string
```

Names lists the sets added on app, sorted (for providers).

### Parse

```go
func Parse(base, overlay fs.FS) (*template.Template, error)
```

Parse builds a set's templates: every \*.tpl in base, then every \*.tpl in overlay (nil for none), which replaces the template of the same name. Providers and an extension rendering its own set without a provider both use it.

### Set

```go
func Set(app core.App, name string) (fs.FS, bool)
```

Set returns the files added under name (for providers).

### Write

```go
func Write(e *core.RequestEvent, t *template.Template, page string, status int, data any) error
```

Write executes page of t with data and writes it as the whole HTML response to e (status 0 = 200). Nothing is written if the template fails.

## Types

### ExistsError

```go
type ExistsError struct{ Files []string }
```

ExistsError is Eject's refusal: the project's copies of these files differ from the built-in ones.

### ExistsError.Error

```go
func (e *ExistsError) Error() string
```

### Templates

```go
type Templates interface {
	// Render writes page of set name as the whole response to e (status 0 = 200), with data as the template's dot.
	// Each template comes from the project's copy when it has one, else from the set.
	Render(e *core.RequestEvent, name, page string, status int, data any) error

	// Eject copies set name's files into the project's copy, for the project to edit. Files the copy lacks are written
	// and files identical to the built-in ones are left alone; files that differ (the project's edits) are only
	// overwritten with force: otherwise it refuses with an *ExistsError naming them, writing nothing. It returns the
	// files written.
	Eject(name string, force bool) (written []string, err error)
}
```

Templates renders and ejects the sets added with [Add](#add).

# tlsv1

```go
import tlsv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/tls/v1"
```

Package tlsv1 is the tls/v1 contract: the TLS of a multisite host's main listener (automatic certificates). With no provider the host uses the certificate files in its \`server\` section, or plain HTTP.

A host-scope service contract: providers register on the host's scope (ProvideIn), not on an app.

Source: [`ext/contracts/tls/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/tls/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Provider]("tls/v1", extkit.One)
```

Contract is tls/v1, on a host's scope.

## Types

### Provider

```go
type Provider interface {
	TLS(ctx context.Context, served func(host string) bool) (cfg *tls.Config, httpHandler func(http.Handler) http.Handler, err error)
}
```

Provider supplies the main listener's TLS. served reports whether a hostname belongs to an instance, for providers that must not issue certificates for anything else. httpHandler, if not nil, wraps the plain-HTTP listener's handler (tls.http\_listen), e.g. to answer ACME challenges. A nil config means "not this time" (the host falls back to its certificate files or plain HTTP).

# vacuumv1

```go
import vacuumv1 "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/vacuum/v1"
```

Package vacuumv1 is the vacuum/v1 contract: an app's databases are compacted (SQLite VACUUM) so space freed by deleted records goes back to the disk, and its admins can see when that last happened. On a single app the vacuum extension does it, on a schedule its admins set; a multisite host may provide it for its instances instead, compacting them on its own schedule, and then the app's admins see its status but have no setting.

A wire contract at /api/\_c/vacuum/v1.

Source: [`ext/contracts/vacuum/v1`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/vacuum/v1).

## Variables

<a id="contract"></a>

```go
var Contract = extkit.NewContract[Vacuum]("vacuum/v1", extkit.One).HostProvidable()
```

Contract is vacuum/v1.

<a id="w"></a>

```go
var W = extkit.NewWire(Contract, "vacuum", func(inner Vacuum, g *extkit.Guard[Vacuum]) Vacuum {
	return &guardVacuum{inner, g}
},
	extkit.Op[Vacuum]{
		Name:   "status",
		Desc:   "Says who compacts the app's databases, whether and how often, and how the last run went.",
		Method: "GET",
		Path:   "",
		Scope:  "vacuum:read",
		Out:    extkit.OutJSON,
		Invoke: func(ctx context.Context, impl Vacuum, a extkit.Auth, req extkit.OpRequest) (any, error) {
			return impl.Status(ctx, a)
		},
	},
)
```

W is vacuum/v1's wire side: routes at /api/\_c/vacuum/v1/\<op>, action hooks, MCP tools and the client.

## Functions

### OnStatus

```go
func OnStatus(owner any, fn func(e *extkit.CallEvent) error)
```

OnStatus binds fn to status calls on owner (an app, or a host's scope for calls the host answers). Call e.Next() to continue; return an error to refuse.

## Types

### Client

```go
type Client struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Client is vacuum/v1 over HTTP, for the CLI and other apps. It implements Vacuum; the token it was made with is the credential, so the extkit.Auth argument is ignored.

### NewClient

```go
func NewClient(baseURL, token string, hc *http.Client) *Client
```

NewClient calls vacuum/v1 on the app at baseURL with token (a PocketBase auth token or an API token).

### Client.Status

```go
func (c *Client) Status(ctx context.Context, _ extkit.Auth) (Status, error)
```

### Run

```go
type Run struct {
	At      time.Time `json:"at"`
	Saved   int64     `json:"saved"`             // bytes given back to the disk
	Skipped []string  `json:"skipped,omitempty"` // databases with too little free space to be worth it
	Error   string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
}
```

Run is one pass over the app's databases.

### Status

```go
type Status struct {
	Provider string     `json:"provider"` // who compacts: "vacuum" (the app itself) or a host
	Enabled  bool       `json:"enabled"`
	Every    string     `json:"every,omitempty"` // how often, e.g. "168h"
	Last     *Run       `json:"last,omitempty"`
	Next     *time.Time `json:"next,omitempty"`
}
```

Status is the app's vacuum status.

### Vacuum

```go
type Vacuum interface {
	// Status says who compacts the app's databases, whether and how often, and how the last run went.
	//
	//op: GET / scope=vacuum:read
	Status(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth) (Status, error)
}
```

Vacuum reports on compacting the app's databases.

# API Tokens JavaScript API

Everything the [API Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## $apiTokens

API token scopes.

```js
$apiTokens.registerScope({ name: "notes:write", description: "Change notes", paths: ["/api/collections/notes/records"] })
routerAdd("POST", "/api/notes/archive", (e) => { ... }, $apis.requireAuth(), $apiTokens.requireScope("notes:write"))
```

### $apiTokens.registerScope()

```ts
$apiTokens.registerScope(def: tokens.ScopeDef): void
```

Registers a scope (top level of a pb_hooks file); the same name again merges.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `def` | `tokens.ScopeDef` |  |

### $apiTokens.requireScope()

```ts
$apiTokens.requireScope(name: string): any
```

Route middleware: a token, if the request uses one, must hold the scope.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |

Returns `any`.

### $apiTokens.hasScope()

```ts
$apiTokens.hasScope(e: core.RequestEvent, name: string, value?: string): boolean
```

Whether the request may use the scope (always true without a token). With a value: whether it may use the scope
on that value (it holds the bare scope, or "name=value").

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | `core.RequestEvent` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `value` | `string` (optional) |  |

Returns `boolean`.

### $apiTokens.scopeValues()

```ts
$apiTokens.scopeValues(e: core.RequestEvent, name: string): { all: boolean; values: string[] }
```

The values the request holds the scope for: all is true for every value.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `e` | `core.RequestEvent` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  |

Returns `{ all: boolean; values: string[] }`.

### $apiTokens.ruleField()

```ts
$apiTokens.ruleField(name: string): string
```

The collection-rule field for the scope.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |

Returns `string`.

### $apiTokens.scopes()

```ts
$apiTokens.scopes(): tokens.Scope[]
```

Every registered scope.

Returns `tokens.Scope[]`.

## Types

### tokens.ScopeDef

A scope API tokens and OAuth clients can be granted.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | e.g. "notes:read". |
| `description?` | `string` |  |
| `paths?` | `string[]` | Path prefixes the scope covers. |
| `methods?` | `string[]` | HTTP methods it covers (all when empty). |
| `collections?` | `string[]` | Collections whose record APIs it covers. |
| `values?` | `{ description: string }` | Lets a token hold the scope for some values only, written "name=value" (e.g. "notes=abc123"); the bare name still means every value. Routes check the value with hasScope(e, name, value). |

### tokens.Scope

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `header` | `string` | The request header a token's scope shows up in. |
| `ruleField` | `string` | The field to use in collection rules, e.g. "@request.headers.x_token_scope_notes_read". |

# Key-Value Store JavaScript API

Everything the [Key-Value Store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/kv) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## $kv

The app's key-value store (ext/kv, the kv/v1 contract): named JSON values kept without a collection or a migration,
in PocketBase's _params, so they ride along in backups. Names are 1 to 128 characters: letters, digits and
_ - . : / , starting with a letter or digit; start yours with a prefix of your own ("myapp/settings"). Values are any
JSON up to 1 MiB. Every call is local and sync.

### $kv.get()

```ts
$kv.get(name: string): any
```

The value stored under a name, parsed from its JSON.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | the value's name, such as "myapp/settings" |

Returns `any`: the value, or null when the name has none.

```js
const settings = $kv.get("myapp/settings") ?? { theme: "light" }
```

Go: [`kvv1.Get`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/kv/v1#get).

### $kv.set()

```ts
$kv.set(name: string, value: any): void
```

Stores a value under a name, replacing any value it had.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | the value's name, such as "myapp/settings" |
| `value` | `any` | anything JSON.stringify takes, up to 1 MiB as JSON |

```js
$kv.set("myapp/settings", { theme: "dark", lastRun: new Date().toISOString() })
```

Go: [`kvv1.Set`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/kv/v1#set).

### $kv.delete()

```ts
$kv.delete(name: string): void
```

Removes a name's value. Removing a name with no value isn't an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | the value's name |

```js
$kv.delete("myapp/settings")
```

Go: [`kvv1.Delete`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/kv/v1#delete).

### $kv.list()

```ts
$kv.list(prefix?: string): KvEntry[]
```

The values whose names start with a prefix, sorted by name.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix` | `string` (optional) | the start every name shares, such as "myapp/"; omit it for every value |

Returns `KvEntry[]`.

```js
for (const e of $kv.list("myapp/")) console.log(e.name, e.updated)
```

Go: [`kvv1.List`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/kv/v1#list).

## Types

### KvEntry

One value in the app's key-value store.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Its name. |
| `value` | `any` | The value, parsed from its JSON. |
| `created` | `string` | When it was first stored (ISO 8601, UTC). |
| `updated` | `string` | When it last changed (ISO 8601, UTC). |

Go: [`kvv1.Entry`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/kv/v1#entry).

# LLM JavaScript API

Everything the [LLM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## $llm

Cloud models, as $llm. $llm.for(e) is the same API with every call counted for whom the request is for (its user,
else its guest), so the limits in Settings → LLM can cap each user and each guest: pass a route's e or a page's ctx.
A call a limit refuses throws with code "limit" (429), naming the limit and when it resets.

### $llm.text

### $llm.text.completeAsync()

None: the price isn't known. */ prices?: { unit: string; usd: number; source?: "listed" \| "measured"; calls?: number }[]; description?: string; /** parameters, as its maker names them: "1.7B", "30B (3B active)" */ size?: string; /** "tools", "structured output", "vision", "audio input", "voice cloning", "voice design", "built-in voices", "lyrics" */ features?: string[]; /** ISO 639-1 codes */ languages?: string[] }[]` |  |

### LlmCallEvent

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"text" \| "image" \| "speech" \| "transcribe" \| "align" \| "music" \| "video" \| "embed"` |  |
| `op` | `string` | The operation: "complete", "stream", "generate", "speak", "transcribe", "align", "create" or "embed". |
| `model` | `string` | "provider/model"; change it to send the call to another model. |
| `subject` | `string` | Whom the call is for: "user:<collection>/<id>", "guest:<id>", "guest:ip:<address>", "" or your own ("team:acme"). Change it to count the call elsewhere. |

| `guest` | `boolean` | The call is for a guest. |
| `input` | `Record<string, any>` | The operation's input (prompt, maxTokens, ...); change it as you like. |
| `guestsCapped` | `boolean` | Set it when this handler caps what guests may spend, so guest calls don't need a limit on all guests together. |
| `next()` | `(): void` | Lets the call go on. A handler that neither calls it nor throws refuses the call. |
| `refuse()` | `(message: string): Error` | An error refusing the call with your message (code "limit", 429): throw e.refuse("..."). |

# MCP JavaScript API

Everything the [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## $mcp

The app's MCP server (`/mcp`): tools map to the app's own REST endpoints.

```js
$mcp.addEndpoint({ name: "blog_publish_post", description: "Publish a draft post.", method: "POST",
  path: "/api/blog/posts/{id}/publish", inputSchema: { type: "object", required: ["id"], properties: { id: { type: "string" } } } })
```

### $mcp.addEndpoint()

```ts
$mcp.addEndpoint(def: mcp.Endpoint): void
```

Declares a tool, at the top level of a pb_hooks file. Adding the same name again replaces it.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `def` | `mcp.Endpoint` |  |

### $mcp.pathValue()

```ts
$mcp.pathValue(value: string): string
```

Escapes a value for one {name} part of a tool's path.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` |  |

Returns `string`.

### $mcp.instructions()

```ts
$mcp.instructions(text: string): void
```

Adds text to the server's instructions for the model.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

### $mcp.tools()

```ts
$mcp.tools(): string[]
```

The names of every tool.

Returns `string[]`.

## Types

### mcp.ToolRequest

The REST request a tool makes; a request transform may change it.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` |  |

# Pages JavaScript API

Everything the [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## Types

### pages.Data

What `ctx.data` holds: shared by middleware, handlers and templates. Add your own keys by redeclaring it.

### pages.Params

Route parameters (`[id]` in a path), strings. Never includes query parameters.

### pages.CookieOptions

Options for `ctx.res.cookie` and `ctx.res.clearCookie`.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `path?` | `string` |  |
| `domain?` | `string` |  |
| `maxAge?` | `number` | Seconds. |
| `expires?` | `Date \| number \| string` | A Date, milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string. |
| `httpOnly?` | `boolean` | Default true. |
| `secure?` | `boolean` | Default: true on HTTPS. |
| `sameSite?` | `"Lax" \| "Strict" \| "None" \| "lax" \| "strict" \| "none"` | Default "Lax". |

### pages.Request

`ctx.req`: the request.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `readonly method` | `string` | `"GET"`, `"POST"`, ... |
| `readonly url` | `{ href: string; origin: string; pathname: string; search: string }` |  |
| `query()` | `(): { [name: string]: string }` | Every query parameter's first value. |
| `query()` | `(name: string, opts: { all: true }): string[]` | Every value of a query parameter. |
| `query()` | `(name: string, opts?: { all?: false }): string \| undefined` | A query parameter's first value, or `undefined`. |
| `header()` | `(name: string): string` | A request header, `''` if absent. |
| `cookie()` | `(name: string, opts: { json: true }): T \| undefined` | A cookie parsed as JSON (`undefined` if absent or not JSON). |
| `cookie()` | `(name: string, opts?: { json?: false }): string \| undefined` | A cookie's value, or `undefined`. |
| `cookies()` | `(): { [name: string]: string }` |  |
| `body()` | `(): T` | The parsed body: a JSON value, or form fields as `{ name: value }` (repeated names as arrays). |
| `files()` | `(name: string): filesystem.File[]` | Uploaded files of a multipart field, ready for a record's file field. |
| `readonly ip` | `string` | The client's IP, as PocketBase resolves it. |
| `readonly event` | `core.RequestEvent` | The underlying PocketBase request event, for anything not covered here. |

### pages.EventStream

| Member | Type | |

| `close()` | `(): void` |  |

### pages.Response

`ctx.res`: the response. Every method that sends ends the request (later steps are skipped).

| Member | Type | |

| `redirect()` | `(location: string, opts?: number \| { status?: number; flash?: any }): Response` | Sends a redirect (3xx, default 302). `flash` sets a one-time message the next request reads with `ctx.flash()`. |

| `json()` | `(status: number, data: any): Response` |  |

| `html()` | `(status: number, html: string): Response` |  |
| `text()` | `(text: string): Response` |  |
| `text()` | `(status: number, text: string): Response` |  |
| `file()` | `(path: string): Response` | Sends a file from pb_pages (path relative to pb_pages). |
| `sse()` | `(opts?: { keepAlive?: number }): EventStream` | Starts a `text/event-stream` response. `keepAlive` (seconds) writes a comment that often while the handler runs, so proxies keep a quiet stream open. |
| `layout()` | `(on: boolean): Response` | `layout(false)` renders this page without layouts (e.g. an htmx fragment). |

### pages.Realtime

`ctx.realtime`: PocketBase realtime from page code. Present when the `realtime` plugin is on.

| `subscribe()` | `(topic: string, opts?: { filter?: string; expand?: string; fields?: string }): RealtimeSubscription<T>` | Listens to `topic` like a browser on `/api/realtime`, as this visitor: the collection's list/view rules apply, and `filter`, `expand` and `fields` work as in the JS SDK's subscribe options. # WASM JavaScript API

Everything the [WASM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm) extension adds to `pb_hooks` and page code, generated from the TypeScript declarations it ships (your app's `types.d.ts` has the same, so your editor knows them). For how to use it, see its docs; for Go, the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

## $wasm

The app's modules, the pb_hooks/<name>.pb.wasm files. A module is a closed box: it gets its input and gives its output,
and reaches no database, file, network, environment or process.

Calls are async only: a module runs off the app's JS VM while the hook awaits it, so the app serves other requests
meanwhile. `$wasm.run(...)` without `.async` throws.

The output is the module's stdout: JSON parsed, a string when it isn't JSON, null when it's empty.

### $wasm.run

### $wasm.run.async()

```ts
$wasm.run.async(name: string, input?: WasmInput): Promise<T>
```

Calls the module's "run". Rejects with a `WasmError` when the call fails.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `input` | `WasmInput` (optional) |  |

Returns `Promise<T>`.

```js
onRecordCreate(async (e) => {
  const out = await $wasm.run.async("summary", { title: e.record.get("title"), body: e.record.get("body") })
  e.record.set("summary", out.text)
  return e.next()
}, "posts")
```

### $wasm.call

### $wasm.call.async()

```ts
$wasm.call.async(name: string, fn: string, input?: WasmInput): Promise<T>
```

Calls one of the module's functions (its first argument). Rejects with a `WasmError` when the call fails.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `fn` | `string` |  |
| `input` | `WasmInput` (optional) |  |

Returns `Promise<T>`.

```js
const r = await $wasm.call.async("crypto", "decrypt", { key, data })
```

### $wasm.inspect

### $wasm.inspect.async()

```ts
$wasm.inspect.async(name: string, fn: string, input?: WasmInput): Promise<WasmInspection<T>>
```

Calls a function to try a module out: never rejects for the call, and gives its log and timings.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `fn` | `string` |  |
| `input` | `WasmInput` (optional) |  |

Returns `Promise<WasmInspection<T>>`.

### $wasm.modules()

```ts
$wasm.modules(): Array<WasmModuleInfo>
```

Every module in pb_hooks/ and how it's doing.

Returns `Array<WasmModuleInfo>`.

### $wasm.limits()

```ts
$wasm.limits(): WasmLimits
```

What every call runs within: memory, time, how many calls and how many MB of modules at once.

Returns `WasmLimits`.

## Types

### WasmInput

What a module gets on stdin: a string or bytes (a typed array or an ArrayBuffer) as they are, nothing for undefined or null, anything else as JSON.

```ts
type WasmInput = string | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array | Array<number> | object | number | boolean | null | undefined
```

### WasmExample

One call to try a module with, from its manifest (what it prints for `<name> --describe`).

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `function` | `string` | "run" when the manifest leaves it out. |
| `input` | `any` | A string is the module's stdin as it is (EDIFACT, XML, CSV); anything else is sent as JSON. |
| `output?` | `any` | What it gives, when the example says. |

### WasmModuleInfo

How one module in pb_hooks/ is doing, with what it says for --describe.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `running` | `boolean` | Its module checks out: it can be called. |
| `description?` | `string` |  |
| `version?` | `string` | The author's version, as the manifest writes it. |
| `functions?` | `Array<string>` | The functions it says it has; ["run"] by default. |
| `language?` | `string` | What it's written in: what the module says, else what its manifest says. |
| `repository?` | `string` | Where its source is: an http(s) URL. |
| `examples?` | `Array<WasmExample>` |  |
| `size?` | `number` | Its module's size in bytes: what a call of it takes of the app's `maxModulesMB` while it runs. |
| `error?` | `string` | Why it can't run (running false), or what's wrong with what it printed for --describe. |

### WasmLimits

What every module call in the app runs within.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `maxCallMemoryMB` | `number` | Memory each call may allocate (heap, stack, input). Every call has its own, not shared. |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | Time limit for a call's run (compiling comes before it). |
| `maxConcurrent` | `number` | Calls running at once. |
| `maxModulesMB` | `number` | MB of modules running at once: the sizes of the calls' modules, added up. With 10, two calls of a Go module (~4.4 MB) run at once, and `maxConcurrent` of a Rust or Zig one (~0.1 MB). Also the largest module that loads. |
| `maxPayload` | `number` | Largest input or output of a call, in bytes. |

### WasmErrorCode

The codes ext/wasm gives; a module can give its own (it exits non-zero with {"code", "message"} on stderr).

### WasmError

What a failed $wasm.run.async or $wasm.call.async rejects with: catch it to decide what the hook does next.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `"WasmError"` |  |
| `module` | `string` | The module's name. |
| `code` | `WasmErrorCode` |  |
| `retryable` | `boolean` | Whether the same call may work later (busy, timeout...). |

### WasmInspection

What $wasm.inspect.async gives: one call, with its log and its timings.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `output` | `T \| null` | The output; null when the call failed or the module wrote nothing. |
| `stderr` | `string` | What the module wrote to stderr: its log. |
| `error` | `{ code: WasmErrorCode; message: string; retryable: boolean } \| null` | Why the call failed, or null. |
| `compileMs` | `number` |  |
| `runMs` | `number` |  |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript/contracts

# Contract hooks JavaScript API

See [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts); their Go side is in the [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go).

| `schema` | `any` |  |
| `maxTokens` | `number` |  |
| `temperature` | `number \| null` |  |
| `model` | `string` | Model is the text model to answer with ("provider/model", required). |
| `reasoning` | `string` | Reasoning is how much a reasoning model thinks first: "", "off", "low", "medium" or "high". Enrich adds the best passages from the app's search buckets after the question, beside Context (search/v1); |
| `enrich` | `LlmEnrich \| null` | the answer's Passages lists them. |
