Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/search

# Search and RAG

**Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)** means searching your own content for the passages that answer a question,
and sending them to the model with the prompt, so the answer is **grounded** in your content instead of the model's
memory. PocketOne does the whole pipeline: you put content in a **bucket** (a knowledge base), it's chunked and
embedded in the background, and one option on any `$llm` call does the retrieval:

```ts
const answer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({
  model: "vultr/glm-5.3",
  system: "Answer from the passages given. Say so when they don't cover it.",
  prompt: "How do I export my notes?",
  enrich: ["help"], // RAG: search the "help" bucket and send the best passages with the prompt
})
// answer.text is the answer; answer.passages are the passages it was grounded in
```

It uses the provider you added in Settings → LLM ([AI in your app](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm)), which needs embedding models
(Vultr's, for one). The embedding model is picked for you and kept; you never name one.

## Why not just put everything in the prompt?

You can, for a little content: that's **context stuffing**, and long context windows make it tempting. It gets slow
and expensive as content grows (every call pays for all of it), and models pay less attention to the middle of a long
prompt. RAG sends only the few passages that match the question, so a question costs the same whether the knowledge
base is one page or ten thousand.

## How it works

1. **Ingestion.** Each **source** you add (a file, a folder, a zip, a web page, a Git repository, a collection) becomes
   **documents**, and each document is split into **chunks** of about 500 tokens: Markdown at its headings (each chunk
   keeps its heading path, like "Install › macOS"), code and text at blank lines.
2. **Embeddings.** Each chunk is turned into a vector by your embedding model, in the background. A chunk whose text
   didn't change is never embedded again, and identical text anywhere in the app is embedded once.
3. **Retrieval.** A question is embedded too, and ranked against the chunks by meaning (**semantic search**, vector
   similarity) and by words (**keyword search**, BM25 over a local index) at once: **hybrid search**. Keywords catch
   exact names like `onRecordCreate` that embeddings blur; meaning catches a reworded question.
4. **Generation.** `enrich` sends the best chunks after the prompt, numbered so the model can cite them, and the answer
   lists them in `passages`.

## 1. Make a bucket

A bucket is a knowledge base: content that's searched together. Your app makes the bucket it needs, once at startup.
The description is what your admins see on the dashboard's Search screen, so say what belongs there:

```ts
// pb_hooks/search.pb.js
onBootstrap((e) => {
  e.next()
  $llm.search.ensure({
    name: "help",
    title: "Help center",
    owner: "Help desk",
    description: "Our help articles, as Markdown. The help desk answers from these.",
  })
})
```

Calling it again changes nothing, so your admins' changes stick. You can also make a bucket on the Search screen.

## 2. Add your content

Open the dashboard and choose **Search** in the header. A sidebar lists **Chat**, **Search**, **Settings** and every
bucket. Open yours and add **sources**. Each one is a single row you can refresh, replace or remove, however many
documents it brings:

- **Drop files, folders or zips** on it (Markdown, text or code inside), or choose files.
- **Paste text.**
- **Add a URL or Git repo**: paste any URL. Its server is asked whether it's a Git repository (with or without `.git`,
  on any host), and the form shows how it will be read, with a switch if you want the other. Pick how often to read it
  again: every hour, day or week. A repository brings its default branch's text files and its recent commits.
- **Follow a collection**: pick the collection, check the fields to search (its text fields start checked; the first
  is each record's title) and, if you like, which records (`published = true`). It reads the records there now and
  keeps up as they're saved and deleted.

Adding something with the same name as a source replaces it: files that didn't change cost nothing, and files it no
longer has are removed. For a new version under another name (`guide-v2.zip`), use **Upload a new version** on the old
one's row. Each source goes from `reading` to `ready`, and its documents from `in line` to `embedding` to `ready`; open
a row to see its documents.

To try a bucket out, use **Chat** in the sidebar: pick buckets and a model, ask questions in words, and read the
answers with the passages they're grounded in (follow-ups keep the conversation). **Search** shows the raw hybrid
search results instead: exactly what `$llm.search` and `enrich` get.

### From code

Everything the screen does, your code can do with `$llm.search`. Adding returns at once; ingestion happens in the
background.

```ts
// a file's text, or text you put together (a source of one document; the same name again replaces it)
$llm.search.add({ bucket: "help", name: "export.md", text: "# Exporting\n\nChoose File → Export…" })

// a web page or a Git repository, read again every day
$llm.search.addURL({ bucket: "help", url: "https://github.com/acme/help-articles", every: "day" })

// a collection: a document per published article, kept in sync as records are saved and deleted
$llm.search.follow({ bucket: "help", collection: "articles", fields: ["title", "body"], filter: "published = true" })

// a folder of the app's own files (your docs pages), read again every five minutes; each result links to its page
$llm.search.addFolder({ bucket: "help", path: "pb_pages/docs", include: ["*.md"], url: "/docs/{path}" })
```

Then look at what's there, and tidy up:

```ts
const sources = $llm.search.sources("help")          // [{ name, kind, status, documents, pending, error, ... }]
const docs = $llm.search.documents({ bucket: "help", source: "export.md" })
$llm.search.refresh("help", "https://github.com/acme/help-articles") // read it again now
$llm.search.remove("help", ["export.md"])            // take sources out, with their documents
const { model, chunks, embedded } = $llm.search.status() // embedded < chunks: still embedding
```

A source's name is how it's found again: the file name you gave, the URL, or the collection.

## 3. RAG with enrich

`enrich` works on `$llm.text.completeAsync`, `$llm.text.streamAsync` and LLM Chat (on a chat's options or a send):

```ts
const chat = $llm.chat.open(id, { model: "vultr/glm-5.3", system: preamble, enrich: ["help"] })
const answer = await chat.sendAsync("And as PDF?")
```

Name several buckets to search them together (`enrich: ["help", "changelog"]`), or pass `{ buckets, limit, query }`:
`limit` is how many passages go in (5 by default, at most 20) and `query` searches for something other than the prompt.
LLM Chat saves the passages with each question, so later turns send the same thing.

## Search directly

To show results yourself (a search box, related articles), run the hybrid search without a model call:

```ts
const found = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: ["help"], query: "export notes", limit: 5 })
// found.results: [{ bucket, source, document, heading, text, record, score }, ...], best first
```

Leave `buckets` out to search every bucket. It's the only async `$llm.search` call: it embeds the query (a few tokens;
a repeated query is cached).

## Who sees what

A collection source holds a copy of its records' text, so retrieval skips the collection's API rules unless you say
who's asking. Pass the signed-in user as `viewer` and passages from records they can't view are left out (`null` is a
signed-out visitor):

```ts
const found = await $llm.search.searchAsync({ buckets: ["notes"], query, viewer: ctx.auth })
const answer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model, prompt: question, enrich: { buckets: ["notes"], viewer: ctx.auth } })
```

Without `viewer`, a search sees everything, as your own server code does. Always pass it when the answer is for a user.

## The embedding model

One embedding model embeds every bucket, so any of them can be searched together. **Settings** on the Search screen
shows it and lets you change it; every bucket is then embedded again in the background, with its progress shown.
Search keeps working meanwhile: chunks not yet re-embedded are still found by keyword search.

## What it costs

Embedding is billed to your provider account like any `$llm` call: `qwen3-embedding-4b` on Vultr is $0.05 per million
tokens, about 4 MB of text, embedded once. Each document shows what it cost. Each search embeds only the query, a few
tokens; the model call that uses the passages pays for them as input tokens.

## `$llm.search` at a glance

Every call is local and returns at once, except `searchAsync`.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `buckets()` | Every bucket, with its counts. |
| `bucket(name)` | One bucket. |
| `ensure({ name, title?, description?, owner? })` | Makes the bucket if it's missing and returns it; an existing one keeps its settings. |
| `update({ name, title?, description?, maxDocuments?, maxBytes? })` | Changes a bucket. |
| `deleteBucket(name)` | Deletes a bucket and everything in it. |
| `sources(bucket)` | Its sources: `{ name, kind, status, documents, chunks, embedded, pending, error, refreshed, next, ... }`. |
| `add({ bucket, name, text, replace? })` | A file or text as a source; `replace` names an older source a renamed version replaces. |
| `addURL({ bucket, url, every?, kind?, commits?, exclude? })` | A web page or Git repository (`kind` is decided by asking the server); `every` is `hour`, `day` or `week`. |
| `follow({ bucket, collection, fields, filter? })` | A collection; the first field is each record's title. |
| `addFolder({ bucket, path, include?, exclude?, url? })` | A folder of the app's own files (`path` relative to the app's folder, never `pb_data`), read again every five minutes; `url` (`"/docs/{path}"`) links each result to its page and section. |
| `refresh(bucket, source)` | Reads a source again now. |
| `remove(bucket, sources)` | Takes sources out, with their documents. |
| `documents(bucket \| { bucket, source?, prefix? })` | Documents, with their status and how many chunks are embedded. |
| `status()` | The app's embedding model, and how many chunks are embedded of how many. |
| `await searchAsync({ query, buckets?, limit?, prefix?, viewer? })` | Hybrid search across the buckets (all when none are named): `{ results: [{ bucket, source, document, heading, text, record, url, score }], model, usage }`. |

The same operations are the [llm.search/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.search/v1) contract: over HTTP at
`/api/_c/llm.search/v1/…` (a superuser, or an API token with the `search` scope), from Go with
`searchv1.Contract.Must(app)`, and as MCP tools. The [LLM Search extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-search) has the
details: what's skipped in folders, zips and repositories, the limits, and how ranking works.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits

# Limits

Every model call spends money on your provider account. On a page anyone can open, every visitor spends it. Limits cap
that: you set them in **Settings → LLM**, and every call passes them before it reaches a provider. A call a used-up
limit refuses never reaches the provider and costs nothing.

The limits on this screen are PocketOne's built-in limits: one handler on the hook every call passes through
before it reaches a provider. Anything they can't express, such as a user's plan, credits they bought or the team
they're on, you write as your own handler on the same hook ([Custom limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits)). Yours run first, and
the built-in limits count what they settled on.

This page covers the built-in limits. [Users and guests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests) covers the one line page code adds so per-user and
per-guest limits work, and [Spend and the ledger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend) covers the record every call leaves and how to read what's
left.

## Setting a limit

Open the dashboard, go to **Settings → LLM**, and scroll past the providers to **Limits**. Press **New limit**, fill
in the row, and press **Save changes**. Limits apply from the next call, with no restart.

![Settings → LLM: four limits (all guests together $1 a day, each guest $0.10 a day, the whole app $25 a month, and 20 video calls a month) under today's and this month's spend](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits-settings.png)

Each limit reads as a sentence: **who** may use **at most** so much of **what**, **per** day or month.

| Field | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Who** | Whose calls the limit counts. **The whole app**: every call. **Each signed-in user**: each user separately, so one user using theirs up leaves the others theirs. **Each guest**: each visitor who isn't signed in, separately. **All guests together**: every guest's calls in one shared bucket. |
| **Counts** | What it counts. **US dollars**: what the calls cost. **Output tokens**: what the model wrote. **Input tokens**: what was sent to it. **Calls**: how many calls reached a provider. |
| **At most** | The amount. Dollars may have cents (`0.10`); tokens and calls are whole numbers. `0` refuses every call the limit counts. |
| **Per** | **a day** or **a month**, in UTC: a day starts at 00:00 UTC, a month on the 1st at 00:00 UTC. |
| **Kind** | Count only one kind of call: `text`, `image`, `speech`, `transcribe`, `align`, `music`, `video` or `embed`. **Every kind** counts all of them. |
| **Model** | Count only calls to one model, named as `provider/model` (`vultr/glm-5.3`). Empty counts every model. |

A limit with a kind or a model counts only those calls toward its amount, and refuses only those calls. Add as many
limits as you like: a call has to pass every one that counts it.

Above the limits, the screen shows what the whole app has spent today and this month, and how many calls today a limit
refused. The numbers come from [the ledger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend).

## When a limit is used up

Before each call, every limit that counts it is checked against what's been used so far in its window. If one is used
up, the call is refused before it reaches the provider. In page code the `$llm` call throws, over HTTP the contract
answers `429`, and either way the error's code is `limit` and its message names the limit and when it resets:

```
limit reached: each guest, $0.10 a day (used $0.10); it resets at 00:00 UTC
limit reached: the whole app, 20 calls a month of video (used 20 calls); it resets on Dec 1 (UTC)
```

The message is written to show to the person who made the call. [Users and guests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests#when-a-call-is-refused)
shows how to catch it in a page.

A refused call still gets a row in the ledger, with the limit's message, so you can see how often visitors hit it.

## Guests need a total

A guest is told apart by a cookie (see [Users and guests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests#guests)), and anyone can clear their cookies and
come back as a new guest with a fresh allowance. A limit on **each guest** keeps one visitor from using everything up
by accident, but it doesn't cap what guests spend. Only a limit on **all guests together** does.

So guest calls are refused until there's a limit on all guests together that counts them. Until you add one, a guest's
call fails with:

```
guest calls are off until the app caps what all guests together may spend: add a limit for all guests in Settings → LLM
```

and the Limits section shows a warning. Calls for signed-in users, and calls that aren't for anyone in particular,
aren't guest calls and aren't affected.

## Checked before, counted after

A call's cost and tokens are known only once the provider answers, so a limit is checked before each call and the call
is counted after it. Two things follow:

- **The last call a limit lets through can take it over**, by that call's own cost. With $0.10 left and a call that
  costs $0.15, the call goes through and the next one is refused. Keep your amounts a call or two under what you can
  afford.
- **Calls running at the same moment can all pass the check** before any of them is counted, so a burst of calls can
  take a limit further over than one call. Limits keep spending in the right range day to day; they aren't an exact
  meter.

## Dollars need prices

A call's cost is what the provider reports, or else what its listed prices say. A model with no price, such as a model
on your own machine (Ollama, llama-server) or an OpenAI-compatible server that lists no prices, costs $0 as far as the
ledger knows, so a dollar limit never fills up for it. Count **tokens** or **calls** for those models instead.

Music and video are jobs: a call starts the job, and the job's cost is known once it's done. A job counts as a call as
soon as it starts, and its cost is added to its ledger row once `createAsync` with `wait` sees it finish, or once
`getAsync` does. A job nobody checks again after starting keeps a cost of $0.

## Limits for common apps

**An internal tool**, where everyone is signed in and trusted: one ceiling.

- The whole app, US dollars, at most 20, per month.

**A public demo**, like an [ask your docs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/ask) page, where visitors aren't signed in:

- All guests together, US dollars, at most 1, per day.
- Each guest, US dollars, at most 0.10, per day.
- The whole app, US dollars, at most 20, per month.

**An app with accounts**, where users sign in to use the model:

- Each signed-in user, output tokens, at most 200000, per day.
- The whole app, US dollars, at most 50, per month.

**An expensive kind on its own**, next to whatever else you have:

- The whole app, calls, at most 20, per month, kind video.
- The whole app, US dollars, at most 5, per day, kind image.

Plan tiers, credits users buy, and anything else that depends on who the user is belong in your app's own code: see
[Custom limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests

# Users and guests

[Limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits) on each user, each guest and all guests together need to know which user or guest made each call.
Page code says so with one change: call the model through `$llm.for(ctx)` instead of `$llm`. In Go, the same thing is
the call's context, carrying the subject `llm.SubjectOf(app, e)` works out from the request.

```ts
// pb_pages/ask.ts
export async function post(ctx: pages.Context) {
  const { question } = ctx.req.body()
  const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.for(ctx).text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question })
  return ctx.res.json({ answer: r.text })
}
```

```go
se.Router.POST("/ask", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
	body := struct{ Question string }{}
	if err := e.BindBody(&body); err != nil {
		return e.BadRequestError("send {question}", err)
	}
	ctx := llmc.WithSubject(e.Request.Context(), llm.SubjectOf(app, e))
	r, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{
		Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: body.Question})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return e.JSON(200, map[string]string{"answer": r.Text})
})
```

`$llm.for()` takes the request you're answering: a page's `ctx`, or a `pb_hooks` route's `e`. It returns the same API as
`$llm`, every kind, chats and streams included, with each call counted for that request:

- **its signed-in user**, when the request carries an auth record (counted as `user:<collection>/<id>`);
- else **a guest**, told apart by a cookie (below).

Keep the object (in Go, the context) for the whole request when you make several calls, so they all count for the same
person:

```ts
const llm = $llm.for(ctx)
const chat = llm.chat.open(chatId, { model: "vultr/glm-5.3" })
const r = await chat.sendAsync(question)
const more = await llm.text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: `Three follow-up questions to: ${question}` })
```

```go
ctx := llmc.WithSubject(e.Request.Context(), llm.SubjectOf(app, e))
r, err := chatv1.Contract.Must(app).Send(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.SendInput{ID: chatID, Text: question, Model: "vultr/glm-5.3"})
// ...
more, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{
	Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: "Three follow-up questions to: " + question})
```

## Calls that aren't for anyone

Plain `$llm`, or a context with no subject, counts toward limits on **the whole app** only. Use it for work that isn't
on someone's behalf: a cron, a hook that tags new records, a migration. Those calls are recorded with no subject, never
count as a guest's, and are never refused for a missing guest total.

```ts
// pb_hooks/tags.pb.ts: tags every new post; counted toward the whole app only
onRecordAfterCreateSuccess(async (e) => {
  const r = await $llm.text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: "Three tags for: " + e.record.get("title") })
  e.record.set("tags", r.text)
  $app.save(e.record)
  e.next()
}, "posts")
```

```go
app.OnRecordAfterCreateSuccess("posts").BindFunc(func(e *core.RecordEvent) error {
	r, err := textv1.Contract.Must(e.App).Complete(context.Background(), extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{
		Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: "Three tags for: " + e.Record.GetString("title")})
	if err == nil {
		e.Record.Set("tags", r.Text)
		err = e.App.Save(e.Record)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return e.Next()
})
```

Calls over HTTP and MCP (`/api/_c/llm.text/v1/...`) come from superusers and API tokens, never from visitors, so they
also count toward the whole app only.

## Guests

A visitor who isn't signed in is a guest. Guests are told apart by a cookie, `pocketone_llm_guest`, which the first
`$llm.for()` call (in Go, `llm.SubjectOf`) for a visitor sets on the response:

- It holds a random id and a signature, so a visitor can't pick someone else's id. The signing key is made the first
  time it's needed and kept in the app's [key-value store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/kv) at the private name `_llm/guest-key`.
  Deleting it gives every guest a new id.
- It lasts a year, is `HttpOnly` (page JavaScript can't read it), `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when the app is served
  over HTTPS.
- Until the browser sends it back, the visitor counts by IP address (`guest:ip:<address>`). The first call of a visit
  is counted that way, and so is every call from a client that never keeps cookies, so dropping cookies doesn't get a
  fresh allowance on every call.

A visitor who clears their cookies comes back as a new guest. That's why guest calls need [a limit on all guests
together](limits.md#guests-need-a-total) before they're answered: it's the only limit a visitor can't reset.

## When a call is refused

A refused call fails, whether a built-in limit refused it or one of your [onCall handlers](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits) did. Its
code is `limit` and its message is written for the person who made the request ("limit reached: each guest, $0.10 a day
(used $0.10); it resets at 00:00 UTC", or your handler's own words), so the simplest handling is to show it:

```ts
// pb_pages/ask.ts
export async function post(ctx: pages.Context) {
  const { question } = ctx.req.body()
  try {
    const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.for(ctx).text.completeAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question })
    return ctx.res.json({ answer: r.text })
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err.code === "limit") return ctx.res.json(429, { error: err.message })
    throw err
  }
}
```

```go
r, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: question})
var xe *extkit.Error
if errors.As(err, &xe) && xe.Code == llmc.ErrLimit.Code {
	return e.JSON(429, map[string]string{"error": xe.Message})
}
if err != nil {
	return err
}
return e.JSON(200, map[string]string{"answer": r.Text})
```

A streamed answer fails the same way, before any text arrives. With server-sent events, send the message as an event
the page shows in place of the answer, as pocketone.dev's ask box does:

```ts
// pb_pages/chat.ts
export async function post(ctx: pages.Context) {
  const { question } = ctx.req.body()
  const stream = ctx.res.sse()
  try {
    const r = await $llm.for(ctx).text.streamAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question },
      (text) => stream.send("text", JSON.stringify(text)))
    stream.send("done", JSON.stringify({ usage: r.usage }))
  } catch (err: any) {
    stream.send("error", JSON.stringify(err.message))
  }
  stream.close()
}
```

```go
s, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Stream(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: question})
if err != nil {
	return err // a bad model, before the stream starts
}
e.Response.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
send := func(event string, data any) {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(data)
	fmt.Fprintf(e.Response, "event: %s\ndata: %s\n\n", event, b)
	_ = e.Flush()
}
err = s.Run(ctx, func(v any) error {
	if c, ok := v.(textv1.Chunk); ok && c.Text != "" {
		send("text", c.Text)
	}
	return nil
})
if err != nil {
	send("error", err.Error()) // a limit's refusal arrives here
}
return nil
```

Over HTTP, refused calls answer `429` with `{"code": "limit", "message": "..."}`.

## Showing what's left

`$llm.for(ctx).ledger.remaining()` lists the limits that count this visitor, with what's used and left, so a page can
say "4 questions left today" before anyone hits a refusal ([Spend and the ledger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend#whats-left)):

```ets
<% const left = $llm.for(ctx).ledger.remaining()[0] %>
<% if (left) { %><p><%= left.left %> of <%= left.amount %> left today</p><% } %>
```

```go
ctx := llmc.WithSubject(e.Request.Context(), llm.SubjectOf(app, e))
rem, err := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app).Remaining(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.RemainingInput{})
if err == nil && len(rem.Limits) > 0 {
	left := rem.Limits[0] // the tightest
	fmt.Fprintf(e.Response, "<p>%v of %v left today</p>", left.Left, left.Amount)
}
```

## The Go side

- `llmc.WithSubject(ctx, s)` and `llmc.SubjectOf(ctx)` (in `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`) set and read the
  subject; `llmc.UserSubject(collection, id)` builds a user's. A call whose context has no subject counts toward the
  whole app only.
- `llm.SubjectOf(app, e)` (in `pocketone.dev/ext/llm`) is what `$llm.for(e)` uses: the request's user, else its guest
  cookie (set on `e`'s response when missing), else its IP.
- Pass the context on and the subject goes with it: LLM Chat's calls to `llm.text/v1` count for the subject of the
  send that made them.
- A refused call returns an `*extkit.Error` with `Code` `"limit"` and `Status` `429` (`llmc.ErrLimit`'s).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend

# Spend and the ledger

Every call that reaches a provider, and every call a limit refuses, is recorded in the app's ledger: its kind and
model, whom it was for, what it used and what it cost. The limits count from it, Settings → LLM shows today's and this
month's spend from it, and `$llm.ledger` reads it for you:

```ts
const llm = $llm.for(ctx)
llm.ledger.remaining()                                  // what's left of each limit, for this visitor
llm.ledger.spent("day")                                 // what this visitor has spent today
$llm.ledger.summary({ by: "model", window: "month" })   // where the money went this month
$llm.ledger.calls({ status: "refused", limit: 20 })     // the latest calls a limit refused
```

```go
ledger := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app) // pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm/ledger/v1
ctx := llmc.WithSubject(e.Request.Context(), llm.SubjectOf(app, e))
ledger.Remaining(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.RemainingInput{})                    // what's left, for this visitor
ledger.Spent(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SpentInput{Window: "day"})                // what this visitor has spent today
ledger.Summary(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SummaryInput{By: "model", Window: "month"}) // where the money went
ledger.Calls(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.CallsInput{Status: "refused", Limit: 20})    // the latest refused calls
```

These read the app's own database, so they're plain calls, not `Async` ones. In Go they're the `llm.ledger/v1` contract;
each returns its result and an error.

## What's left

`remaining()` lists every limit in Settings → LLM that counts the subject's calls, with how much is used and left in
its current window, the tightest first:

```ts
// pb_pages/ask/index.ts, beside ask/index.ets: "4 questions left today"
export function load(ctx: pages.Context) {
  const tightest = $llm.for(ctx).ledger.remaining()[0]
  return { left: tightest }
}
```

```go
ctx := llmc.WithSubject(e.Request.Context(), llm.SubjectOf(app, e))
rem, err := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app).Remaining(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.RemainingInput{})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
var tightest *ledgerv1.LimitLeft
if len(rem.Limits) > 0 {
	tightest = &rem.Limits[0]
}
```

It answers:

```js
[
  {
    limit: "each guest, 10 calls a day",   // the limit in words
    scope: "guest", window: "day", metric: "calls",
    amount: 10, used: 6, left: 4,           // in the metric's unit: dollars for cost, else tokens or calls
    resets: "2026-11-23T00:00:00Z",         // when its window ends
  },
  { limit: "all guests together, $1.00 a day", metric: "cost", amount: 1, used: 0.31, left: 0.69, ... },
]
```

It's the same count the limits use, so it agrees with what the next refusal would say. Limits your own
[onCall handlers](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits) enforce aren't in it: they're your code, so show their numbers your way.

## What someone has spent

`spent()` is the totals for one subject in a window:

```ts
$llm.for(ctx).ledger.spent("day")         // this request's user or guest, today (UTC)
$llm.for(ctx).ledger.spent("month")
$llm.ledger.spent({ subject: "user:users/abc", since: "2026-11-01", until: "2026-11-15" })
$llm.ledger.spent({ window: "month" })    // no subject: the whole app
// { calls: 42, refused: 3, input: 51200, cached: 20480, output: 9800, seconds: 0, costMicroUSD: 312000 }
```

```go
ledger := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app)
ledger.Spent(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SpentInput{Window: "day"}) // ctx's subject (llmc.WithSubject), today (UTC)
ledger.Spent(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SpentInput{Window: "month"})
ledger.Spent(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SpentInput{Subject: "user:users/abc", Since: "2026-11-01", Until: "2026-11-15"})
ledger.Spent(context.Background(), extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SpentInput{Window: "month"}) // no subject: the whole app
// ledgerv1.Totals{Calls: 42, Refused: 3, Input: 51200, Cached: 20480, Output: 9800, CostMicroUSD: 312000}
```

`calls` counts calls that reached a provider and `refused` the ones a limit refused. `costMicroUSD` is in millionths of
a US dollar, like every result's `usage.costMicroUSD`: divide by 1,000,000 for dollars. Add `kind` or `model` to count
only those calls.

Windows are UTC: `"day"` and `"month"` are the calendar day and month holding now, the same windows limits count in.
`since` and `until` take a date (`2026-11-01`) or a full time; `until` is exclusive.

## Where the money goes

`summary()` groups the totals, costliest first:

```ts
$llm.ledger.summary({ by: "model", window: "month" })
// [{ key: "vultr/glm-5.3", calls: 812, costMicroUSD: 4120000, ... }, { key: "vultr/z-image-turbo", ... }]

$llm.ledger.summary({ by: "subject", window: "day", limit: 10 })   // today's ten biggest spenders
$llm.ledger.summary({ by: "kind", window: "month" })                 // text vs pictures vs video
$llm.ledger.summary({ by: "day", since: "2026-11-01" })              // a row per day, latest first
```

```go
ledger := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app)
ledger.Summary(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SummaryInput{By: "model", Window: "month"})
// .Rows: []ledgerv1.SummaryRow{{Key: "vultr/glm-5.3", Totals: ledgerv1.Totals{Calls: 812, CostMicroUSD: 4120000}}, ...}

ledger.Summary(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SummaryInput{By: "subject", Window: "day", Limit: 10}) // today's ten biggest spenders
ledger.Summary(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SummaryInput{By: "kind", Window: "month"})            // text vs pictures vs video
ledger.Summary(ctx, extkit.Internal, ledgerv1.SummaryInput{By: "day", Since: "2026-11-01"})          // a row per day, latest first
```

Narrow it with `subject`, `kind` or `model`, as with `spent`.

## The calls themselves

`calls()` lists the rows, newest first, 50 at a time:

```ts
const page = $llm.ledger.calls({ subject: "user:users/abc", window: "month", limit: 20 })
page.calls  // [{ id, created, kind, model, subject, via, input, cached, output, seconds, costMicroUSD, estimated, refused, job }]
page.more   // true when there are more: ask again with offset: 20
```

```go
page, err := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(app).Calls(ctx, extkit.Internal,
	ledgerv1.CallsInput{Subject: "user:users/abc", Window: "month", Limit: 20})
// page.Calls: []ledgerv1.Call{{ID, Created, Kind, Model, Subject, Via, Input, Cached, Output, Seconds, CostMicroUSD, ...}}
// page.More: true when there are more: ask again with Offset: 20
```

`status: "refused"` lists only refused calls (each with the limit's message in `refused`), and `status: "ok"` only the
ones that reached a provider.

## Over HTTP

The same four operations are the `llm.ledger/v1` contract, at `/api/_c/llm.ledger/v1/remaining`, `spent`, `summary`
and `calls`, with the options as query parameters (`?window=day`). `remaining` and `spent` answer a signed-in user
about themselves, so a frontend can show "4 left" with the user's own token; superusers may name any `subject`.
`summary` and `calls` are for superusers (or a superuser's token with the `llm:read` scope). Guests can't ask over
HTTP, since the operation sees credentials, not the guest cookie: answer them from page code with `$llm.for(ctx)`.

## The rows

The ledger is the `_llm_calls` collection, if you'd rather query it yourself:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `text`, `image`, `speech`, `transcribe`, `align`, `music`, `video` or `embed`. |
| `model` | The model, as `provider/model`. |
| `subject` | Whom the call was for: `user:<collection>/<id>`, `guest:<id>`, `guest:ip:<address>`, a name an `onCall` handler gave it, or empty for calls made with plain `$llm`. |
| `via` | How the call arrived: `go` (page code and hooks), `http`, `mcp`. |
| `input`, `cached`, `output` | Input tokens, the input tokens billed at the cheaper cached rate, and output tokens. |
| `seconds` | Seconds of audio or video, for the kinds billed by length. |
| `cost` | What it cost, in millionths of a US dollar. |
| `estimated` | True when the cost was worked out from the model's listed prices because the provider didn't report one. |
| `refused` | Why the call was refused (the limit's or handler's message); empty for a call that reached the provider. |
| `job` | A music or video job's id. Its cost is filled in once the job is done. |
| `created` | When the call was made. |

It's a system collection with no API rules: superusers see it in the dashboard (Collections → `_llm_calls`), and only
your app's code and the contract above read it. Rows are kept for 13 months; a daily job deletes older ones.

To act on each call as it's recorded, such as spending a user's credits, use
[`$llm.onCallDone`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits#credits) rather than a hook on the collection: it gets the call's usage and its
user already taken apart.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/structured

# Structured answers

Most of what your code wants from a model is data, not prose: a label, a few fields pulled out of an email, a list of
tags. Pass a JSON schema as `schema`, and the answer's parsed value is `r.data`:

```ts
const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.text.completeAsync({
  model: "vultr/glm-5.3",
  reasoning: "off",
  system: "Extract the order from the email.",
  prompt: email,
  schema: {
    type: "object",
    properties: {
      name: { type: "string" },
      city: { type: "string" },
      items: {
        type: "array",
        items: {
          type: "object",
          properties: { what: { type: "string" }, count: { type: "integer" } },
          required: ["what", "count"],
          additionalProperties: false,
        },
      },
    },
    required: ["name", "city", "items"],
    additionalProperties: false,
  },
})
// "Hi, this is Dana. Please send 3 blue mugs and 2 red plates to our Austin office."
// r.data: { name: "Dana", city: "Austin", items: [{ what: "blue mugs", count: 3 }, { what: "red plates", count: 2 }] }
```

```go
r, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Complete(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{
	Model:     "vultr/glm-5.3",
	Reasoning: "off",
	System:    "Extract the order from the email.",
	Prompt:    email,
	Schema: json.RawMessage(`{
	  "type": "object",
	  "properties": {
	    "name": {"type": "string"},
	    "city": {"type": "string"},
	    "items": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
	      "properties": {"what": {"type": "string"}, "count": {"type": "integer"}},
	      "required": ["what", "count"], "additionalProperties": false}}
	  },
	  "required": ["name", "city", "items"],
	  "additionalProperties": false
	}`),
})
var order struct {
	Name, City string
	Items      []struct {
		What  string
		Count int
	}
}
err = json.Unmarshal(r.Data, &order) // {Dana Austin [{blue mugs 3} {red plates 2}]}
```

## How the schema reaches the model

The schema goes to the provider as OpenAI's `response_format` (Workers AI gets it in its own form). Most current models
follow it exactly. If an answer still isn't JSON, the call throws `bad_answer` with the start of what the model wrote.

## Tips

- An `enum` is the most reliable way to get one of a few labels.
- Say `reasoning: "off"` for extraction and labels: the thinking adds nothing and costs tokens.
- Leave room in `maxTokens`, or leave it out: an answer cut off part-way isn't valid JSON.
- OpenRouter asks models for strict JSON, which wants `additionalProperties: false` on every object.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/streaming

# Streaming answers

A model writes its answer a few words at a time. `$llm.text.streamAsync()` hands you each piece as it's written, so a page
can show the answer as it appears instead of after a wait:

```ts
const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.text.streamAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question }, (text) => {
  // called with each piece, in order; return false to stop the answer there
})
// r is the whole answer, as $llm.text.completeAsync returns it
```

```go
s, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Stream(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: question})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
var r *textv1.CompleteResult
err = s.Run(ctx, func(e any) error {
	c := e.(textv1.Chunk) // a piece of text, in order; the last one is Done, with the whole answer
	if c.Done {
		r = c.Result
	}
	return nil // an error stops the answer there
})
```

A third argument, `onReasoning`, gets the model's thinking as it's written, when the provider sends it. The callbacks
run on the app's JS VM between pieces; the waiting for each piece doesn't, so other requests are served meanwhile.

## In a page

A Pages API route forwards the pieces to the browser as server-sent events:

```ts
// pb_pages/ask.ts
module.exports = {
  async post(ctx) {
    const { question } = ctx.req.body()
    const stream = ctx.res.sse()
    try {
      const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.text.streamAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question }, (text) => stream.send("text", JSON.stringify(text)))
      stream.send("done", JSON.stringify({ usage: r.usage }))
    } catch (err: any) {
      stream.send("error", JSON.stringify(String(err.message || err)))
    }
    stream.close()
  },
}
```

In the browser, read the response as it arrives:

```js
// in the browser
const res = await fetch("/ask", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ question }) })
const reader = res.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader()
let buf = "", answer = ""
for (;;) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read()
  if (done) break
  buf += value
  let i
  while ((i = buf.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
    const block = buf.slice(0, i)
    buf = buf.slice(i + 2)
    const event = (block.match(/^event: (.*)$/m) || [])[1]
    const data = (block.match(/^data: (.*)$/m) || [])[1]
    if (event === "text") answer += JSON.parse(data) // show it
  }
}
```

The browser's `EventSource` only makes GET requests, which is why this reads the stream with `fetch`.

## Over HTTP

Outside your app's code, `POST /api/_c/llm.text/v1/stream` does the same, with the same body as `complete`, as a
superuser or with a token that has the `llm` scope. Each piece is an `event: stream` with `{"text": "..."}`, and the
last one is `{"done": true, "result": {...}}`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/media

# Pictures, speech and music

Pictures, audio and video come back as files: `{ name, type, data }`, with the bytes in `data`. `$llm.file()` turns one
into a PocketBase file, so it goes straight into a record's file field.

## Pictures

```ts
const r = await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model: "vultr/z-image-turbo", prompt: "a small lighthouse at dusk, watercolor" })
const page = new Record($app.findCollectionByNameOrId("pages"))
page.set("picture", $llm.file(r.files[0]))
$app.save(page)
```

```go
r, err := imagev1.Contract.Must(app).Generate(ctx, extkit.Internal, imagev1.GenerateInput{
	Model: "vultr/z-image-turbo", Prompt: "a small lighthouse at dusk, watercolor"})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
f, _ := filesystem.NewFileFromBytes(r.Files[0].Data, r.Files[0].Name)
page.Set("picture", f)
```

`n` asks for several, `size` (`"1024x768"`) or `aspectRatio` (`"16:9"`) shapes them, as the model allows.
`references: [file]` gives the model pictures to draw from: one to change as the prompt says, or one whose style and
characters a new scene keeps. Paint an anchor picture first and pass it with every other picture, and they share one
look:

```ts
const anchor = (await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model, prompt: "a red fox in a blue scarf, watercolor" })).files[0]
const next = await $llm.image.generateAsync({ model, references: [anchor],
  prompt: "Same style and characters as the reference. Show the fox asleep under the stars." })
```

Only models whose listing has the feature `reference images` take them (`$llm.image.modelsAsync()`, each model's
`features`): on Vultr `qwen-image-2.1` (up to 10; evaluation only, under the Qwen Research License) and `minimax-h3`
(up to 9, a still at a time), and OpenRouter's image models that read images. Cloudflare and other OpenAI-compatible
APIs answer `not_supported`.

## Speech

```ts
const r = await $llm.speech.speakAsync({ model: "vultr/qwen3-tts-12hz-1.7b", text: storyPage, voice: "vivian", instructions: "slow and calm" })
page.set("narration", $llm.file(r.file))
```

`$llm.speech.voicesAsync(model)` lists a model's voices, where the provider says. `format` picks `mp3` (the default), `wav`,
`opus` or what else the model makes.

### A voice of your own

Some models read in the voice of a clip you give them (voice cloning). Record 10 to 30 seconds read the way the story
should sound, store it in a file field, and send it as `reference` with what it says:

```ts
const clip = $app.findFirstRecordByData("voices", "name", "mine")
const r = await $llm.speech.speakAsync({
  model: "vultr/qwen3-tts-12hz-1.7b",
  text: storyPage,
  reference: { audio: $llm.fromRecord(clip, "audio"), text: clip.getString("passage") },
})
```

`$llm.fromRecord(record, field)` reads a stored file with its bytes, ready to send to a model. Leave out `voice` and
`instructions`: a cloned voice takes its delivery from the clip. A model clones when one of its voices from
`voicesAsync` has `mode: "clone"`. Nothing is saved at the provider, so the clip goes along on every call. Vultr and
OpenRouter clone; Cloudflare and other OpenAI-compatible APIs refuse a `reference` with `not_supported`. Clone only a
voice you have the right to use.

## Transcription

Send audio as a file with its bytes in `data` (base64) and a name that says its format:

```ts
const r = await $llm.transcribe.transcribeAsync({ model: "vultr/whisper-large-v3-turbo", audio: { name: "memo.mp3", data: base64Audio } })
// r.text: what was said
```

## Timing words to audio

When you already know the words (you wrote them, then had them spoken), alignment says when each line and word is
said. Give the audio and the text, one line per line; every word comes back with its start and end in seconds:

```ts
const text = "Once upon a time, a small fox lived at the edge of a quiet wood.\nEvery night, she counted the stars."
const speech = await $llm.speech.speakAsync({ model: "vultr/auk", text })
const r = await $llm.align.alignAsync({ model: "vultr/aligner-1", audio: speech.file, text, mode: "speech" })
// r.lines: [{ index: 0, text: "Once upon a time, ...", start: 0.3, end: 5.0, certain: true }, ...]
// r.words: [{ line: 0, text: "Once", start: 0.3, end: 0.44 }, ...]
```

Use `mode: "speech"` for a voice; the default, `"lyrics"`, first separates a sung vocal from its music. A line in square
brackets (`[Chorus]`) labels the lines under it and isn't timed. Vultr's `aligner-1` costs a fraction of a cent per
minute of audio.

## Music and video

These take a while, so they're jobs. The simplest way is to wait for it:

```ts
const job = await $llm.music.createAsync({ model: "vultr/ace-step-1.5", prompt: "gentle lullaby, music box and soft strings", seconds: 60, wait: "5m" })
if (job.status === "done") page.set("music", $llm.file(job.files[0]))
```

Or start it and look again later, when you'd rather not hold a request open:

```ts
const job = await $llm.music.createAsync({ model: "vultr/ace-step-1.5", prompt: "gentle lullaby", seconds: 60 })
page.set("music_job", job.id) // "vultr:music_02a2…"

// later, in a cron or the next request
const now = await $llm.music.getAsync(page.getString("music_job"))
if (now.status === "done") page.set("music", $llm.file(await $llm.music.contentAsync(now.id, 0)))
```

Video works the same with `$llm.video` (on Vultr and OpenRouter); `image` gives it a first frame to start from.

## What it costs

Media is billed per picture, per second or per character by your provider. `usage.costMicroUSD` says what a call cost, in millionths of a dollar: the provider's figure
when it reports one, else estimated from the model's listed prices (`usage.costEstimated`). `$llm.image.modelsAsync()` and
the others list each model's prices.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/conversations

# Conversations

Cloud models remember nothing between calls: every call sends the whole conversation. For a short exchange, send it
yourself as `messages`:

```ts
const r = await $llm.text.completeAsync({
  model: "vultr/glm-5.3",
  system: "You help with our notes app. Be brief.",
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: "How do I export my notes?" },
    { role: "assistant", content: "Settings → Export, then pick Markdown or PDF." },
  ],
  prompt: "And can I export just one folder?", // added as the last user message
})
```

For chats that last, the [LLM Chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-chat) extension stores them for you: it keeps every turn,
sends the recent ones with each question, and folds older ones into a summary so long chats stay quick and cheap.

```ts
const id: string = $llm.chat.new({ meta: { user: ctx.auth.id } })
const chat = $llm.chat.open(id, { model: "vultr/glm-5.3", system: "You help with our notes app. Be brief." })
const answer: LlmTextAnswer = await chat.sendAsync("How do I export my notes?")
```

Keep the id on your own record (or hand it to the browser) and open the chat again on the next question. `history()`
reads its turns, `forget()` deletes it, and `$llm.chat.list({ meta })` finds a user's chats. With `onText`, `send`
streams the answer as it's written.

## Keep the start the same

Providers cache the start of recent prompts and bill it cheaper when the next prompt starts the same way. LLM Chat
keeps the start of each turn identical until the next summary: the same system text, the same summary, the same earlier
turns. Do the same in your own calls: put what changes (the question, the passages that answer it) at the end, and keep
the system text the same from call to call.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits

# Custom limits

The [limits in Settings → LLM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits) cover how much the app, each user and each guest may spend per day or month.
Anything that depends on your app, such as a user's plan, credits they bought, or the team they belong to, goes in your
own code, in two hooks every model call passes through:

- **`$llm.onCall`** runs before every call that reaches a provider, of every kind. It can change the call (its model,
  its input, whom it counts for) or refuse it.
- **`$llm.onCallDone`** runs after a call that reached a provider, with what it used and cost. It can't refuse; the
  call has happened.

The limits in Settings → LLM are themselves an `onCall` handler, built in. Yours run before it, so the built-in limits
count the model and the user your code settled on.

Bind them once, when the app starts: in a hook file in TypeScript, or in your build's Go code. The Go hooks are
`llm.OnCall(app)` and `llm.OnCallDone(app)` in the shared contract package (`llmc` below is
`pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/llm`), so another extension, a billing one say, can bind them too.

```ts
// pb_hooks/limits.pb.ts
$llm.onCall((e: LlmCallEvent) => {
  // e.kind ("text", "image", ...), e.op, e.model, e.input, e.subject, e.user ({ collection, id } or null), e.guest
  if (String(e.input.prompt ?? "").length > 20000) throw e.refuse("That question is too long.")
  e.next()
})
```

```go
llmc.OnCall(app).BindFunc(func(e *llmc.CallEvent) error {
	// e.Kind, e.Op, e.Model, e.Input (a pointer to the operation's input), e.Subject
	if in, ok := e.Input.(*textv1.CompleteInput); ok && len(in.Prompt) > 20000 {
		return e.Refuse("That question is too long.")
	}
	return e.Next()
})
```

## onCall

A handler gets one call on its way to a provider:

| TypeScript | Go | |
|---|---|---|
| `e.kind` | `e.Kind` | `text`, `image`, `speech`, `transcribe`, `align`, `music`, `video` or `embed`. |
| `e.op` | `e.Op` | The operation: `complete`, `stream`, `generate`, `edit`, `speak`, `transcribe`, `align`, `create` (music and video) or `embed`. |
| `e.model` | `e.Model` | The model, as `provider/model`. Set it to send the call to another model. |
| `e.input` | `e.Input` | The call's input: `prompt`, `messages`, `maxTokens`, `size`... as the page passed it. Change any of it. In Go it's a pointer to the operation's input (`*textv1.CompleteInput` for text, `*imagev1.GenerateInput` for pictures, ...). |
| `e.subject` | `e.Subject` | Whom the call is for (see [Users and guests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests)). Set it to count the call for someone else, or for a name of your own (`team:acme`). |
| `e.user` | `llmc.ParseSubject(e.Subject)` | The signed-in user the call is for, as `{ collection, id }`, or `null`. |
| `e.guest` | `llmc.IsGuest(e.Subject)` | `true` when the call is for a guest. |
| `e.guestsCapped` | `e.GuestsCapped` | Set it to `true` when your handler takes care of what guests spend (see below). |

Then it does one of two things:

- **`e.next()`** (Go: `return e.Next()`) lets the call go on, with whatever the handler changed.
- **`throw e.refuse("message")`** (Go: `return e.Refuse("message")`) refuses it. The page's `$llm` call throws with
  `err.code` `limit` (HTTP 429) and your message, the same as a built-in limit's refusal, so one `catch` handles both,
  and the ledger records it as refused, with your message.

A handler that does neither refuses the call too, with a message saying a handler didn't call `e.next()`: forgetting
`next()` never lets a call through unchecked.

Handlers run in the order they're bound, all before the built-in limits. A TypeScript handler runs on the app's JS VM,
but the model call itself doesn't: the handler runs, then the model works off the VM, and the app keeps serving other
requests. A handler may be `async`, but every call waits for it, so keep it to quick reads.

## onCallDone

A handler gets a call that reached a provider, with what it used:

| TypeScript | Go | |
|---|---|---|
| `e.kind`, `e.op`, `e.model`, `e.subject`, `e.user`, `e.guest` | `e.Kind`, `e.Op`, `e.Model`, `e.Subject` | As in `onCall`, with the values the call was made with. |
| `e.usage` | `e.Usage` | What it used: input, output and cached tokens, seconds, and the cost in millionths of a dollar (`costMicroUSD`, Go `CostMicroUSD`). |
| `e.job` | `e.Job` | A music or video job's id. A job's `onCallDone` comes once it's done and its cost is known (when `createAsync` with `wait`, or a later `getAsync`, sees it finish). |

A refused call has no `onCallDone`. An error a handler throws is logged and doesn't affect the call. The ledger row is
already written when `onCallDone` runs.

## Plan tiers

Free users get 10 questions a day and the small model; paid users get the big one. The plan lives on the user's record;
the count comes from [the ledger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend):

```ts
// pb_hooks/plans.pb.ts: users have a "plan" select field, "free" or "pro"
$llm.onCall((e: LlmCallEvent) => {
  if (!e.user) return e.next() // guests and background work: the built-in limits handle them
  const user = $app.findRecordById(e.user.collection, e.user.id)
  if (user.get("plan") !== "pro") {
    e.model = "vultr/glm-5.3-mini"
    e.input.maxTokens = Math.min(e.input.maxTokens || 800, 800)
    if ($llm.ledger.spent({ subject: e.subject, window: "day" }).calls >= 10) {
      throw e.refuse("Free accounts get 10 questions a day. Upgrade for more, or come back tomorrow.")
    }
  }
  e.next()
})
```

```go
llmc.OnCall(app).BindFunc(func(e *llmc.CallEvent) error {
	p := llmc.ParseSubject(e.Subject)
	if p.Kind != "user" {
		return e.Next() // guests and background work: the built-in limits handle them
	}
	user, err := e.App.FindRecordById(p.Collection, p.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if user.GetString("plan") != "pro" {
		e.Model = "vultr/glm-5.3-mini"
		if in, ok := e.Input.(*textv1.CompleteInput); ok && (in.MaxTokens == 0 || in.MaxTokens > 800) {
			in.MaxTokens = 800
		}
		spent, err := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(e.App).Spent(e.Context, extkit.Internal,
			ledgerv1.SpentInput{Subject: e.Subject, Window: "day"})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if spent.Calls >= 10 {
			return e.Refuse("Free accounts get 10 questions a day. Upgrade for more, or come back tomorrow.")
		}
	}
	return e.Next()
})
```

## Credits

Users buy credits; every call spends them. Refuse before a call when the balance is empty, and take the cost off after:

```ts
// pb_hooks/credits.pb.ts: users have a "credits" number field, in millionths of a dollar
$llm.onCall((e: LlmCallEvent) => {
  if (e.user && $app.findRecordById(e.user.collection, e.user.id).getInt("credits") <= 0) {
    throw e.refuse("You're out of credits.")
  }
  e.next()
})

$llm.onCallDone((e: LlmCallDoneEvent) => {
  if (e.user && e.usage.costMicroUSD > 0) {
    $app.db()
      .newQuery("UPDATE " + e.user.collection + " SET credits = credits - {:cost} WHERE id = {:id}")
      .bind({ cost: e.usage.costMicroUSD, id: e.user.id })
      .execute()
  }
  e.next()
})
```

```go
llmc.OnCall(app).BindFunc(func(e *llmc.CallEvent) error {
	if p := llmc.ParseSubject(e.Subject); p.Kind == "user" {
		user, err := e.App.FindRecordById(p.Collection, p.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if user.GetInt("credits") <= 0 {
			return e.Refuse("You're out of credits.")
		}
	}
	return e.Next()
})

llmc.OnCallDone(app).BindFunc(func(e *llmc.CallDoneEvent) error {
	if p := llmc.ParseSubject(e.Subject); p.Kind == "user" && e.Usage.CostMicroUSD > 0 {
		_, err := e.App.DB().NewQuery("UPDATE {{" + p.Collection + "}} SET [[credits]] = [[credits]] - {:cost} WHERE [[id]] = {:id}").
			Bind(dbx.Params{"cost": e.Usage.CostMicroUSD, "id": p.ID}).Execute()
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return e.Next()
})
```

The check comes before the call and the cost after it, so a user's last call can take their balance a little below
zero.

## Team buckets

Count every member's calls toward their team, so a team shares one allowance:

```ts
// pb_hooks/teams.pb.ts: users have a "team" relation
$llm.onCall((e: LlmCallEvent) => {
  if (e.user) {
    const team = $app.findRecordById(e.user.collection, e.user.id).get("team")
    if (team) e.subject = "team:" + team
  }
  e.next()
})
```

```go
llmc.OnCall(app).BindFunc(func(e *llmc.CallEvent) error {
	if p := llmc.ParseSubject(e.Subject); p.Kind == "user" {
		if user, err := e.App.FindRecordById(p.Collection, p.ID); err == nil && user.GetString("team") != "" {
			e.Subject = "team:" + user.GetString("team")
		}
	}
	return e.Next()
})
```

The ledger then records the team as the subject, and `$llm.ledger.spent({ subject: "team:" + teamId, window: "month" })`
is what the team has used. The built-in limits on **each signed-in user** and **each guest** count users and guests,
not teams: a team's own allowance is a check in your handler, like the plan tier's above.

## Guests in your own code

Guest calls are refused until there's a limit on all guests together, because a guest can clear their cookies and come
back with a fresh allowance ([Limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits#guests-need-a-total)). If your handler takes care of guests itself,
say so with `e.guestsCapped = true`, and the built-in limits let guest calls through without that limit:

```ts
// pb_hooks/guests.pb.ts: guests get the small model, short answers, and 200 calls a day between them
$llm.onCall((e: LlmCallEvent) => {
  if (e.guest) {
    e.model = "vultr/glm-5.3-mini"
    e.input.maxTokens = 300
    if ($llm.ledger.spent({ subject: "guests", window: "day" }).calls >= 200) {
      throw e.refuse("We've answered all the questions we can today. Come back tomorrow.")
    }
    e.subject = "guests" // count every guest in one bucket of our own
    e.guestsCapped = true
  }
  e.next()
})
```

```go
llmc.OnCall(app).BindFunc(func(e *llmc.CallEvent) error {
	if llmc.IsGuest(e.Subject) {
		e.Model = "vultr/glm-5.3-mini"
		if in, ok := e.Input.(*textv1.CompleteInput); ok {
			in.MaxTokens = 300
		}
		spent, err := ledgerv1.Contract.Must(e.App).Spent(e.Context, extkit.Internal,
			ledgerv1.SpentInput{Subject: "guests", Window: "day"})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if spent.Calls >= 200 {
			return e.Refuse("We've answered all the questions we can today. Come back tomorrow.")
		}
		e.Subject = "guests" // count every guest in one bucket of our own
		e.GuestsCapped = true
	}
	return e.Next()
})
```

Counting every guest under one subject of your own makes their shared total one `spent` call. The ledger then shows
`guests` instead of each guest's id; keep the subject as it is if you'd rather see each one. Only set `guestsCapped`
when your code really does cap what guests spend. Otherwise add the limit in Settings → LLM.

## Order and the built-in limits

Handlers run by priority, then in the order they're bound. Bound the usual way they have priority 0, and the built-in
limits are bound with the id `llmc.LimitsHandlerID` and priority `llmc.LimitsPriority` (1000), so yours run first. In
Go, bind with a higher priority to run after the built-in limits, or unbind them to replace them entirely:

```go
llmc.OnCall(app).Bind(&hook.Handler[*llmc.CallEvent]{
	Priority: llmc.LimitsPriority + 1, // after the built-in limits: only calls they let through reach it
	Func: func(e *llmc.CallEvent) error {
		e.App.Logger().Info("llm call allowed", "model", e.Model, "subject", e.Subject)
		return e.Next()
	},
})

llmc.OnCall(app).Unbind(llmc.LimitsHandlerID) // no built-in limits: your handlers decide everything
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/overview

# Overview of Pages

Pages turns a folder of files into a server-rendered website, inside PocketOne. It is built in as the `pages` extension (`ext/pages`): no npm package, no boot file, no build step.

Use Pages to create slim and modern web apps:

- Start small and iterate
- SEO-first principles
- No build step
- Fast server-side rendering

## Hello world in just one file

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/index.ets -->
<%= `Hello, world!` %>
```

<%- include('browser', { content: `Hello, world!` }) %>

Inside `<%` and `%>` you write TypeScript; types are stripped, never checked, so plain JavaScript works too. Every page gets a `ctx` object with the request, the response, your data, and the app itself (`ctx.app`), so you can read and write records directly.

## Retro file-based routing

Files become URLs, and `+layout.ets` files wrap the pages below them:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ets -->
<html>
  <body style="background-color: #b5dcb5">
    <%- slot() %>
  </body>
</html>
```

<%- include('browser', { bodyTags: `style="background-color: #b5dcb5"`, content: `Hello, world!` }) %>

## Coming from the npm package?

Pages is a clean API. Apps written for PocketPages 0.x (the npm package) don't run unchanged. See [Moving from PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x

# Moving from PocketPages 0.x

Pages is part of PocketOne (the `pages` extension). It keeps the ideas of the npm package (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for 0.x don't run unchanged.

There is no migration tool. Start a new app with `pocketone pages create <name>`, then move your pages over using the list below. The npm package is being retired.

## Folder and boot

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `pb_hooks/pages/`, booted by `require('pocketpages')` in a `.pb.js` file | `pb_pages/` next to `pb_data`. No boot file, no npm install. |
| `create-pocketpages` | `pocketone pages create <name> [--starter <kit>]` |

Delete the `.pb.js` boot file and the `pocketpages` dependencies, and move the contents of `pb_hooks/pages/` to `pb_pages/`.

## JavaScript or TypeScript

Your `.ejs` templates, `+middleware.js`, `+config.js` and `_private/` modules stay as they are. v1 also runs
TypeScript (`.ts` code and `.ets` templates, types stripped, never checked), and the rest of these docs use it.
Renaming a file from `.js` to `.ts` or `.ejs` to `.ets` changes nothing else, so you can switch a file at a time or not
at all. A route's own code (a page's loaders and handlers, an endpoint) is always `.ts`, since a `.js` file on a route
path is served to the browser as-is; plain JavaScript is valid there. This guide shows the rest of v1's code as `.js`
to match yours. See [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types).

## The context object

0.x passed an `api` object and spread its members into each template. v1 passes one `ctx` object with `req`, `res`, `data`, `params`, `route` and helpers. See the [ctx reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx).

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `request`, `response` | `ctx.req`, `ctx.res` |
| `body()`, `formData` | `ctx.req.body()` |
| `redirect(path)` | `ctx.res.redirect(path)` |
| `response.redirect(path, status)` | `ctx.res.redirect(path, status)` (unchanged) |
| `env()`, `store()`, `dbg()`, `info()`, `warn()`, `error()` | `ctx.env()`, `ctx.store()`, `ctx.log.debug()` / `info()` / `warn()` / `error()` |
| `auth`, `request.auth` | `ctx.auth` |
| `resolve(name)` | `ctx.resolve(name)` |

Inside templates, `data`, `params`, `asset` and `meta` are still available without the `ctx.` prefix. The other
0.x template globals are gone, including `resolve`, `redirect` and `env`: use `ctx.resolve()`, `ctx.res.redirect()` and
`ctx.env()`.

## Parameters, query strings and cookies

- Query parameters are no longer mixed into `params`, and nothing is JSON-parsed for you. `ctx.params` holds route parameters only; read the query string with `ctx.req.query(name)`, which returns strings.
- Cookies are strings. Pass `{ json: true }` to parse one: `ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true })`.

## Middleware

0.x middleware either returned a value or called `next(extra)`, depending on how many arguments it declared. v1 has one signature:

```js
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.user = ctx.auth
  return next()
}
```

Put shared data on `ctx.data`. See [Middleware](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware).

## Loaders

`+load.js`, `+get.js`, `+post.js` and friends are replaced by one `.ts` file beside each page (`products.ts` beside `products.ejs`) that exports `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`. Returned objects are shallow-assigned into `ctx.data` (no deep merge). As in 0.x, every handler is optional and a page renders for any method, so templates that check the request method keep working (`request.method` becomes `ctx.req.method`).

```js
// 0.x: +load.js
module.exports = (api) => ({ products: $app.findAllRecords('products') })

// v1: products.ts, beside products.ejs
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') }
  },
}
```

See [Loading Data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data).

## JSON

0.x sent template output as JSON if it parsed as JSON. v1 never does. Send JSON with `ctx.res.json()`, usually from an endpoint: a `.ts` file with no template, such as `feeds/latest.ts`. See [Endpoints and JSON](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes).

## Layouts and slots

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `<!-- slot:name -->` comments in the page | `slot('name', () => { %>...<% })` |
| `slot` and `slots.name` in layouts | `slot()` and `slot('name')` |

See [Layouts and Slots](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts).

## Output

`echo()` is gone. A template returns its text; anything you want in the output goes through a tag. For streaming, use `ctx.res.sse()`.

## Flash messages

0.x put the message in a `?__flash=` query parameter with `redirect(path, { message })`. v1 uses a one-time cookie:

```js
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
```

Read it on the next request with `ctx.flash()`. See [flash](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash).

## Assets

`asset()` URLs now carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256, not the full hash.

## Configuration and plugins

- `+config.js` still takes plugin package names, which are loaded with `require` as before, but the packages must be
  v1 plugins: the 0.x `pocketpages-plugin-*` packages don't run on v1. `auth` and `realtime` are built in, EJS and
  Markdown are always on, and Datastar is an [add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar) you copy into `pb_pages/_private/` and list as `'datastar'`. Its API is 0.x's, with `signals()` added alongside `readSignals`. npm plugin package names and EJS options are gone.
- `+config.js` must export an object (`module.exports = { ... }`). 0.x's function form, `module.exports = (api) => ({ ... })`, is an error.
- A `package.json` at the app's root still works: bare `require('pkg')` looks in the app folder's `node_modules` after `pb_pages`.
- EJS and Markdown are always on. `pocketpages-plugin-ejs` and `pocketpages-plugin-marked` have no v1 equivalent because they aren't needed.
- The auth plugin no longer goes through the JS SDK over HTTP (`api.pb()`). Use `ctx.session.*`, which calls the app directly. See [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth).

See [+config.js](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config) and [Plugins](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins).

## Behavior that changed quietly

These don't fail with an error, so check for them when porting:

- **Cookies are `HttpOnly` by default.** Pass `{ httpOnly: false }` to `ctx.res.cookie` for a cookie your page's JS reads. The `pb_auth` cookie stays `HttpOnly`, so `pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie)` in the browser no longer works.
- **Realtime messages are JSON-encoded.** `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data)` sends `JSON.stringify(data)`, so a string (such as an HTML fragment) arrives in quotes: `JSON.parse` it on the client. A `filter` now gets one argument, the client, and only narrows clients already subscribed to the topic.
- **`.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` files are always pages**, never served as static files.
- **Front matter is plain YAML.** EJS tags inside it aren't run.
- **`require` never leaves `pb_pages`.** To load code from `pb_hooks`, use `require(__hooks + '/lib/x')`.
- **Hook files (`*.pb.js`) go in `pb_hooks`.** In `pb_pages` they're an error and aren't served.

## Removed globals

| 0.x | v1 |
|---|---|
| `url()` | `ctx.req.url` |
| `stringify()` | `JSON.stringify` |
| micro-dash | plain JavaScript |
| `pb()` (JS SDK plugin) | `ctx.pb()`, built in: same SDK, no host setting, runs in-process as the signed-in user |

## Routing

A route with fewer segments no longer matches a longer URL. Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ejs` serves `/products/123` but not `/products/123/reviews`.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/agents

# Installation

Pages is built into PocketOne as the `pages` extension (`ext/pages`). There is nothing to install from npm: the standard `pocketone` binary includes it.

<%- include('quickstart') %>

`pocketone pages create myapp` creates a new app. Add `--starter <kit>` to start from a [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits).

_Note: `--dir` tells `pocketone` where `pb_data` is. Pages looks for `pb_pages` next to it. Create the superuser before the first `serve`; otherwise PocketBase opens its superuser installer in your browser._

Browse to `http://localhost:8090` and you'll see the starter's home page. The default `minimal` kit is one splash page:

<%- include('browser', { content: `<h1>PocketOne</h1>` }) %>

To start editing, open

```
myapp/pb_pages/index.ets
```

Changes appear on the next refresh. The app doesn't restart.

## Where pages live

Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/  pb_hooks/  pb_migrations/  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
```

- Pages finds the folder at `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, or wherever `--pagesDir` points.
- If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app.
- Under a multitenant host, every instance has its own `pb_pages`.

## How does it work?

Pages is a multi-page app server for PocketOne. It listens for requests and renders pages using file-based routing rules, like old-school PHP. URLs under `/api/` and `/_/` always belong to PocketBase. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits

# Starter Kits

To start a new app from a starter kit, run:

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter <kit>
```

Without `--starter`, `pocketone pages create myapp` creates a plain app (the `minimal` kit). `pocketone pages starters`
lists the kits. The folder must not exist yet. Then run it:

```bash
cd myapp
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

`pocketone` keeps `pb_data` next to its executable unless you pass `--dir`; `pb_pages` and `pb_migrations` are found next
to `pb_data`.

Each kit, with its files and what each one does, has its page under [Starter kits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters).

Each starter kit is an ordinary `pb_pages` folder written against the v1 API, in TypeScript with [ETS templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets), so everything in these docs applies to it. The **tsx** kit starts an app in the [component style](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx) instead.

| Starter | What it shows | Live demo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **minimal** | A minimal Pages starter with just the basics | [pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-minimal.pockethost.io) |
| **mvp** | MVP.css, a minimalist classless CSS framework | [pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-mvp.pockethost.io) |
| **auth** | Password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 sign-in, plus verification, password reset and email change | [pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io) |
| **daisyui** | Tailwind CSS with DaisyUI components | [pocketpages-daisyui.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-daisyui.pockethost.io) |
| **daisyui-docs** | Documentation site template with DaisyUI and navigation | [pocketpages-daisyui-docs.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-daisyui-docs.pockethost.io) |
| **htmx** | HTMX integration for dynamic interactions | [pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-htmx.pockethost.io) |
| **datastar** | Realtime chat and counter using Datastar | [pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-datastar.pockethost.io) |
| **tsx** | The minimal app written as TSX components (layout, page and a partial) | |
