# Creating a Page

A **page** is a template file, `.ets` or `.md`, anywhere in `pb_pages/`. Its path becomes its URL. (A `.tsx` component works too; see [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types).)

## Creating pages

1. **Create a file**: inside `pb_pages/`, create an `.ets` file. For example, an "About" page:

```text
pb_pages/about.ets  -> serves "/about"
```

2. **`index` files**: `index` maps to its folder.

```text
pb_pages/index.ets           -> serves "/"
pb_pages/products/index.ets  -> serves "/products" (and "/products/")
```

3. **Nested pages**: folders become URL segments.

```text
pb_pages/
├── index.ets         -> "/"
├── about.ets         -> "/about"
├── contact.ets       -> "/contact"
└── products/
    ├── index.ets     -> "/products"
    └── details.ets   -> "/products/details"
```

4. **Markdown pages**: a `.md` file works the same way. Its tags run first (plain JavaScript), then Markdown. See [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown).

```text
pb_pages/docs/routing.md  -> "/docs/routing"
```

The extension is always dropped from the URL. To add data or handle forms, put a `.ts` file with the same name next to the page (`about.ts` beside `about.ets`); see [Loading Data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/directory-structure

# Directory Structure

All pages live in the `pb_pages/` folder, next to `pb_data/`:

```
myapp/
  pb_data/
  pb_hooks/
  pb_migrations/
  pb_public/
  pb_pages/
    +config.ts
    +layout.ets
    index.ets
    about.ets
    _private/
      nav.ets
    assets/
      app.css
    products/
      [id].ets
      [id].ts
    feeds/
      latest.ts
```

## Special names

A file or folder name starting with one of these characters is never a URL:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file: `+layout.ets` (or `+layout.tsx`) and `+middleware.ts`, one of each per folder. `+config.ts`, `+error.ets` and `+404.ets` are allowed only at the top of `pb_pages`. Any other `+` name, any other extension (such as `+layout.md`), and a top-only file in a subfolder are errors at startup. |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules for `include()` and `ctx.resolve()`. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes). |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level `.well-known/`, which is served as static files (ACME challenges, `security.txt`, app links). |

`node_modules/` is never routed either.

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` groups files without adding a URL segment: `(marketing)/pricing.ets` serves `/pricing`. A group can have its own `+layout.ets`, `+middleware.ts` and `_private/`.

## What else

- A `.ts` file beside a template of the same name is that page's code (`products/[id].ts`); any other `.ts` is an
  [endpoint](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes) at its own URL (`feeds/latest.ts` serves `/feeds/latest`).
- Every other file, `.js` included, is a [static file](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content), served as-is.
- Page code can `require()` modules by name from `_private/` folders (nearest first), then `pb_pages/node_modules`, then
  `pb_hooks/node_modules` and the app folder's `node_modules`, then the app's usual module paths.
- Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves `pb_pages`.
- A `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup, because `/api/` belongs to PocketBase.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types

# File types

PocketOne apps are server-rendered pages with no build step. Every file in `pb_pages` is either code, a template or
a static file, and you write code and templates in TypeScript. PocketOne strips the types when it first uses a file,
with esbuild built into the binary; it never checks them.

## Code

A route's `.ts` (a page's code, or an endpoint), `+middleware.ts`, `+config.ts` and the modules in `_private/` are
TypeScript files. They export functions and objects, and never produce HTML themselves. To check their types with your editor or `tsc`, see
[TypeScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/typescript).

## Templates: pick one style

A template turns data into HTML. There are two styles, and an app uses one of them:

| | ETS | TSX |
|---|---|---|
| A file is | HTML with code in `<% %>` tags | a function that returns markup |
| Pages | `about.ets` | `about.tsx` |
| Layouts, error pages | `+layout.ets`, `+error.ets`, `+404.ets` | `+layout.tsx`, `+error.tsx`, `+404.tsx` |
| Partials | `_private/card.ets`, `include('card', { item })` | `_private/Card.tsx`, `<Card item={item} />` |
| Good for | HTML-first apps, HTMX, Datastar, content sites | apps built from components, typed props |
| Read more | [ETS templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets) | [Components with TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx) |

These docs use ETS. It's the closest to what the browser gets: open the file and you see the page.

Both styles render on the server and send plain HTML. Neither has a client runtime, hydration or state; interactivity
comes from links, forms, HTMX, Datastar or a `<script>`.

The styles can include each other, which helps when you move an app from one to the other, but an app that mixes them
is harder to read. [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown) pages are the exception every app shares: a `.md` file runs EJS tags with
plain JavaScript inside, as a small escape hatch in content.

## JavaScript works too

Templates, `+middleware`, `+config` and `_private/` modules have JavaScript twins that behave the same, without
types. Rename a file and nothing else changes:

| TypeScript | JavaScript |
|---|---|
| `.ts` | `.js` |
| `.ets` | `.ejs` |
| `.tsx` | `.jsx` |

A route's code is the one exception: it is always `.ts`, because a `.js` file on a route path is a browser script,
served as-is. Apps written for [PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x) use `.js` and `.ejs`. A folder can't have two
framework files with the same name, such as `+layout.ets` beside `+layout.ejs`.

## Everything else

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `.ts` on a route path | A page's [code](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#page-code), or an [endpoint](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes) |
| `.d.ts` | Type declarations: neither served nor run |
| `.md` | A [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown) page or partial |
| `.json` | Data you can `require` |
| `.js` and any other file | A [static file](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content), served as-is |


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/routing

# File-Based Routing

URLs come from the files and folders in `pb_pages/`.

## Pages

| File | URL |
|---|---|
| `index.ets` | `/` |
| `about.ets` | `/about` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` (and `/docs/`) |
| `docs/routing.md` | `/docs/routing` |
| `products/[id].ets` | `/products/123`, with `ctx.params.id = "123"` |
| `[org]/[repo]/index.ets` | `/acme/web`, with `ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" }` |

- The extension is dropped. `index` maps to its folder.
- `[name]` matches exactly one non-empty segment. A parameter must be the whole segment: `post-[id].ets` is an error at startup.
- Segment counts must match: `products/[id].ets` doesn't match `/products/123/reviews`.
- A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one.
- Matching is case-sensitive.

See [Accessing Parameters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/parameters).

## Groups

A folder named `(name)` doesn't add a URL segment. Use groups to give part of the site its own layout or middleware:

```text
pb_pages/
  (site)/
    +layout.ets     # wraps everything in (site)
    index.ets       # /
    about.ets       # /about
  xapi/
    count.ets       # /xapi/count, outside the (site) layout
```

## Code: `.ts` files

A `.ts` file runs, the way a `.php` file does. Its path is its URL, as for a page:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `about.ts` beside `about.ets` | that page's code: `load` feeds the template, a `post` handles its form. See [Loading data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#page-code). |
| `feeds/rss.ts` | an endpoint at `/feeds/rss`, with no template: its handlers send the whole response (JSON, a feed, a redirect). See [Endpoints and JSON](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes). |
| `feeds/index.ts`, `products/[id].ts` | the folder's URL, a `[param]` route, as for pages |

Only `.ts` runs. A `.js` file is a [static file](#static-files) like any other, so browser scripts can sit anywhere in `pb_pages`. `.d.ts` files are neither served nor run.

## Static files

Every other file is served as-is at its path, with groups removed: `assets/app.css` serves `/assets/app.css`. See [Static content](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content).

## Which route wins

1. `/api/...` and `/_/...` belong to PocketBase. Pages never see them.
2. Among matching routes the most specific wins: segments are compared from the left, and a literal segment beats a `[param]`. So `products/new.ets` beats `products/[id].ets` for `/products/new`.
3. Two files can't claim the same URL: a page and a static file, or an endpoint and a page (`feed.ts` and `feed/index.ets`). A `.ts` beside a template of the same name is that page's code, not a second claim. These are startup errors.
4. A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, then to PocketBase.

## When routes change

The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads `pb_hooks`. Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path, and the previous route table keeps serving.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/parameters

# Route and Query Parameters

Route parameters come from the URL path. Query parameters come from the query string. v1 keeps them apart.

## Route parameters

Use square brackets in file or folder names to capture a URL segment:

```
pb_pages/
  products/
    [productId]/
      index.ets
      reviews/
        [reviewId].ets
```

This handles URLs like `/products/123` and `/products/123/reviews/456`.

Read them through `params` (the same object as `ctx.params`):

```ets
<!-- products/[productId]/reviews/[reviewId].ets -->
<h1>Product: <%= params.productId %></h1>
<p>Review: <%= params.reviewId %></p>
```

Route parameters are always strings. `ctx.params` never includes query parameters.

## Query parameters

Read the query string with `ctx.req.query()`:

```
/products/123?sort=latest&tag=red&tag=blue
```

```ets
<p>Sort by: <%= ctx.req.query('sort') %></p>
<p>Tags: <%= ctx.req.query('tag', { all: true }).join(', ') %></p>
```

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `ctx.req.query(name)` | First value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `ctx.req.query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `ctx.req.query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |

Values are strings. Nothing is parsed for you; if you pass JSON in a query parameter, parse it yourself:

```ts
const filters = JSON.parse(ctx.req.query('filters') ?? '{}')
```

## The route itself

`ctx.route` describes the matched route: `{ path, name, file }`. For `products/[productId]/index.ets`, `path` is `/products/[productId]`, `name` is `index`, and `file` is `products/[productId]/index.ets`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data

# Loading Data in Pages

You can load data right in a template, or in a `.ts` file of the same name next to it.

## Inline data loading

The simplest way is a `<% %>` block at the top of your template:

```ets
<%
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
%>

<h1>Products</h1>
<% for (const product of products) { %>
  <div class="product">
    <h2><%= product.getString('name') %></h2>
  </div>
<% } %>
```

## Server script blocks

For better formatting support in editors, you can write `<script server<%- '>' %>` instead of `<% %>`. They mean the same thing:

```ets
<script server<%- '>' %>
  const products = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
  const categories = ctx.app.findAllRecords('categories')
</script>

<h1>Products by Category</h1>
<% for (const category of categories) { %>
  <h2><%= category.getString('name') %></h2>
<% } %>
```

## Page code

A `.ts` file beside a template, with the same name, is that page's code. It keeps data loading and form handling out of the template: `about.ts` goes with `about.ets`, `index.ts` with `index.ets`, `[id].ts` with `[id].ets`.

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { qty } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
    return ctx.res.redirect(`/products/${ctx.params.id}`, { flash: 'Added to cart' })
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id].ets -->
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %><p><%= flash %></p><% } %>
```

### Exports

Page code exports any of `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`.

1. `load` runs first, for every method.
2. Then the handler for the request method runs, if there is one.
3. Then the page renders.

A handler can set fields on `ctx.data`, or return a plain object. A returned object is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data` (`Object.assign`); there is no deep merge.

```ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') }
  },
  get(ctx) {
    ctx.data.mode = 'view'
  },
}
```

If a handler sends a response (`ctx.res.redirect`, `json`, `html`, `text`, `file`, `sse`), the page doesn't render.

### Async loading

`load` and the method handlers can be `async`. Pages waits for them before it renders. Every Go function has an
`.async` twin that does its work outside the JS VM, so other requests keep running while it waits:

```ts
// pb_pages/dashboard.ts, beside dashboard.ets
module.exports = {
  async load(ctx) {
    const [orders, users] = await Promise.all([
      ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders'),
      ctx.app.countRecords.async('users'),
    ])
    return { orders, users }
  },
}
```

What an async handler returns is used just like a returned object, and an error it throws (or a rejected promise)
fails the request like any other error. You can also `await` right in a template: see [ETS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets#await) and
[JSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx#async-components).

### Code several pages share

Each page has its own code file. Put code that several pages share in a `_private/` module and `require` it, or in a [`+middleware.ts`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware) when a whole section needs it:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts
const { reviewsFor } = require('./_private/reviews')

module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { reviews: reviewsFor(ctx.app, ctx.params.id) }
  },
}
```

### Methods without a handler

Every handler is optional. A page renders for any method, like PHP, so a template can handle a form on its own:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/contact.ets, no contact.ts -->
<% if (ctx.req.method === 'POST') { %>
  <p>Thanks, <%= ctx.req.body().name %>!</p>
<% } else { %>
  <form method="post"><input name="name" /><button>Send</button></form>
<% } %>
```

A `post` (or `put`, ...) handler in the page's code is the tidier place for form logic as a page grows, but you don't
need one. Only [endpoints](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes), which have nothing to render, answer `405` for a method they have no
handler for.

## Example: a contact form

```ts
// pb_pages/contact.ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { departments: ctx.app.findAllRecords('departments') }
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, message, department } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      const record = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId('messages'))
      record.set('email', email)
      record.set('message', message)
      record.set('department', department)
      ctx.app.save(record)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: 'Failed to send message', values: { email, message, department } }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/contact', { flash: 'Thanks, we got your message.' })
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/contact.ets -->
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %><p><%= flash %></p><% } %>
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>

<form method="post">
  <input name="email" type="email" value="<%= data.values?.email %>" />
  <select name="department">
    <% for (const d of data.departments) { %>
      <option value="<%= d.id %>"><%= d.getString('name') %></option>
    <% } %>
  </select>
  <textarea name="message"><%= data.values?.message %></textarea>
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>
```

## Pages without a template

A `.ts` file with no template of the same name serves its URL from code: an [endpoint](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes). Use one for a
page you'd rather build in code, or for a URL that only acts and redirects:

```ts
// pb_pages/logout.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ts
// pb_pages/hello.ts
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    return ctx.res.html(`<h1>Hello ${ctx.auth ? ctx.auth.getString('name') : 'there'}</h1>`)
  },
}
```

- With no template to render, each handler must send a response; returning without one is a 500.
- Methods without a handler answer `405`, `GET` included: `/logout` above only takes `POST`.
- Folder middleware runs; layouts don't, so wrap HTML yourself (or render a partial with `ctx.include`).
- Errors are JSON, or your `+error.ets` page when the request asks for HTML first (a browser opening the URL).

## Middleware or page code?

- Only the page's own `.ts` runs.
- Every `+middleware.ts` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder runs, root first.

Use [middleware](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware) for data or checks that a whole section of the site shares.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes

# Endpoints and JSON

A `.ts` file with no template of the same name is an **endpoint**: it serves its own URL from code. Use one for JSON, feeds, webhooks, event streams and anything else that isn't an HTML page.

```ts
// pb_pages/feeds/latest.ts
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20)
    return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') })))
  },
}
```

A request to `/feeds/latest` returns:

```json
[{ "id": "abc123", "title": "Hello" }]
```

## How it works

- The URL comes from the file's path, as for pages: `feeds/latest.ts` serves `/feeds/latest`, `feeds/index.ts` serves `/feeds`, `products/[id].ts` serves `/products/123`.
- An endpoint has the same exports as [page code](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#page-code): `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`.
- There is no template, so a handler must send a response. Returning without one is a `500`.
- A method with no handler answers `405`, `GET` included, with an `Allow` header listing the methods it has.
- An endpoint and a page can't claim the same URL: `feed.ts` and `feed/index.ets` is an error at startup.
- Middleware runs for endpoints too; layouts don't.
- Handlers can be `async`. The response is sent once the handler settles.

## Errors

An error thrown in an endpoint (`ctx.httpError()` or any other) answers with JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "..." }`. When the request's `Accept` header puts `text/html` first, as a browser does when someone opens the URL, the error is your `+error.ets` page instead.

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByFilter('products', 'id = {:id}', { id: ctx.params.id })
    if (!product) throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product')
    return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') })
  },
}
```

## Async handlers

```ts
// pb_pages/stats.ts
module.exports = {
  async get(ctx) {
    const orders = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders')
    return ctx.res.json({ orders })
  },
}
```

An async handler still has to send a response. Returning a value without calling `ctx.res.json` (or another
`ctx.res` method) is a `500`, as it is for a sync handler.

## Sending responses

| Call | Sends |
|---|---|
| `ctx.res.json(data)` / `ctx.res.json(status, data)` | JSON |
| `ctx.res.text(text)` / `ctx.res.text(status, text)` | Plain text |
| `ctx.res.html(html)` / `ctx.res.html(status, html)` | HTML as-is, without layouts |
| `ctx.res.file(path)` | A file from `pb_pages` |
| `ctx.res.redirect(location)` | A redirect |
| `ctx.res.sse()` | A `text/event-stream` |

See [res](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res).

## JSON from a page

JSON is only sent through `ctx.res.json` (and an endpoint's errors). Template output is never parsed as JSON, even if it looks like JSON. A page's code can still answer with JSON for one method:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts, beside products/[id].ets
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
    return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') })
  },
}
```

## Keep `/api/` free

`/api/` belongs to PocketBase. Pages never see it, and a `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup. Put your endpoints somewhere else, such as `feeds/`, `xapi/` or `hooks/`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets

# ETS templates

An `.ets` file is an HTML page with TypeScript in it. The tags are EJS's, and the code inside them is TypeScript:
PocketOne strips the types when it compiles the template, with esbuild built into the binary. Types are stripped, not
checked, so they document your code and help your editor without ever stopping a page. There is nothing to install or
configure, and no build step.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/products/index.ets -->
<% type Product = { name: string; cents: number }
const products: Product[] = [{ name: 'Widget', cents: 1999 }] %>
<ul>
<% for (const p of products) { -%>
  <li><%= p.name %>: $<%= (p.cents / 100).toFixed(2) %></li>
<% } -%>
</ul>
```

Nothing checks the types inside an `.ets` file, your editor included: editors don't know `.ets` yet, so associate it
with EJS for highlighting. For checked types, keep logic in the page's `.ts` or a `_private/` module (see
[TypeScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/typescript)).

What you write is what the browser gets, with the tags filled in. ETS is the template style these docs use
throughout. [Components with TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx) is the alternative; pick one style per app (see [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types)).

## Tags

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<% code %>` | Run code, no output |
| `<%= expr %>` | Output, HTML-escaped |
| `<%- expr %>` | Output, raw |
| `<%# comment %>` | Nothing |
| `<%%` | A literal `<%` |
| `-%>` | Also remove the newline right after the tag |
| `<%_` / `_%>` | Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line |
| `<script server<%- '>' %> code </script>` | Same as `<% code %>` |

## Escaping

`<%= %>` replaces `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` with `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&#34;` `&#39;`. `null` and `undefined` output as an empty string.

```ets
<p><%= '<b>"x"</b>' %></p>   <!-- <p>&lt;b&gt;&#34;x&#34;&lt;/b&gt;</p> -->
<p><%- '<b>raw</b>' %></p>    <!-- <p><b>raw</b></p> -->
<p><%= null %></p>            <!-- <p></p> -->
```

Use `<%-` only for HTML you trust, such as the output of `include()` or `slot()`.

## In scope

Inside a template you can use:

| Name | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx) |
| `data` | `ctx.data` |
| `params` | `ctx.params` |
| `include` | Render a [partial](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials) |
| `slot` | Define or read a [slot](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts) |
| `asset` | `ctx.asset` |
| `meta` | `ctx.meta` |
| `require` | Load a module: a path, or a name looked up in `_private/` then `node_modules` (see [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm)) |

## Output

A template returns its text. There is no `echo()`; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

```ets
<ul>
<% for (const n of [1, 2]) { -%>
  <li><%= n %></li>
<% } -%>
</ul>
```

## await

A template can `await`. Any tag that uses `await` turns the template into an async one, and Pages waits for it
before it sends the page:

```ets
<% const orders = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders') %>
<p><%= orders %> orders</p>
```

- Including a partial that uses `await` gives you a promise. Print it with `<%- await include('stats') %>`.
- Printing a promise without `await` is an error, so you won't get `[object Promise]` in your page.
- A slot whose content awaits takes an async function: `<% await slot('title', async () => { %>...<% }) %>`.
- A template without `await` runs as a plain function, so sync templates cost nothing extra.

## Errors

A TypeScript syntax error names the file and the template line, like any other template error:
`index.ets: line 3: TypeScript: Unexpected "="`. A type that's wrong but well formed isn't an error at all, since
nothing checks it.

## Caching

A template is compiled once per content hash and reused, so an edited file is recompiled on the next request.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown

# Markdown Support

A `.md` file is a page, just like an `.ets` file. Markdown is always on.

## How it works

1. **Tags first**: the file runs through EJS, so the same tags as [ETS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets) work in Markdown. Markdown is content, and its tags are a small escape hatch: plain JavaScript inside, with no TypeScript stripping.
2. **Then Markdown**: the result is rendered as Markdown: CommonMark plus GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists and autolinks.

## Front matter

YAML between `---` lines at the top of the file is front matter. Each top-level key is passed to `ctx.meta(key, value)`:

```markdown
---
title: My Blog Post
description: A detailed guide about something interesting
---

# Content starts here...
```

Read the values in a layout with `meta`:

```ets
<title><%= meta('title') %></title>
<meta name="description" content="<%= meta('description') %>">
```

## Headings

Headings get `id`s, so you can link to them: the text is lowercased, characters other than `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, `_` and space are removed, and spaces become `-`. `## Front matter` gets `id="front-matter"`.

## Images

Relative image paths go through [`ctx.asset`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset), so they get fingerprinted URLs:

```markdown
![Logo](logo.png)
```

## Markdown partials

A `.md` file in a `_private/` folder can be included from an `.ets` template with `include()`. It's rendered the same way, tags then Markdown:

```ets
<%- include('intro') %>
```

## Notes

- Layouts are `+layout.ets` (or `+layout.tsx`, see [TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx)). A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at
  startup. A Markdown page is still wrapped by the layouts above it.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials

# Using Partials in Pages

Partials are reusable templates that you include from other templates. They live in `_private/` folders, which are never routed.

## Including a partial

```ets
<%- include('nav') %>
<%- include('card', { product }) %>
```

- `include(name, locals?)` renders a template from a `_private/` folder and returns its text. Use `<%-` so its HTML isn't escaped.
- `name` may omit the extension; `.ets`, `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx` are tried, in that order (see [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types)).
- The partial sees the same `ctx`, plus `locals` as top-level variables.
- `locals` is also the whole object, as in EJS. Use it for optional values: `<%= title %>` throws if `title` wasn't passed, but `<% if (locals.subtitle) { %>` doesn't.
- Including more than 32 levels deep is an error.

## Where partials are found

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    header.ets
    footer.ets
  blog/
    _private/
      sidebar.ets
    posts/
      _private/
        post-card.ets
      index.ets
```

Pages looks in `_private/` in the current template's folder, then in each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`.

```ets
<!-- In blog/posts/index.ets -->
<%- include('post-card', { post }) %>  <!-- blog/posts/_private/post-card.ets -->
<%- include('sidebar') %>              <!-- blog/_private/sidebar.ets -->
<%- include('header') %>               <!-- _private/header.ets -->
```

A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`:

```ets
<%- include('/header') %>  <!-- always pb_pages/_private/header.ets -->
<%- include('/blog/_private/sidebar') %>  <!-- a path that names a _private folder: blog/_private/sidebar.ets -->
```

The extension is optional. A dotted name such as `include('nav.main')` finds `nav.main.ets`.

This means you can:

- Keep section-specific partials in that section's `_private/`.
- Hoist a shared partial up to a common parent.
- Override a parent's partial with a local one of the same name, and still reach the root one with `/name`.

## Passing data

Pass only what the partial needs:

```ets
<%- include('user-card', { name: user.getString('name'), joined: user.getString('created') }) %>
```

```ets
<!-- _private/user-card.ets -->
<div class="card">
  <h3><%= name %></h3>
  <p>Joined <%= joined %></p>
</div>
```

Partials can also read `ctx`, `data` and `params` directly. Passing values explicitly keeps them easy to reuse.

## Markdown partials

A `.md` partial is rendered like a Markdown page: its tags run as plain JavaScript, then Markdown (see [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown)):

```ets
<%- include('intro') %>  <!-- _private/intro.md -->
```

## JavaScript modules

`_private/` folders also hold TypeScript modules. Load them with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve), which uses the same lookup.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts

# Layouts and Slots

`+layout.ets` files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every `+layout` from its own folder up to `pb_pages/`, applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout, written as `+layout.ets` (or `+layout.tsx`, see [TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx)). A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at startup.

```plaintext
pb_pages/
  +layout.ets          # applied last (outermost)
  products/
    +layout.ets        # applied first
    [id].ets
```

For `/products/123`, `[id].ets` renders, then `products/+layout.ets` wraps it, then `+layout.ets` wraps that.

## `slot()`

In a layout, `slot()` returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ets -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>My Application</title>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <%- slot() %>
  </main>
  <footer>&copy; <%= new Date().getFullYear() %> My Application</footer>
</body>
</html>
```

`<%- slot %>` without parentheses prints the same content, so 0.x layouts that wrote it still work.

## Named slots

A page (or an inner layout) defines a named slot with `slot(name, fn)`. `fn`'s output is captured and nothing is output in place. A layout reads it with `slot(name)`, which returns `''` if it isn't defined.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id].ets -->
<% slot('title', () => { %><%= data.product.getString('name') %><% }) %>
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ets -->
<html>
  <head><title><%- slot('title') || 'My shop' %></title></head>
  <body><%- slot() %></body>
</html>
```

- Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout.
- Defining the same name again replaces it. Inside the new definition's `fn`, `slot(name)` still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/docs/+layout.ets -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Docs: <%- slot('title') %><% }) %>
<main><%- slot() %></main>
```

## Data in layouts

Layouts render after the page, with the same `ctx`. Everything middleware, the page's code and the page put on `ctx.data` or `ctx.meta` is there.

## When layouts are skipped

- When the response isn't HTML (a handler set another `Content-Type`).
- When a handler or middleware sent the response itself (`ctx.res.json`, `ctx.res.html`, `ctx.res.redirect`, ...).
- For [endpoints](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes), which have no template.
- After `ctx.res.layout(false)`, called from middleware, the page's code or the page itself.
- With the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar), for requests that carry `Datastar-Request: true`.

To serve HTML fragments without the site layout, call `ctx.res.layout(false)`, put the layout in a group (`(site)/+layout.ets`) and the fragments outside it, or send them with `ctx.res.html()`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx

# Components with TSX

Pages has two template styles. [ETS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets) is HTML with code in it, and it's the one these docs use. TSX is
code that returns HTML: every page, layout and partial is a function component. Pick TSX if you think in components
and want typed props. Either way the page is rendered on the server and sent as plain HTML; nothing runs in the
browser.

A `.tsx` file can be a page, a layout (`+layout.tsx`), an error page (`+error.tsx`, `+404.tsx`) or a partial in
`_private/`. PocketOne compiles it the first time it's used, with esbuild built into the binary: no Node, no
`npm install`, no build step. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked; to check them, see [TypeScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/typescript). The `tsx` [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits)
begins an app in this style.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default function Product({ data, slot }: pages.Props) {
  slot('title', data.product.getString('name'))
  return (
    <article class="product">
      <h1>{data.product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={data.product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/_private/Price.tsx
export default ({ cents }: { cents: number }) => <span class="price">${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}</span>
```

## Props

The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. It gets:

| Prop | |
|---|---|
| `ctx` | The [request context](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx). |
| `data`, `params`, `meta` | The same as `ctx.data`, `ctx.params` and `ctx.meta`. |
| `asset`, `include` | The same helpers EJS templates have. `include(name, locals)` returns HTML you can put in JSX. |
| `slot` | `slot(name)` reads a named slot, `slot(name, content)` sets one, `slot()` is the inner content. |
| `children` | In a layout, the inner content. |

A partial also gets the locals it was included with, as props.

In TypeScript, these props are `pages.Props` (a partial's locals: `pages.Props<{ label: string }>`). A component you import and use as `<Price />` gets only the props you pass it. See [TypeScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/typescript).

## Server-rendered HTML only

TSX looks like React, but it isn't: it renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration,
no state and no client-side React. Interactivity comes from the same places as in an ETS app: links, forms, HTMX,
Datastar or a `<script>`.

- Event handler props (functions) are dropped. Use plain attributes: `onclick="..."`, `hx-get`, `data-on:click`.
- Text and attribute values are escaped. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }}` inserts raw HTML.
- `class` and `className` both work, as do `for` and `htmlFor`.
- `style` takes a string or an object: `{ marginTop: 4 }` renders `margin-top:4`.
- `true` renders a bare attribute. `false`, `null` and `undefined` leave it out.
- `<html>` gets `<!doctype html>` in front of it, since JSX can't write a doctype.

## Async components

Any component can be `async`, including the file's default export. The render waits for every async component in the
tree, and sibling components run at the same time:

```tsx
// pb_pages/dashboard.tsx
async function Count({ collection }: { collection: string }) {
  const n = await $app.countRecords.async(collection)
  return <b>{n}</b>
}

export default async function Dashboard({ ctx }: pages.Props) {
  const user = ctx.auth ? await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('users', ctx.auth.id) : null
  return (
    <main>
      <p>Hi {user ? user.getString('name') : 'there'}</p>
      <p>
        <Count collection="orders" /> orders, <Count collection="users" /> users
      </p>
    </main>
  )
}
```

`include()` of a partial that awaits, and `slot(name, content)` with async content, work the same way.

## Layouts

```tsx
// pb_pages/+layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ children, slot }: pages.Props) {
  return (
    <html>
      <head>
        <title>{slot('title')}</title>
      </head>
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

## One style per app

Use TSX for every template in an app: pages, layouts, partials and error pages. Code files (a page's `.ts`, endpoints,
`+middleware.ts`, `+config.ts`) are the same in both styles.

The two styles can include each other, so you can move an app from one to the other a folder at a time: an ETS page
can sit inside a TSX layout, and `include()` returns a partial's HTML in either style. Markdown pages are the one mix
you can't avoid, since `.md` files always run EJS tags (see [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown)).

## Imports

Components are ordinary modules, so `import Card from './_private/Card'` resolves the same way as
[`require`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm). A module whose only export is `export default` behaves like `module.exports = ...`.
`include('card')` without an extension tries `.ets`, `.ejs`, `.md`, `.jsx` and `.tsx`, in that order.

`.jsx` works exactly like `.tsx`, without types; see [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/private-files

# Working with Private Files and Directories

## Names that are never routed

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `+` | Framework file (`+layout.ets`, `+middleware.ts`, ...) |
| `_` | Private. `_private/` folders hold partials and modules. Other `_` names are ignored. |
| `-` | Ignored (drafts, notes) |
| `.` | Ignored (dotfiles) |

```
pb_pages/
  _private/        # private (not routable)
  -drafts/         # ignored
  helpers/         # normal folder (routable)
  +middleware.ts   # framework file (not routable)
  +layout.ets      # framework file (not routable)
  index.ets        # page
```

## The `_private` folder

`_private/` folders serve two purposes:

1. Template partials, rendered with [`include()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials)
2. TypeScript modules and other files, loaded with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve)

Both use the same lookup: `_private/` in the current template's folder, then each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`. A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`.

```
pb_pages/
  _private/
    header.ets
    format.ts
  products/
    _private/
      product-card.ets
      queries.ts
    index.ets
```

```ets
<!-- In products/index.ets -->
<%
  const queries = ctx.resolve('queries')   // products/_private/queries.ts
  const format = ctx.resolve('format')     // _private/format.ts
%>
<%- include('header') %>                  <!-- _private/header.ets -->
<% for (const p of queries.featured(ctx.app)) { %>
  <%- include('product-card', { p, format }) %>
<% } %>
```

## Modules

A module in `_private/` is a CommonJS file:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/_private/queries.ts
module.exports = {
  featured: (app) => app.findRecordsByFilter('products', 'featured = true', '-created', 10),
}
```

## Notes

1. Files in `_private/` are never served.
2. Keep secrets in environment variables (see [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets)), not in files.
3. Keep private files close to where they're used, and hoist them up when several sections share them.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware

# Middleware

Middleware files (`+middleware.ts`) run before your handlers and templates. Use them to:

- Check authentication
- Load data a whole section shares
- Set headers
- Validate requests

## Basic example

```ts
// pb_pages/admin/+middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  ctx.data.section = 'admin'
  return next()
}
```

- One signature: `(ctx, next)`. Call `next()` to continue, and return its result.
- Returning without calling `next()` ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (a `500`; in dev mode the error page names the middleware file).
- Share data through `ctx.data`.
- Middleware can be `async`. `await next()` returns once the rest of the request has run, and throws what it threw.

```ts
// pb_pages/+middleware.ts
module.exports = async (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.unread = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('notifications', $dbx.hashExp({ read: false }))
  const started = Date.now()
  await next()
  ctx.log.info('rendered', ctx.route.path, Date.now() - started, 'ms')
}
```

## Order

Every `+middleware.ts` from `pb_pages/` down to the route's folder runs, root first. Groups count too.

```
pb_pages/
  +middleware.ts         # runs first (all routes)
  products/
    +middleware.ts       # runs second (/products/...)
    [id]/
      +middleware.ts     # runs third (/products/[id])
```

The full order for a request is:

1. Plugins' `onRequest`
2. Middleware, root first
3. The route's `.ts`, the page's code or the endpoint (`load`, then the method's handler)
4. The template, then layouts, innermost first
5. The response

If any step sends a response, the later steps are skipped.

## Common uses

### Auth guard

```ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

### Request validation

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!/^[a-z0-9]+$/.test(ctx.params.id)) throw ctx.httpError(400, 'Invalid ID')
  return next()
}
```

### Shared data

```ts
// pb_pages/+middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.categories = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('categories', 'active = true', 'name', 100)
  return next()
}
```

```ets
<nav>
  <% for (const c of data.categories) { %>
    <a href="/categories/<%= c.id %>"><%= c.getString('name') %></a>
  <% } %>
</nav>
```

### Headers

```ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.res.header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management

# Asset Management

Static files in `pb_pages` (images, CSS, JS, fonts) can be served with fingerprinted URLs that change when the file changes.

## Where to put assets

Anywhere in `pb_pages`, next to the pages that use them or in a shared folder:

```
pb_pages/
  assets/
    app.css
    logo.png
  feature/
    index.md
    header.jpg
```

## In templates

Use `asset()` (the same as `ctx.asset()`):

```ets
<link rel="stylesheet" href="<%= asset('/assets/app.css') %>">
<img src="<%= asset('header.jpg') %>">
```

`asset('/assets/app.css')` returns something like `/assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css`.

- Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; `/`-paths from `pb_pages`.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged.

## In Markdown

Relative image paths go through `asset()` automatically:

```markdown
![Header](header.jpg)
```

## How it works

1. A fingerprinted name carries the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: `name.<hash>.ext`.
2. Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
3. When the file changes, its hash and URL change, so browsers and CDNs fetch the new one.

See [asset](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset) and [Caching](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/caching).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content

# Serving Static Content in Pages

Any file in `pb_pages` that isn't a page (`.ets`, `.md` or `.tsx`, or the [JavaScript versions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types#javascript-works-too) `.ejs` and `.jsx`), a framework file (`+...`), private (`_...`) or ignored (names starting with `-` or `.`) is a static file. It's served as-is at its path, with groups removed:

```
pb_pages/
  assets/
    app.css            -> /assets/app.css
    logo.png           -> /assets/logo.png
  documents/
    terms.pdf          -> /documents/terms.pdf
  (marketing)/
    brochure.pdf       -> /brochure.pdf
  favicon.ico          -> /favicon.ico
  index.ets            -> /  (a page, not static)
```

- The content type comes from the extension.
- The `ETag` comes from the content hash; a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304`.
- A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error).

For cache-friendly URLs, reference files through [`asset()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management).

## `pb_pages` and `pb_public`

A URL nothing in `pb_pages` matches goes on to `pb_public`, so you can keep using `pb_public` for files you don't want next to your pages.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets

# Managing Secrets in Pages

Keep API keys, passwords and other secrets in environment variables, and read them with `ctx.env(name)`. It returns `''` when the variable is unset.

```ts
// pb_pages/checkout.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY')
    if (!key) throw new Error('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not set')
    // ...
  },
}
```

`ctx.env` reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment.

## Best practices

1. **Never put secrets in the page.** Anything a template outputs goes to the browser.

   ```ets
   <!-- DON'T -->
   <meta name="api-key" content="<%= ctx.env('API_KEY') %>">

   <!-- OK: a public value -->
   <meta name="api-endpoint" content="<%= ctx.env('PUBLIC_API_ENDPOINT') %>">
   ```

2. **Check for required variables** and fail clearly when one is missing.
3. **Use descriptive names**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, not `KEY`.
4. **Never commit secrets** to version control, and use different values in development and production.

## Setting environment variables

```bash
# Shell
export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
pocketone serve
```

```dockerfile
# Docker
ENV STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config

# Configuration with `+config.ts`

Create `pb_pages/+config.ts` to configure Pages for the app. It's only allowed at the top of `pb_pages`; a `+config.ts` in a subfolder is an error at startup.

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
  debug: false,
}
```

## Options

| Key | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `[]` | Built-in plugins by name, or custom plugin factories. ETS templates and Markdown are always on. |
| `debug` | `false` | Detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output even outside dev mode. |

`+config.ts` must export an object; exporting a function (0.x's `(api) => ({...})` form) is an error.

`+config.ts` runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a
module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the
reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

## Plugins

Each entry in `plugins` is one of:

- **A name**, loaded with `require`: a `_private/` file (`'datastar'` for the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar)),
  then a package in `node_modules`, then a built-in (`'auth'` or `'realtime'`). It must export a plugin factory. See
  [Plugins](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins).
- **A custom plugin factory**: a function that returns hooks, such as `require('./_private/my-plugin.ts')`. A `require`
  with a path loads exactly that file, skipping the name lookup, so it's how you choose one copy over another.
- **An object with a factory and options**: `{ factory, ...options }`. The object is passed to the factory as its `config`.

```ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: [
    'auth',
    'realtime',
    { factory: require('./_private/banner.ts'), text: 'Hello' },
  ],
}
```

Plugin hooks run in the order the plugins are listed. See [Plugin Authoring](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring).

## Debug

`debug: true` turns on what dev mode (`--dev`) turns on: detailed error pages and `ctx.log.debug` output. See [Debugging](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/caching

# Understanding Caching in Pages

## Fingerprinted assets

`asset()` adds a content hash to a file's URL:

```ets
<img src="<%= asset('/images/logo.png') %>">
<!-- <img src="/images/logo.3f9a1c2b7d4e.png"> -->
```

- The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256.
- Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, so browsers and CDNs keep them for a year.
- When the file changes, the hash changes, and so does the URL. Old copies are never served for the new URL.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged (and not fingerprinted).

## Static files

Every static file gets an `ETag` from its content hash. A request with a matching `If-None-Match` gets `304 Not Modified`.

## Templates

A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. Edit a file and the next request uses the new version, in every mode.

## Routes

The route table is built at startup and rebuilt whenever anything in `pb_pages` changes. A rebuild never restarts the app.

## Pages

Rendered pages aren't cached. To let browsers or a CDN cache a page, set a header in a handler or middleware:

```ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.res.header('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=60')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors

# Errors

## Thrown errors

Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a `500`.

- **Dev mode or `debug: true`:** an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the `.ets` or `.md` source), and the stack trimmed to `pb_pages`-relative paths.
- **Otherwise:** a plain "Something went wrong" page.

The full error always goes to the app's log.

## `ctx.httpError(status, message)`

Throw `ctx.httpError()` to answer with a specific status:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    let product
    try {
      product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByData('products', 'slug', ctx.params.id)
    } catch (e) {
      throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product') // findFirstRecordByData throws when nothing matches
    }
    ctx.data.product = product
  },
}
```

- In a page, it sends that status with a plain page showing `message`.
- In an [endpoint](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes), it sends JSON (unless the request's `Accept` puts `text/html` first): `{ "status": 404, "message": "No such product" }`.

## A custom error page

Create `pb_pages/+error.ets`. It renders for every `ctx.httpError` and for every `500` outside dev mode, inside the root layout, with `ctx.error = { status, message }`:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+error.ets -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Error <%= ctx.error.status %><% }) %>
<h1><%= ctx.error.status %></h1>
<p><%= ctx.error.message %></p>
```

`+error` and `+404` live only at the top of `pb_pages`. Either may be `.ets` or `.tsx`.

## A custom 404 page

Create `pb_pages/+404.ets`. It renders inside the root layout, with status `404`, for a `GET` or `HEAD` that nothing answers: no page, no file in `pb_public` and no PocketBase route. It never renders for `/api/` or `/_/`. The root `+middleware.ts` runs first, and page code can still change the status.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+404.ets -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Not found<% }) %>
<h1>Not found</h1>
<p>Nothing lives at <%= ctx.req.url.pathname %>.</p>
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging

# Debugging in Pages

## Dev mode

Run `pocketone` with `--dev`:

```bash
pocketone serve --dev
```

Dev mode turns on:

- detailed error pages (message, file and line, trimmed stack; see [Errors](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors));
- `ctx.log.debug` output.

## `debug: true`

To get the same in production, set `debug: true` in `+config.ts`:

```ts
module.exports = {
  debug: true,
}
```

Turn it off again when you're done. Detailed error pages show error messages, file paths and stack traces to anyone who triggers an error.

## Logging

`ctx.log` writes to the app's log:

```ts
ctx.log.debug('loaded product', ctx.params.id)  // only in dev mode or with debug: true
ctx.log.info('order placed')
ctx.log.warn('stock is low')
ctx.log.error('payment failed')
```

See [log](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log).

## Template changes

Templates are cached by content hash and the route table is rebuilt on any file change, in every mode. If a change doesn't show, check the app's log for a startup error (bad file name, route conflict): the previous route table keeps serving until the error is fixed.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/deploying

# Going Live

A PocketOne app is a `pb_pages` folder. To go live, run PocketOne on your server (pages is built in) and put `pb_pages` next to `pb_data`, along with your other `pb_*` folders:

```
pb_data/
pb_hooks/
pb_migrations/
pb_public/
pb_pages/
```

Or point `pocketone` at it with `--pagesDir`.

## Updating

Copy the changed files into `pb_pages`. The route table is rebuilt on any change, and templates are cached by content hash, so updates show on the next request without restarting the app. If an update has a startup error (a bad name or a route conflict), it's logged with the file path and the previous route table keeps serving.

## Before you go live

- Run without `--dev`, and keep `debug: false` in `+config.ts`.
- Set secrets as environment variables (see [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets)).
- Serve over HTTPS. Cookies set with `ctx.res.cookie` are marked `Secure` on HTTPS requests.

## Multitenant hosts

Under a multitenant PocketOne host, every instance has its own `pb_pages`, and page code runs with the same limits as the rest of the instance's JS.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins

# Plugins

Plugins add features to `ctx` and hook into each request. Turn them on in `+config.ts`:

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'],
}
```

Each entry is one of:

- **A name in quotes.** It's loaded with `require`, which looks in this order:
  1. a `_private/` folder in `pb_pages` (`'datastar'` finds `_private/datastar.js`)
  2. `pb_pages/node_modules`, for a package from your `package.json`
  3. the built-in plugins, `'auth'` and `'realtime'`

  A path such as `'./plugins/my-plugin.ts'` works too.
- **A plugin factory**, usually `require('./_private/my-plugin.ts')`. Writing the `require` yourself with a path skips
  the lookup above and loads exactly that file, which is how you pick one copy over another: `'datastar'` would find
  `_private/datastar.js` first, while `require('./node_modules/datastar')` always loads the package.

Datastar isn't built in. It's an add-on file you copy into `pb_pages/_private/` and list by name.

ETS templates and Markdown are always on; they aren't plugins.

## Built-in plugins

| Name | Adds |
|---|---|
| [`auth`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth) | Cookie sessions on PocketBase auth: sets `ctx.auth` from the `pb_auth` cookie and adds `ctx.session.*` sign-in methods. |
| [`realtime`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime) | `ctx.realtime.send()` to PocketBase realtime subscribers. |

## Custom plugins

A custom plugin is a module that exports a factory returning hooks. List it by name, or `require()` it yourself, which you
need for options (`{ factory, ...options }`):

```ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth', 'my-plugin', { factory: require('./_private/other-plugin.ts'), color: 'blue' }],
}
```

See [Plugin Authoring](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring).

| Add-on | Adds |
|---|---|
| [Datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar) | `ctx.datastar.*` helpers for [Datastar](https://data-star.dev). Copy [`addons/datastar.js`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/datastar.js) into `pb_pages/_private/`; the `datastar` starter kit already has it. |

## Order

Plugins' hooks run in the order they're listed, and `onRequest` hooks run before any middleware.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth

# Authentication Plugin

The `auth` plugin gives you cookie sessions on PocketBase auth. It calls the app directly, not over HTTP.

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

## What it does on every request

It reads the `pb_auth` cookie, validates the token and sets `ctx.auth` to the authenticated record. A bad cookie is cleared.

`ctx.auth` is also set without the plugin when a request carries PocketBase's own `Authorization` header.

## `ctx.session`

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }?)` | Create an auth record. `data` holds extra fields. `verify` sends the verification email; `signIn` signs the new account in (returns `{ token: '', record }` when `false`). |
| `signInWithPassword(email, password, { collection }?)` | Sign in with a password. |
| `requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }?)` | Send a one-time password. Returns the `otpId`. An unknown email still gets an id, one that never validates; with `create: true` the account is created first. |
| `signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }?)` | Sign in with a one-time password. |
| `signInAnonymously({ collection }?)` | Sign in as a new anonymous user. |
| `requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }?)` | Store state in a cookie and return the provider's URL. With `redirect` it also sends the redirect; pass `redirect: false` to send the URL some other way. `redirectPath` must be a path on this site. |
| `signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?)` | Complete an OAuth2 sign-in on the redirect path. Returns `{ token, record, meta }`; `meta.isNew` is `true` for a new account. |
| `signIn(record)` | Set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. It skips the MFA check below. |
| `signOut()` | Sign out. |
| `authMethods({ collection }?)` | The sign-in methods a collection has turned on: `{ password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } }`, as PocketBase's auth-methods API. |

### MFA

Pages doesn't have a second sign-in step yet. If a collection has MFA turned on (Collections → `users` → Options →
Multi-factor authentication) and its MFA rule matches the account, every sign-in method above refuses it with "This
account needs a second sign-in step (MFA), which pages doesn't support yet." An empty rule matches every account. To
use pages sign-in, turn MFA off for the collection, or give it a rule that leaves out the accounts that sign in here.

Every sign-in method sets `ctx.auth` for the rest of the request and returns `{ token, record }`.

### Email flows

These use PocketBase's own checks and mail templates. The request methods never reveal whether an email exists.

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `requestVerification(email, { collection }?)` | Send the verification email (skipped for an account that's already verified). |
| `confirmVerification(token)` | Mark the account verified. Returns the record. |
| `requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }?)` | Send the password reset email. |
| `confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm)` | Set the new password (and mark the account verified). Returns the record. |
| `requestEmailChange(newEmail)` | Send a confirmation email to `newEmail`. Needs a signed-in user (`ctx.auth`). |
| `confirmEmailChange(token, password)` | Change the email after checking the current password. Returns the record. |

A bad or expired token throws an error.

## Example

```ts
// pb_pages/login.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: 'Invalid email or password', email }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ts
// pb_pages/logout.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

See the [Authentication guide](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication) for complete flows: registration, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sign-in.
