Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar

# Datastar Add-on

The Datastar add-on adds helpers for [Datastar](https://data-star.dev). It's a custom plugin that ships with Pages
rather than a built-in: copy [`addons/datastar.js`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/pages/addons/datastar.js)
into `pb_pages/_private/` (the `datastar` starter kit already has it) and list it in `+config.ts` by name:

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['datastar'],
}
```

Add the script tags to your root layout's `<head>`. They load [Datastar](https://data-star.dev) v1.0.5. Datastar 1.0 uses
a colon between the attribute name and its key (`data-on:click`, `data-bind:name`, `data-signals:count`,
`data-class:active`, `data-attr:href`); the older hyphen form (`data-on-click`) is ignored. See the
[Datastar attribute reference](https://data-star.dev/reference/attributes).

```ets
<head>
  <%- ctx.datastar.scripts() %>
</head>
```

## `ctx.datastar`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `scripts({ spa, realtime }?)` | Returns the script tags. |
| `open({ keepAlive }?)` | Starts the SSE response now instead of with the first patch, for a route that waits for changes. The stream sends a keep-alive comment every `keepAlive` seconds (30 by default; `0` turns it off), whether it was opened here or by the first patch. |
| `patchElements(html, { selector, mode, useViewTransition, viewTransitionSelector, namespace }?)` | Sends a patch-elements SSE event on the current response. `mode` is `outer` (default), `inner`, `replace`, `prepend`, `append`, `before`, `after` or `remove`; `namespace` is `html` (default), `svg` or `mathml`. |
| `patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?)` | Sends a patch-signals SSE event (JSON Merge Patch: `null` removes a signal). |
| `executeScript(js, { autoRemove, attributes }?)` | Sends a script to run in the browser. |
| `consoleLog(msg)` / `consoleError(err)` | Logs to the browser console. |
| `redirect(url)` | Sends the browser to `url` (a full page load). A Datastar fetch can't follow `ctx.res.redirect`, so use this from `@get`/`@post` handlers. |
| `dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector }?)` | Fires a `CustomEvent` on `document`, or on the elements matching `selector`. |
| `replaceURL(url)` | Changes the address bar without a navigation (`history.replaceState`). |
| `prefetch(urls)` | Adds speculation rules so the browser prefetches `urls`. |
| `signals()` | Reads the request's signals as an object: from the `datastar` query parameter for GET and DELETE, from the body otherwise. |
| `readSignals(target)` | Merges the request's signals into `target` and returns it (0.x's `readSignals(request, target)` also works). |
| `realtime.*` | Sends the same patches to realtime subscribers. Needs the [`realtime`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime) plugin. |

Every send also takes `eventId` and `retryDuration` (in ms; the default 1000 isn't sent).

## Pages as patches

When a request has the `Datastar-Request: true` header, the rendered page is sent without layouts, as a `patchElements` event. If the request has a `Datastar-Selector` header, the patch goes into that element.

This is how this site navigates between docs pages: the layout calls

```ets
<%- ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope: '#toc', selector: '#content' } }) %>
```

so links in the table of contents fetch the page and patch it into `#content`. Plain left-clicks are intercepted;
modified clicks (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt, middle-click), links with a `target` attribute and links to other origins navigate
normally. Back/Forward work, including back to the page you landed on: each page opens at the top, and Back/Forward
return you to where you were scrolled.

## Example: a counter

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/counter/index.ets -->
<button data-on:click="@post('/counter')">
  Count: <span id="count"><%= ctx.store('count') || 0 %></span>
</button>
```

```ts
// pb_pages/counter/index.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const count = (ctx.store('count') || 0) + 1
    ctx.store('count', count)
    ctx.datastar.patchElements(`<span id="count">${count}</span>`)
  },
}
```

## Example: reading signals

```ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { name, email } = ctx.datastar.signals()
    if (!name || !email) {
      ctx.datastar.patchSignals({ error: 'Please fill all fields' })
      return
    }
    ctx.datastar.patchElements('<div id="form">Thanks!</div>')
  },
}
```

## Live updates

To patch the page whenever records change, open a stream with `data-init="@get('/todos/live')"`, call
`ctx.datastar.open()`, and turn each change from [`ctx.realtime.subscribe()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime#with-datastar) into a patch. Only the visitor's own stream
gets them, with the collection's rules applied for that visitor.

## Broadcasting

With the `realtime` plugin on, `ctx.datastar.realtime.*` sends patches to every realtime subscriber instead of the current response:

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime', 'datastar'] }
```

```ts
ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(`<span id="count">${count}</span>`)
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime

# Realtime Plugin

The `realtime` plugin sends messages to [PocketBase realtime](https://pocketbase.io/docs/realtime/) subscribers, and
lets a page listen to record changes itself, to stream them to the browser.

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['realtime'],
}
```

## `ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?)`

Sends `data` to the subscribers of `topic`. `filter(client)` may limit the recipients.

```ts
// pb_pages/ping.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.realtime.send('ping', { at: new Date().toISOString() })
    return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
  },
}
```

On the client, subscribe with the PocketBase JS SDK:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pocketbase/dist/pocketbase.umd.js"></script>
<script>
  const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)
  pb.realtime.subscribe('ping', (data) => console.log('Received:', data))
</script>
```

## Filtering recipients

```ts
ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Maintenance at 10:00', {
  filter: (client) => !!client.get('auth'),
})
```

## Sending HTML

For hypermedia libraries (HTMX, Datastar), send rendered HTML. `include()` is available in templates, so render the partial there:

```ts
// pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ts
module.exports = {
  post() {}, // accept POST; the page renders and sends
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/xapi/chat/index.ets -->
<% ctx.realtime.send('chat', include('chat-msg', { message: ctx.req.body().message })) %>
```

See [Realtime Events](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/realtime) and the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar), which can send Datastar patches over realtime.

## Listening to record changes

`ctx.realtime.subscribe(topic, { filter, expand, fields }?)` listens to `topic` the way a browser does on `/api/realtime`, as the visitor of this request, and gives each message
to a `for await` loop. Pair it with [`ctx.res.sse()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res#server-sent-events) to stream changes to the
browser with no polling:

```ts
// pb_pages/posts/live.ts
module.exports = {
  async get(ctx) {
    const stream = ctx.res.sse({ keepAlive: 30 }) // a comment every 30 s, so proxies keep a quiet stream open
    for await (const { action, record } of ctx.realtime.subscribe('posts/*', { filter: 'published = true' })) {
      stream.send(action, record)
    }
  },
}
```

- **Topics** are PocketBase's: `posts/*` for every record of a collection, `posts/RECORD_ID` for one. Each message is
  `{ action, record }`, with `action` `create`, `update` or `delete`. Any other topic gives the data sent to it
  with `ctx.realtime.send()`, so pages can talk to each other (a chat room needs no collection).
- **Rules apply as for the visitor.** The collection's list rule (view rule for one record) decides what reaches the
  page, with `ctx.auth` as `@request.auth`, kept current when that user's record changes. `filter`, `expand` and
  `fields` work as in the JS SDK's subscribe options. Hidden fields stay hidden unless the visitor is a superuser.
- **It ends with the request**: when the visitor leaves, the handler returns, or the stream reaches the app's await
  time (15 minutes by default; `EventSource` and Datastar reconnect). `close()` ends it early, and a `for await` that
  breaks out of the loop closes it too.
- **A page that falls behind is cut off.** Up to 64 messages wait for the loop. If more arrive before the page reads
  them, the subscription ends and the loop throws, so the client reconnects and loads fresh state instead of
  missing an update.
- Messages for different records may arrive in a different order than the changes were made, as on `/api/realtime`.

### With Datastar

With the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar), each change becomes a patch:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/todos/index.ets -->
<ul id="todos" data-init="@get('/todos/live')">
  <% for (const todo of ctx.app.findAllRecords('todos')) { %>
    <%- include('todo', { todo }) %>
  <% } %>
</ul>
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/todos/_private/todo.ets -->
<li id="todo-<%= todo.id %>"><%= todo.title %></li>
```

```ts
// pb_pages/todos/live.ts
module.exports = {
  async get(ctx) {
    ctx.datastar.open() // start the response now, not with the first change
    for await (const { action, record } of ctx.realtime.subscribe('todos/*')) {
      if (action === 'delete') {
        ctx.datastar.patchElements('', { selector: `#todo-${record.id}`, mode: 'remove' })
      } else if (action === 'create') {
        ctx.datastar.patchElements(ctx.include('todo', { todo: record }), { selector: '#todos', mode: 'append' })
      } else {
        ctx.datastar.patchElements(ctx.include('todo', { todo: record }))
      }
    }
  },
}
```

The add-on's stream sends a keep-alive comment every 30 seconds while the route waits.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring

# Plugin Authoring Guide

A custom plugin is a factory that returns hooks:

```ts
// pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.ts
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'my-plugin',
  onRequest(ctx) {},                                   // before middleware
  extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () => 'hi' },
  transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html },      // after each template or layout renders
})
```

Turn it on in `+config.ts`:

```ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['my-plugin'], // pb_pages/_private/my-plugin.ts
}
```

## `config`

`config` is the plugin's entry in `+config.ts` when that entry is an object (`{ factory, ...options }`), else `{}`:

```ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: [{ factory: require('./_private/banner.ts'), text: 'Beta' }],
}
```

```ts
// pb_pages/_private/banner.ts
module.exports = (config) => ({
  name: 'banner',
  transform({ html }) {
    return html.replace('<body>', `<body><div class="banner">${config.text}</div>`)
  },
})
```

## Hooks

Every hook is optional. Hooks run in the order plugins are listed in `+config.ts`.

| Hook | When |
|---|---|
| `name` | The plugin's name. |
| `onRequest(ctx)` | At the start of each request, before middleware. |
| `extendContext(ctx)` | Add members to `ctx`. |
| `transform({ html, ctx, file })` | After each template or layout renders. Return the new HTML. |

## Example: a context helper

```ts
module.exports = () => ({
  name: 'format',
  extendContext(ctx) {
    ctx.formatDate = (d) => new Date(d).toLocaleDateString()
  },
})
```

```ets
<p>Posted <%= ctx.formatDate(data.post.getString('created')) %></p>
```

## Permissions

Custom plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's code. Under a multitenant host, that means the instance's sandbox.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx

# The `ctx` Object

Pages creates one `ctx` object per request and passes it to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

```ts
// +middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => next()

// about.ts (beside about.ets), or an endpoint such as feeds/rss.ts
module.exports = { load(ctx) {} }
```

```ets
<!-- any template -->
<p><%= ctx.req.url.pathname %></p>
```

In templates, `data`, `params`, `asset` and `meta` are shortcuts for `ctx.data`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.asset` and `ctx.meta`.

## Members

| Member | |
|---|---|
| [`ctx.req`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req) | The request: method, URL, query, headers, cookies, body, files |
| [`ctx.res`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res) | The response: status, headers, cookies, redirects, JSON, HTML, text, files, SSE |
| [`ctx.data`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data) | Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates |
| [`ctx.params`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data#ctxparams) | Route parameters |
| [`ctx.route`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data#ctxroute) | The matched route: `{ path, name, file }` |
| [`ctx.flash()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash) | The one-time message from the previous redirect |
| [`ctx.auth`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/auth) | The authenticated record, or `null` |
| [`ctx.app`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app) | The app (`$app`) |
| [`ctx.pb()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/pb) | A JS SDK client acting as the visitor (API rules apply) |
| [`ctx.env(name)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/env) | Environment variable |
| [`ctx.log`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log) | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` |
| [`ctx.meta(key, value?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/meta) | Per-request page metadata |
| [`ctx.asset(path)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset) | Fingerprinted URL for a static file |
| [`ctx.include(name, locals?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials) | Render a `_private/` partial from JS and get its text (same lookup as `include`, from the route's folder) |
| [`ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve) | Load a module from `_private/` |
| [`ctx.store(name, value?)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/store) | The app's in-memory store |
| `ctx.pagesDir` | Absolute path of the app's `pb_pages` folder (read-only), e.g. for `$os.readDir` |
| `ctx.dev` | `true` in dev mode |
| [`ctx.httpError(status, message)`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors) | An error to throw for a specific status |
| [`ctx.error`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors) | `{ status, message }`, in `+error.ets` |

## Added by plugins

| Member | Plugin |
|---|---|
| `ctx.session` | [auth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth) |
| `ctx.realtime` | [realtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime) |
| `ctx.datastar` | [datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar) |

Custom plugins can add their own members with [`extendContext`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req

# `ctx.req`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `method` | `"GET"`, `"POST"`, ... |
| `url` | `{ href, origin, pathname, search }` |
| `query(name)` | First value of a query parameter as a string, or `undefined` |
| `query(name, { all: true })` | Every value, as an array of strings |
| `query()` | `{ name: firstValue }` for every parameter |
| `header(name)` | Request header, `''` if absent |
| `cookie(name)` | Cookie value as a string, or `undefined` |
| `cookie(name, { json: true })` | Cookie parsed as JSON (`undefined` if absent or not JSON) |
| `cookies()` | `{ name: value }`, strings |
| `body()` | Parsed body: a JSON object, or form fields as `{ name: value }` (repeated names as arrays) |
| `files(name)` | Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase `*filesystem.File` values ready for a record field |
| `ip` | Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) |
| `event` | The underlying PocketBase `RequestEvent`, for anything not covered here |

Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

## Examples

```ets
<p>You asked for <%= ctx.req.url.pathname %><%= ctx.req.url.search %></p>
<p>Page <%= Number(ctx.req.query('page') ?? 1) %></p>
<p>Browser: <%= ctx.req.header('User-Agent') %></p>
```

### Forms

`body()` parses JSON, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data`:

```ts
// pb_pages/contact.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, message } = ctx.req.body()
    // ...
  },
}
```

### File uploads

```html
<form method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <input type="file" name="avatar" />
  <button>Upload</button>
</form>
```

```ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const record = ctx.app.findRecordById('users', ctx.auth.id)
    record.set('avatar', ctx.req.files('avatar')[0])
    ctx.app.save(record)
    return ctx.res.redirect('/account')
  },
}
```

### Cookies

```ts
const theme = ctx.req.cookie('theme')                     // 'dark' or undefined
const prefs = ctx.req.cookie('prefs', { json: true }) ?? {}
```

Set cookies with [`ctx.res.cookie()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res#cookies).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res

# `ctx.res`

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `status(code)` | Status for the rendered page. Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `header(name, value)` | Set a response header. `header(name)` reads it back. |
| `cookie(name, value, options?)` | Set a cookie. |
| `clearCookie(name, options?)` | Expire a cookie (same `path` / `domain` as when set). |
| `redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?)` or `redirect(location, status)` | Send a redirect. `status` must be a 3xx code. `flash` sets a [one-time message](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash). |
| `json(data)` / `json(status, data)` | Send JSON. |
| `html(html)` / `html(status, html)` | Send HTML as-is (no layouts). |
| `text(text)` / `text(status, text)` | Send plain text. |
| `file(path)` | Send a file from `pb_pages` (path relative to `pb_pages`). |
| `sse()` | Start a `text/event-stream` response. |
| `layout(false)` | Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). Returns `ctx.res`. |
| `sent` | `true` once a response has been sent. |

Once a response is sent, the later steps of the request (handlers, template, layouts) are skipped.

## Status and headers

```ets
<% ctx.res.status(404).header('Cache-Control', 'no-store') %>
<h1>Not here</h1>
```

## Redirects

```ts
return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
return ctx.res.redirect('/new-home', 301) // or { status: 301 }
```

## Cookies

```ts
ctx.res.cookie('theme', 'dark', { maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 })
ctx.res.cookie('prefs', { compact: true })   // objects are JSON.stringify'd
ctx.res.clearCookie('theme')
```

- Non-string values are `JSON.stringify`'d. The value is then percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`), and `ctx.req.cookie` decodes it.
- Defaults: `path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and `Secure` when the request is HTTPS.
- Options: `path`, `domain`, `maxAge` (seconds), `expires` (a `Date`, milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with `maxAge` too, browsers use `maxAge`), `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`.

## JSON, HTML, text and files

```ts
return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
return ctx.res.json(201, { id: record.id })
return ctx.res.html('<p>Fragment</p>')
return ctx.res.text(404, 'Not found')
return ctx.res.file('downloads/manual.pdf')
```

## Server-sent events

`sse({ keepAlive }?)` starts a `text/event-stream` response and returns `{ send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() }`.
`comment(text)` writes an SSE comment (`: text`), which browsers ignore. `keepAlive` is a number of seconds: while the
handler runs, a comment is written that often, so proxies that close quiet connections (Cloudflare after about
100 seconds) keep the stream open.

```ts
// pb_pages/clock.ts
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const stream = ctx.res.sse()
    stream.send('time', new Date().toISOString())
    stream.close()
  },
}
```

To keep a stream open, make the handler `async` and let it wait. While it waits (on a timer or an `.async` call), the
app serves other requests. When the client goes away, the handler stops at its next `await` and its timers are
cleared:

```ts
// pb_pages/ticks.ts
module.exports = {
  async get(ctx) {
    const stream = ctx.res.sse({ keepAlive: 30 })
    setInterval(() => stream.send('time', new Date().toISOString()), 1000)
    await new Promise(() => {}) // wait until the client leaves
  },
}
```

A stream stays open for at most the app's await time (15 minutes unless `pocketone.yaml` sets `js_limits.await_time`).
`EventSource` and Datastar reconnect when it ends. To stream record changes, see
[`ctx.realtime.subscribe()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime#listening-to-record-changes).

Streaming is only available through `sse()`. Templates return their text all at once.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data

# `ctx.data`, `ctx.params`, `ctx.route`

## `ctx.data`

A plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. It starts as `{}`. In templates it's also available as `data`.

```ts
// +middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  ctx.data.user = ctx.auth
  return next()
}
```

```ts
// products.ts, beside products.ets
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return { products: ctx.app.findAllRecords('products') }  // Object.assign'd into ctx.data
  },
}
```

```ets
<% for (const p of data.products) { %>
  <li><%= p.getString('name') %></li>
<% } %>
```

A handler's returned object is shallow-assigned into `ctx.data`. There is no deep merge.

## `ctx.params`

Route parameters from `[name]` segments, as strings. Never includes query parameters (use [`ctx.req.query()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req)). In templates it's also available as `params`.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/[org]/[repo]/index.ets, at /acme/web -->
<p><%= params.org %>/<%= params.repo %></p>  <!-- acme/web -->
```

## `ctx.route`

`{ path, name, file }`: the route pattern, the page name and its file relative to `pb_pages`.

| Page file | `path` | `name` |
|---|---|---|
| `products/[id].ets` | `/products/[id]` | `[id]` |
| `docs/index.md` | `/docs` | `index` |

Each page has its own `.ts`; code several pages share goes in a `_private/` module or `+middleware.ts`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash

# `ctx.flash()`

A flash is a one-time message that survives one redirect, such as "Saved" after a form post.

## Setting a flash

```ts
return ctx.res.redirect('/account', { flash: 'Saved' })
```

The message is stored as JSON in a cookie (`pp_flash`, `HttpOnly`, `Max-Age=300`). It can be any JSON value:

```ts
return ctx.res.redirect('/cart', { flash: { type: 'success', text: 'Added to cart' } })
```

## Reading it

On the next request, `ctx.flash()` returns the message and clears the cookie. It returns `undefined` when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value.

```ets
<% const flash = ctx.flash() %>
<% if (flash) { %>
  <div class="alert alert-<%= flash.type %>"><%= flash.text %></div>
<% } %>
```

Read it in your layout to show flashes on every page.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/auth

# `ctx.auth`

The authenticated record, or `null`. It's set by:

- PocketBase's own auth, when the request has an `Authorization` header;
- the [`auth` plugin](../plugins/auth.md), from its `pb_auth` cookie.

```ets
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <p>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></p>
  <% if (!ctx.auth.verified()) { %><p>Please verify your email.</p><% } %>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```

`ctx.auth` is a PocketBase record, so the usual record methods work: `get(field)`, `getString(field)`, `email()`, `verified()`, `isSuperuser()`, `collection()`.

## Protecting pages

```ts
// pb_pages/account/+middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app

# `ctx.app`

The app (`$app`): records, collections, settings. Page code calls it directly, with no HTTP round trip.

```ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    return {
      product: ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id),
      latest: ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 10),
    }
  },
}
```

Everything in PocketBase's [JavaScript records](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-records/) and [database](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-database/) docs that uses `$app` works on `ctx.app`.

Calls through `ctx.app` don't apply collection API rules: page code is trusted server code. Check `ctx.auth` yourself before reading or changing data on a user's behalf.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/pb

# `ctx.pb()`: the JS SDK in page code

`ctx.pb()` returns a [PocketBase JS SDK](https://github.com/pocketbase/js-sdk) client, the same API you use in the
browser:

```ts
// pb_pages/posts.ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    const page = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getList(1, 20, {
      filter: 'published = true',
      sort: '-created',
      expand: 'author',
    })
    return { posts: page.items }
  },
}
```

- **It acts as the visitor.** When someone is signed in (`ctx.auth`, for example through the `auth` plugin), the
  client is authenticated as them; otherwise it's a guest. Your collections' API rules, `expand` and hidden fields
  apply exactly as they would in the browser.
- **It's synchronous.** Calls return their result directly; no `await`.
- **No network.** Requests go straight to your app's own API, in-process. There's no host or port to set, and
  it works the same on any server.
- **Errors** throw the SDK's `ClientResponseError`:

  ```ts
  try {
    const post = ctx.pb().collection('posts').getOne(ctx.params.id)
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.status === 404) throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such post')
    throw e
  }
  ```

- **Limits:** only `/api/` routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported, so use `ctx.app` for those.

## `ctx.pb()` or `ctx.app`?

| | `ctx.pb()` | `ctx.app` |
|---|---|---|
| Permissions | the visitor's: API rules apply | full access, no rules |
| API | the JS SDK, same as the browser | PocketBase's JSVM API (`findRecordsByFilter`, `save`, ...) |
| Use it for | reading and writing on the visitor's behalf | admin work, background jobs, anything rules shouldn't limit |

When in doubt, use `ctx.pb()`: if a page shows something, the visitor is allowed to see it.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/env

# `ctx.env(name)`

Returns an environment variable, or `''` if it's unset.

```ts
const key = ctx.env('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY')
```

It reads the app's environment. Under a multitenant host's sandbox, it reads the instance's environment.

See [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets).

# `ctx.log`

Writes to the app's log.

```ts
ctx.log.debug('cart', ctx.data.cart)
ctx.log.info('order placed')
ctx.log.warn('stock is low')
ctx.log.error('payment failed')
```

`debug` only shows in dev mode (`--dev`) or with `debug: true` in `+config.ts`. See [Debugging](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging).

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/meta

# `ctx.meta(key, value?)`

A per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. In templates it's also available as `meta`.

```ets
<!-- a page -->
<% meta('title', data.product.getString('name')) %>
<% meta('description', data.product.getString('summary')) %>
```

```ets
<!-- +layout.ets -->
<title><%= meta('title') || 'My shop' %></title>
<meta name="description" content="<%= meta('description') %>">
```

Layouts render after the page, so they see what the page set.

## Front matter

In a `.md` page, each top-level key of the YAML front matter is passed to `ctx.meta(key, value)`:

```markdown
---
title: About us
description: Who we are
---
```


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset

# `ctx.asset(path)`

Returns the URL for a static file in `pb_pages`, with its content hash. In templates it's also available as `asset`.

```ets
<link rel="stylesheet" href="<%= asset('/assets/app.css') %>">
<!-- <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css"> -->
```

- Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; `/`-paths from `pb_pages`.
- A path that isn't a file in `pb_pages` is returned unchanged.
- The hash is the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: `name.<hash>.ext`.
- Fingerprinted URLs are served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

Relative image paths in Markdown pages go through `ctx.asset` automatically.

See [Asset Management](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve

# `ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?)`

Loads a module from a `_private/` folder. The lookup starts at the **route's** folder (the page being served), wherever `ctx.resolve` is called from, so a layout or partial gets the same answer as the page: `_private/` in the route's folder, then each parent folder up to `pb_pages/`. A name starting with `/` looks only in `pb_pages/_private/`. Without an extension, the name, then `.js`, `.ts` and `.json` are tried.

```ts
// pb_pages/_private/shout.ts
module.exports = (s) => String(s).toUpperCase()
```

```ets
<p><%= ctx.resolve('shout')('hi') %></p>  <!-- HI -->
```

## Modes

| Mode | Returns |
|---|---|
| `require` (default) | The module's exports |
| `raw` | The file's text |
| `script` | The text wrapped in `<script>` |
| `style` | The text wrapped in `<style>` |

```ets
<head>
  <%- ctx.resolve('theme.css', { mode: 'style' }) %>
  <%- ctx.resolve('widgets.js', { mode: 'script' }) %>
</head>
```

## Modules from `node_modules`

Page code can also `require()` by name: `_private/` folders first (nearest to the file calling `require`), then packages from `pb_pages/node_modules`, then the app's usual module paths. See [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/store

# `ctx.store(name, value?)`

The app's in-memory store (`$app.store()`). Set with two arguments, read with one.

```ts
ctx.store('visits', (ctx.store('visits') || 0) + 1)
```

```ets
<p>Visits since start: <%= ctx.store('visits') %></p>
```

- Values are shared by every request to the app.
- The store lives in memory: it's empty again after the app restarts. Keep anything that must last in a collection.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm

# JavaScript Runtime

Middleware, handlers, templates and plugins run in PocketBase's JavaScript runtime. It is neither a browser nor Node.js, so there are no Web APIs or Node APIs such as `Buffer` and `require('fs')`.

Each request runs as one unit under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory). Under a multitenant host, that's the instance's sandbox.

## Talking to the app

Use [`ctx.app`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app), which is `$app`. PocketBase's [JS docs](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-overview/) cover [database operations](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-database/) and [record operations](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-records/):

```ts
const records = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter(
  'articles',
  'status = {:status} && author = {:author}',
  '-created',
  20,
  0,
  { status: 'pending', author: ctx.auth.id }
)
```

## Can I use my favorite npm package?

Maybe. Page code can `require()` modules by name from `_private/` folders (nearest first), then from `pb_pages/node_modules`, then `pb_hooks/node_modules` and the app folder's `node_modules`, then from the app's usual module paths. A `_private/` file with the same name as a package wins. Packages that are plain CommonJS JavaScript, with no Node or browser APIs, have the best chance of working.

Install packages in the app folder (next to `pb_pages`), not inside `pb_pages`. Every file in `pb_pages` that isn't
private is served, so a `package.json` there would be public:

```bash
cd myapp
npm install some-package
```

```ts
const somePackage = require('some-package')
```

Your own modules go in `_private/` and load with [`ctx.resolve()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/typescript

# TypeScript

PocketOne strips the types from `.ts` and `.tsx` files and runs them; it never checks them. To check them, use `tsc` or your editor with the types PocketOne writes for your app.

When the app starts, it writes `types.d.ts` next to `pb_pages` (in the project folder, beside `pb_data` and `pocketone.yaml`) with the declarations of the whole JS API, Pages included. Pages adds no globals: its types live in the `pages` namespace and you use them by name.

## Set up

The app also writes a `tsconfig.json` there when you don't have one. It includes `types.d.ts`, `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations` and `pb_pages`, with JSX checking on (`"jsx": "preserve"`, so no React runtime is needed). Start the app once, then run `npx tsc -p .` or open the folder in your editor. Commit both files, so a fresh checkout is typed before the app first runs.

If you keep your own `tsconfig.json`, include `types.d.ts` and `pb_pages/**/*`, and set `"jsx": "preserve"` and `"skipLibCheck": true` (PocketBase's generated declarations have two type errors of their own).

## The types

| Type | For |
|---|---|
| `pages.Context` | `ctx`: `req`, `res`, `data`, `params`, `route`, `auth`, `app` and the helpers |
| `pages.Handlers` | A page's `.ts` or an endpoint: `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete` |
| `pages.Middleware` | A `+middleware.ts`: `(ctx, next) => ...` |
| `pages.Config` | `+config.ts` |
| `pages.PluginFactory`, `pages.Plugin` | A custom plugin |
| `pages.Props<L>` | A `.tsx` page, layout or partial; `L` types an `include`'s locals |

`satisfies` keeps your own return types and checks the shape:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts
export default {
  async load(ctx) {
    ctx.data.product = await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('products', ctx.params.id)
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { qty } = ctx.req.body<{ qty: number }>()
    return ctx.res.redirect(`/products/${ctx.params.id}`, { flash: `Added ${qty}` })
  },
} satisfies pages.Handlers
```

```ts
// pb_pages/admin/+middleware.ts
const admin: pages.Middleware = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
export default admin
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/_private/badge.tsx, rendered with ctx.include('badge', { label: 'new' })
export default function Badge({ label, asset }: pages.Props<{ label: string }>) {
  return <span class="badge"><img src={asset('star.svg')} />{label}</span>
}
```

A component you import and use as `<Card />` gets only the props you pass it, not `ctx` or `asset`, so give it a props type of its own.

## Your own data, plugins and helpers

`ctx.data` accepts any key. To type yours, or what a custom plugin adds to `ctx`, add to the interfaces in a `.d.ts` file of your own, say `pb_pages/_private/types.d.ts` (in `_private/`, so it isn't served like other files in `pb_pages`):

```ts
declare namespace pages {
  interface Data {
    product?: core.Record
    section?: string
  }
  interface Context {
    hello(): string // added by your plugin's extendContext
  }
}
```

`ctx.session` and `ctx.realtime` are typed as always there; at runtime they exist only when the `auth` and `realtime` plugins are on in `+config.ts`.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication

# Authentication

Pages keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie with the built-in [`auth` plugin](plugins/auth.md). Turn it on:

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = {
  plugins: ['auth'],
}
```

## How a request is authenticated

- If the request has PocketBase's own `Authorization` header, `ctx.auth` is that record.
- Otherwise, the `auth` plugin reads the `pb_auth` cookie, validates the token and sets `ctx.auth` (or clears a bad cookie).
- With neither, `ctx.auth` is `null`.

Every `ctx.session` sign-in method sets the cookie, sets `ctx.auth` for the rest of the request, and returns `{ token, record }`. `ctx.session.signOut()` clears it.

## Protecting pages

```ts
// pb_pages/account/+middleware.ts
module.exports = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
```

```ets
<% if (ctx.auth) { %>
  <p>Welcome, <%= ctx.auth.email() %></p>
  <form method="post" action="/logout"><button>Log out</button></form>
<% } else { %>
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
<% } %>
```

## Passwords

```ts
// pb_pages/login/index.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithPassword(email, password)
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message, email }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/login/index.ets -->
<form method="post">
  <label>Email</label>
  <input name="email" type="email" value="<%= data.email %>" />
  <label>Password</label>
  <input name="password" type="password" />
  <button type="submit">Log in</button>
</form>
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>
```

### Registration

```ts
// pb_pages/register.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { email, password, name } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      ctx.session.register(email, password, { data: { name } })
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: `Error registering: ${e.message}` }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Welcome!' })
  },
}
```

## One-time passwords

A two-step form: request a code, then sign in with it. Turn on OTP for the collection in the dashboard and set up mail (Settings > Mail settings).

```ts
// pb_pages/login/otp/index.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const { step, email, otpId, code } = ctx.req.body()
    try {
      if (step === 'request') {
        return { otpId: ctx.session.requestOTP(email), email }
      }
      ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code)
      return ctx.res.redirect('/', { flash: 'Signed in' })
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message, otpId, email }
    }
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/login/otp/index.ets -->
<% if (data.error) { %><mark><%= data.error %></mark><% } %>

<% if (!data.otpId) { %>
  <form method="post">
    <input type="hidden" name="step" value="request" />
    <input name="email" type="email" required />
    <button type="submit">Send code</button>
  </form>
<% } else { %>
  <p>Check your email for the code.</p>
  <form method="post">
    <input type="hidden" name="step" value="confirm" />
    <input type="hidden" name="otpId" value="<%= data.otpId %>" />
    <input name="code" required />
    <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
  </form>
<% } %>
```

## OAuth2

Configure the provider in the dashboard (Collections > users > Options > OAuth2). Then start the flow from a form:

```html
<form method="post" action="/auth/oauth">
  <input type="hidden" name="provider" value="google" />
  <button type="submit">Sign in with Google</button>
</form>
```

```ts
// pb_pages/auth/oauth.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.requestOAuth2(ctx.req.body().provider)
  },
}
```

`requestOAuth2` stores its state in a cookie and redirects to the provider. The provider sends the user back to `/auth/oauth/confirm` (change it with `{ redirectPath }`):

```ts
// pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/index.ts
module.exports = {
  load(ctx) {
    try {
      ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(ctx.req.query('state'), ctx.req.query('code'))
    } catch (e) {
      return { error: e.message }
    }
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/auth/oauth/confirm/index.ets -->
<mark><%= data.error %></mark>
```

See the [Google OAuth2 speedrun](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2) for setting up Google.

## Anonymous sign-in

```ts
// pb_pages/try.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signInAnonymously()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/dashboard')
  },
}
```

## Your own auth flow

If you authenticate a record yourself, set the session cookie with `ctx.session.signIn(record)`.

## Signing out

```ts
// pb_pages/logout.ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.session.signOut()
    return ctx.res.redirect('/')
  },
}
```

## Security

1. Serve over HTTPS in production.
2. Turn on PocketBase's rate limiting.
3. Turn on email verification for your auth collection.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/realtime

# Realtime Events

PocketBase pushes realtime messages to browsers over server-sent events. In Pages, page code sends, and browsers receive.

## Sending from a page

Turn on the [`realtime` plugin](plugins/realtime.md) and call `ctx.realtime.send()`:

```ts
// pb_pages/+config.ts
module.exports = { plugins: ['realtime'] }
```

```ts
// pb_pages/rooms/[id].ts
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    ctx.realtime.send(`rooms/${ctx.params.id}/delta`, ctx.req.body())
    return ctx.res.json({ ok: true })
  },
}
```

Limit recipients with a filter:

```ts
ctx.realtime.send('alerts', 'Hi', { filter: (client) => !!client.get('auth') })
```

## Listening from a page

`ctx.realtime.subscribe()` listens to a topic as the visitor, with the collection's rules applied, and gives each
change to a `for await` loop. Stream them with `ctx.res.sse()`, or as Datastar patches:

```ts
// pb_pages/rooms/[id]/live.ts
module.exports = {
  async get(ctx) {
    const stream = ctx.res.sse()
    for await (const msg of ctx.realtime.subscribe(`rooms/${ctx.params.id}/delta`)) {
      stream.send('delta', msg)
    }
  },
}
```

See [`ctx.realtime.subscribe()`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime#listening-to-record-changes).

## Receiving in the browser

Use the [PocketBase JS SDK](https://github.com/pocketbase/js-sdk#realtimeservice):

```js
const pb = new PocketBase(location.origin)

const unsubscribe = await pb.realtime.subscribe(`rooms/${ROOM_ID}/delta`, (e) => {
  console.log('Received delta:', e)
})

// Later
unsubscribe()
```

The SDK reconnects on its own and resubscribes to its topics after a reconnect.

## Hypermedia

To push HTML instead of data, see [HTMX Integration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/htmx#realtime-updates) and the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar#broadcasting).

# Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite

The process of setting up a new email domain in Google Suite involves several steps. In this guide, we will walk you through the process, from adding the domain to activating Gmail and setting up a catch-all email. By following these steps, you'll be able to configure your email domain effectively and ensure smooth communication within your organization. Let's get started!

<!-- @import "[TOC]" {cmd="toc" depthFrom=2 depthTo=6 orderedList=false} -->

<!-- code_chunk_output -->

- [Add the domain](#add-the-domain)
- [Domain Verification](#domain-verification)
- [Activating Gmail](#activating-gmail)
- [Adding a Catch-All Email](#adding-a-catch-all-email)
- [Test Your Email Setup](#test-your-email-setup)
- [Add a Sender Account to Gmail](#add-a-sender-account-to-gmail)

<!-- /code_chunk_output -->

## Add the domain

Go to the [domains admin](https://admin.google.com/ac/domains/manage) and add a new domain.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-12-14.png)

Set up an "alias domain," which involves a verification step where you need to update your DNS records. Otherwise, you may have to do the following steps manually.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-04-47.png)

## Domain Verification

If you're using Cloudflare as your DNS manager, Google will automatically recognize it and add the necessary DNS records.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-06-15.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-07-10.png)

Then, wait for domain verification to complete. It should be fast.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-07-35.png)

## Activating Gmail

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-11-38.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-12-59.png)

Once again, Cloudflare makes it easy and automatic. Otherwise, this may involve manual steps if Google is not integrated with your DNS provider.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-14-04.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-15-06.png)

## Adding a Catch-All Email

I set up a catch-all email so that any email sent to `<anything>@pocodex.dev` is routed to `ben@pocodex.dev` if the specific email address doesn’t exist. This is optional, but you might want to consider what happens to unrecognized email addresses in your setup.

[This Google help article](https://apps.google.com/supportwidget/articlehome) covers it, but here it is below too:

I like to go to [Default Routing](https://admin.google.com/ac/apps/gmail/defaultrouting) and add a rule:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-21-45.png)

Use a regex to match the entire domain like `@pocodex\.dev$`. I also like to prepend `[CATCHALL] - ` to the subject so I know that it wasn't sent to my "real" address.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-25-59.png)

Redirect the emails to your "real" email address:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-25-14.png)

Finally, make sure you only perform this on unrecognized email addresses.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-24-55.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-51-48.png)

## Test Your Email Setup

Send an email to yourself using the new domain to ensure that everything is working correctly.

You may need to wait a bit for the MX records to propagate. Just because Google says everything is verified doesn't mean the Internet at large has received the memo.

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-39-27.png)

If you want to be extra sure, try sending from a completely different email provider like Proton or AOL.

Once you receive messages, you're all set!

## Add a Sender Account to Gmail

Sometimes you might want to send email FROM your domain, such as replies or customer messages. To do that, go to your user settings in Gmail and add an account:

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-56-56.png)

![](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail/2024-09-08-19-57-35.png)

# Ask starter

Its files are in [`ext/pages/starters/ask`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/starters/ask). See every [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters).

![The ask kit: a question box over the docs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-ask.jpg)

![A sample docs page in the ask kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-ask-docs.jpg)

Ask your docs a question and get a short answer with links to the pages it came from. The docs are Markdown files in
`pb_pages/docs/`, served as pages and kept in an [LLM Search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/search)
bucket that's read again whenever they change. Each answer is one model call, counted for the visitor, so the limits in
Settings → LLM keep a public copy from running up a bill.

```bash
pocketone pages create mydocs --starter ask
cd mydocs
pocketone superuser upsert you@example.com <password> --dir ./pb_data
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

Then, in the dashboard (http://127.0.0.1:8090/_/):

1. **Settings → LLM:** add a provider with chat and embedding models (Vultr has both), and a limit for **all guests
   together**, such as $1 a day. Answers to visitors who aren't signed in are refused until there is one.
2. Open http://127.0.0.1:8090 and ask something. The first question after a start waits a moment while the docs are
   embedded; **Search** in the dashboard shows the `docs` bucket and its progress.

Make it yours:

- Replace the pages in `pb_pages/docs/` with your own. Every `.md` file there is a page and part of what answers draw on.
- `pb_pages/_private/ask.ts` holds the model (`ASK_MODEL` overrides it), the instructions the model gets, and how many
  passages it reads.
- To answer from another site instead of local files, swap `addFolder` for `addURL` with that site's pages.

## Files

```
pb_pages/
  +layout.ets                    the page shell (MVP.css), with links to Ask and Docs
  index.ets                      the question form and the answer, written on the server (/?q=...)
  _private/ask.ts                the docs bucket, the search and the model call
  docs/                          your docs as Markdown pages: what answers draw on
```

# Auth starter

Its files are in [`ext/pages/starters/auth`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/starters/auth). See every [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters).

![The auth kit's home page, with Login and Register links](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-auth.jpg)

![The auth kit's sign-in page: anonymous and password sign-in](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-auth-login.jpg)

Multi-page app (MPA) auth with the built-in `auth` plugin: register, password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 login, logout, email verification (with a resend page), password reset by email, email change with confirmation, and a protected `/account` section (`account/+middleware.ts`). Sessions are a `pb_auth` cookie managed through `ctx.session.*`; the logged-in user is `ctx.auth`. The included migrations point PocketBase's mail at a local maildev and its email templates at this app's `/auth/confirm/{TOKEN}/...` pages.

Templates are `.ets` (EJS whose tags hold TypeScript) and code files (`+config`, `+middleware`, and the `.ts` beside a page or serving an endpoint) are `.ts`; Pages strips the types when it loads them, so there is still no build step.

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter auth
cd myapp
pocketone superuser upsert you@example.com <password> --dir ./pb_data
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090.

In another terminal, run a local mail catcher for verification, OTP, password reset and email change emails (the migrations send mail to `localhost:1025`; maildev's web UI is at http://localhost:1080):

```bash
npx maildev
```

Notes:

- Anonymous login needs password login enabled (PocketBase's default).
- OTP login is enabled by the migrations. OAuth2 is enabled with no providers: add one in the dashboard under Collections > users > Options > OAuth2.

## Files

```
pb_migrations/                   the users collection's auth settings and email templates
pb_pages/
  +config.ts                     turns on the auth plugin
  +layout.ets
  auth/login/                    index.ts signs in; _private/ holds one form per method (password, otp, oauth2, ...)
  auth/forgot/                   asks for a password reset email
  auth/confirm/[token]/          the pages the emails link to: verification, password reset, email change
  account/+middleware.ts         sends anyone not signed in to the login page
  account/                       the signed-in user's page, and change-email
```

# Datastar starter

Its files are in [`ext/pages/starters/datastar`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/starters/datastar). See every [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters).

![The Datastar kit: chat rooms with a message sent, and a live counter](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-datastar.jpg)

A realtime chat with rooms and a live counter, built with [Datastar](https://data-star.dev/) and the Datastar add-on (`_private/datastar.js`, listed as `'datastar'`) and the built-in `realtime` plugin. Datastar's `@post` calls (the button, or Enter in the message box) hit `/fragments/chat` and `/fragments/count`, sending the page's signals as the JSON body that `ctx.datastar.signals()` reads. `/fragments/count` has a template: because the request carries `Datastar-Request: true`, the rendered page comes back as a `patchElements` event. `/fragments/chat` is an endpoint (`fragments/chat.ts`, no template), so its `post()` builds the response itself. A chat message is also broadcast to every tab in the same room with `ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements`, and `ctx.datastar.patchSignals` clears the input. Open two tabs to watch it update.

Templates are `.ets` (EJS whose tags hold TypeScript) and code files (`+config`, `+middleware`, and the `.ts` beside a page or serving an endpoint) are `.ts`; Pages strips the types when it loads them, so there is still no build step.

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter datastar
cd myapp
pocketone superuser upsert you@example.com <password> --dir ./pb_data
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090.

## Files

```
pb_pages/
  +config.ts                     the datastar add-on and the realtime plugin
  (site)/index.ets               the lobby
  (site)/[roomName]/index.ets    a chat room
  _private/                      the chat, message and counter partials, and datastar.js
  fragments/chat.ts              posts a message and patches every tab in the room
  fragments/count/               the counter, returned as a patchElements event
```

# Choosing a language

A module is a plain WASI program, so any language that builds one works. The program reads its input on stdin, writes its output on stdout, and gets the function it was asked for as its first argument (`run` unless your code says otherwise). It fails by exiting non-zero with a JSON error on stderr. [Writing a module](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/extension#writing-a-module) has the whole contract; each page here shows it in one language, with a module you can build and page code that calls it.

## What each language costs

A module's first call compiles it, which takes time in step with its size, and keeps the machine code in a cache on disk; later calls, after a restart too, load it from there, 20 to 30 times faster. Measured on a laptop (2026-11-18) with the summary example in each language, one call at a time.

| Language | Example | Module | First call | Later calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [C](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/c) | [`summary/c`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/c/main.c) | 25 KB | 17 ms | 0.5 ms |
| [AssemblyScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/assemblyscript) | [`summary/assemblyscript`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/assemblyscript/assembly/index.ts) | 10 KB | 13 ms | 0.5 ms |
| [Rust](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/rust) | [`summary/rust`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/rust/src/main.rs) | 98 KB | 33 ms | 1.3 ms |
| [Zig](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/zig) | [`summary/zig`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/zig/src/main.zig) | 95 KB | 30 ms | 1.2 ms |
| [TinyGo](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/tinygo) | [`summary/tinygo`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/tinygo/main.go) | 284 KB | 74 ms | 3 ms |
| [Go](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/go) | [`summary/go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/go/main.go) | 4.3 MB | 1.05 s | 38 ms |
| [WAT](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/wat), by hand | [`summary/wat`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/wat/summary.wat) | 1.8 KB | 9 ms | 0.4 ms |
| [LLVM IR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/llvm), by hand | [`summary/llvm`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/summary/llvm/summary.ll) | 3.8 KB | 7.5 ms | 0.5 ms |

The last two are written by hand in assembly languages, for fun: they show how small a module can get when nothing comes along that the program doesn't use. Running the summary itself takes under a millisecond in every language; the rest is compiling or loading. A bigger program (a library that parses XML, a crate that resizes images) takes longer in every language, about in step with its size. A call also holds its module's machine code in memory while it runs: under 1 MB for C, Rust, Zig or TinyGo, 18 MB for Go.

## How to pick

- **On a hot path** (every record save, every request): C, Rust, Zig or AssemblyScript. TinyGo if you'd rather write Go.
- **Off the hot path** (a cron job, an import, an admin action): any of them, Go included. Go's 38 ms and 18 MB per call are fine there, and its standard library is all there.
- **For a library that only exists in one language:** that language. Rust has the most libraries that build for WASI as they are; C libraries that only compute (parsers, codecs, compression) build with `zig cc`.
- **Many calls at once:** smaller modules run more at once. With the defaults, 8 calls of a Rust or Zig module run side by side, but only 2 of a Go one (`MaxModulesMB`, in [Configure](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/extension#configure)).

## What runs

Modules run in [wazero](https://wazero.io), which runs WebAssembly 2.0 (SIMD, bulk memory, multi-value and reference types included) and WASI preview 1. Building for these targets works:

| Language | Target |
|---|---|
| C, C++ | `wasm32-wasi` (`zig cc`, or clang with wasi-libc) |
| Rust | `wasm32-wasip1` |
| AssemblyScript | `asc` with `@assemblyscript/wasi-shim` |
| Zig | `wasm32-wasi` |
| TinyGo | `wasip1` |
| Go | `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` |
| WebAssembly text | `wat2wasm` (WABT) |
| LLVM IR | `wasm32-wasi` (`zig cc`, or clang) |

These don't run, and fail when the module loads, with a message that says why:

- **WASI preview 2 and components** (Rust's `wasm32-wasip2`, `cargo component`, `componentize-py`): a component isn't a preview 1 program.
- **Languages that need WebAssembly GC or exception handling** (Kotlin/Wasm, Dart, Java through WasmGC, C++ with exceptions on).
- **Modules that import anything but WASI**, such as an Extism plugin or a module built for the browser (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`, wasm-bindgen).

[Other languages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/others) covers the rest.
