Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/collections

# Collections API

The endpoints the dashboard uses to manage [collections](https://pocketone.dev/docs/collections). All of them are for **superusers**. For
changes that travel with your code, prefer [migrations](https://pocketone.dev/docs/migrations); these are for tools and scripts.

## List collections

`GET /api/collections`

Takes the [list parameters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest#lists) (`page`, `perPage`, `sort`, `filter`, `fields`, `skipTotal`), filtering
on the collection's own properties (`name`, `type`, `system`).

```bash
curl --get http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "filter=type = 'auth'"
```

## View a collection

`GET /api/collections/{collection}`

The collection by name or id: its `fields`, rules, `indexes` and, for auth collections, their sign-in options.

## Create a collection

`POST /api/collections`

The body is the collection, the same shape `GET` returns:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "notes",
    "type": "base",
    "listRule": "owner = @request.auth.id",
    "fields": [
      {"type": "text", "name": "body", "required": true},
      {"type": "relation", "name": "owner", "collectionId": "_pb_users_auth_", "maxSelect": 1}
    ]
  }'
```

## Update a collection

`PATCH /api/collections/{collection}`

Send the properties you change. `fields` is the whole list: fields you leave out are removed (with their data), so send
every field, with its `id`, to keep it.

## Delete a collection

`DELETE /api/collections/{collection}`

Deletes it and all its records (answers `204`). A collection another collection's relation points to can't be deleted
until that relation is removed.

`DELETE /api/collections/{collection}/truncate` deletes all its records and keeps the collection (`204`).

## Import collections

`PUT /api/collections/import`

| Body | |
|---|---|
| `collections` | the collections, as exported (Settings → Export collections) |
| `deleteMissing` | `true` to delete collections (and their records) that aren't in the list |

Answers `204`. Collections are matched by id: existing ones are updated, new ones created.

## Helpers

| Endpoint | Answers |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/collections/meta/scaffolds` | a blank collection of each type (`base`, `auth`, `view`), with its default fields |
| `GET /api/collections/meta/oauth2-providers` | every OAuth2 provider PocketOne knows, with its display name and URLs |
| `POST /api/collections/meta/dry-run-view` | the fields a view collection's `{"query": "SELECT ..."}` would have, without saving it |

## Next

- [Collections and fields](https://pocketone.dev/docs/collections): the collection shape and every field type.
- [Migrations](https://pocketone.dev/docs/migrations): the same changes, versioned with your code.

# Crons API

The app's scheduled jobs: its own (backups, cleanups, whose ids start with `__pb`) and the ones your code adds with
`cronAdd`. All endpoints are for **superusers**.

## List jobs

`GET /api/crons`

```json
[
  { "id": "__pbLogsCleanup__", "expression": "0 */6 * * *" },
  { "id": "nightlyReport", "expression": "0 6 * * *" }
]
```

## Run a job now

`POST /api/crons/{id}`

Starts the job at once, outside its schedule, and answers `204` without waiting for it to finish.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/crons/nightlyReport -H "Authorization: $TOKEN"
```

## Next

- [JavaScript API: `cronAdd`](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase#cronadd): add a job from a hook file.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/files

# Files API

A record's files are uploaded with the record itself (a `multipart/form-data` create or update, see the [Records
API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records#create-a-record)); a `file` field then holds the stored file names. This API serves them.

## Download a file

`GET /api/files/{collection}/{recordId}/{filename}`

| Query | |
|---|---|
| `thumb` | for images: a thumbnail size from the field's `thumbs` list (`100x100`, `0x300`, `300x0`; `t` for top-crop, `b` bottom, `f` fit) |
| `token` | a file token, for a protected file |
| `download` | `1` to download it as an attachment instead of showing it |

```bash
curl -O "http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/files/posts/bxt6kzt400873g5/cover_8k2jd9a1p3.jpg?thumb=100x100"
```

Anyone who may view the record may download its files, unless the field is **protected**.

## Protected files

A field set to **protected** needs a file token. Get one while signed in, then add it to the URL:

`POST /api/files/token`

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/files/token -H "Authorization: $TOKEN"
# {"token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..."}
```

A file token lasts a few minutes (set per collection), so ask for one when you show the file. The download is then
allowed if the token's record may view the file's record.

## Storage

Files are kept in `pb_data/storage`, or in S3-compatible storage when the app's settings say so (**Settings → Files
storage**, or `PATCH /api/settings` with `s3`). The URLs above stay the same either way.

## Next

- [Records API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records): upload and remove files.
- [Collections and fields](https://pocketone.dev/docs/collections): the `file` field's options (size, types, thumbnails, protected).

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/health

# Health API

`GET /api/health`

Answers `200` while the app is serving. Anyone may call it, so it suits load balancers and uptime checks.

```json
{ "code": 200, "message": "API is healthy.", "data": {} }
```

With a superuser's token, `data` also has:

| Key | Is |
|---|---|
| `canBackup` | `false` while a backup or restore is running |
| `realIP` | the client IP the app sees |
| `possibleProxyHeader` | a proxy header the request carried that the app isn't set to trust (set **Settings → Trusted proxy**) |

# Logs API

Every request and every `$app.logger()` line is kept in the app's logs database for **Settings → Logs → Max days**
(5 by default). All endpoints are for **superusers**.

The dashboard's **Logs** screen shows the same entries, with a chart by hour:

![The Logs screen: requests by hour, and each entry with its level, message and data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/dashboard-logs.jpg)

## List logs

`GET /api/logs`

Takes the [list parameters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest#lists). Filter on `level` (`-4` debug, `0` info, `4` warn, `8` error),
`message`, `created` and any of `data`'s keys:

```bash
curl --get http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/logs -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "filter=level >= 4 && data.url ~ '/api/collections/posts'" \
  --data-urlencode "sort=-created"
```

```json
{
  "page": 1, "perPage": 30, "totalItems": 1, "totalPages": 1,
  "items": [{
    "id": "lg6x2m9k4p1q8z0", "created": "2026-11-23 03:40:41.512Z", "level": 8,
    "message": "POST /api/collections/posts/records",
    "data": { "status": 400, "method": "POST", "url": "/api/collections/posts/records", "execTime": 1.2, "error": "Failed to create record." }
  }]
}
```

## View a log

`GET /api/logs/{id}`

## Count by hour

`GET /api/logs/stats`

How many log entries per hour, for a chart; takes `filter`:

```json
[{ "date": "2026-11-23 03:00:00.000Z", "total": 42 }]
```

## Delete all logs

`DELETE /api/logs` empties the logs database (answers `204`).

## Next

- [Custom routes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/routes#middleware-of-your-own): write log lines from your own code with `$app.logger()`.
- [Settings API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/settings): how long logs are kept and at which level.

# Realtime API

Realtime sends record changes to clients as they happen, over [server-sent
events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events). A client connects once, says what it
wants to hear about, and gets an event for each create, update and delete that its auth may see.

The JS SDK does all of this with `pb.collection("posts").subscribe("*", callback)`. Underneath, it's two endpoints.

## Connect

`GET /api/realtime`

Opens the event stream. The first event is `PB_CONNECT`, with the client's id:

```
id:r8vS3kq9vZ0W1x7yBqA2nC5d
event:PB_CONNECT
data:{"clientId":"r8vS3kq9vZ0W1x7yBqA2nC5d"}
```

Keep the connection open. The server closes one that has had no events for 5 minutes, and any connection after 30
minutes; reconnect when it closes (the SDK does, and subscribes again).

## Subscribe

`POST /api/realtime`

| Body | |
|---|---|
| `clientId` | the id from `PB_CONNECT` |
| `subscriptions` | the topics to hear about; replaces the client's current ones (send `[]` to stop) |

Send the client's `Authorization` header with this request: its events are checked against that auth.

| Topic | Gets |
|---|---|
| `posts/*` | every change to any `posts` record the client may list |
| `posts/RECORD_ID` | changes to that one record, if the client may view it |
| `posts/*?options={"query":{"filter":"published=true"}}` | the same, narrowed by a filter (and `expand`, `fields`) |

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/realtime \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"clientId": "r8vS3kq9vZ0W1x7yBqA2nC5d", "subscriptions": ["posts/*"]}'
```

Answers `204`.

## Events

Each change arrives as an event named for the topic it matched:

```
event:posts/*
data:{"action":"create","record":{"collectionName":"posts","id":"bxt6kzt400873g5","title":"Hello World!"}}
```

`action` is `create`, `update` or `delete`. The record is shaped as the Records API would answer it, for this client:
hidden fields left out, [onRecordEnrich](https://pocketone.dev/docs/hooks) applied.

Which events a client gets follows the collection's rules: **list** for `collection/*` topics, **view** for a single
record's topic. A client never hears about a record it couldn't fetch.

## Your own messages

Hooks can send any message to subscribed clients, on topics of your own: see `$app.subscriptionsBroker()` in the
[JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/subscriptions) and the realtime hooks in [Hooks](https://pocketone.dev/docs/hooks#the-apps-own-events).

## Next

- [Records API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records): fetch what changed.
- [API rules and filters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules): what each client may hear about.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records

# Records API

Each collection's records are at `/api/collections/{collection}/records`, where `{collection}` is the collection's
name or id. Who may call each endpoint is the collection's [API rule](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules) for that action; superusers may
call them all.

## List records

`GET /api/collections/{collection}/records`

Allowed by the **list** rule, which also filters what comes back: a client only ever sees the records the rule
matches.

| Query | |
|---|---|
| `page`, `perPage`, `sort`, `filter`, `expand`, `fields`, `skipTotal` | as for [every list](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest#lists) |

```bash
curl --get http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "filter=published = true" \
  --data-urlencode "sort=-created" \
  --data-urlencode "expand=author" \
  --data-urlencode "perPage=10"
```

```json
{
  "page": 1,
  "perPage": 10,
  "totalItems": 1,
  "totalPages": 1,
  "items": [
    {
      "collectionId": "pbc_1125843985",
      "collectionName": "posts",
      "id": "bxt6kzt400873g5",
      "title": "Hello World!",
      "slug": "hello-world",
      "published": true,
      "author": "0slkeutr0bxpw3v",
      "created": "2026-11-23 03:41:28.670Z",
      "updated": "2026-11-23 03:41:28.670Z",
      "expand": {
        "author": { "collectionName": "users", "id": "0slkeutr0bxpw3v", "name": "Ada" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## View a record

`GET /api/collections/{collection}/records/{id}`

Allowed by the **view** rule; a record the rule doesn't match answers 404.

| Query | |
|---|---|
| `expand`, `fields` | as for lists |

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records/bxt6kzt400873g5?expand=author
```

## Create a record

`POST /api/collections/{collection}/records`

Allowed by the **create** rule, checked against the record the body would create. The body is the record's fields, as
JSON, or as `multipart/form-data` to upload files. Leave out `id` to have one made, or send your own (15 characters,
`a-z0-9`).

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title": "Hello World!", "author": "0slkeutr0bxpw3v", "published": true}'
```

With a file:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -F "title=With a cover" \
  -F "author=0slkeutr0bxpw3v" \
  -F "cover=@cover.jpg"
```

It answers the created record (`expand` and `fields` work here too). For an auth collection, send `password` and
`passwordConfirm` with the other fields: that's how sign-up works.

## Update a record

`PATCH /api/collections/{collection}/records/{id}`

Allowed by the **update** rule, checked against the record as it is now (and, with `@request.body`, what's being
sent). Send only the fields you change.

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records/bxt6kzt400873g5 \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title": "Hello again", "views+": 1, "tags+": ["news"]}'
```

Field modifiers change a value relative to what it is:

| Key | Does | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `field+` | adds to a number; appends to a list | number, multi-select, multi-relation, multi-file |
| `+field` | prepends to a list | multi-select, multi-relation, multi-file |
| `field-` | subtracts from a number; removes items from a list | number, multi-select, multi-relation, multi-file |

To remove one file, send `cover-` with its file name; to remove all, send the field empty. To change an auth
record's password, send `oldPassword` (unless a superuser), `password` and `passwordConfirm`.

## Delete a record

`DELETE /api/collections/{collection}/records/{id}`

Allowed by the **delete** rule. Answers `204` with no body. Records pointing at it through a relation with **cascade
delete** are deleted too; otherwise a required relation pointing at it blocks the delete.

```bash
curl -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections/posts/records/bxt6kzt400873g5 \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN"
```

## Expand

`expand` includes related records in `expand` on each record, instead of only their ids:

- `expand=author`: the record a relation points to.
- `expand=author,tags`: several, comma-separated.
- `expand=author.team`: nested, up to 6 levels.
- `expand=comments_via_post`: backwards: the `comments` whose `post` relation points at this record.

Expanded records follow their own collection's **view** rule: one the client may not view is left out.

## Next

- [Authentication API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/authentication): get the token these examples send.
- [Realtime API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/realtime): hear about changes as they happen.
- [Batch API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/batch): several writes in one transaction.
- [Records](https://pocketone.dev/docs/records): the same from your own code.

# Settings API

The app's settings, as the dashboard's **Settings** shows them. All endpoints are for **superusers**.

## Read the settings

`GET /api/settings`

```json
{
  "meta": { "appName": "Acme", "appURL": "https://acme.example.com", "senderName": "Support", "senderAddress": "support@acme.example.com", "hideControls": false, "accentColor": "#1055c9" },
  "smtp": { "enabled": true, "host": "smtp.example.com", "port": 587, "username": "acme", "authMethod": "", "tls": false, "localName": "" },
  "s3": { "enabled": false, "bucket": "", "region": "", "endpoint": "", "accessKey": "", "forcePathStyle": false },
  "backups": { "cron": "", "cronMaxKeep": 3, "s3": { "enabled": false, "bucket": "", "region": "", "endpoint": "", "accessKey": "", "forcePathStyle": false } },
  "batch": { "enabled": false, "maxRequests": 50, "timeout": 3, "maxBodySize": 0 },
  "rateLimits": { "enabled": false, "rules": [] },
  "trustedProxy": { "headers": [], "useLeftmostIP": false },
  "logs": { "maxDays": 5, "minLevel": 0, "logIP": true, "logAuthId": false, "maxDataSize": 0 },
  "superuserIPs": []
}
```

Secrets (`smtp.password`, the `s3` secrets) are never sent back; send them only to change them.

## Change the settings

`PATCH /api/settings`

Send only the sections and keys you change; the answer is the full settings:

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/settings -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"meta": {"appName": "Acme"}, "batch": {"enabled": true}}'
```

## Send a test email

`POST /api/settings/test/email`

| Body | |
|---|---|
| `email` | where to send it |
| `template` | `verification`, `password-reset`, `email-change`, `otp` or `login-alert` |
| `collection` | optional: the auth collection whose template to use (default `_superusers`) |

Answers `204` once the mail server took it.

## Check S3

`POST /api/settings/test/s3` with `{"filesystem": "storage"}` (or `"backups"`) tries the saved S3 settings for files
or backups; `204` if they work, `400` with the reason if not.

## Apple sign-in secret

`POST /api/settings/apple/generate-client-secret` makes the client secret Sign in with Apple needs, from `clientId`,
`teamId`, `keyId`, `privateKey` and `duration` (seconds), and answers `{"secret": "..."}`.

## Next

- [Logs API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/logs), [Backups API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/backups): what some of these settings control.
- [pocketone.yaml](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketone-yaml): PocketOne's own settings, kept in a file.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/sql

# SQL API

`POST /api/sql` (**superusers**)

Runs one SQL statement on the app's main database and answers its result. Reads answer at most 1,000 rows.

| Body | |
|---|---|
| `query` | the statement |

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/sql -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "SELECT author, COUNT(*) AS posts FROM posts GROUP BY author"}'
```

```json
{
  "execTime": 1,
  "affectedRows": 0,
  "columns": [
    { "name": "author", "type": "TEXT", "nullable": true },
    { "name": "posts", "type": "", "nullable": true }
  ],
  "rows": [["0slkeutr0bxpw3v", "1"]]
}
```

`type` is the column's declared type, empty for an expression like `COUNT(*)`; values come back as SQLite gives
them, so an expression's number may arrive as a string.

It runs as written, past rules and hooks, so a write here skips validation: use it for reading and repairs, and the
[Records API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records) for normal writes.

## Next

- [Records](https://pocketone.dev/docs/records#queries-and-raw-sql): queries from your own code, with bound parameters.
